And their Instagram is surprisingly good – lots of behind-the-scenes stuff. See? That gives you insight! You can say you've analyzed their social media presence and noticed their engagement with [mention a specific campaign or feature you observed]. It's about  showing  you can recognise trends and understand audience behaviour, not about knowing complex algorithms. That's a much less intimidating way to look at it. Thank you. It just felt like I was trying to pretend to be someone I’m not. Exactly! They're not expecting you to be a completely different person. They’re employing you for your ability to communicate, your organizational skills – things you’ve got in spades with teaching.

"Right, so, let's actually drill down a bit, shall we? We've been rambling about wanting 'more' for… well, far too long now. The house-sitting has been bliss, honestly, but it's also given us a lot of uninterrupted time to think. More thinking than I'm sure either of us bargained for, actually." “Exactly! Blissful avoidance, almost. It’s beautiful here, absolutely, but it’s really highlighted how…stuck I feel back in Dorchester. Teaching's become more admin than actual teaching, you know? Grading essays feels like a part-time job in itself now. I’m just… drained.” She sighs, tapping her pen against the notepad. "Okay, so you're saying we need concrete steps. Beyond vaguely dreaming of 'something different'." "Precisely. And I think ‘something different’ needs defining. We keep circling back to this idea of a little online business, right? You’re brilliant at crafting, your pottery is gorgeous, and you have a knack for teaching even remotely. Something like selling your pieces online, maybe offering some basic virtual pottery workshops?" "Workshops… I hadn't really thought about that. I always just assumed no one would want to ‘learn pottery’ over Zoom. It feels so… tactile. But you’re right, I suppose. There are people who’d be interested. It's definitely a way to connect and share my passion without the exhaustion of a full classroom." She scribbles something quickly. "Marketing, though. That's the scary bit." "Marketing is… solvable. Honestly, with social media these days, it’s not as daunting as it seems. We could contract someone initially, just to get things off the ground. Etsy, Shopify... we'll research platforms, see what fits. And I’ve a bit of experience with online promotion from my previous ventures. I'm not saying I'm an expert, but I can certainly help get the ball rolling." “That's massively reassuring, actually. I'm good at  making  things, not at shouting about them. What about the legal stuff? Insurance, business registration… the dryer bits.” "Right, the dryer bits. Definitely need to look into that. Australia, thankfully, seems quite straightforward with small business registration. We'll need to do some research on Australian regulations regarding selling handmade goods and running online workshops. I can start looking into that this week – there are some online resources, and we could always consult a business advisor down here, now that we’re experiencing it firsthand."

Honestly, I still think beards are frightfully modern. It's only since that… what’s-his-name, Prince Harry, started sporting one that everyone's suddenly grown them. I mean, a proper gentleman used to be clean-shaven, you see. Oh, Arthur, you’re always so delightfully old-fashioned. Though I have to say, a well-groomed beard can be rather dashing. My grandson, Liam – Speaker_2 – he's fascinated by them. Keeps trying to pull at Daddy’s. He does, doesn't he? It’s a constant battle. "Beard! Beard!" he shouts. He thinks all men should have one. It’s probably because he sees all the builders working on the new housing estate nearby. They all have magnificent beards! Beard! Big beard! Well, I’m flattered, young man. Though it  is  rather unruly some days. It takes a fair bit of tending, you know. A good conditioner, a balm... it's quite the routine. Speaking of routines, and things being difficult, have you heard anything more about the school situation, Eleanor? The waiting list is still terrifying. Apparently, there are more children than places. It’s dreadful, isn’t it? I’ve been on hold with the council for hours this week. They keep saying they'll look into it, but… you know. I'm starting to panic. Liam needs a proper school, not just another temporary solution. It's not fair on him. The housing shortage is a root cause, of course. Bristol’s the same. Developers building massive estates, but no thought given to the infrastructure. And schools are always the last thing on their agenda. They're building houses for…well, for people who evidently don't need to prioritize education. It’s heartbreaking. We've got Polish families moving in, desperate for work, adding to the pressure. And I understand their need to come, of course, but it does exacerbate the problem. When I was teaching, we had a wonderful influx of different cultures, enriched the children’s experiences enormously... but there was still room! Now… It’s just so overwhelming. And with everything else, the cost of food deliveries has skyrocketed. Trying to keep to a healthy diet when it's easier to just order a takeaway is... well, it's a struggle. I’m trying to cut down on sugar, but Liam… he’s a  very  persuasive little negotiator when it comes to biscuits. Ah, the perils of parenthood.

Honestly, Janet, this whole Brexit thing… it’s just exhausting, isn’t it? I’m spending half my day chasing down updates for clients. They’re all panicking, wanting to know what impact it’s going to have on their marketing. Tell me about it, love. It's been a right kerfuffle. Even down at the school, parents are talking about it. Little Timmy's dad works for a firm that exports to Germany, you know? He’s proper worried. But I tell you what, I’m more bothered about getting a car park pass for the school. They've made the rules tighter this year – utter chaos trying to drop off lunches. A car park pass! You’d think with everything going on, that wouldn’t even register. But I can imagine the madness. Remember when we were at sixth form together? The parking was horrendous then, too! Used to have to park miles away and run across the fields in the rain. Oh, goodness me, yes! Those were the days. Mr. Harding used to chase us for being late. And remember David Miller’s awful haircut? He thought he was the bee's knees! I’ve just realised, he’d be about fifty now. Wonder what he's up to. David Miller! Barely remember him, to be honest, that long ago. Though I do remember the piano recitals. You were always so much better than me. I was the one who always ended up playing the wrong notes. You weren’t  that  bad! You were just a bit shy. I always loved playing, though. Still do, sometimes. Little Amy - my granddaughter – she’s showing some interest, you know? Might try to get her lessons started. She’s only six months old, but she already loves banging on the keys. A six-month-old and a piano! That’s adorable. Wonderful to nurture that early interest. How’s Mark coping with all the baby paraphernalia? He’s a proper softie, that one. Completely besotted. Gets up with her every night. Sore as anything! He’s been trying to get back into running, you know, to burn off the energy. Poor thing, he’s struggling. Keeps pulling his hamstring. Oh, that's a shame. Maybe he needs to see a physio. I know a good one near Lichfield, actually. He tends to overdo it, doesn’t he? Always has. Remember when he tried to enter that triathlon?

Och, this is grand, isn’t it? Brucefield Farm, a proper escape. Needed this after wrestling with that Twitter storm this morning. Honestly, thought I’d lose my hair. A Twitter storm, eh? Let me guess, someone decided to make a meal of the latest grant application announcement? They do love to pick at those, don't they? Burns Academy’s accounts are never safe. Worse, actually. Someone started accusing the Scottish Heritage Society – my client, you know – of deliberately obscuring records about a historical battle. Total fabrication, of course, but the outrage… the sheer volume of it… I spent two hours crafting a response that was measured and factual, and it barely made a dent. Measured and factual is rarely what people  want  to see, Alasdair. They want to be inflamed. It's the nature of that platform. I've considered just abandoning it entirely for the Academy. Feels like constantly firefighting. I'm starting to think you're right. The ROI on my time feels dreadful sometimes. What about you? Do you use Twitter much for the Academy? Sparingly. Mostly to highlight student achievements, announce events. Occasionally, I’ll use it to share a particularly interesting historical article, but I avoid anything remotely controversial. Learned my lesson after the wee debate we had about the Jacobites. Remember that? Nearly cracked the entire student body in two. Oh, aye! Good times. Though I did think your point about the romanticism surrounding Bonnie Prince Charlie was spot on, even if it riled a few people up. I mean, it’s all perspective, isn’t it? That’s what I try to remind folks on Twitter – things are rarely as black and white as they appear online. Easier said than done. Their echo chambers are strong, Alasdair. Sometimes, I think the algorithm actively  encourages  polarisation. What about Instagram for you? Do you find that less… volatile? Instagram's a different beast entirely. It’s all carefully curated, isn't it? Gorgeous images, aspirational snippets... I use it for the Society to showcase some of the heritage sites they manage. Gets a good following, surprisingly. More engagement than Twitter, definitely. Though, of course, it's a very different kind of engagement. Less about dialogue, more about pretty pictures. I find Instagram largely pointless for the Academy, to be honest. Trying to make ancient history  visually  appealing is a challenge. We had one student try to recreate a medieval manuscript on TikTok… it was… experimental, to say the least.

Honestly, I need a full body massage. This weekend was… a lot. Tell me about it. You look like you’ve been wrestling alligators. What happened? I’ve just finished a particularly rough shift myself. Double the anxiety, half the sleep. It's just… the community festival. They really leaned on me this year. The gazebo nearly collapsed during Saturday afternoon's pie-eating contest, you wouldn’t believe the chaos. And then the bouncy castle needed constant supervision because some little tyke was trying to climb onto the roof! A bouncy castle roof, really? Sounds like your weekend was a masterclass in crisis management. Pie-eating chaos too? Did you at least get a decent slice? I did not! I was too busy stopping a rogue rhubarb pie from splattering on Mrs. Higgins' prize-winning dahlias. It was a horrifying, sticky situation. How was your shift? Anything exciting, or just the usual existential dread hanging in the air? The usual, unfortunately. Mostly supporting people through panic attacks and trying to convince someone that eating a pint of ice cream isn’t the solution to all their problems. Although, there  was  a breakthrough with David. He actually spoke about his feelings, properly spoke. It was really rewarding. That’s brilliant! Seriously, you’re doing amazing work. It must be exhausting, though. Are you eating properly? You look a bit peaky. I'm trying to. This is lentil soup, my attempt at healthy eating. It's… rustic. Want some? Rustic is a polite word for 'might need more seasoning'. But I’ll try a bit. So, David – proper feelings, you say? Is there a 'she' involved? Not… not necessarily. It was more about his relationship with his family, unresolved stuff from childhood. He's making progress, though. It’s good to see. Anyway, enough about my slightly depressing work life. What about your social life  outside  of stressed-out pie-eating? Any sign of Liam? Not really. He’s been… distant. Keeps saying he’s busy, but his Instagram story always seems to feature him at the pub with his mates. Oh, no. That’s not a great sign, is it? You've only been together for six months. I know, I know. But I thought things were going well. He seemed genuinely interested… or maybe I just wanted him to be. I don’t know. Are all relationships this much of a minefield?

Honestly, Mum, you’d think after all these years, Dad would have his story straight. He was going on about how he "saved" Uncle George from that pub brawl last Saturday, but I heard from Sarah afterward that George was the one doing most of the saving! Oh, your father. Always has to be the hero, doesn't he? It’s endearing, really, in a slightly maddening sort of way. Typical Arthur. Remember when he tried to fix the roof and ended up calling a professional after three hours and a shower of tiles? It's just… exhausting sometimes. He enjoys the drama, you know? Making himself the centre of everything. And George, bless him, just plays along. Keeps the peace, I suppose. It's tiring for everyone involved. Especially for ANON, having to navigate all that when he's just trying to relax. You’re right. Speaking of which, how’s ANON feeling about George's visit next week? Still anxious about the… conversations? Yes, a bit. He’s worried about triggering something, as he always is. We’ve talked about gently steering the conversation away if things get too heavy. And I'll be here to back him up, of course. I might pop over for a bit on Tuesday. Just to lend a hand and take some of the pressure off. Though, I'll probably just end up adding to the chaos, knowing my luck. Don’t say that, Dad! Your presence is always appreciated, even if it does involve recounting some rather embellished story about your days at the firm. Speaking of visits, have you managed to sort out the travel for George? I know he'd rather not take the train again after that debacle with the delayed service last time. I booked him a taxi. Should get him here just after lunch on Monday. It's a bit more expensive, but worth it for the peace of mind. I confirmed everything with the company this morning. Good thinking. He gets so worked up about being late. Remember when he missed Auntie Margret’s wedding because of a bus strike? He was absolutely inconsolable. Oh, George. He’s a character. Still, we have to be mindful. It’s a long trip for him to make. That new car of yours, ANON, will be handy for taking him back on Tuesday. It is, isn’t it? I'm still getting used to the automatic gearbox, but it's a massive upgrade from my old banger.

Cor, this Spanish is brekin’ me, Robert! I swear, I’ve been at it for six months now, and I still feel like I’m just parrotin’ sounds. It's not like learnin' French, y'know? French, you could pick up a few phrases and get by. This…this is a whole different kettle of fish. Tell me about it, Maggie. Six months, eh? I'm on nearly a year, and I'm still struggling with the subjunctive. It’s like they deliberately made it complicated, isn’t it? Just to keep us humble. Humble, aye! More like frustrated! I tried that Duolingo thing, but it just felt like endless repetition without any real understandin’. I switched to that Babbel course, and it’s a bit better, but still… I miss the days of actually  talking  to someone. Back when I was teaching English, gettin' students to speak, even with their mistakes, was brilliant! You could  hear  their progress. I know what you mean. Babbel’s alright, I suppose. A bit robotic for my tastes. You’ve tried italki, have you? With a tutor? I’ve got a lovely woman from Madrid, Elena. She’s very patient. Italki, yeah. Tried one session, cost a fortune! And I froze up completely, couldn't string two words together. Felt a right fool, I did. I’m thinkin’ maybe the problem is  how  I'm learnin'. I'm tryin’ to learn all the grammar rules first, like you do with English. That doesn't seem to be workin'. You're right about that. That's the classic trap. You’ve gotta immerse yourself, Maggie. Just listen, listen, listen. I started watching Spanish telly, even though I understood practically nothing at first. Now, I can follow the gist of things. It’s amazing what your brain can pick up. Have you seen “Money Heist” yet? "Money Heist"? Is that any good? I keep hearin' about it. Brilliant! Very addictive! Lots of slang too, so you get a feel for how people really talk. And you can switch the subtitles on, naturally. Honestly, watching that has made a bigger difference to my Spanish than any textbook ever did. Hmm, that’s a thought. I’ve been tryin’ to learn vocabulary lists, flashcards…all that palaver. Maybe I've been overthinking it. I saw a documentary the other day about Catalonia, did you know they speak Catalan there too?

Right, Dad. So, this bank statement from 2018… do we need to keep all of these? It feels like archaeological evidence at this point. Nah, not that far back, son. Seven years is pushing it. They usually only need five for tax purposes, don't they? Though, knowing the taxman, they'll ask for it anyway. Best to err on the side of caution, I reckon. What about this lot here? Looks like old bills and junk mail. Bin it all, I say. I was thinking the same. There's just… so much. And all these different formats. Honestly, a corpus linguistics project would be fascinated by the variety of fonts and layouts on financial documents over the last twenty years. Think about it – the evolution of fonts alone! Right, you and your fancy words. Corpus linguistics? Sounds like something they’d teach at bloody Oxford. I just want to clear this room so I can actually sit down and watch the football later. Oh, and have you seen anything about Kelly Brook? Remember that shoot she did for… what was it? Something about sausages? I think you're remembering a dream, Dad. Though, she does have a habit of appearing in… unexpected places. More importantly, these flight confirmations – we need to scan those, definitely. They’re likely to ask for proof of travel for the visa renewal. Flying again? Where are you off to this time? Always jetting about, you are. Don't you ever just want to stay put for a bit? I'm still trying to figure out this online banking, by the way. Keeps asking me for two-factor authentication, but I'd rather stand in a queue for an hour than deal with that technology. It’s all designed to confuse old blokes, I tell you. I can show you, Dad. It’s surprisingly straightforward once you get the hang of it. And it's much safer than keeping all your details written down. Speaking of which – these utility bills… should we scan those too? Just the recent ones, I’d say. Anything older than a year is gone. Honestly, I can't believe how much paperwork accumulates. It's like tumbleweed, just rolling around and filling up every space. Did you ever have a good roast here? Mum’s was always top class. I’m proper peckish. I’m thinking of doing one on Sunday.

Honestly, this petrol price is  criminal . I swear it's gone up another 5p since last week! Are you sure you filled up properly back there? I feel like we've barely moved an inch. I absolutely did fill it properly, Liv. Checked the meter myself. It’s just... well, everywhere's charging ridiculous prices right now. It’s the global situation, supply and demand, you know. It’s not personal. Though I  do  feel a pang of sympathy for anyone on a fixed income. Sympathy?! I’m practically living on sympathy at this point! And “global situation,” right. That’s a handy excuse, isn’t it? Anyway, are we absolutely certain this is the right way? It seems awfully…narrow. And bumpy. Trust me. Google Maps said this shortcut would shave off ten minutes. It  should  be fine. Though, I'll admit, it’s a bit more...rural than I anticipated. Rural is one word for it. It's like driving through someone’s backyard. Look at that! A flock of sheep! You’d never see this in Sunderland. Though, I do miss the proper chip shops, to be fair. This countryside air doesn't compensate for a decent battered sausage. You and your chip shops. Alright, alright, point taken. Though, I did find a particularly good pub in a village we drove through earlier. Proper Sunday roast. Want me to find it somewhere so we can go to it later? A proper Sunday roast  does  sound rather tempting. Maybe. But first, let’s just get to ANON’s place, yeah? My bladder’s not exactly cooperating with these bumpy roads. Always thinking of the important things. Right. Speaking of things…did you see that biker gang pulling away from that garage just as we arrived? Quite a sight. Oh, aye! A right load of them. Leather jackets, chrome, the lot. One of them had a proper skull on his headlamp! Proper intimidating, weren't they? I felt a bit…small. They looked pretty organized. Probably heading to a rally or something. I've always been fascinated by bikers, you know? The whole freedom and rebellion thing. It’s almost admirable. Admirable? They looked like they were about to cause some trouble! Reckon they were all going for the same petrol station to try and fuel up for cheap? I wouldn't put it past them to be causing a petrol depletion crisis.

Right, so, David, we were saying earlier… about your tennis. You seemed a bit down after your practice session yesterday. What was it exactly that wasn’t quite right? Just... felt a bit flat, I suppose. Like I wasn't connecting with my shots. And Martin kept saying I wasn't moving my feet enough. Martin's a good coach, you know. Forthright, but good. He wouldn’t say it to be difficult. He sees potential, that’s why he pushes you. Exactly. He's invested in your progress. It’s like proofreading, really – you want someone to pick up on all the little errors, not just the obvious ones, so you can improve. Yeah, but he was going on about Federer for like, ten minutes. About how he anticipates, his footwork, everything. It’s just… Federer. It’s a bit unrealistic, isn’t it? Unrealistic to  aspire  to be like Federer? Not at all! It's about identifying elements you can work on. Think of it this way, David, when I first started managing, I read biographies of CEOs. Some of it was wildly out of reach for me, but the core principles – planning, adaptability, clear communication – those were things I  could  learn and apply. It's the same with tennis. Absolutely. It's about the  principles , love. Federer's footwork isn't just random dancing about the court, it’s incredibly deliberate. He’s constantly moving, reacting, getting himself in the optimal position. That’s something you  can  work towards. But it’s hard! I keep getting caught out, flat-footed. We all do! Remember that time I tried to take up pottery? I was so convinced I'd be making beautiful bowls in a week, and I ended up with a misshapen lump of clay that looked suspiciously like a… well, never mind. The point is, skill takes time and effort. It's not instant. Have you been doing those agility drills Martin suggested? The shuttle runs and the ladder work? Some of them. I kept forgetting to do the ladder ones. Right. Okay. Small steps. Maybe just five minutes before your next practice? It's about building the habit. It's like learning Korean – you can't master it overnight. You do a little every day. And don't get discouraged by comparing yourself to the pros. Even they have off days. I remember watching a match, years ago, between Murray and Nadal… Nadal was just  destroying  Murray.

Honestly, these napkins are a right laugh, aren't they? They look like… well, they look like underpants! Who designs these things? They do, Dad! Auntie Maureen got 'em. She said they were "festive." I reckon she's having a giggle at our expense. Maureen's always been a bit of a card. Remember that Christmas jumper she wore with the reindeer doing… well, let’s just say  interesting  things? Don’t remind me, Mum! It’s a miracle the children didn't choke on their sprouts. Still, adds a bit of character, doesn’t it? Everything's a bit bland if it's all perfectly serious. Speaking of sprouts, anyone want a second helping? Please, Mum! I actually like ‘em this year. University food isn't exactly gourmet, you know. This turkey’s amazing, by the way, Dad. Proper job. Glad to hear it, lass. Been slaving over it since this morning. Hope you’re all enjoying yourselves this Christmas. Makes all the effort worthwhile, doesn’t it? So, El, how are your friends planning on spending theirs? Loads of ‘em are going home, obviously. Sarah and Liam are doing a massive board game night - Monopoly, apparently. They always argue over that game. And Mark's family’s having a Caribbean-themed Christmas. Can you believe it? Baubles and reggae! Caribbean Christmas? That’s rather unusual! We used to just stick to the classics. Wishbone, crackers, the whole shebang. Do you children even know how to break a wishbone anymore? Yeah, I know! You pull each end, right? And whoever gets the bigger piece gets a wish. I wished for a new guitar amp. He's into that heavy music, isn't he? Reminds me of me back in my day! Still listening to that awful… headbanging stuff, are you, lad? It’s not awful, Mum! It's... energetic. Anyway, have you heard that new Christmas song, "Snowflake Symphony"? It’s everywhere. “Snowflake Symphony”? Sounds a bit cheesy, to be honest. Give me Mariah Carey any day. Classic Christmas tune. Oh, I love Mariah! Plays it every year. It's not Christmas without 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'. Do you think they’ll be showing  Downton Abbey  again this Christmas? I always record it. They probably will, Grandma. Loads of people re-watch it every year. I actually used a bit of Downton Abbey inspiration for one of my essays this semester, surprisingly enough.

So, you wouldn't believe the week I’ve had! The Henderson project has been absolutely manic. Honestly, I was living on coffee and adrenaline for a solid three days. Oh, bless you, love. Project Co-ordinator, you always sound so busy. Henderson, you say? Is that the one for the new leisure centre? I vaguely remember hearing about it. Henderson... Henderson... right, that's the one. Big deal for the local area, isn't it? Brings some jobs, hopefully. You are working hard, then, Elodie? Yeah, that’s the one. And it  is  a big deal, but getting all the contractors aligned has been a nightmare. One wanted to use a completely different tile supplier than the other, and they both dug their heels in! I spent hours mediating. It's good when it all comes together though. Did you manage to mark all those exams, Margaret? I know you were stressing about those. Don’t remind me! The Year 11s this year... well, let’s just say they weren’t exactly bursting with enthusiasm. Marking those essays felt like wading through treacle. Though, young Thomas Higgins, he surprised me. Actually quite insightful, that boy. Thomas Higgins, eh? Remember his dad, Derek? Used to work on my uncle’s farm over in Atherstone. Good lad, that Derek. Always had a smile on his face. It's amazing the connections you make, isn't it? And completely random! Dad was telling me the other day about a colleague of his who went to school with someone who ended up being a professional darts player. People are always meeting someone who’s “a bit famous.” It's all relative, isn't it? Still, it’s nice to hear some news that isn’t all doom and gloom. How are things on the farm going, David? The weather's been terrible lately. It's been… challenging. Rain, rain, and more rain. The barley’s struggling, and we’ve had to postpone the sheep shearing by a week. Not ideal, but what can you do? Farmers are resilient, aren't we? Though my back isn't what it used to be. Oh, Dad, you really need to take it easy more. Maybe get a professional in for some of the heavier work? Nonsense. I’m not paying someone to do what I can still manage. Besides, it gets me out of the house. Speaking of which, are you two coming over next weekend for the BBQ?

Honestly, this Bolognese needs a serious amount of seasoning. It's tasting a bit…bland. Did you manage to grab that Parmesan from M&S? They had that really good aged stuff last week. Yep, got it. The food hall there is a revelation, isn't it? Seriously contemplating just buying all my dinners from them from now on. Saves so much faffing about. Are you thinking of getting that new blender they have too? The one with the multiple settings? The one that claims to make perfect smoothies  and  crush ice like a champ? Tempting, very tempting. But our current one soldiered on through years of questionable smoothie concoctions. Feels a bit mean to retire it. Though, the kids are constantly asking for frappés. They’ll be wanting elaborate cheesecakes next! Speaking of which, should we just order a pizza instead? We’re both exhausted. Don't even suggest it. After that disastrous attempt last time? Remember when the delivery guy brought us a pepperoni when we specifically asked for margherita? A dark day. Okay, okay, Bolognese it is. How’s your work been? Anything exciting in the transcription world? Not exactly riveting, no. Had my appraisal this week, actually. The usual – “reliable, accurate, needs to be more proactive.” Proactive at  transcribing , apparently. As if that's a thing. Oh, the joys of corporate speak. Did they at least give you a decent raise? A token gesture, let’s say. Enough to cover the M&S Parmesan, but not enough to buy the fancy blender. And my line manager keeps going on about ‘leveraging synergies’. Synergies! What is she even talking about? Sounds like management jargon designed to impress rather than actually communicate. Reminds me of the endless meetings we used to have back in the public sector. Fourteen-year-old Rioja, I think? Treating ourselves. Excellent choice. Thank you. You know, I was reading about the work the RDA is doing with rescued horses. It’s heartbreaking, some of those stories. The neglect… Absolutely dreadful. We should donate again, shouldn’t we? It’s easy to forget how much care those animals need. Are you still doing the Sunday newspaper crossword? Slowly chipping away at it. The cryptic clues are infuriating! This one about a “feline fascination” had me stumped for ages. Turns out it was “catnip.” You’re getting the hang of it! Speaking of infuriating, did you ever finish  The Walking Dead ?

Honestly, I'm feeling a right state. This dress is itching me to bits. Mum thought it looked lovely, bless 'er, but it's like sandpaper against me skin. Aye, that sounds grim, lass! You shoulda known better than to trust yer mum’s fashion sense entirely. She still thinks corduroy trousers are at the height of style. What  is  it, anyway? Some cheap polyester? Oh, don’t start on mums! Mine tried to get me into a jumpsuit. A  jumpsuit , Chloe! And it was beige. Beige! I managed to convince her a sparkly top was a better option. This skirt's doing the trick though, innit? Shows off the legs nicely. Sparkly, eh? I went for something a bit more understated. This little black dress is always reliable. Smart enough for a night out, comfy enough for a decent amount of dancing. Plus, it hides a fair bit of prosecco, which is always a bonus. Dancing? With these heels?! . I'm gonna be hobbling by ten o'clock, I swear. Why do women even  wear  heels? Torture devices, that's what they are. I'm gonna have blisters the size of Yorkshire puddings by the end of the night. You are a drama queen, Liv! They make yer legs look longer. And who's gonna notice yer blisters when you're having a good time? Besides, I've got these fabulous new boots on. Got 'em in Sheffield, they're a steal. Proper block heel, so they're actually manageable. Sheffield, eh? Proper bargain hunting then! I was in Liverpool ONE today, and it's just… ridiculous. Everything's so expensive. I ended up just browsing. Spotted the cutest little bag, though – bright pink, with little pom-poms. Tempted… very tempted. Pink pom-poms? That sounds… intense. I can’t carry that off. I'd look like a giant toddler. I'm sticking to black. Always a safe bet. Although, I do wish I'd bought that velvet blazer. Saw it in Primark, and it was gorgeous. Should've just gone for it. Primark’s got some real gems, if you’re willing to rummage. I picked up a killer sequin top there last week. You can’t beat a bit of sparkle for a night out. Just gotta be careful about quality control, you know? Don't want it falling apart halfway through the night. Quality control is a myth with student budgets, isn’t it?

You know, I was thinking this morning about that documentary we watched last week, the one about ancient Egypt? The sheer scale of it all… building the pyramids, the religious fervour… it’s just mind-boggling. Makes you wonder what we’ll leave behind, doesn’t it? It does. Though I suspect our legacy will be considerably less impressive than a monumental structure designed to house a pharaoh’s remains for eternity. Though, think of the data centres we build – maybe  that’s  our pyramids. Holding information, essential to our… afterlife, in a way. A digital tomb. You and your IT metaphors! A digital tomb. Rather bleak, isn’t it? I was hoping for something a bit more… whimsical. Like throwing a massive party across time. Imagine, everyone from Cleopatra to Bowie, Shakespeare to Marie Curie, all crammed into the garden, sipping cocktails and arguing about the merits of different eras. Now  that  is more appealing. Though the logistics… trying to explain indoor plumbing to Henry VIII would be a nightmare. And can you imagine the arguments about music? “No, Cleopatra, this isn’t worthy entertainment! Where is the lyre player?!” Exactly! But it would be glorious chaos. And think about the conversations. What would Bowie say to Shakespeare about iambic pentameter? Would Marie Curie try to explain radioactivity to Cleopatra? She’d probably just tell her it involved shiny rocks. Simplify things for the ancient royalty. It would be tempting to assign people seating arrangements strategically. Keep the Tudors away from the French, for example. The Wars of Religion wouldn’t need re-enacting at my garden party! Agreed. Though, I’d secretly love to see Elizabeth I and Joan of Arc in a proper debate. Two incredibly strong women, clashing ideologies... It would be fascinating. It makes you think about soulmates, doesn’t it? Not just romantic ones, but intellectual soulmates. People who just  get  you, challenges you, even if you disagree. Absolutely. I often think about that. I mean, I feel pretty content with you, don't I? I find you incredibly stimulating, you always have a unique perspective. It's not just about romantic connection. Well, you’re pretty stimulating too. Arguably  too  much sometimes, with all your philosophical musings. Though occasionally I find myself thinking about my spiritual journey, or lack thereof. Do you ever feel like you're searching for something… more? I used to, much more.

Honestly, Sarah, this new air conditioning unit is a lifesaver. Peterborough in July – it’s unbearable! I was melting just getting the groceries in. I can imagine! We had a dreadful heatwave in London last week. Took me three hours to get across town. People were just… grumpy, you know? Completely non-functional. Did you manage to get any knitting done in this heat? I was hoping to finish that scarf for Emily's baby. Ooh, a baby scarf! Cute! Are you using that chunky merino again? It’s so lovely. I keep meaning to learn to knit properly. My nan used to make the most amazing things. Proper blankets and jumpers. It's a dying art, isn't it? It is a little. Though, there’s been a bit of a resurgence online, hasn't there? Loads of young people getting into it. Carol from accounts started knitting during lockdown – apparently, it’s really therapeutic after dealing with spreadsheets all day. Anyway, speaking of work… I'm having a nightmare with Janice in HR. She keeps calling in sick. Again. It’s impacting everything. Oh, that’s dreadful. Is she genuinely unwell? Or do you suspect…? I’ve had colleagues like that, you know, milk it for all it’s worth. It's so frustrating, especially when everyone else is carrying the load. It's awful, isn't it? My mate, Liam, at the office, he’s been struggling too. His dad's been ill. He's trying to juggle work and looking after him. It’s a lot. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About how little support people often get. Absolutely. It does. We're trying to be supportive, but it puts a strain on resources. Speaking of things that put a strain on things... have you been seeing all this on the news about the gun violence in America? It’s just… horrifying. It is. It feels like a regular occurrence now, doesn’t it? It’s so foreign to our experience here. I mean, you hear about stabbings, sadly, but the scale of gun violence… it’s just unimaginable. It makes you appreciate the safety we have here. It does, yeah. Though, you hear stories, don’t you? About petty crime and stuff, which is worrying. It feels like things are escalating, somehow. My nan always says Peterborough used to be so much safer. Even the graveyard down on Park Road… she used to wander around there as a kid, reading the tombstones.

Right, this is a disaster. Absolutely a blooming disaster. What's up, Liv? You sound like you’ve just stubbed your toe on a badger. Worse, Finn. Much worse. Remember I said I was meeting Chloe and Ben for drinks tonight? Yeah? What happened? Did Ben finally reveal his secret collection of porcelain dolls? No, nothing that weird, thank goodness. But Chloe’s invited… Gareth. Gareth from our history seminar. Gareth? The one who smells vaguely of mothballs and only talks about the Treaty of Versailles? The very same. And he's  really  keen on Chloe. Like, aggressively keen. He kept staring at her and making these… intense pronouncements about the symbolism of her scarf. Oh, that’s rich. Poor Chloe. She’s too nice to tell him to pipe down. Exactly! She looked absolutely mortified. I tried to subtly steer the conversation away from the war, but he kept bringing it back! He even tried to compare her cocktail to the conditions in the trenches. Honestly! That’s… impressively awful. You’re a good friend for trying to intervene. I felt bad for her, but even worse, I’m now worried about the football match Saturday! We all promised to go and watch the lads play, but if Gareth decides he wants to spend the whole time reciting historical facts about the stadium… Well, that’s one way to ruin a perfectly good afternoon, isn't it? Listen, Liv, you’re not responsible for Gareth's social awkwardness. Chloe can handle herself. And if things get truly unbearable, you both can just disappear for a pint. True. A pint sounds amazing, actually. I’m also proper broke. Rent's due, and I forgot about the deadline for that tax form thing. Oh yeah, the tax form. I still haven’t done mine. Honestly, no one explains that properly, do they? It’s just… a wall of numbers and jargon. It is! Thankfully, the uni has a drop-in session next week. I’m going. We should all go together. Misery loves company, and tax forms. You’re terrible. But yeah, that’s a good idea. Maybe we can borrow some tips from someone who actually knows what they're doing. Speaking of borrowing, Finn, you still got that extra copy of the textbook for Roman History? I'm struggling with the chapter on Hadrian’s Wall. Yeah, it’s under my bed somewhere.

Right then, that sea bass was absolutely spot on, wasn't it? Honestly, after navigating Birmingham New Street Station this morning, this is exactly what I needed. A bit of sunshine, decent food, and… family squabbling. Aye, don't start, Dad. It wasn’t  that  bad. And I’m not squabbling, I’m just asking a perfectly reasonable question. What's this reasonable question then, love? You’ve been simmering about it for half an hour. It's about Liam's tattoo, Mum. Honestly, a dragon breathing fire? On his leg? At fifteen? It’s a bit… much, isn't it? It's cool! Everyone's getting 'em! And it’s not  just  a dragon, it's a Lancashire dragon! It represents where I'm from. You wouldn't understand. Lancashire dragon, eh? Well, I'm not sure about the artistic merit, son, but I appreciate the sentiment. Shows some pride in your roots. Although, a subtle rose might’ve been a bit more… versatile for future job applications. Honestly, your dad, always worrying about job applications. Liam, are you at least thinking about what you want to do after school? Are you sticking with the A-Levels? I dunno, Mum. Still thinking about it. Mrs. Davies says I’m good at History, but I’m not that bothered about it. I was thinking maybe a welding course at the college. Welding? Seriously? Well, that’s… different. It's hands-on though, isn’t it? Better than just sitting behind a desk all day. It’s a solid trade, Liam. Always a demand for skilled welders. Far more practical than, say, becoming a… social media influencer. Dad! No one wants me to be a social media influencer! Don’t be cheeky, love. Though, that Facebook group you were on about the other day... all those pictures of the dogs at the park... it  is  quite addictive, isn't it? Tell me about it! I've been trying to convince you to join, Mum. It'd be great to see pictures of the new puppies at the hospital. It's a nice pick-me-up for the parents. I’m on the fence, lass. I worry about the privacy. You know how people post things... all that personal information floating around. Absolutely. It’s terrifying. That’s why I stick to LinkedIn. All very professional, very controlled. Though, finding a decent supermarket delivery service in Istria is proving to be less controlled.

Blimey, that was a drive! Worth it though, wasn't it? Cornwall’s just… revitalising. Even with the downpours. Absolutely, love. Just look at these photos! I've been sorting through them. Your cycling, dear - you were a blur! Cor blimey! You were movin’ like a whippet, weren’t you, lad? That cycle race… looked dashed exciting. Nearly fell off the bench tryin’ to follow it. Is that the Lizard Point Lighthouse, then? Always wanted to see that. It is! We finally made it out to it on the last afternoon, just after a particularly biblical shower. Magnificent, wasn't it? That Cornish light… just cuts right through you. Though I nearly blew away trying to get a good photo of it. You always do, David. You and your photos! Remember that time in Whitby? You nearly ended up in the North Sea! Don't remind me! The wind was something else. Still, got a brilliant shot of the Abbey. Anyway, the YHA was lovely, wasn't it, Margaret? Such a friendly bunch of volunteers. It was, dear. The young girl who was managing the place, Emily, was just a gem. So enthusiastic. Made us feel quite old, though, all those youngsters bounding about! Youngsters, eh? They don’t know what it’s like to wait for the job centre to ring, do they? Used to spend a good few hours down there, hopin’ for somethin’. But Cornwall… birdsong, sea air… right tonic that. Took me right back to my youth, it did. Used to go fishin’ down the Broads, you know. Catchin' some right beauties. I wish we’d made more time for the coast path. It looked stunning. We spent a silly amount of time chasing crabs on the beach with the kids, though. Lily and Tom were absolutely captivated! Look at them! Covered in sand and smiles. It’s lovely to see them enjoying themselves so much. Actually, I was thinking… next year we could try somewhere different. Maybe Yorkshire? Yorkshire? Cor! A whole county in a day? Sounds a bit ambitious, don't you think? My legs wouldn’t thank you for it, they wouldn’t. Margaret’s got a proper itinerary planned, Brian. She wants to see the Moors, York Minster, and… something about a pudding? Yorkshire pudding, dear! Of course! And we could do a bit of hiking. A gentle bit, just for Brian, of course.

This shepherd's pie is absolutely lovely, Anon. Seriously, your grandma really outdid herself this time. Proper comfort food. Aye, it is good. Mum's shepherd's pie never quite hits the same, you know? Always a bit… bland. You’re tellin’ me! My nan’s shepherd's pie is legendary. She puts extra Worcestershire sauce in, you can practically taste the savoury. It’s the secret, she says. Though she'd probably murder me if she knew I was tellin’ everyone. Worcestershire sauce is a game changer. So, Elara, you've been awfully quiet tonight. Everything alright? Still feeling a bit off after that… incident with the dating app? Aye, still a bit raw, to be honest. He seemed alright in photos, right? Funny banter, said he liked hiking, indie music... All my stuff. Then, first date, he spent the entire time talking about his vintage stamp collection. Like, non-stop. Stamps? Seriously? That’s a bit… niche. Niche is putting it mildly! He brought a magnifying glass and kept showing me tiny pictures of different monarchs. I felt like I was at a museum, not on a date. I ended up fabricating a phone call from my gran just to escape. Oh, Elara, that’s awful! You did the right thing, though. Run away from stamp enthusiasts, honestly. There are plenty of other fish in the sea. Did he at least offer to buy you a drink? He did, but then proceeded to lecture me on the history of brewing techniques. Don’t get me wrong, proper interesting stuff, but not exactly what you want on a first date, is it? I’m starting to think online dating is a complete waste of time. It can be. I've had a few… interesting encounters myself. Once met someone who genuinely believed they were descended from Vikings. Kept trying to teach me Old Norse. Oh, you're kidding! I wish I was. It was mental. But y’know, it makes for a good story. You gotta take the rough with the smooth, innit? True enough. But still, it’s disheartening. I just want someone who’s… normal. Someone who enjoys a pint and a chat, without analysing the hops or the historical significance of the glassware. Normal is overrated, Elara. You're a brilliant, funny, slightly quirky person. You’ll attract someone who appreciates that. Maybe try a different app?

Oh my  god . Barcelona was… incredible. Seriously, I feel like I need a week just to process it all. You wouldn’t  believe  the tapas. Welcome back! I was starting to think you’d escaped to another dimension. How was it  really ? I saw your Insta stories, obviously, but those don’t even scratch the surface, do they? No way! Insta is just snippets. It was so much more than just beaches and sangria, though there was plenty of that, naturally. We did the Sagrada Familia, which… wow. Just… wow. Pictures don’t do it justice. The light, the detail… it was genuinely moving. I know, right? I've seen photos, but experiencing it in person must be something else. Did you manage to get tickets beforehand? I hear they sell out instantly. Thankfully, yes! My friend Chloe is a legend with online booking. We scored tickets for the early morning tour. Best decision ever, because it wasn’t swarming with people. Then we wandered around the Gothic Quarter, got utterly lost in the best possible way, and stumbled across this tiny little bakery selling the most amazing  crema catalana . Sounds idyllic. I'm jealous! I had a pretty chilled weekend, to be honest. Caught up on some reading, binged that new true crime documentary… you know, nurse stuff – a bit morbid but strangely relaxing. Oh, what documentary was it? I'm always on the lookout for recommendations. And don’t sell yourself short! Being a mental health nurse is  anything  but chilled! You're doing really important work, you know. True, true. It's just… quieter than wrangling patients on a Friday night. This one was about a string of disappearances in a small town. Pretty bleak, but brilliantly put together. Anyway, tell me more about Barcelona! Paris is still on the cards for next year, right? We talked about it forever ago. Absolutely! Barcelona has totally renewed my wanderlust. Paris feels even more essential now. We should start looking at flights soon. What about you? Any exciting plans coming up? Aside from the potentially unsettling true crime viewing, of course. Nothing concrete yet. Mum keeps hinting about a family trip to Cornwall in the summer, which would be… nice. Though I'm secretly hoping to finally get that week off to visit my cousin in Edinburgh. He’s been going on about the Fringe Festival for ages. Cornwall sounds good for a relaxed break.

Honestly, this is just… bliss. I didn’t realise I needed this so much. Teaching can be utterly draining, you know? It’s lovely seeing the kids learn, of course, but the paperwork… the meetings… it's relentless. Tell me about it. Though my ‘paperwork’ tends to involve spreadsheets and contracts rather than lesson plans. It’s a different kind of relentless, believe me. Running your own business, you’re always  on . Even on a Sunday morning in North Cyprus, part of my brain is still ticking over, thinking about logistics and marketing. Logistics and marketing! Sounds terribly important, whatever you do. What  is  it exactly? You mentioned something about… tech solutions? Yeah, roughly. I develop software for small businesses, mainly in the hospitality sector. Online booking systems, inventory management, that sort of thing. Boring to most, crucial to them. I started just after university, really. A bit of a gamble, saving every penny, renting a tiny office… but it's taken off, surprisingly. That’s astonishing! So, you always knew you wanted to be an entrepreneur? Some of my students dream of being YouTubers, you know, but few have the drive to actually  do  it. Not at all. I studied Economics, thinking I’d end up in a City bank, all suits and sharp numbers. Horrified me, to be honest. The whole culture just felt… devoid of meaning. My first job was as a junior analyst, and I lasted about six months. I felt my soul slowly shrivelling up. Hence the software. It was born out of frustration, really – seeing how many pubs and restaurants were struggling with outdated systems. I completely understand that. Feeling trapped. I actually started out wanting to be a marine biologist, can you believe it? Dorchester is right on the coast, so I was obsessed with the sea. Ended up studying Biology at university, and then… well, life happened. Teaching felt like the sensible thing to do. Stable, rewarding in its own way, but… not the ocean. Sensible rarely equates to fulfilling, does it? My mum was forever telling me to get a "proper job." Still does, actually. Though I think she's grudgingly accepted that I haven’t completely ruined my life. What was the biggest draw to teaching? The kids, definitely. Seeing that lightbulb moment, when something finally clicks. Plus, I’m quite good at explaining things, I think. My sister always used to moan I'd explain how to make a cup of tea like giving a lecture.

Honestly, Liam, I'm proper stressed about this house situation. It's gettin' to me, it really is. What's up, love? More trouble with Finn again? He leave the teabags on the counter  again ? It's not just the teabags, is it? It's everything. It’s the never-ending pile of washing buildin' up in the bathroom, the dishes stackin' up in the sink lookin' like a archeological dig… and don’t even get me started on the pizza boxes! They're like little monuments to Finn's laziness. He does have a fondness for pizza, that’s true. But you know Finn. He means well. Meanin' well and actually  doing  somethin' are two entirely different things, aren’t they? And then there's Chloe. She's lovely, don't get me wrong, but she just… drifts. Like a little cloud. Everything's fine, fine, fine, until suddenly it isn't, and then I'm left pickin' up the pieces. So, you feel like you're doing all the housework? Aye, pretty much. I’m not askin' for a spotless house, Liam. Just a bit of effort! I mean, I work part-time and I’m studyin’, I’m not made of time. It’s just… tiring, eh? Makes you feel a bit taken advantage of. I can see that. It’s not ideal. Have you tried having a proper sit-down with them? Like, a house meeting? I did, last week. It went about as well as you’d expect. Finn promised to "be better" and Chloe mumbled something about being "really busy" with her pottery. Pottery! Like that excuses a sink full of dirty plates! Alright, alright, pottery’s a valid hobby. But I get your frustration. So, it didn’t go well. What did you try to say? I tried to explain, you know, that we all need to chip in and contribute. That it’s not fair for me to be constantly cleaning up after everyone. That I’m not their maid! But they just sort of looked at me with those blank faces. Honestly, you’d think I was asking them to move mountains. Maybe they don’t realise how much you're doin’? Sometimes people are just oblivious. They get used to a certain routine, and don’t notice what’s not being done. Aye, that’s probably it. They’re just… comfortable.

Right then, that’s the lot. My goodness, didn’t realise it was so much when we left! You wouldn’t believe the queue at the greengrocer’s today. Absolutely rammed, it was. Aye, seems like everyone's stocking up, doesn't it? Bit nippy out today, too. Felt a right chill wind when I was bringing the car round. Did you get those plums I asked for? Of course, love. Two punnets. The ones from Kent, just like you like 'em. And some of those biscuits you’re always on about – the custard creams. They were a bit pricey, mind you. Everything is, isn’t it? Always are, Maggie. Can’t escape it, can you? Though, custard creams are worth every penny. Proper treat they are. Did you see Mrs. Higgins down at the shops? Looking a bit peaky, she was. I did, poor dear. Said she's got that rheumatiz acting up something awful. She was moaning about the doctor not being able to do anything proper about it. Seems a bit dismissive of the older folks, doesn't he? He always was a bit green behind the ears, that doctor. Reminds me of the one we had back in Costessey. Always rushing, never really listening. You felt like you were just a number on a sheet, you know? Exactly! It’s just… you need someone who understands. Someone who remembers what it was like when things were done properly. It's not just about prescriptions, is it? It’s about feeling like someone cares. That’s it exactly. You realize that as you get a bit older, don’t you? All this newfangled technology, doctors ordering things online… where's the personal touch gone? Don’t even get me started on online booking! Trying to navigate that website was a nightmare. I nearly threw the tablet out the window. Ended up asking young Thomas next door to do it for me. Bless him. He's a good boy, Thomas. A good lad, aye. Always polite. Reminds me of your grandson, Daniel, when he was little. Remember how he used to bring me daisies? He was a right sweetheart, that boy. Oh, I do. He’d present them to me with such pride. He’s a fine young man now, though. Working in that advertising agency in London, can you believe it? Fancy that, can you. London! A long way from Costessey.

Right then, let’s have a proper look at this, shall we? Gareth, put your feet up, love. Grandma and Grandpa are just settling in. Honestly, these gas bills are something else, aren't they? Proper daylight robbery, I say. Yeah, they’re mental. Is there anything on telly worth watching tonight? Think they got that new detective series on? Detective series? Bah! All that fancy forensic stuff. Give me a good old Poirot any day. Solving things with his brain, not a load of gadgets. Used to love Poirot, me and Arthur. Poirot was alright. Bit slow, though. Needed a bit more action, he did. Remember that time we tried to build a bird table, Elsie? Now  that  was action. Oh, Grandpa! You nearly hammered your thumb off, didn't you? Gareth, love, could you pop out to the shops and get some biscuits? Grandma loves a digestive with her tea. And some of those shortbread ones, if they've got 'em. Fine, fine. Anything else? I’m heading out, you know. Need to grab some controllers. Just be back before dark, lad. And Gareth, watch you don't spend all your savings on them games! And a bottle of that fizzy water Grandma likes, won't ya? She's been moaning about the lack of bubbles. Fizzy water indeed. Back in my day, fizzy water was a treat. Now they fill it with all sorts of things. Makes you wonder, doesn’t it? Everything’s changed, Elsie. Changed for the worse, most of it. Remember when you could get a loaf of bread for tuppence? Don't start going on about the old days, Arthur. You'll be talking about rationing again! Least we've got central heating now, eh? It’s just costing a fortune! Gareth, quick action, no time to waste. Those biscuits! Right, biscuits and fizzy water. And maybe some of those chocolate ones, just for me. Grandma, Grandpa, you comfy? Want me to turn on the telly for you? Just put on something nice and quiet, love. No need for all that shouting and explosions. Give us a bit of classical music, if you will. Classical music? Makes me sleepy. Put on some Vera Lynn! Now  that's  music. Reminds me of the war. Vera Lynn? Alright, alright. Gareth, when you're back, maybe you can sort the playlist out, eh? Rest your brain cells for a bit...

Right, so the dentist’s due any minute now. Anyone else feel like their teeth are actively plotting against them? Nah, I'm alright, honestly. Just a bit bored waitin’, innit? Wish they’d given us a more accurate time. Feels like we’ve been here an hour already. Don't remind me! I was  just  getting into a decent game on my phone. Speaking of which, anyone tried out those new sleep trackers? I saw an ad pop up, apparently they're brilliant for monitoring your sleep cycles. Yeah, I’ve been looking at those. My mate, Liam, swears by his. Says it showed him he was snoring like a freight train and he got a nasal strip from it. He reckons it’s improved his morning energy levels. Bit weird, innit? Snoring’s not weird. It's a biological imperative. My dad's a champion snorer. You could hear him two rooms away. Used to drive my mum mad. She tried everything – earplugs, white noise machines... nothing worked. Sounds familiar. My mum’s always going on about how my dad's snoring disrupts her sleep. Says he sounds like a seal. My grandma’s the same! She’s convinced my grandad is single-handedly responsible for climate change 'cause of the noise he makes at night. Little bit extreme, that. Right! Okay, moving on from the nocturnal noises… Has anyone seen that new show on Netflix, ‘Cyberpunk Dreams’? It’s mental. All neon lights and dodgy tech. I streamed the first episode. It’s alright, bit overdone for me though. Too much grit, not enough… well, I don’t know…  heart , maybe? I’m more of a period drama man myself. Just finished ‘Bridgerton’ again. Can’t get enough of the costumes and the gossip. Bridgerton's trash. You're all wasting your time. Oh, yeah? What’s your sophisticated taste, then? Dusting off ancient scrolls? I appreciate documentaries. Things with actual substance. Like… I watched one on the history of basket weaving last week. Fascinating. Basket weaving?! Seriously? You’re pulling my leg, right? I wasn’t joking. It's a complex craft with a rich history. Alright, alright, settle down, you two. Let's not get into a documentary debate. So... anyone been doing any gym recently? I'm trying to get back into a routine after exam season. Felt like I’d forgotten what my muscles were for.

Right, so, this trip to the shops tomorrow – we really need to be organised. I’ve got a conference call first thing, so I’ll be running late. Who's doing the main shop? I can do the big shop, Dad. Just need to figure out what everyone wants. Mum, what are we needing? Well, we’re almost out of milk, definitely need bread, and some eggs. And some of that special camomile tea for me, the one from Holland & Barrett. My bite's still a bit itchy. Can we get crisps? Proper, thick-cut ones! And maybe some chocolate bars? Always the essentials, eh, Liam? Alright, crisps, chocolate bars – added to the list. Mum, how bad is the bite? Did you try anything for it? It’s just a wee thing, but it's been driving me mad all afternoon. I put some cream on it, but it’s not really helping. Probably a midge bite. There’s been a right swarm of them lately. Awful. True, I got bitten something shocking down the park yesterday. I used some of that insect repellent spray, the lavender one. Does that work at all, Mum? Nah, not really. Just smells nice. Honestly, I think having a cold compress is the best thing. Maybe some bicarbonate of soda paste? Used to work wonders when you were little, love. Right, bicarbonate of soda – adding to the list. And lavender spray for you, love, just in case. Though, frankly, with the state of the weather we're having, anything could be biting us. Speaking of which, have you noticed how many wasps there are this year? Nasty little things. I saw one buzzing around the bin earlier! It was huge! They’re terrible this year, aren't they? I almost got stung last week. I think it was because I was drinking juice outside. They’re drawn to sugary things, you know. Aye, that's right. Remember Uncle George getting stung by a wasp when he was a lad? Swelled up like a balloon! Oh, I remember that! He was off work for a week. Right, so, stop reminiscing about Uncle George. Crisps, chocolate, milk, bread, eggs, camomile tea, bicarbonate of soda, lavender spray… Anything else? We also need to pick up a new football for Liam. His old one’s practically falling apart. Can it be the Man U one? Please, please? You always want the Man U one, don't you?

Ugh, seriously, Mr. Davies  still  hasn't posted the P.E. marks. It's been like, three days. I need to know if I passed the fitness test! Relax, Liv. He’ll post them. Probably massively delayed because he's too busy trying to film those awful TikToks with the other teachers. Did you see Mrs. Peterson attempting a dance move? It was...cringey, to say the least. Oh my god, no! Don’t tell me! I'm trying to avoid anything school-related right now. The science practical today was a disaster. I somehow managed to spill the iodine all over Chloe's lab coat. No way! Chloe’s gonna be fuming. She's so precious about her things, isn't she? You should have seen her face when that happened! It was proper dramatic. I know! I felt awful. Mrs. Harrison gave me this look, like I’d intentionally ruined Chloe’s coat. I tried to explain, but… iodine is messy! And it just… happened. Science is just not my thing. I’d rather be watching Alfie Deyes’ latest vlog, honestly. Alfie's good. Have you seen his Q&A? He answered that question about wanting to start a proper studio – sounds likely that will happen soon. It's amazing how he's built that whole thing. I'm trying to get into editing, you know? Maybe I could do some little videos for my Instagram. Seriously? That’s a cool idea! What kind of videos? I don't know yet. Maybe some beauty stuff, or just little snippets of what I’m doing. I’ve been trying to follow some of those American beauty YouTubers, but their makeup is just so…extra. Like, who needs that much highlighter? Exactly! It looks like they’re trying to blind people. I prefer the more natural looks, definitely. Have you seen Izzy's new reel? The one with the autumnal vibes? It's gorgeous. I want her wardrobe! Oh yeah! The oversized jumpers and the boots! Total goals. I wish Mum would let me wear more stuff like that to school. She’s always going on about ‘appropriate attire’. Tell me about it! It’s like we’re back in primary school. Remember when Mrs. Davies used to make me tuck my shirt in because it was "distracting the boys"? As if! Ugh, the worst. Speaking of teachers, have you heard anything about Mr. Henderson leaving?

Honestly, I feel like death warmed up. This cold's got me proper knackered, hasn't it? I can barely focus on anything. Even trying to watch telly is a struggle. You look awful, love. Really, awful. You’re all red-nosed and bleary-eyed. Did you actually manage to get any work done today? Nah. Tried, mostly. Did a bit o' desk resaerch, but my brain’s like mush. I kept forgettin' where I put my pen, and I swear I tried to open the biscuit tin with a stapler. Ridiculous. Speaking of ridiculous, remember Lloyd Grossman's Masterchef? That was peak telly, wasn’t it? So cheesy, but brilliant. Oh, absolutely. The "Fantastically Frugal" bit always got me. It was such a commitment to being… eccentric. My nan used to record it every week. Do you think they'd ever bring something like that back? A genuinely fun, low-stakes cooking competition? With flamboyant judges? I reckon they’d need to, wouldn’t they? Everything’s so serious now. All those bake-offs and Michelin-starred chefs. Where's the silly? Remember when I got that dodgy paella in Barcelona and had full-on food poisoning? That was  not  fantastically frugal. Just… awful. Oh, I remember. You were a mess. Green, I think, was the predominant colour. Did you ever think about getting that flu jab this year? Might be worth considering, given this...performance. I know, I know. Mum’s been on at me. Always says to look after yourself proper. Truth is, I'm a bit wary, y’know? Read something online about… well, never mind, it was probably rubbish. What about you? Are you getting it? You and your petri dishes. It’s a necessity with all the lab work. Lots of… questionable samples floating about. I had it last month. No ill effects. It's not worth risking getting poorly, especially with your thesis deadline looming. I hate hospitals though. Me too! That antiseptic smell makes me wanna curl up in a ball and never come out. Remember that time Gran had to go in after she fell? The waiting room was awful. All sorts of faces, all lookin' worried. It is. Makes you think, doesn't it? About how fragile everything is. Have you been looking into that body language recognition research at all? It's incredible what they can do now. They're using cameras to track micro-expressions...

“'Quixotic' – forty points! Right, your turn, David. Honestly, how many Qs  do  they print these days?” “Manchester’s a notoriously tricky place for Scrabble, Eleanor. All those Welsh words, all those proper nouns. Quixotic, eh? Bit much, isn't it? Just trying to impress your mother?” “Don’t be cheeky, David. Eleanor’s vocabulary is impressive. Besides, ‘quixotic’ is a perfectly valid word, and a rather fitting descriptor for the state of traffic at the Arndale this afternoon. I was trapped for twenty minutes, absolutely gridlocked!” “Traffic was dreadful even back in my day. Although we didn’t have 'shopping centres' then. Just a butcher’s shop and a baker, and you were lucky to get a decent piece of sirloin without queuing for half an hour.” “Oh, speaking of queues, I was at Mr. Henderson's butcher’s this morning. Absolutely rammed! Some woman was having a full-blown hushed argument with him about the fat content of his sausages. Honestly, people!” “Sounds about right. Sometimes I think people just enjoy complaining. Remember that article in  Sounds  magazine last month? About the resurgence of vinyl? People meticulously complaining about the 'warble' and the 'surface noise' as if that’s part of the charm!” “ Sounds ? Goodness, that’s a throwback! I used to scour Melody Maker religiously back in the 60s. Far more discerning, if you ask me. Though, I confess, vinyl does have a certain nostalgia. It’s the ritual of it, isn’t it? Listening to a whole album, uninterrupted.” "The ritual. Exactly. You youngsters with your streaming services don't understand the patience it cultivated. It made you truly  listen  to music." He places a tile – 'Zenith' - for a substantial score. "Impressive, Harold." "Forty-seven points! You're trying to bankrupt me, aren't you, Arthur? Mother, are you even  trying  to make words? You’ve been staring at your tiles for five minutes.” “I'm contemplating. This is a strategic game, Eleanor. I'm seeking optimal placement. Oh! ‘Luster’ – a nice little score.” “It’s a wonderful word, isn’t it? ‘Luster’. Like the sheen on a well-aged cheese.” "Now you're just being deliberately obscure, aren't you? Although, aged cheddar… that  does  have a certain luster. Speaking of which, I’m thinking of making a cheese and onion tart for dinner. Any objections?" “A cheese and onion tart sounds lovely, David! Much better than Facebook dinners.

Oh, my word, that last pile of flyers was a beast! My back’s playing up something awful. Fancy a cuppa, Arthur? They’ve got a rather decent brew in the canteen, I hear. That would be most agreeable, Penelope. My knees aren’t exactly thanking me for crouching down to distribute those leaflets either. A moment’s respite is precisely what’s needed. Though, I daresay, we’ll be back at it shortly. This whole working party is rather admirable, isn’t it? Keeping the TME chugging along. It is, it truly is. A lovely bunch of people, all dedicated to preserving this wonderful line. Though, I must admit, I never thought I'd find myself handing out flyers in my twilight years. Still, keeps the mind active. You were saying earlier about your work... printing systems, wasn't it? Rather a different world from my little gallery, wouldn't you say? Quite a different world indeed. I specialized in automation for printing presses, actually. Developed a few key systems for ink distribution and paper handling. Marketing them was the… interesting part. A lot of German exhibitions. A fascinating country, although endlessly confusing when it came to bureaucracy. Germany! Gosh, that sounds exciting. Somerset's a bit… quiet, shall we say. Did you travel extensively? Oh, yes. Dusseldorf, Frankfurt, Munich… quite the circuit. The trade fairs were enormous. Picture halls packed with the latest machinery, flashing lights, rather ostentatious displays… and a constant hum of negotiation. One year in Dusseldorf, I secured a contract with a major printing house, purely by charming the factory owner’s wife. Her taste in orchids, you see, was remarkably similar to mine. Orchids! You’re pulling my leg, surely? I assure you, Penelope. The woman positively glowed when I complimented her Phalaenopsis. While the men discussed metrics and efficiency, I bonded over the care of delicate blooms. It's amazing what a shared appreciation of horticulture can accomplish. Secured a deal worth a considerable sum. That's brilliant, Arthur! Absolutely brilliant! You’re a charmer. I dealt mostly in antiques – furniture, mostly. A bit of porcelain, a few quirky bits and bobs. Never had to charm anyone with orchids, I can tell you that. Though dealing with difficult collectors could certainly test one’s patience. One woman once insisted a chipped teacup was a priceless Ming Dynasty relic because it “felt right.” Human nature, I suppose.

Are we nearly there yet, Dad? My phone’s almost dead, and I’ve scrolled through TikTok a thousand times. Now, now, love. Cornwall’s a fair bit further than you think. We’ve still got a good chunk of the journey ahead. Least we’ve stopped at that service station for a cuppa, eh? Best bacon butty I’ve had in ages, to be fair. It was alright. But honestly, all service stations are the same, aren’t they? Just…beige. And overpriced. At least they’ve got decent Wi-Fi this time. I gotta try and get a signal to message Chloe. She’s gutted she couldn't come. Chloe's a good lass. So, you were moaning about English lessons the other day. Something about essay deadlines? Ugh, don’t remind me! We’re doing a whole unit on the evolution of the English language, which is actually kinda interesting when you think about it. Like, how words change their meaning over time, or where they even  come  from. Did you know "nice" used to mean foolish or ignorant? Aye, I did hear something like that. Proper different from what it means now. It's fascinating, isn't it? All these influences – Latin, French, Norse… it’s built up over centuries. Reminds me of that philosophy class I took at the adult learning centre, years ago. Lots of pondering on the nature of language and how it shapes our thinking. Philosophy? You took a philosophy class? Wow. What did you learn? Mostly that I don’t know as much as I thought I did. But proper made you think, it did. We were arguing about Plato and Aristotle for weeks. Course, a lot of it was over my head. Still, good for broadening the mind, I reckon. What about you? Thinking about uni, are you? I’m looking at it. Probably English Lit, but I'm a bit unsure about the courses. There's one in Exeter that looks interesting, but the modules are a bit… obscure. I saw one called "The Poetics of Weather.” Seriously! The poetics of weather? Typical. Always a clever blighter coming up with that sort of thing. They'll be dissecting every raindrop, won't they? Look, you need to pick a course you’re passionate about, lass. Something that grabs you. Don't worry about sounding clever to other folk. You're right.

Right, so, I've got the peppers almost done. Jamie, are you sure you can handle those sausages? Don't want to end up with anything resembling charcoal, love. Relax, Lucy. I've grilled sausages before. I’m not  completely  useless. Just… slower than most. They're browning nicely, actually. Though I'm starving, I am. This chopping takes ages, doesn’t it? My Elsie used to make a cracking sausage casserole. Back when I used to, you know,  eat  properly. Real gravy, not that instant stuff. Used to simmer it all day. The smell alone would make your mouth water. Oh, Uncle Barry, you always make me hungry with your stories! Elsie was a legend. I wish I’d learned some of her recipes. This instant gravy is a bit… disappointing, I'll admit. Jamie, you wouldn't fancy making a proper gravy sometime, would you? With stock and flour and everything? Me? Making gravy? Look, I can handle sausages, okay? Gravy is a different level of skill. It requires... finesse. And frankly, I’m still recovering from this vegetable warfare. Finesse? Elsie didn't know finesse. She threw it all in the pot and stirred it until it looked right. That was her secret. Simplicity. And a lot of butter. Don't be scared of butter, lad. Makes everything better. You and butter, Uncle Barry! Always a winning combination. So, how’s your knee today? Still needing the walking stick? It's… cooperating, mostly. Still twinges now and then, though. Doctor says it's just age catching up. Age! Can you believe it? Feels like yesterday I was chasing squirrels in the garden. Squirrels? Seriously? You were chasing  squirrels ? Don’t look so surprised. It was good fun. Keeps you active. Now look at you two, stuck in a kitchen. That's hardly a life, is it? Easier than chasing squirrels, Uncle Barry. Besides, someone's gotta cook. And it’s lovely having you here. It's not often we all get together like this. So, how’s your daughter, Carol, doing? I haven’t seen her in ages. Carol's well. She's running that little shop down in the High Street, you know, the one selling those… those little painted stones. Seems to be doing alright. She sends her love, by the way. Keeps asking after you, Lucy. Says you were a smashing little girl. Oh, that’s lovely to hear.

…Honestly, it was brutal. Three back-to-back birthday parties on a Saturday night. You wouldn't believe the sheer volume of prosecco people get through. My feet are absolutely killing me. Oh, Liam, you poor thing! That sounds exhausting. Bartending on a Saturday… it’s a whole different level of chaos, isn't it? I always admired your ability to handle it, though. My feet ache just  thinking  about standing that long. Admired? It’s mostly survival at this point. What about you? How’s the language learning going? You mentioned you were prepping for the end-of-term exams. It's going well, actually. The students are surprisingly engaged this year. I’ve finally cracked a way to make subjunctive mood less terrifying for them. They actually laughed at a joke about it yesterday, which is a victory in my book. Though, marking all those essays? It feels like a slow descent into madness. I can imagine! Essays… I'm glad I don't have to mark those. Just pouring drinks, occasionally dealing with spilled vodka. Much simpler, in many ways. Do you teach French or Spanish, still? Primarily Spanish, although I do a bit of French with the younger ones. It's rewarding, seeing them progress. I've been thinking about doing a postgraduate qualification focusing on bilingual education, actually. That’s ambitious! Sounds intense. You’ve always been driven, you know that? It's a world away from what I'm doing. I briefly considered teaching, actually. Back in sixth form, thought about maybe English Lit. Really? Why did you veer away from it? Just… didn’t feel right. Needed to do something more immediate, you know? Plus, the student loan debt was looming large. Bartending pays the bills, keeps a roof over my head. How's the dating scene in Hitchin these days? Still quiet? Quiet is putting it mildly. It's… limited. Actually, I'm trying to be a bit more proactive. Joined a badminton club. It's surprisingly social. You play any sport? Badminton? Never tried it. I used to kick a football about as a kid, played a bit for school. Nothing serious. I’d probably end up hitting you in the face. I’m more of a sofa-and-Netflix kind of guy these days. You should come along sometime! It’s really good fun. Gets you moving. Besides, I need someone to blame when I inevitably lose.

Oh dear, look at the time! Nigel will be wanting his biscuit and a cuppa. We're dreadfully late for break time, aren't we? Aye, you're right, Doris. Time does fly when you're… well, when you're talkin’ about bell ringing and Gambia, don't it? Fancy that, Gambia. Who’d have thought? It really is a fascinating place, isn’t it? The potential for a good project is enormous. I’ve been doing some initial research – the schools are desperately in need of resources. The proposal I'm drafting involves funding some basic supplies and, ideally, a small library. A library! That’s lovely, Robert. Much better than just sendin’ money, isn't it? You know, seeing good done, tangibly? It feels proper. Proper, aye. Like when you finally get a decent bloom on your roses, innit? Took me ages this year, felt like givin’ up halfway through. Kept thinkin’ about those poor children in Gambia, workin’ hard already. Indeed. We could even incorporate a donation box here, at your place. Something simple. We could decorate it with some Gambian flags, a little banner… A banner! Oh, Robert, that’s a marvellous idea! We should get Nigel to help. He’s surprisingly good with a bit of glitter glue and sticking things. Remember that Christmas display he made last year? Glitter glue, eh? That’ll be a sight! Though, talkin' about things bein' a bit… elaborate, did you read about that fella, the one with the Munchausen Syndrome? Dreadful business, that. Pretendin’ to be ill to get attention. A deeply troubling condition. It highlights the complexities of human behaviour, doesn’t it? Exploiting the health system, suffering… it's heartbreaking for everyone involved. It’s a far cry from the simple act of helping a community. It is, isn't it? I always thought it was awful when children were involved, if the parents were doing it. Poor little things. It's hard to imagine someone wanting that kind of attention. Makes you think, doesn't it? Reckon it does. Makes you think about why people do what they do. Anyways, back to Gambia. So, you’re thinking plants as well, Robert? To brighten the place up a bit? Yes, absolutely. Some hardy, drought-resistant varieties. They could be used to create some small gardens around the schools. A little green space for the children. And it teaches them valuable skills too.

Honestly, I’m still having nightmares from “Smile.” Did you guys see it? I tried to! Ben insisted, said it was “a classic.” But I got about halfway through and had to turn it off. Too creepy!
