Liam, that's gold! Go on, spill. Was it a hidden cove? A dramatic cliff edge? It was… a very murky lake near Galway. Let’s just say the water temperature was… bracing. And I kept thinking about leeches. Leeches! Oh my god, Liam. You’re mad. Why would you even  do  that? It was a dare, alright? Don’t judge. Ben, that idiot, dared me, and I, of course, accepted. I always regret accepting his dares, by the way. Classic mate stuff. Reminds me of the things we used to do in Aussie back in the day – reckless abandon, basically. Did you see any fairies in this lake, Liam? Because that’s what they say about Ireland. Just a lot of reeds. And a very large frog. Definitely no fairies. Honestly, I was too busy trying to avoid hypothermia. Right, well, that’s enough of the near-death experiences. Let's talk about something lighter. Maya, how’s the café doing? Still battling the morning rush? It's manic, Chloe, as always. But good manic, you know? People are actually asking for oat milk lattes  without  me having to explain what oat milk  is  anymore. Progress! I’m trying to get some local poets in for a little open mic night next month. That's brilliant, Maya! Seriously, put me down for that. I need a dose of culture. Speaking of culture… this food is amazing, by the way, ANON. Seriously, your bubkes are incredible. It  is  good! That slow-cooked brisket is unreal. You’ve seriously outdone yourself, ANON. It reminds me of my grandma's brisket. It does! It's actually a recipe from Claudia Roden's  The Book of Jewish Food . Have you guys got it? It's a bible. I’ve seen it, but haven’t picked it up yet. It looks massive. I'm always looking for good recipes - gotta keep the menu exciting at the café. Do you have a favourite Jewish joke, Liam? Something light-hearted? Right, okay, here’s one... Why did the bagel break up with the cream cheese? Because it felt spread thin! Oh, Liam! That’s terrible! But in a good way.

Honestly, this is a state. They're all tiny! Remember when pubs used to give you a massive bowl of peanuts? You could practically build a fort with ‘em. Nostalgia, eh? Everything seems bigger and better when you're looking back from the future. They’re probably trying to cut costs. Speaking of things being smarter, have you seen the new  Baldur's Gate 3  patch? Aye! I’ve been dabbling a bit. I'm struggling with that goblin camp, though. The ambush tactics are brutal. I’m playing a Halfling rogue, you know. Trying to be all sneaky and stuff. It’s nae going well. You need to use the environment! There’s a hollowed-out tree you can hide in that gives you a massive advantage. And for goodness sake, invest in some poisoned daggers. Seriously, that’s the key. I just cleared it on Tactician difficulty, and poison was my saviour. Tactician difficulty, are you showing off now? I’m barely surviving on Explorer! You’re always so methodical with these sorts of games. Remember trying to get me into  Civilization ? I lasted about an hour before deleting the entire thing. That’s because you got distracted by building a pyramid and then got conquered by the Mongols. It was glorious to witness, in a chaotic sort of way. So, pyramids aside, what have you been up to? Still buried in your research? It's mental busy. The new project on digital identity is taking over my life. Masses of data to sift through, endless interviews. It’s fascinating, but draining. I need a proper getaway. Maybe Alton Towers? I haven’t been since I were a bairn. Alton Towers? You know, Thorpe Park is closer. And they just revamped Stealth. The launch is ridiculous – 55mph in two seconds. You'd scream your head off. Aye, I probably would. But there’s something about Alton Towers' cheesy charm, innit? The Nemesis ride, the pirate ship… It's a proper childhood memory. And have you seen  Oppenheimer  yet? Everyone’s raving about it. Saw it last week. Absolutely brilliant. Nolan really outdid himself. The sheer tension… it’s almost unbearable at times. Made me think a lot about the ethics of scientific progress, actually. Which is relevant to your digital identity work, I suppose. Both are about creating powerful tools with potentially dangerous consequences. You're right. It’s a weird parallel.

Oh, this is  delicious . Proper chips, too. Not those skinny ones you get everywhere these days. They are good, aren't they? Such a treat. Needed this after that frankly disastrous attempt at rowing yesterday. Disastrous? I thought you were quite enjoying yourself, despite nearly capsizing! I saw you laughing. Laughing nervously, more like! It was exhilarating, undeniably. But the technique… oh dear. Apparently, my back muscles aren't what they used to be. The instructor kept saying 'engage your core!' as though it were some magical incantation. My core is engaged in trying to eat this fish! Fair enough! I’ve been thinking about trying kayaking. Seems a little more… stable, doesn’t it? It is, much more so. I did a bit of kayaking a few years back in the Lake District, absolutely beautiful. But you do need proper gear. I bought a fantastic waterproof jacket once, a Rohan one. Expensive, but worth every penny. Nothing worse than being soaked to the bone while you’re trying to enjoy the scenery. I know exactly what you mean. I’ve invested in a few things for walking, but I’m always a bit dubious about the quality. Everything feels like it's going to leak eventually. I’ll have a look at Rohan, though. Thanks for the tip. Speaking of investments… Did you ever hear back from Aunt Maggie about meeting up? Actually, I did. She rang me last week. It was… quite something. She sounded a bit hesitant at first, you know, all those years apart, and the family history being the way it was. Her mum never spoke about her. Goodness. That must have been incredibly difficult. It was. But we talked for over an hour. Mostly just catching up, you know. Where she’s lived, what she does… She’s a pottery teacher in Cornwall, can you imagine? We’re meeting up next month, down there. I'm… apprehensive but really looking forward to it. It feels like closing a circle, somehow. That's wonderful, really! I’m so glad. It sounds like it will be lovely. We should both come down for a weekend, have a potter ourselves. That would be lovely. Though, recently… things have been a bit difficult on the home front. My brother, David... Oh? What’s happened? He seemed fine last time we spoke. He’s been diagnosed with… well, something fairly serious.

Honestly, Dad, it’s like nobody communicates properly anymore. It's all emojis and abbreviations. "LOL" this, "OMG" that. It's exhausting! Now, now, lass. Don't get yourself in a twist. It's just the way things are. When I were a lad, we sent letters! Took weeks to get a reply. Think about that! Weeks? That's insane! I'd forget what I even  wrote  about by the time a reply came. I mean, I'm half tempted to start using Morse code just to be different. Morse code? You? You couldn’t tap out “hello” without getting it wrong! Remember when you tried to learn it for that school project in primary? Took you a week to learn the alphabet and you kept getting the dots and dashes muddled. Okay, point taken. But texting is just… shallow. No nuance. It’s like trying to explain quantum physics with a thumbs-up emoji. So, what's got you so wound up this evening then? All this talk of communication... Is it about results day? You look a bit stressed. A bit! They’re online tomorrow. I keep replaying all my exams in my head. What if I messed up the essay on… on… Chaucer? Now, don't you worry your pretty little head about Chaucer. You’re a clever girl, you'll have done fine. Remember what Gran always says: “A watched pot never boils, and a replayed exam never changes.” That’s a bit cheesy, Gran. Though, she’s probably right. Speaking of watched pots… I’m starving. I hope Mum's made something decent. She’s been trying to get me to eat more vegetables, you know. Like, full plates of broccoli. Your mum’s got good intentions. She worries about you and all that student finance you’re juggling. Did you manage to sort out the top-up application? I’ve started it, but it’s a nightmare. So much paperwork! I wish I could just... teleport all my stationery needs to me. I’m running out of pens, you know? Amazon’s delivery’s been a disgrace lately. Took three days to get my highlighters. Tell me about it. I ordered a glass water bottle from eBay last week, still hasn't turned up. Probably lost in a warehouse somewhere, swallowed by a mountain of cardboard boxes. Waste of plastic, all that packaging. Exactly! It’s awful.

Blimey, this place is cozy, innit? Zara’s got good taste, I gotta say. Feels a million miles away from that library I’ve been practically living in. Tell me about it! You look like you’ve aged a decade in the last month. Exams really hit you hard, yeah? I managed to escape pretty early, thankfully. This apartment is a good choice for a recharge. So, how’d the coding exam go? You were stressing about that, weren’t you? Stressing? That’s a  massive  understatement. I think I pulled an all-nighter, every night for a week. Honestly, the algorithms were brutal. Felt like I was battling ancient demons made of logic gates. Think I passed, though. Fingers crossed. Did you finish your dissertation alright? That sounded like a beast. Yeah, man, submitted it last week. Got the initial feedback – apparently, my section on the impact of Jamaican cultural coding on early internet design was… “innovative.” Professor Thompson nearly choked when I pitched it to him. No way! That’s brilliant! You’re always pulling rabbits out of hats like that. Remember that time you said you'd build a functioning AI chatbot using only Python and a Raspberry Pi for the final year project? Don't remind me! That was a whole different level of chaos. It did  mostly  work, though. Anyway, you look like you need serious sustenance. Pizza's on its way. Zara ordered from that new Japanese place down the road – ‘Tokyo Bites,’ she called it. Japanese, eh? Actually, that reminds me, I’ve been thinking… I’m seriously considering a gap year. Maybe travel. Japan’s been on my list forever. Japan! Seriously? You’re actually doing it? That’s amazing, man! Tokyo… it's a sensory overload in the best way. The food, the technology, the culture… Have you started planning anything? A bit. I was looking at rail passes, trying to figure out how long I could afford to stay. Probably six months, max. I need to do  something  after those exams. Feel like my brain's turned to mush. What about you? Any big plans after graduation? Moving back to Brixton with your family, yeah? Most likely. Gotta help Nan out, you know? Plus, I've got this crazy idea to start a community tech hub in Brixton. Offer free coding classes, help people get online... something like that.

Right, look at this! This is from Buckfast Abbey. Honestly, it was lovely, wasn't it? Though I'm not sure why I took a photo of a particularly crumbly bit of wall. Oh, love, you and your photography skills! It  was  lovely though, wasn’t it? Such peace and quiet. I’m glad we went. Did you manage to get a decent look at the gardens? They were particularly beautiful this year, I thought. Buckfast, you say? Always thought that place had a strange power over people. You could practically feel the… the… devotion, you know? Though, I remember going there with my wife, Elsie, back in… oh, must have been the fifties. Elsie was convinced one of the monks looked exactly like my old headmaster. Oh, Grandad! You always have the best stories. Headmaster monks – brilliant! Still, it  was  a really calming day. I was thinking, now we've been to Buckfast, what should we do next? We talked about the Eden Project, but it’s a trek. Eden is always a good shout. A bit pricey, admittedly, but always something new to see. I was flicking through a brochure the other day… they’re doing a rainforest experience now, apparently. Fancy that! Or, we could do something a bit closer to home, you know? Exmoor? Exmoor! Now there’s an idea. I like a good moor. Reminds me of my days as a young accountant, trudging through fields, checking livestock counts. Not quite as scenic as Exmoor, mind you, but a living has to be made, doesn’t it? Speaking of which… did you see anything about that David Cameron business in the paper this morning? Don’t even get me started, Grandad. It’s just… infuriating. Tax avoidance loopholes for the wealthy and average folk struggling to pay their bills. It's enough to make you scream. I saw it all over Facebook, naturally. Everyone's having a right go. Honestly, it's a disgrace. Makes you wonder how much of our taxes actually goes where it ought to. I've been meaning to look at my insurance – car, house, the lot. They’re all up, aren't they? Absolutely ridiculous. Tell me about it! My car insurance went up again last month. I'm starting to think I should just trade it in for a bicycle. Although, with the hills around here… A bicycle! At your age?

Right, so tell me everything! Belgium, eh? Was it as lovely as you said it would be? It sounds incredible. Lovely? It was… different. Beautiful in patches, mind you. Bruges, especially, was postcard stuff. All those canals, the little bridges… proper charming. But… driving was a nightmare. Don't listen to your dad, darling. It was brilliant! We saw so much. And the food! Oh, the food was just divine. Waffles, chocolate, fries… I’m going to need to hit the gym properly now, I think. Sounds like it! Dad, what made driving so bad? Was it the traffic? Traffic wasn't the  worst  of it. It was the roads, love. Narrow, cobbled… and the sat nav! Absolute rubbish. Kept telling me to turn down lanes that were barely wider than my car! We ended up down some… interesting routes. He got a bit lost a couple of times, that's all! But that’s part of the adventure, isn’t it? I said we should have just cycled everywhere! Cycling? Seriously? In Belgium? Absolutely! They’ve got amazing cycling paths, miles and miles of them. Flat as a pancake too, mostly. Much better than wrestling with those tiny roads. We did hire bikes for a day in Ghent, and it was glorious. Saw so much more of the city that way. Glorious for  you , maybe! I nearly had a coronary trying to navigate the ring road whilst dodging cyclists and lorries. And my new phone… it kept losing signal. Trying to zoom in on Google Maps was a waste of time. Should’ve stuck with a proper road map, should have. A road map? Dad, it's 2024! You're supposed to have a fancy phone with GPS! What phone did you get, anyway? That new Galaxy thing. Everyone said it was brilliant. Clearly, they haven't tried using it in a foreign country. It cost a fortune too. Should’ve just stuck with the old Nokia. Don’t worry about it, dear. These things happen. Besides, we found some lovely little markets in Antwerp. Remember those, love? All those cheeses, and the beer! So, you actually bought some Belgian cheese? Did it taste as good as everyone says? Oh, absolutely! We got some incredible cheddar-style cheese, and a proper farmhouse brie. I’m going to try and recreate some of those sauces I had with them. You’d be better off trying to recreate Bruges in the back garden.

Honestly, I don’t know why I bother trying new recipes. It’s always this lamb tagine that actually gets eaten. Everything else is met with polite, yet pointed, disinterest. That’s because your lamb tagine is brilliant, love. It’s consistently brilliant. You’re setting an impossibly high bar for yourself, that's all. And put down the spatula for a second, you’re going to fling lamb everywhere. Easy for you to say, you’re not the one battling a rogue cinnamon stick. I was thinking about trying that saffron risotto, though. Remember that one Amelia made? The smell alone was heavenly. Right, yes. The one that took her three hours and nearly flooded the kitchen? I have fond memories. Let's stick with the tagine, shall we? Less drama. Speaking of smells, have you smelled that new perfume I got? "Midnight Bloom." Quite potent. Oh, really? I haven't. What's it like? Is it one of those sickly sweet florals? Because I can’t stand those. I'm clinging to Jo Malone’s Wild Fig at the moment. It’s just... comforting. No, no, it's not sickly. It’s… woodsy, almost. A bit musky. Very sophisticated. Reminds me of walking through a forest at dusk. Though perhaps a  slightly  more glamorous version of a forest at dusk. You and your romantic descriptions. Right, I’m going to pop this into the oven. While it’s doing its thing, did you see what Sarah posted on Facebook? The one about the flower arranging class? Just glanced. Something about needing 'floral inspiration'? She’s getting awfully keen on those things, isn't she? Always has been a creative one. Remember when she tried to make those papier-mâché owls? Oh goodness, yes! They looked like traumatized pigeons. She's much better with flowers. I saw a gorgeous bouquet of anemones at the market yesterday. Such a lovely, dusty pink. I thought about getting some, but then I remembered we're heading out on Friday. They'd be drooping by Saturday. True. Still, they’d brighten up the place. Maybe we could get some for the fireplace? I was thinking about lighting it tonight. It's getting properly chilly. That’s a brilliant idea! The fire and the tagine... perfect autumnal evening. You know, listening to you talk about "Midnight Bloom" reminds me – I’ve been meaning to ask you, do you notice my accent getting stronger when I’m tired?

It’s lovely here, Anon. Very… welcoming. You’ve made a proper home for yourself. I still find it all so astonishing, moving so far. Australia, eh? A whole different world. Astonishing, yes. Though, I did spend a fair bit of time there myself, years ago. Not as a permanent resident, of course. Business trips. Mostly Queensland. Spectacular coastline. Though, the humidity… dreadful for the suits. Can’t imagine trying to run a company in that heat. Do you find that a problem, Anon? Queensland! Lovely part of the world. Not the dress code, though. My nephew, Mark, he’s out there now, teaching English in Brisbane. He says you have to basically ditch anything remotely formal. "Boardroom attire," he called it, "is a recipe for heatstroke." He looked like a boiled lobster in a pin-striped suit at first. Now he just wears linen shirts and shorts. Much happier. Linen shirts and shorts! Sounds blissfully sensible. I’ve been reading up on it, and the sheer vastness of the place is what gets me. Everywhere is “huge.” Makes Gloucestershire seem rather… diminutive, doesn’t it? I’ve been trying to imagine applying for a bank loan out there. They’d probably ask for the deeds to half the continent! They are quite keen on collateral, I’ll grant you that. Particularly when dealing with overseas applicants. Did you have any trouble securing funding to get out there, Anon? I remember when I last looked into something like that, the paperwork alone was enough to daunt a saint. Speaking of paperwork, you wouldn't  believe  the forms they make you fill out for a simple overdraft here. It's ridiculous. Reminds me of a time I had to get a grant for my department at the University. Pages and pages, all in that terribly formal academic language. I nearly lost my mind. You know, the way people talk in Sheffield, you wouldn't always realise how much they're hiding underneath all the "ee"s and the dropped 'h's. It’s a very precise dialect, really. Oh, I’ve found that with seemingly simple dialects. There's so much nuance. It's similar with the accents around Bristol, actually. People dismiss them as just "West Country," but there's a subtle shift depending on which village you're from. It can be surprisingly confusing for a freshly-minted EFL teacher! Bristol… yes.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that Bridgerton finale. Did you see it, Eleanor? Oh, yes, darling. Quite the dramatic ending, wasn't it? Though, I must confess, I found it a touch… predictable. All that scheming. It’s rather exhausting, isn’t it? All the embroidery and elaborate dances, just to get a husband. Exhausting, yeah, but that's the point, isn’t it? The whole suffocating societal pressure. I really felt for Eloise this season. She’s so determined to be independent, and the way she's trying to break free... it resonated, you know? I’m all about women forging their own paths. Absolutely. Though I find myself wondering, is it all a bit… artificial? This obsession with historical drama. All perfectly coiffed hair and pristine gowns, when life was so much harder. My grandmother used to tell me stories, you know, about what it truly was like for women in those times. It wasn’t all balls and bonnets. True. But I think it’s escapism, isn’t it? We all need a bit of that sometimes. And it’s beautifully produced, I’ll give them that. Still, I’m more into true crime podcasts these days. Have you heard "Crime Junkie"? It's utterly addictive. Oh dear, no. Not really my cup of tea, I'm afraid. All that talk of… well, you know. Rather morbid. I prefer something uplifting. I’ve been listening to “Stuff You Should Know” – it’s surprisingly fascinating. They covered the history of rubber bands the other day! Rubber bands? Seriously? See, that’s why we’re so different! But I get it – sometimes you need something utterly random and a bit silly to switch off your brain. How's your social media going? You were saying you were trying out TikTok? Oh, TikTok. It’s… a phenomenon. I managed to create one video of the pigeons in my garden. Utterly boring, I’m sure, but I was determined to give it a go! No one seemed terribly interested, though. Very few views. It's all dancing, isn't it? And challenges. I’m not sure I’m quite nimble enough for that. It can be a bit overwhelming. I try to stick to educational stuff on there, mostly. Quick language tips for my students, you know? And some funny memes, of course. It's a great way to reach a younger audience.

Right, you two, almost lunchtime. Are you having a good time with ANON? She’s been brilliantly inventive, hasn't she? She built a castle! A sparkly rainbow castle with a dragon! And I’m the knight!  swings an imaginary sword  I’m fighting the dragon! Wonderful. I’m glad you're enjoying her. I’m really hoping we can manage to get to that Travelling Circus she mentioned. It’s a bit of a drive, but… The circus! With the funny clowns? Yes, that’s right. Though I think it’s more a collection of oddities than just clowns, if truth be told. It's a bit like, well, she's a bit like a walking oddity, isn't she? In the best possible way, of course. Can I be the lion tamer? Possibly, Finn. We’ll see. Now, we need to think about that Blue Peter badge. You need to send in a photograph to get your badge, don’t you, Pippy? Yes! But what photo should I send? That’s what we need to decide. We could take one of you both doing something creative. Or perhaps one of you at the circus? It would be a brilliant memory. Can we build a rocket ship out of cardboard boxes and take a picture with that? A rocket ship, are we? That’s very ambitious, Finn. But not a bad idea! We’d need to get it built before Sunday, though. But Mum, how are we going to get to the circus? Do we need…passports? Passports? No, darling, it’s in Somerset, not Switzerland! Passports aren't needed for Somerset. Honestly, your imagination is running wild. But what about her age? Is she old enough to be a babysitter? That’s a good question, Finn. She says she’s fifteen, but sometimes I think she’s been around for centuries. She’s certainly seen more than most fifteen-year-olds. I’ve never met anyone who knows so much about… well, everything, really. Last night she was explaining the proper way to eat century eggs, you know, those Chinese preserved eggs? Century eggs? Eww! They look yucky! She said they taste like… like smelly socks! Precisely. Not to my taste, I must admit. But she was so earnest about it! Said it was a delicacy. Told us a whole history of it, honestly. So she's really clever?

Right, so… you won't think I’m mental will ya? Asking about… this. Mental? No, love, why would I think you're mental? It's a bit awkward, maybe, but not mental. What's on your mind? You look like you’re about to confess to something major. It’s just… Liam. Aye, Liam. Things haven't been… right, lately. You know? I don’t wanna go into loads of detail, but… well, it's a bit physical, innit? Okay. Physical how? Don't worry about being delicate. You can tell me. Is he… alright? I think so. He seems fine, like, generally. Happy and all that. But… sometimes… he can’t, you know? Finish. It’s embarrassing even saying it out loud. Like, he'll apologize afterwards, says it's just nerves or something, but it’s happening more often now. And I don’t know what to do. I feel a bit… responsible? Even though it’s clearly not my fault. I’ve googled it, obviously, and... erectile dysfunction keeps cropping up. Oh, love. That  is  awkward to talk about, but you’re doing the right thing by bringing it up. Responsible? Absolutely not. It's not on you at all. Erectile dysfunction… it's more common than people think. And it can be caused by loads of things – stress, anxiety, even just a change in medication. Googling is good to understand it, but don’t get bogged down in worst-case scenarios, alright? I know, I know. But I'm worried he's stressed about his uni course. He's working part-time too, and it's just… a lot. But he doesn’t really talk about feeling stressed. He just bottles it up, like he always does. That’s a classic bloke move, isn't it? Bottling things up. Have you tried just… talking to him? Not specifically about  that , but generally about how he's feeling? Just saying you’ve noticed he seems a bit quieter, or more tired? I’ve tried. He just says he’s fine. Gets all prickly about it. It’s like pulling teeth to get him to admit anything's bothering him. Right. Tough. Okay. Well, maybe don’t push him on it directly. Have you gently suggested he see a doctor? Like, framed it as a general health thing? “Just get a check-up, love, it’s good to stay on top of things.”

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a walking, talking Weight Watchers manual. Slimming World's Healthy Extras are just…a lot. I mean, do I  really  need to eat three sticks of celery to get my fibre in? Welcome to the club. It’s relentless, isn’t it? But at least it's  free , right? Beats using ‘syns’ on everything. Though, I still can’t believe balsamic vinegar counts as a syn. Seriously?! I know! And are you going to believe it?! I had a tiny drizzle on my salad yesterday and Siri kept bugging me about my syns! Like a digital nag. I’m tempted to throw her across the room. Oh, Siri is the worst for that. Put a reminder in  your  calendar to ignore her when it comes to food. I've got a lot of reminders in mine just to keep myself focused. What are you making tonight, anyway? It smells amazing. Cauliflower cheese with a roast. Keeping it relatively sensible. I'm using Frylight, obviously – you know I’m not messing about with oil! And plenty of spices. Found this brilliant spice mix in Aldi, it’s got paprika, cumin, a bit of chilli... really lifts the flavour without adding syns. Ooh, sounds good! I'm thinking a veggie roast – Quorn’s really stepped up their game, hasn’t it? Tesco’s got the best range, I reckon. Less…beige than some of the others. Thinking about ordering a veg box too, actually, to make it easier. Good idea! I’ve been looking at those. Do you find they’re actually worth the money, or do you end up with loads of stuff you don’t use? It depends. You have to be strategic. I'm thinking a smaller box, just basics. And we can freeze anything we won't use immediately. Remember those double peas I bought last week? Lifesaver. Absolutely! Although, my scales are being utterly useless. I swear they’re out to get me. They were saying I’d gained half a pound this morning. I’m convinced they’re lying. Scales are notorious liars. Don’t trust them! Especially first thing in the morning. Are you getting to the gym at all this week? Trying to. I’m aiming for three times, but work has been insane. The pharmacy is rammed this week; we’ve got targets to hit, you know how it is.

Right, so, Greece or Italy? Honestly, I'm leaning towards Italy this year. The photos of Tuscany are just… breathtaking. Imagine, sun-drenched hills, vineyards stretching as far as the eye can see… Tuscany’s lovely, yeah, but last time we did Italy, it was absolutely overrun with tourists. Remember Florence? Felt like being herded like cattle. Greece has that island hopping appeal, though. Santorini, Mykonos… proper postcard stuff. I know, but the heat in Greece… I worry I’d spend half the time melting. And the history is fascinating in Italy, definitely more to explore. Plus, the food! Pasta making classes… wandering through little markets… Okay, you're selling it. But promise me, no ancient ruins for three days straight? I need a beach. Even just a little bit of sand, sunshine and a cold beer. My shoulders are already aching from staring at a screen all day. Deal. We'll definitely factor in some beach time. Maybe a week in Tuscany, then a few days on the Amalfi Coast? What do you think? That sounds blissful, actually. Right, while we’re dreaming… hypothetically, if we won the lottery, a  huge  lottery, what would we do first? Honestly, forget buying a mansion, what's the first splurge? Oh, that's a good one. Hmm… I wouldn’t buy a car. I’d commission a proper tattoo. One of those elaborate sleeves, something floral and intricate, inspired by Pre-Raphaelite art. I’ve been wanting one for  years , but it’s just such a commitment, you know? And the cost! A sleeve? Wow, that's ambitious! I was thinking something relatively small, maybe a simple geometric design on my forearm. But a Pre-Raphaelite sleeve… that’s bold. What would it represent? Everything! Beauty, nature, strength, resilience… all the things I aspire to. And it would be a work of art, something I’d be proud to wear. What about you? Aside from the bland geometric design? What’s your  real  desire? Alright, you caught me. The real thing is a recording studio. A properly decent one, not some DIY shed with cardboard soundproofing. I’d finally get to finish that blues album I’ve been talking about for fifteen years. You and your blues! No one wants to listen to you play the blues, darling. They'd run a mile! But a recording studio… that’s actually wonderful. It's a proper passion project.

Right then, Nigel, let’s solidify this weekend. I was thinking a quiet Saturday, perhaps a bit of gardening, then a leisurely dinner here. Sunday, though… Sunday needs a bit more planning. Sounds agreeable, David. Gardening's always a gamble, isn't it? Dependent on whether the rain decides to give us a break. Sunday… well, I was thinking we could pop over to see Eleanor and the children. It’s been a good few weeks. Eleanor and the children – a splendid idea! They are growing up so fast. Little Thomas practically towers over my prized roses now. I’ll give her a ring this afternoon, shall I? See if they’re free. Please do. And while you're at it, could you ask if they're still on for that board games night we talked about? The kids were desperate to play Scrabble again. You know how they love to try and stump you with obscure words. Indeed! Those children are remarkably cunning with their vocabulary. I'll check on the board games. Now, speaking of unusual words, I received this utterly charming postcard from Amelia. Look where she’s been - the Outer Hebrides! Blimey, that's a right desolate beauty, isn’t it? Stunning scenery though, you can almost feel the wind whipping off the sea. Amelia’s having a smashing time, it seems. Did she say much about it? She did. She raved about the walking, the sheer peace. Apparently, the locals have a distinct dialect – full of ancient Gaelic influences. She sent a few phrases she was trying to learn, but I confess, they were rather beyond me. "Ciamar a tha thu?" I believe was the greeting. Sounds like a tongue twister! I reckon tryin' to learn the Scots language and Gaelic must be like tacklin' a live wire. Reminds me of the arguments I was hearin' on the radio this morning. Back to the Scottish independence question, eh? Yes, the perennial debate. It's…exhausting, isn't it? All that division. Though, I must admit, the economic arguments are compelling on both sides. And the social ones, well, they’re even more complex. Do you think they'll ever truly settle it? I honestly don't know, David. It’s got such deep roots, that desire for independence. Generations of it. I mean, look at history – centuries of fighting for some form of autonomy. It's not something that's easily shaken off.

Right, you two. Let's see if we can make a proper picture for the charity, eh? Remember what we talked about? It's for those lovely people who've had to leave their homes in Syria. Are they cold, Mummy? They might be, darling. It’s not always warm where they are now. That’s why people are collecting things for them, and we’re going to do our bit with pictures. Think of a chair, Rosie. A comfy chair, so they have somewhere to sit. A throne! Like a king! A throne, Leo? That's a bit grand, isn't it? Though, I suppose everyone deserves to feel important. A normal chair will do, love. Think about your chairs at school. What kind are they? Hard! They’re scratchy! And sometimes I fall off! Yes, school chairs can be a bit…firm. Remember Grandma’s armchair? Now  that  was a comfy chair. All fluffy and soft. Mine’s got armrests. For putting my elbows. It’s a teacher’s chair. Miss Davies’ chair. Good detail, Leo. Miss Davies’ chair. That’s a proper observation. So, you can draw a chair with armrests, a chair without armrests, a really fluffy one, or a hard, scratchy one. It's up to you! What kind feels best? A bouncy chair! Like the one at the park! A bouncy chair for refugees, Rosie? That’s a wonderful idea, but I don't think we can  actually  give them bouncy chairs, can we? Imagine trying to move a bouncy chair! It would be all over the place. My chair at school wobbles. It needs a new leg. It does, doesn’t it? Right, so maybe you could draw a wobbly chair then, Leo. A chair that needs fixing. That shows you understand chairs aren’t always perfect, are they? Sometimes they need a little bit of help. Can I draw a chair with rainbow stripes? Absolutely! A chair with rainbow stripes, that's brilliant! That would cheer anyone up. They need cheering up, don't they? Are we going to have a test about chairs later? Like in Maths? No, no test about chairs, darling. This isn’t school. This is…art! And kindness. We’re doing something nice for other people. Look, Mummy! A very happy chair! It is a very happy chair, sweetheart. Absolutely lovely. Leo, how’s your wobbly chair coming along?

Honestly, I’m still reeling from Sarah’s announcement. A  triplet  announcement! Three! Can you imagine? Three? Blimey. That's… ambitious, isn't it? I saw a quick post, but I hadn't fully processed it. How’s she holding up? She always seemed like the low-key, quiet type. That’s what I keep thinking! She seemed perfectly happy with just Tom. Last time we spoke, she was complaining about him drawing on the walls. Now, that's going to be like… a miniature riot zone. Apparently, the ultrasound was a complete shock to them both. Wow. A proper surprise then. Poor Tom. He’s going to need a very large bedroom and a serious nap strategy. Do they know the genders yet? Apparently, two boys and a girl. They seemed thrilled, though utterly terrified. She sent a voice note, which I didn’t fully understand because she was practically hyperventilating, but I think she said they’re having a massive nursery makeover. All pastels and woodland creatures, apparently. Very…Instagrammable. Of course it is. Everything has to be Instagrammable these days. Still, that's a lot of expense. Are they financially prepared for that? That’s what I was thinking. Mark and I are doing alright, but three babies? That's a whole different level. I bet her parents are chipping in. Her dad always did spoil her rotten. Speaking of which, have you heard from Liam lately? Not recently. Just the occasional birthday message. He's still buried in that research project in Cambridge, isn't he? Last I heard, he was living off instant noodles and sheer willpower. He really needs to come down for a proper weekend. We should actually suggest it. Absolutely. He looks utterly exhausted in all his pictures. And remember how he was moaning about the lack of decent coffee in Cambridge? This place would be heaven for him. Although, with Sarah and her… burgeoning brood… it might be a bit overwhelming. True. Still, he'd appreciate the company. Teaching's been pretty draining this week, hasn't it? That seminar on Victorian literature felt like I was wading through treacle. The students just weren’t engaging. Tell me about it! I had to practically drag them through Shakespeare. Honestly, some of them look at  Hamlet  like it's a foreign language. I spent half the session explaining iambic pentameter. You’d think they’d  want  to understand it, given how much of modern music is based on it!

Honestly, the response to that online article was utterly ludicrous. Did you see the comment about me summoning rain clouds with my "unsettling aura"? Unsettling aura! Only because it was so ridiculous, love. People online will latch onto anything. A bit of publicity for the university, though, isn't it? That's got to be a plus. A plus if they weren't suggesting I’m a modern-day rain witch. My mum nearly had a heart attack. Apparently, Grandma Elsie used to say Norfolk folk were particularly susceptible to weather magic. Elsie and her superstitions! She used to insist we couldn't start the Christmas decorations before December 1st, or it would bring bad luck. Remember that year we put the baubles up in November, and the plumbing exploded? Don’t remind me! I blamed it on the early decorations, obviously. Elsie certainly did. Still, there’s something to be said for sticking to traditions, isn't there? Though I suspect the plumbing was just old. Probably. But it makes for a good story, doesn’t it? Speaking of stories, did you hear about that incident with the police in Wymondham? Apparently, a flock of geese held up traffic for a good hour. Geese?! Seriously? That’s… incredibly Norwich. I can just imagine the scene. Policemen looking utterly bewildered while a gaggle of geese slowly waddled across the road. Exactly! The local news was having a field day. And, of course, someone had filmed it all on their phone. The comments section was even more chaotic than the reaction to your article. People were saying the geese were protesting something. Protesting the price of birdseed, no doubt! You know, it's funny, we spend our lives analyzing Shakespeare and Milton, dissecting metaphors and allusions, and then reality comes along and delivers something far more absurd. That's the beauty of it, isn't it? The real world is often stranger than fiction. It’s the perfect fodder for a comedy routine. You should work it into your next lecture. "Superstition, Shakespeare and Swanning Geese: A Norfolk Perspective." You’re giving me ideas. It'd be a bit niche, though, wouldn't it? I don't want to alienate the students. They're already muttering about me being eccentric enough after the rain cloud business. Eccentric is good! It grabs their attention. Besides, you're brilliant at making even the most obscure topics engaging.

Honestly, Dad, this new phone update is awful. Everything’s moved around. I can't even find the camera quickly anymore! It’s so frustrating when they “improve” things and it just makes it more complicated. Complicated, eh? That’s all modern technology is, innit? Just a heap o’ complication. Back in my day, a phone was a phone. You picked it up and you rang someone. Simple as that. No fancy screens, no apps, no… whatever it is you young’uns are doing on 'em. Well, I like apps! I use them for everything, Dad. Navigation, banking, listening to music... And the camera’s brilliant, when I can actually  find  it. Speaking of which, did you manage to look at those removals quotes yet? We need to get a van sorted, and soon. Mum’s getting twitchy about the move. Quotes... right, right. Had a quick gander online. Prices are scandalous, they are. Remember when we used to borrow Arthur’s lorry for a fiver? Those were the days. This generation, everything's got a pound sign slapped all over it. Though, Arthur’s long gone, of course. Sad, that was. Yeah. Still, we need something reliable, though. And big enough for all Mum’s… well,  stuff . It's a mountain. I was thinking a Luton van, something with a tail lift. Saves our backs, eh? Luton, tail lift… sounds awfully posh for moving a few boxes. We could get some of those lads from Facebook Marketplace. Cheaper, probably. Though you have to be careful these days, don't you? People aren’t what they seem. That's what I’m worried about. Mum’d be a nervous wreck if anything went wrong. It's a big move for her, leaving the house she and Gran lived in. Speaking of, did you remind Uncle Barry we’re hoping to get everyone together for a proper farewell barbecue? Barry? Oh, aye, I’ll give him a ring. He’s always full of excuses, that one. Last time he said he had a… a badger infestation. Badgers! In Chelsea! Honestly, Dad, you’re making that up. No, I’m not! Asked him if he needed help, he just mumbled something about a specialist and put the phone down. Anyway, barbecue’s a good idea. We should get some proper sausages. And maybe a few of those pork pies from the baker’s. Reminds me of the Great Dorset Steam Fair.

Honestly, this teal is just… too much. It’ll swallow the room whole. Remember that awful avocado green they had in the library back in the seventies? This feels like that, but more aggressively. Aggressively teal? Right, well, I thought it was quite vibrant. Though, I suppose with the light in here, it does seem a bit… overwhelming. What about that beige one? The linen-look? Beige? David, we're not re-upholstering a government building! We need something with a little personality. Something that won't make the room feel like a waiting room. It needs to hold up to, you know… life. The cat, clumsy guests… You’re always anticipating a disaster. It’s a very British thing, I think. “It’ll stain, it’ll rip, the cat will….” Anyway, the beige is practical. And it would go with everything. What did you think of that article in the  Guardian  about the library? Don't even get me started. It’s outrageous. Demolishing it for another block of flats? It's a landmark! And it's a vital resource for the community. Where will the kids go for their reading groups? Where will the elderly go to access the internet? They keep bleating on about needing more housing. Apparently, the council thinks a bland concrete structure is the solution. They're even talking about demolishing parts of the old Town Hall to make way for… something. I can't even remember what. Some monstrous shopping complex, I think. It’s the same everywhere, isn't it? They just don't value history. They’re obsessed with ‘progress,’ which usually means stripping away everything that makes a place unique. Look at that new development on Elm Street - a blank slate of glass and steel. No character whatsoever. It could be anywhere in the world. Though, I must say, I did read something about encouraging developers to retain the facades of older buildings. Apparently, there’s a grant scheme now. It's no guarantee, but… A grant scheme? You think that'll stop them? The council’s more interested in lining their pockets than preserving our heritage. They probably saw the flats, the profit margins… that's all they care about. Did you see old Mrs. Higgins at the shop today? She’s practically beside herself about the library. I did. She was muttering about petitions and protests. Do you think we should sign something?

Right then, Hampshire countryside, good music playing…this is the life, isn't it? Though, honestly, I'm still slightly baffled by that playlist Chloe put together. Is that…techno polka? It’s experimental, Dad! Chloe's very into experimental music. You just don't  get  it. Besides, it's much better than your endless classical selections. I have to say, I appreciate Chloe’s adventurous spirit when it comes to music. I’m usually stuck listening to podcasts about Victorian literature, so a bit of… that …is a welcome change. Though, I agree, techno polka might be a stretch. Experimental is one word for it! Reminds me of those awful student parties I had to endure back in the day. Though, at least it’s got energy. Did anyone get anything nice for Mum’s birthday, by the way? We’re getting close. I got her that aromatherapy diffuser she’s been wanting. With lavender oil, obviously. She keeps saying she needs to relax more. Good thinking, love. I went a bit rogue, I'm afraid. I found this gorgeous hand-painted ceramic bird feeder at a little shop in Winchester. A robin, naturally. She’s mad for robins. That’s lovely, Richard! Very thoughtful. I got her a subscription to that online gardening course she mentioned. 'Grow Your Own Herbs and Vegetables' – rather practical, I thought. A subscription, eh? That’s solid. I went for something a bit more… sentimental. A framed print of that watercolour painting she’s always admired, the one of the Lake District. Took me ages to track down a good quality reproduction. Ooh, David, that's really sweet! Mum's going to love it. You always know how to pull out all the stops. Are you still doing your pottery, David? I haven’t seen your creations in ages. Trying to, yes. It’s a bit difficult fitting in the wheel with all the departmental meetings and reports these days. My throwing skills are definitely rusting a bit, I must admit. It's a shame, you were quite good at it, weren’t you? You used to make fantastic little bowls. Speaking of hobbies, Chloe, still doing your hair artistry? Any big projects on the go? Yeah, still loving it! Actually, I'm prepping for a competition next month. It's a 'Avant-Garde Hair Design' thing. It’s terrifying and exciting all at the same time.

Right then, Liam, love. Let’s have a proper look at this car insurance. Seems a bit steep, doesn’t it? I’ve been fiddling with it for an hour now. Yeah, it's a bit mental, isn’t it? They keep saying "excess" this and "mileage" that. What even  is  excess? Aye, it’s a bit of a jargon fest, innit? Well, it’s the amount you have to pay yourself if you need to make a claim. So, if you bash your car up and need to claim, you'll fork out that excess, and the insurance company will cover the rest, up to your policy limit, of course. Makes sense, doesn’t it? The higher the excess, often the cheaper the policy. So, like, if I chose an excess of £500, I’d pay £500 if I had an accident? That's right, petal. Exactly. It encourages you not to claim for every little scratch, doesn’t it? Now, this mileage... they're quoting you for 8,000 miles a year. Is that right? Seems a bit ambitious for just getting to college and back. I was being honest! I mean, there's the occasional weekend trip to see Sarah, and sometimes we go further afield with the lads. Plus, Dad's car’s been playing up so I’ve been giving him a lift more often than usual. Aye, I get that. Right. Let’s try 6,000 then, shall we? See if that makes a difference. Just a minute… Right, it’s dropped a bit, but not as much as I’d hoped. They're still bumping it up because you’re a young driver, you see. It’s a risk for them. It’s so unfair though! I’m a careful driver. I haven't even had a parking ticket! That’s true, love. You’re a good lad. But statistically, young drivers  are  more likely to have accidents. Sadly, it's just how it is. Have you considered adding me as a named driver? Would that even work? Wouldn't they know I'm the main driver? They might, but it can sometimes lower the premium, especially if they see a more experienced driver on the policy. I’ve been driving for donkeys' years, after all! Although don’t tell them that makes me old! We’d have to be honest about who’s driving most of the time though.

Jaysus, this curry’s grand, alright. But the chicken’s a bit… rubbery, isn't it? Not as tender as I'd like. It's okay, Dad. I like it. More rice? Don't knock it, Sean. It's a Tuesday night. Chinese is a win. And honestly, after battling little Maisie all day, I’m grateful for anything. Aye, I know, I know. Just being picky. Work’s been a right pressure cooker lately. This new project… it's testing me, it really is. I swear, I’m bordering on permanently stressed. Stress? Like, what even is stress, really? Miss Davies was talking about it in PSHE. Something about adrenaline and your heart beating fast. It's more than that, Liam. It's that feeling like there’s a knot in your stomach, you can't sleep, and you snap at people. Sean probably has a stress test at work, doesn’t he? With spreadsheets and graphs. Something like that. They make you take these questionnaires, you know? Rate your anxiety, your sleep patterns, stuff like that. Trying to convince you that the ‘biofeedback’ apps are going to solve everything. I’d rather a pint. Biofeedback? Is that like… backwards feedback? Sort of. Trying to use your body’s signals to control your stress. All a bit complicated, truth be told. I’d rather have a good laugh and forget about it for a bit. Speaking of which, did you hear the one about the… Sean, dear, please. After three hours of Peppa Pig, I think my brain needs a break from bad jokes. How are things with Sarah, by the way? Still got the new position? Aye, she's thriving. It’s good to see her happy. It's bringing us closer, you know? Sometimes I think I forgot how important a good partnership is. You know, someone to lean on. It’s not all about those bloody spreadsheets. You and Mum always seem solid, though. Like, you’re always joking around. Don't let his jokes fool you, Liam. They're a carefully crafted defense mechanism. I resent that! I'm simply lightening the mood. Besides, something a wee bit lighter would be good. Have you ever thought about how weird it is the current marriage equality vote was in Ireland, just a few years ago? It’s astonishing, isn’t it? Yeah, Miss Davies said it was a big thing.

Right then, according to this, we're still another forty minutes out from Hawkshead. Anyone need a break? My back's starting to ache. Nah, I'm alright, Dad. Just admiring the view. Proper bleak, innit? All these hills. Makes you realise how small you are, doesn't it? Aye, lass. It does. Bolton seems flat as a pancake now, after this. Remember when we used to come up here as kids, Jamie? You were terrified of the sheep. They were smelly, Mum. And they kept headbutting me. Basic instinct, innit? Sheer animalistic aggression. Spot on, Jamie. Textbook. Though, I suspect your own aggression played a part in provoking them. Tell you what, son, you need to put that phone down and look at the scenery. It's a bit more interesting than whatever you’re scrolling through. Hawkshead is lovely, proper picture postcard. Like something out of Shakespeare, really. Shakespeare, Dad? Seriously? It’s just…a village. All stone cottages and tea rooms. Though, I suppose they probably had a bit of drama going on back then too, eh? They certainly did. Look, Michael, are you still thinking about that law conversion course? You said you were last week. Yeah. Still weighing it up. It's just...a lot of money, isn’t it? And what if I hate it? I mean, what if I'm more of a Bear Grylls type? Surviving in the wilderness, eating bugs... Right. I’m not entirely sure the Lake District wilderness constitutes a survival situation, Jamie. Though, I suppose a rogue sheep  could  be a threat. Seriously though, a law degree would be a solid foundation. Good earning potential. Think about it practically. Gran, don't push him too hard. He needs to do what HE wants. Plus, it's not like he needs to worry about earning potential.  Someone's  funded his entire existence so far. Now, now, Elara. That's hardly fair. We’re supporting him while he figures out what he wants to  do . It's an investment. Besides, bearing in mind the ridiculous price of petrol these days, a career that generates a decent income will be a necessity soon enough. Speaking of ridiculous prices, did you see how much a pint of milk is at Tesco now? Daylight robbery, it is! I swear, they're running the country. Makes you think about the EU referendum all over again, doesn’t it?

Honestly, this is surprisingly good, Chloe. You've really outdone yourself. Though, I still miss a proper Sunday roast sometimes. Thanks, Elara! It's a bit of an experiment, trying to make things interesting. Sunday roasts are a classic, though. Maybe we can make a vegetarian one next week, massively scaled down though, right? I’m not confident enough to tackle a whole beast without meat. This  is  good, Chloe. Really. You've managed to make lentils… palatable. It's a miracle. But I still maintain, a good bit of venison is hard to beat. Not the farmed stuff, mind you. Properly hunted, you know? Hunting? Liam, really? You know how I feel about that. It just feels… aggressive. All that tracking and waiting and then… But it’s natural, Elara. Part of the cycle! And a properly managed hunt is far better for the deer population than letting them overpopulate and starve. It's about balance. And significantly more humane than what goes on in most abattoirs, let's be honest. That’s a valid point about the abattoirs, Liam. They  are  horrific. I volunteered at an animal sanctuary once, and the stories… the sheer scale of suffering... It’s why I’m seriously considering looking into cultured meat, or shmeat as they call it sometimes. Shmeat? Seriously? It sounds like something out of Curb Your Enthusiasm. I bet Larry would have a meltdown about it. Oh, he absolutely would. "Shmeat! It's not real meat! It's… manufactured!" He’d be muttering for days. But I’m intrigued by the idea, actually. Less environmental impact, no animal suffering... Exactly! Apparently, it needs significantly less land and water than traditional meat production. And think of the resources! We could feed so many more people. I don't know… it just feels… unnatural. Like, are we playing God? And what will it  taste  like? It's not like you can just order a steak from a lab and expect it to be exactly the same. We’re already manipulating nature loads, Elara. Selective breeding, intensive farming… this is just a slightly different approach. Plus, they’re getting pretty close to replicating the taste and texture. I read an article that said they’re on the verge of making a really convincing chicken breast. And think about the ethical implications. No more factory farms, no more animals crammed into tiny cages… Okay, okay, you're swaying me a little.

Nah, change it, this is mingin’. What were we watchin’ earlier? That sci-fi one, ‘Across the Void’? Aye, relax, Liam. It's comin' back on in five. I’m just checkin’ this offer on Amazon. See, they’ve got that new Playstation controller, the one with the haptic feedback, on sale. Five quid off? Seriously, Ethan? You're going to spend money on  another  controller? You’ve got like, five already. It’s not just five quid, Maisie! It’s significant when you're skint. And this is different, right? This promises to make the games feel...proper. Like you’re actually  there . Plus, I can use it at your place, Liam, when we’re over. Aye, because you'll be over my place beating me at FIFA again, will ya? With your fancy new controller and all. It’s rigged, Ethan, it’s always rigged. You two are ridiculous. Honestly. Speaking of ridiculous, I just saw Chloe posted a picture from Barcelona. Sun, sangria, and a tiny little balcony overlooking the harbour. Barcelona? Fancy! She's really livin' the high life, eh? Wish I was her. Remember when we all talked about goin' to Spain after Sixthform? Aye, just a pipe dream, wasn’t it? Me bein' stuck here doin’ engineering, you stuck… well, you’re stuck, Ethan. And you're stuck studyin' for uni, Maisie. I'm not  stuck , Liam. University is going well. And Barcelona's just a holiday. I'm saving up for a proper trip, not just a sun-soaked jaunt. Maybe next summer? Proper trip…right. That’d be nice. Remember Nan’s Christmas decorations? She went all out. Massive tree, tinsel everywhere... It felt like proper Christmas. Aye, that were good times. Actually, I was thinkin' 'bout gettin' meself a new phone. Mine's on its last legs. Battery barely lasts an hour. Seriously? Again? You only got a new one last year. This one's fallin' to bits. Plus, I need a better camera for takin’ pictures of the lakes. You know, for Instagram. Gotta keep up with Chloe, right? Oh, so  now  you want to keep up with Chloe. Not when she’s boastin’ about Barcelona. Shut up, you. Liam, have you looked at those new foldable phones? They’re pretty crazy. A bit pricey, though. Foldable? Like…a flap? Seems impractical. I don’t know. What about that new game, ‘Starlight Frontier’?

Honestly, I still can’t believe we’re actually  at  Alumni Day. Feels a bit surreal, doesn’t it? Like, remember when we were stressing about getting into Cambridge in the first place? Don’t remind me! My mum nearly drove me mad with revision guides. And you, I recall, were constantly disappearing to the Aylesbury library, muttering about phonological shifts. Are you  still  obsessed with language quirks? Always! It’s my job now, after all. Coordinating language research…it's a bit grander than I ever imagined when I was writing essays about Old English. What about you? Still enjoying the admin side of things? It’s good, actually. Less intense than I feared. Lots of organising, which I’m surprisingly decent at. Though I do miss the lectures sometimes. Did you catch any of Professor Davies' talk? The one on legal linguistics? Briefly! I was mostly trying to navigate the crowds and find a decent coffee. Davies is brilliant, though. Absolutely fascinating stuff. Speaking of crowds, did you see Aunt Susan and Uncle Clive hovering around the Provost? They looked utterly thrilled to be in the same room as anyone vaguely important. Classic Susan and Clive. They’re determined to network their way into the aristocracy. Speaking of family, how's your Nan doing? Last I heard, she was planning a trip to the Lake District. She’s amazing! Just got back actually. She took about five thousand photos of sheep, apparently. Said it was 'a cultural experience'. And she’s already planning her next adventure - Portugal! She’s always wanted to learn Portuguese, but just never found the time. Portugal's lovely. My parents went last year. They were completely charmed by Lisbon. You should suggest it to Nan. It’s got history, beautiful tilework, and ridiculously good custard tarts. I will! She’s always been drawn to the idea of southern Europe. It's so nice she's finally getting to explore. I’m thinking of booking a holiday myself. I’ve been eyeing up Iceland. Iceland! That’s ambitious. A bit colder than Portugal, though. Are you a winter person? My sister went last year. Said it was beautiful, but she spent most of the time shivering. I like the dramatic landscapes, y’know? The glaciers, the volcanoes...and the Northern Lights, obviously. Plus, I've been reading about their language – Icelandic is incredible, so ancient and preserved.

Honestly, Liam, I’m ready to chuck my laptop out the window. This Modernist Literature module is killing me. Dramatic as ever, love. What’s got your knickers in a twist this time? Another impenetrable essay on Virginia Woolf? Worse, actually. It’s Eliot. “The Waste Land.” I’ve read it three times and I still feel like I’m wandering around a desert wearing a blindfold. Dr. Harding expects us to glean some profound meaning from it! Pro-found! It’s just… confusing. And long. So, so long. Alright, alright. Deep breaths. It  is  dense. Remember what Professor Davies said in his lecture last year? About it being a reflection of post-war disillusionment? Try approaching it from that angle, see if it helps. I  did ! I read his lecture notes like five times. Still just words. Fancy a massage? My shoulders are permanently hunched after staring at scholarly articles. Always thinking with your shoulders, aren’t you? Let me finish this chapter, yeah? It’s a crucial point about… well, never mind, you wouldn’t be interested. Then, yes. Massage sounds good. Honestly, though, about the Eliot thing... don’t torture yourself trying to over-analyze every single line. Sometimes you just need to feel the poem, you know? Feel it? I'm feeling a headache coming on, that's what I'm feeling! You always make it sound so easy. You practically  breathe  academia. Postgraduate degrees and all that. I'm just a girl from Doncaster trying to get through sixth form, let alone university. Hey, don't talk like that. You’re brilliant, Elara. You just have a different way of understanding things. And my postgraduate degree was mostly fueled by copious amounts of coffee and late nights staring at screens, just like you. It's not some magical superpower. Easy for you to say. You actually  like  all that stuff. You get excited by footnotes and obscure literary references. I just want a nice cup of tea and a box set. There’s nothing wrong with that! Honestly, have you considered talking to Dr. Harding? Just to clarify your understanding? Sometimes just hearing it explained in a different way can make all the difference. I don’t know... I feel a bit daft asking. Like I'm the only one struggling. Rubbish! Loads of people struggle with it. Modernism  is  deliberately obfuscating. And she’s a good lecturer, really.

Right, that’s the greenery sorted. Honestly, I’m starving. Did you two manage to actually  eat  anything before I got here? A biscuit or two, love. Nothing substantial. Been a bit… distracted, you know? Distracted by what, Arthur? The pigeons again? You were out there throwing them scraps for a good hour this morning. They're desperate, Margaret. You can see it in their eyes. Calais is a mess, really. Did you see that report on the news last night? Absolutely heartbreaking. Those people… children… living in those camps. It’s a disgrace, the whole thing. It is awful, isn't it? I try not to dwell on it too much; it's just… overwhelming. But the kids at school have been asking questions. They’re aware, and they’re worried. I try to explain it in an age-appropriate way, but... It’s difficult. We're lucky, aren't we? To have a roof over our heads and a warm meal. My cousin Sarah sent me a link to a charity working in Calais; they’re desperately trying to get warm clothes and blankets there. I might donate. I could spare something. Always got a bit too much around the place, haven't I? Need to clear out some space. All those management meetings… all that paperwork… for what, eh? It wouldn't have mattered if those people in France had a bit of it. It's okay, Dad. You did well. You provided for us. Don’t start feeling guilty about it. Exactly. And we appreciate everything you’ve done. Now, Arthur, stop looking so gloomy and try some of this gravy. I made it extra rich, just the way you like it. Not bad, Margaret. Not bad at all. Though I still think you use a bit too much Worcestershire sauce. Oh, here we go! That’s the secret, Arthur! Don't tell anyone. Speaking of secrets, have you thought any more about that little trip I mentioned last week? To Cornwall? Cornwall! Oh, that would be lovely. I’ve been needing a break. The term's been hectic. Year six SATs looming, you know. Absolutely bonkers. Cornwall… seaside… might be nice. A change of scenery. But what about the pigeons? Who will feed the pigeons? We’ll find someone, Arthur. Don't worry. And honestly, a week away from Southend won’t hurt them. They'll manage.

Honestly, Alun, I’m starting to think renovating a bathroom is more stressful than grading a postgraduate dissertation. And that’s saying something. Tell me about it, David. You know, they say homeownership is the great British dream, but sometimes I wonder. I’ve just been wrestling with the kitchen tiling. The original plan was lovely, you know, a subtle geometric pattern... Oh, I know the type. Something you admire in a magazine and then realise requires the hands of Michelangelo to execute properly. I went for something simple with the bathroom - a classic metro tile. Thought I couldn’t go wrong. Simple is good! I learned that lesson years ago, trying to replicate some elaborate Victorian mosaic. Ended up looking like a dog's dinner. So, what’s the hold-up with your bathroom then? The tradespeople. Honestly, Alun, finding reliable ones is a nightmare. I hired a plumber - seemed perfectly respectable, quoted me a reasonable price. Turns out “reasonable” meant “he’ll take three days and charge you for each one regardless of how much he actually does.” Aye, they are a breed, aren't they? I had a chap in last year to look at the boiler. Said it needed a ‘minor adjustment’ and then proceeded to spend half a day fiddling and charge me a fortune. My neighbour, Maggie – you remember Maggie, from the History department? – she’s just had her whole kitchen redone. Says the joiner was a complete disaster. Kept turning up late, arguments with the electrician... she’s practically aged ten years. Maggie! Good woman. Yes, I remember. The one who always brings those absolutely fabulous Bakewell tarts to the faculty meetings? It’s the communication, isn’t it? Or rather, the lack of it. My plumber kept forgetting to call, then would blame  me  for not answering my phone. As if I spend my entire day waiting for a man to tell me he's arriving sometime between noon and Tuesday. Exactly! It's like pulling teeth. You've got to chase them constantly. Maggie ended up having to practically babysit the whole operation. She said her husband Rhys – a retired miner, bless him – was muttering about how things were more predictable down the pit. Rhys has a point, I'm sure. Though I'd hardly call delving into the earth less stressful than choosing between twenty shades of grout. I was thinking of getting recommendations from the gardening club, actually.

Right, so, that vindaloo was  fierce  tonight. Absolutely fierce. I swear, I felt like I could breathe fire afterwards. Anyone else feelin' the burn? It was good, yeah. A bit spicy, though. Like, properly spicy. Not like the stuff Mum makes, which is just…warm. Warm is exactly what I need most nights, love. Anything bolder than mild and I’m reaching for the Alka-Seltzer before I can even finish a mouthful. Speaking of which, Liam, put the teaspoon down! That’s not food! Shiny! He seems to have developed a fascination with metal. Remember when he tried to eat a corner of the radiator? Nearly gave me a heart attack. Gross. My friend, Finn, he reckons he once ate a whole ten pence piece. Said it tasted like…nothing. Seriously? Finn’s a dramatic one. Children put all sorts in their mouths though. It’s just… concerning. I’ve got a horrible memory of a history book from school. About the Middle Ages. Honestly, it was so dry and full of dates. I nearly fell asleep standing up. It made me feel physical pain, I swear. Biology was better, at least you learned about…well, you know, bodies. History can be brutal. It’s just a relentless list of awful things people did. My Da used to say, “Why bother learnin’ about all the misery? Just focus on makin’ your own life a bit brighter.” Wise man, he was. Though he’d have a wee bit to say about Liam’s fondness for cutlery. My teacher says we have to learn about all the bad stuff so we don’t repeat it. But sometimes…it just feels pointless. Like, knowing about the Black Death doesn’t really help me with my maths test. It’s a complicated thing, isn’t it? It  should  help you understand the present, but often it just makes you feel a bit depressed. Anyway... Liam, no! That’s not a building material! So, about Liam’s birthday next month… have we settled on anything? I was thinking the park event – the one with the bouncy castle? The park's a grand idea. Keeps the wee fella occupied. Do you think we should get him that superhero cape he was drooling over in Smyths? He's convinced he can fly. He  would  love that. I’m working on a new design for mine. It's going to have flashing lights and maybe a grappling hook.

Did you see the decorations, Nan? Mr. Peterson across the road has gone absolutely wild! He’s got a giant inflatable spider and strobe lights! It's brilliant! A giant spider, eh? Blimey. Back in my day, Halloween was just a few apples bobbing in a bucket and maybe a bit of string with paper ghosts hanging from it. None of this fancy business. Costessey wasn't a place for showing off, you know. Simple folk. It  is  rather extravagant, isn’t it? Though, I must admit, I do quite like the inflatable pumpkins. I used to bring the children from my minding group trick-or-treating. The parents were very particular about the sweets, you know. Organic, sugar-free, nut-free… a right faff! Typical. Kids, eh? I've got a lot of discussion about Halloween in school, Matthew. Some parents are objecting to the whole thing, too American they say. Don’t understand the history. Didn’t used to get that kind of pushback. Used to be all about the fun. My History teacher said it started as a Celtic festival to ward off evil spirits. He said the costumes were meant to scare them away! Sounds right enough. A bit of harmless mischief. Nothing like it is now, all commercially driven. Speaking of mischief, remember that time young Timmy swapped Mrs. Higgins’ dentures for a rubber chicken? Oh, good heavens, yes! That was a classic! The look on Mrs. Higgins’ face… priceless. I’d almost forgotten! Imagine doing that now! You’d get in so much trouble! I’m going as a unicorn this year. I’ve made the horn myself out of cardboard and glitter. A unicorn, lovely! Always did like horses. When I were a lad, I used to sneak down to Farmer Giles' field and just watch ‘em. Couldn’t get near ‘em, mind. Too much respect for the animals, we did. I took a few of the children to a riding school once. Little Emily fell off, poor thing. Scraped her knee something awful. But she was brave as anything and wanted to get straight back on. That’s the spirit. Resilience, eh? Something all the children need. I'm trying to teach them about overcoming challenges in my class. It's proving a bit trickier than explaining the history of Halloween, though! I go riding every Saturday at Meadow Farm. It's really relaxing.

Honestly, this is ridiculous. I thought leaving Gillingham at eight thirty would be a genius move. Look at this! It's like the whole of Kent decided to go to Dorset today. Well, it's the Steam Fair, innit? Always popular. Should’ve gone years ago, when I had the time, and no aches and pains to complain about. Don't start on your aches and pains, Bernard. It’ll bring everyone’s spirits down. At least we’re moving now, albeit slowly. I’m just praying we find a decent parking space. Especially with Mum’s wheelchair. That's what I'm worried about! Disabled parking always seems a lottery, doesn’t it? I swear, people just park in those spots when they see a space. Absolutely appalling. It's just the way things are, love. People think they're too important to wait their turn. Remember that time I had to walk a mile from the back of the post office because someone had parked their little Peugeot right across the accessible bay? Took me nearly an hour to get home with the pension books. Oh, Bernard, you and your pension books. Honestly, though, the council needs to be stricter. They should enforce those parking regulations properly. And speaking of the council... I was reading about that new elderly housing development they're proposing in Harlow. Oh really? Where? I haven't heard anything. It's near the Netto, that bit where the old industrial estate used to be. Apparently, it’s supposed to be “affordable.” Affordable for whom? Everything’s affordable for someone who’s got a spare million quid lying around these days. They call it affordable, then charge you a fortune in service charges and put in tiny flats. Exactly! My Nan's been on the council housing list for years. She's in that damp little flat in Gillingham – frankly, it's not fit for a hamster, let alone a 82-year-old. It’s freezing in the winter and stifling in the summer. It's heartbreaking, isn’t it? It’s just not good enough. We need more decent, purpose-built housing for older people. With proper support services, and somewhere they can feel safe and comfortable. Not crammed into some tiny box. My sister, Brenda, she's been trying to get her mum out of that awful retirement home. It's all strip lighting and bland food.

Honestly, this drizzle is relentless. Makes you really crave a bit of sunshine, doesn't it? And a garden bursting with colour, instead of just… grey. Tell me about it! I was just thinking the same thing. That’s precisely why this allotment idea is so appealing, isn't it? A little pocket of sunshine, even when it's pouring like this. So, have you been giving it much thought since we last spoke? We’re actually going to put in a bid for one, right? I have! Loads. I've been trawling the internet for advice. It’s a minefield, isn't it? Everyone has a strong opinion on what you  should  do. I’ve read about raised beds, no-dig gardening, companion planting… it’s a bit overwhelming. I was thinking raised beds might be easiest, especially because the soil in that area probably isn’t fantastic. Raised beds are definitely sensible, particularly as a starting point. Less back strain too, which is always a bonus. I was looking at some plans online - pallets are a really cheap and cheerful way to build them, if you're into a bit of DIY. We could even get Mark to help, he’s surprisingly good with a saw. Oh, that's a brilliant idea! Honestly, I'd be lost without someone handy. I’m good at planting, I think, but construction… that's not really my forte. What about companion planting though? I saw something about planting carrots next to onions to deter pests. Sounds a bit mad, doesn't it? It does sound a little fantastical, but actually, there’s quite a bit of science behind it. Different plants can help each other grow, or repel pests, or improve the soil. It's worth looking into. I was thinking we could dedicate a section to herbs, too. Fresh basil and thyme would be amazing. Oh, YES! Fresh herbs are my weakness. I always end up buying dried ones because I can never keep fresh ones alive. This could be the thing that finally changes that! What about vegetables? I’d love to grow tomatoes, but I’ve heard they're really tricky. Tomatoes  are  a bit of a challenge, but definitely not impossible. You need to give them plenty of sunshine and support. We could try cherry tomatoes – they’re usually a bit more forgiving. And definitely some courgettes. Everyone always has way too many courgettes!

"Ey up, Rach! Fancy seein’ you 'ere! Thought you were still gallivanting about down in Cambridge, lookin' all posh and proper.” “Doncaster, of all places! Don't start, Chloe. I’m here for Mum’s birthday, obviously. And posh? Hardly. Cambridge makes you appreciate a decent Yorkshire brew, that’s all. How’s life in the sticks been treating you?” “Reckon it’s been alright. College is…well, college. Lots of learnin’, not loads of doin’, ya know? Been tryin’ to get my head around this History essay, it’s a right mare. What about you? Still buryin’ yourself in books?” "Always! I’m actually enjoying this term, surprisingly. We're doing a module on Victorian social reform, it's fascinating. But, honestly, I needed a break. All those old buildings and cobbled streets can get a bit oppressive after a while. Plus, I miss proper pubs and proper people.” “Right? Cambridge pubs are all…tables and waitresses. No proper bar chat, no singin’ along to the jukebox. Listen, I were just thinkin’…Now you’re ‘ere, we ‘ave to make the most of it. Remember that new Italian place that opened on St George’s Square?” "The one everyone's been raving about? Yeah, I saw some pictures online. Padronia’s, isn't it? Sounds rather fancy, even for me." “Fancy schmancy. But they do decent pizza. What I were thinking is, me, you, Liam, and maybe Sarah? Saturday night? A proper girls' night out.” "That sounds  amazing , Chloe! I’d love that. Liam’s still being Liam, then?" “Aye, he is. Still tryin' to impress everyone with his ‘deep’ thoughts. Bless 'im. But he's good company. I think Sarah’s free, she's finished her exams, so she should be up for it." "Perfect! I’ve been needing a good laugh. How's things with Mark, by the way? Still going strong?" “Aye, mostly. It's been a bit…difficult, actually. He’s been workin’ ridiculous hours, tryin’ to get that promotion. Barely see ‘im, to be honest." “Oh, Chloe, that’s rough. You deserve someone who makes time for you. Don’t compromise on that, alright? You’re too good for being an afterthought." “I know, I know. It’s just…I don’t want to be difficult. He’s stressin' out something awful, and I just want him to succeed.” "Supporting him is one thing, Chloe, but letting him completely push you aside isn't.

Speaker_1 :   Right, that's it. I’m switching characters. I've been playing Winston for the last twenty minutes and I’m gettin' absolutely battered. It's a right mess, innit? Keep gettin' dinked in corners.   Speaker_2 :   You  are  gettin' a proper trouncing, Liam! Don't blame you for changing. Winston needs a bit more… finesse. You’re just charging in like a bull at a gate, lad.   Speaker_3 :   Finesse is key, yeah. This game  does  punish reckless aggression. Trust me, I learned that the hard way. Been maining Genji for ages, still make dumb mistakes. You should see my kill/death ratio. It’s… tragic.   Speaker_4 :   Reckless aggression is kinda the point sometimes, isn't it? Need a distraction, a bit of chaos. Though, I get what you mean, Rajan. Smash and grab, gotta be quick. What are you all playing? Trying to coordinate a push, or just…?   Liam:   Just flailing about, mostly. I keep tryin' to follow what Chloe’s sayin' about strategy, but I’m a bit slow sometimes, you know? Brain's still catchin’ up from that lecture on Victorian literature. All them proper nouns!   Chloe:   Victorian literature? Sounds intense. Still, you’re better at it than my cousin, honestly. He just screams at the screen. So, Daniel, what have you been up to? Still obsessed with that new Marvel series?   Daniel:   Absolutely.  Echoes of Tomorrow  is brilliant. The storyline’s insane, and the special effects are mind-blowing. You guys watching it?   Rajan:   Nah, I’m more of a  The Boys  man. Proper dark, satirical. Way more my vibe. Marvel’s getting a bit…predictable, don’t you think?   Liam:   See, I'm not bothered about all that superhero stuff. Give me a good fantasy novel any day. Something with dragons and ancient prophecies. My mum keeps trying to get me to read historical fiction, something a bit more…refined, she calls it.   Chloe:   Dragons, eh? Classic. You got a favourite?   Liam:   Always been partial to  Eragon.  Read it when I were a kid. Took me away from all the rain and mud of Yorkshire for a bit.   Daniel:    Eragon ! Good choice. Remember that? Used to read it on the bus to college, gettin’ all the sideways glances. Felt proper cool at the time. Speaking of the bus, have you guys seen the new bus routes? They’ve messed everything up. Now I have to walk twenty minutes to get to campus.
