Honestly, darling, this rain is relentless. Reminds me of a summer in Southend when I was a girl. Remember having to build a sandcastle with an umbrella? Utter madness. Sounds awful, Nan. Cambridge isn't much better, though. Feels like it's been drizzling non-stop for a week. Are you comfy? Want a cushion? Oh, I'm alright, love. Just a bit of a creak in the old bones, you know. So, tell me about this production controller lark. Sounds ever so important. Is it tiring? Not like my Brenda, bless her, who used to work at the biscuit factory. Standing on her feet all day, she was. It’s… alright. Busy. Lots of spreadsheets and making sure things get where they need to be, on time. It’s demanding, definitely, but I like the challenge. More interesting than I thought it would be, actually. And better than waitressing, that's for sure! Waitressing! Oh, you did that, didn't you? Briefly. Remember you saying it wasn’t for you? Good thing you didn't stick with it. You always were a bright one, you are. Speaking of things being on time, did you and Mark manage to book those tickets for "Wonka"? Yeah, we did! Saturday night. I think you’ll really like it, Nan. It's surprisingly charming, even though it's got Timothée Chalamet in it. Don’t let that put you off! Timothée who? Goodness, those names they give these actors! Charm though, you say? I’m always partial to a bit of charm. I saw "Singin' in the Rain" again last week. Still a classic, that one. Gene Kelly, now  he  had charm. Wonderful dancing. Oh, "Singin' in the Rain" is brilliant. We watched that at uni once, during a Film Studies night. It was hilarious. Did you catch the trailer for "Dune: Part Two"? I think Mark would love that. All those sci-fi explosions. "Dune"? Honestly, dear, all those space films. Too much roaring and flashing lights for me. Give me a good old musical any day. Or a nice drama. Something with a bit of heart. Remember "Brief Encounter"? That made me cry every time! You and your classics, Nan! I haven’t seen "Brief Encounter". Is it very…sad? Oh, it’s bittersweet, love. Beautifully sad. About forbidden love. Proper British heartbreak, you know. It’ll make you appreciate what you've got.

Honestly, this is  lovely , ANON. You’ve really made this place your own. So much better than that student hovel you had last year! Glad you like it! It’s taken a while, hasn't it? Still, much preferred to dragging boxes up three flights of stairs. How was the journey in from Essex? Nightmare as always, I presume? You have  no  idea. Seriously considering moving closer to London – maybe Notting Hill? Though the rent...  shudders . But tell me, how’s the magazine side of things going? Still battling deadlines every Tuesday? Pretty much! This month’s feature is all about sustainable fashion, which is interesting, but finding genuinely  new  angles is a killer. Keeps me on my toes, though. You seemed a bit distracted earlier. Anything up? Oh, yeah. The interview. For a potential promotion. It's horrifying, actually. They're thinking about making me Head of Research. Huge responsibility, and… well, presenting to the board? My palms are already sweating just thinking about it. Wow! Head of Research! That’s brilliant, isn’t it? A bit daunting, sure, but massive achievement. What’s the interview format like? Can you practice with me? I’m shockingly good at grilling people, apparently. You are! That’s precisely why I'm slightly terrified. It's a presentation, mostly. On how we can improve data analysis for upcoming language acquisition projects. Sounds dry when I say it out loud, doesn't it? Data… dry… like crackers. Good analogy, love. See? Even ANON agrees it needs some jazzing up. It  does  need jazzing up. I’m struggling to make it engaging. The board are all so… serious. Okay, right. Let's think. What's the  most  exciting part of your research? The part that genuinely gets you buzzing? Don’t start with the methodologies, start with the  impact . Hmm. Well, we're doing a project on how immersive gaming can improve fluency in endangered languages... that's pretty cool, I think. It feels more human than spreadsheets, at least.  That's  your hook! Talk about connecting languages to future generation, about preserving culture through cutting-edge tech! Data can be a tool, babe. A really  powerful  tool. You’re right. I was getting bogged down in the report. Thank you! Seriously, you’ve just helped me immensely. No worries! What about that spa day we were planning? To de-stress  after  the interview? ANON promised to book us in.

Right, this is a state, isn't it? Honestly, I don't know how you cope with this much washing. Back home, Mam used to have a rota, you know? Washin' day was sacred. Tuesdays were whites, Thursdays were colours… proper organised, she was. Well, Tuesdays and Thursdays didn't exactly lend themselves to postgrad life, did they? Between lectures, research, and trying to eat something that isn’t instant noodles… it’s a miracle I even remember to shower, let alone do laundry on a schedule. This machine's been playing up though, hasn't it? I swear it's judging my sock choices. Judgin' 'em, probably! It’s got a right face on it, that thing. I nearly chucked a pair of me favourite woolly socks in the other day and nearly had a heart attack when I realised. You know I cannae live without me woolly socks, especially wi' this Cambridge chill. Still, at least it  does  wash. Mam's had washing machines completely break down mid-cycle, leaving you wi' half-washed clothes floatin' about. Nightmare! Sounds ghastly. My mum’s washing machine once ate a bra. A whole bra! Just... vanished. She was convinced gnomes had taken it. Gnomes! Seriously? That's brilliant! Mam would’ve been lookin’ under the fridge for days, convinced it’d crawled under there. Listen, are you nearly done wi' that? I’m starving. I had a terrible day at work. The new project's a right mess, honestly. Keeps wantin' to change the whole methodology halfway through. Just about. It's lentil soup. Thought we could do with something warming. You had that awful presentation, right? How did it go, aside from the chaos you were mentioning? It went... fine. Everyone pretended to understand what I was sayin', but I could tell they were all lost. The head of research just kept noddin' and lookin' at his watch. It's a nightmare dealin' wi' people who don’t understand the value of proper research. You'd think people would appreciate the effort... Research can be a thankless task sometimes, can’t it? Keeps me in noodle territory, most days. You need a proper hug and a blanket. Maybe we could watch something daft tonight? Remember that series we were talkin' about, ‘Taskmaster’? Oh, aye! That’s perfect! I’ve been meaning to start it. It’s just… work’s been bleedin’ me dry.

Honestly, it’s just… shocking, isn’t it? The sheer scale of the VW emissions scandal. I’ve been transcribing some reports about it for work, and the detail is just mind-boggling. They were essentially cheating the tests, rigging the software. Aye, shocking alright. Didn't expect it from a company with such a good reputation. All that talk about 'think small' and being environmentally friendly... bit of a laugh now, innit? It is quite something, isn’t it? And the implications! Not just financially, but in terms of public trust… I mean, how can anyone trust a car manufacturer now? Especially when so many people relied on their vehicles. I did briefly consider a VW at one stage, but thankfully didn't go through with it. Exactly! My boyfriend’s dad had one, a Passat. He’s been so upset, feeling completely misled. He said he bought it for its fuel efficiency, and now he’s finding it’s practically the opposite. The compensation is… well, it’s something, but it hardly makes up for the betrayal, does it? Betrayal's the word. Proper taking the mickey, they were. Look, I’ve always said buying British is best. Keeps the money here, supports our own lads. Though even  they  ain’t blameless, mind you. Seen some dodgy practices in my time in development planning. It's tempting to go off-grid for a bit, isn't it? Tempting indeed. Though off-grid doesn’t quite pay the bills, does it, Michael? It’s this whole move up here, though, to Hunsonby, that’s really freeing me from all that stress, I think. Less to worry about. Though, house prices even  here  are ludicrous. Tell me about it! We were looking at buying a small cottage nearby, but the prices are ridiculous for what they are. People from down south snapping them up, I reckon. Holiday homes, rentals… driving up the cost for locals. That's the story of the country, Lizzie. Southerners rushing up here, thinking they've found some charming little idyll. Driving up prices, changing the character of places. Honestly, it's a bit galling to see. Though, I suppose, more money coming into the area can't be a bad thing for the local economy. It's a mixed blessing, isn't it? I remember when the market in Dublin was utterly insane, back in the boom.

Right then. That councillor, Mrs. Henderson… honestly. I could’ve told her that planning application stood no chance. Absolutely no chance. Wasting everyone’s time. Henderson, eh? Always was a bit… optimistic, wasn't she? Thought she could charm the planning committee into anything. Remember when she tried to get that miniature golf course built on Farmer Giles' field? Miniature golf. Honestly. The audacity. She’s got a talent for upsetting people, that woman. I overheard her at the shops last week, berating poor Mr. Davies about his overgrown hedge. Overgrown! It was a lovely, natural hedge, full of berries for the birds. It’s the principle of it, isn’t it? She seems to think she’s above everyone else. All that talk about ‘progress’ and ‘development’ when she’s just lining her pockets, I reckon. These housing developments… they're not for us, are they? Nope. Not for us. All these shiny new flats, priced out of reach for anyone who’s actually lived here their whole lives. Remember when this area was fields? Proper countryside. Now it’s all concrete and crammed houses. It's heartbreaking, really. They’re pulling down the old community hall to build yet another block of apartments. That hall held so many memories - my daughter's birthday parties, the WI meetings… Speaking of memories, did you hear anything back about that review of my pension? I sent off the form ages ago. Still nothing. The government, eh? They’ll keep you waiting till the cows come home. Likely lost it anyway. Happens all the time. My brother's still chasing his. I’m worried about you, Arthur. You need that extra bit to keep things ticking over. You know, I saw that advert for a computer training course at the library. Perhaps it could give you something to do, focus your mind? A computer course?! Good heavens, Margaret. I can barely work the telly! All those flashing lights and… and things. I'd be lost. I stick to what I know. Bridges and roads, not those infernal machines. He's got a point, Margaret. Arthur's a civil engineer. He built bridges. Building a computer's not his forte. Remember that time he tried to print out a map online? Nearly set the house on fire with the paper jam! Oh, don’t remind me! It was a sight. But seriously, Arthur, keeping your mind active is important.

"Did you guys see this? Another one! Honestly, it's ridiculous how quickly these things blow up." "What, another 'Is this cake?' thing?" "Worse, actually. It's about this influencer, right? Claiming evolution is a hoax. A hoax! Like, seriously?" He gestures emphatically with the newspaper. "People will believe anything they see on the internet these days. Remember that pigeon ‘wearing’ a tiny hat? Went viral for like, a week.” “Yeah, but this is different. This is actively spreading misinformation. And, like, a lot of people are buying into it. It’s kind of worrying.” "It's always the same pattern, isn't it? Someone says something outrageous, it gets shared a million times, and then suddenly you've got a whole community convinced it's true, despite what actual scientists say." "My mum was trying to explain it to her cousin. Said, 'But where did the dinosaurs go?' Like, it’s all explained! Fossils, carbon dating… everything." "It's the easy explanation thing, I reckon. Evolution’s complicated. It takes a bit of understanding. Dismissing it as ‘a hoax’ is just simpler, even if it's wrong." “It’s frustrating though, isn't it? It makes you question how people learn things. And how you can even have a proper debate about something if one side isn't even bothering with facts.” “Yeah. And it’s not just science. I was reading something about this YouTuber, she claimed feminism is a 'man-hating agenda'. Seriously! Like, what even? It’s about equality!” "It's always the same arguments, recycled and regurgitated. My sister gets it all the time. She studies gender studies and gets bombarded with stuff from random guys online.” "It's the outrage mindset, isn't it? People just want to get a rise out of you. Controversial opinions, no matter how inaccurate or harmful, get more views." "It reminds me of that discussion we had in Religious Studies last week about the burden of proof. The person making the claim should be the one providing the evidence, not expecting everyone else to disprove them." "Exactly! It's like, ‘prove me wrong’ instead of ‘here's my evidence.’ It's not a logical approach." “It’s also tied into this whole thing about… well, the algorithms, isn’t it? They just feed you what they think you want to see, even if it’s total nonsense.” "Totally. My cousin is constantly getting conspiracy theories pushed to him.

Honestly, it’s just lovely to be back here, isn't it? Feels like ages since we all properly sat down together. How’s everything, Mum? And Dad? Oh, it’s alright dear, alright. Bit stiff in the mornings, as always. The damp gets right into your bones, you know. But nothing serious, nothing to fuss about. How was work, love? You’re always dashing about, aren’t you? Dashing is the word for it! Things are absolutely manic at the moment. Big pitch coming up, so everyone’s on edge. The pressure's on, as usual. But the bonus will be worth it, I hope! Sarah, you look well! How's the cleaning going? Are you still doing the community centre? Still at it, love. Keeps me busy, though. The community centre’s good, loads of stories to hear, that is. Mrs. Higgins, you won’t believe, she's convinced the pigeons are spies! Proper little eccentric she is. Oh, and Dad’s complaining about his knee again. Same as always, innit? It’s not complaining, it's stating a fact! Nearly buckled it getting the new tyres on the Rover. Should've left it to the garage. Now I’m hobbling around like an old… Now, now, Arthur! Don't you go getting yourself in a state. A little bit of walking is good for you. Are you still seeing that acupuncturist? Seems to be working wonders for your back, or so you say. Aye, it’s doing something, that's for sure. The bloke’s got magic fingers, I tell you. Less aches, bits and pieces. But the wife still nags me to go for a proper check-up. The NHS waiting lists are horrendous, though. That’s so true. I've got a hospital appointment next month, for a follow-up about that shoulder operation. It's  mostly  better, but still twinges occasionally. They want to do some more scans... Just lovely. More waiting! Do you ever worry about infections, Mum? I've been reading about them. Oh, I worry about everything, darling. These tablets I'm on, they knock you about a bit, you know? Easy to catch something. Brenda down the road had a terrible chest infection last month. Missed a week of bingo! Absolute tragedy, she said. Brenda’s always got a tale to tell. Speaking of tales, remember when you, Arthur, tried to teach me rugby?

Right then, you two. I know this isn't the happiest story, but it’s incredibly important to understand. Are you both comfy? Yes, Miss Emily. Is it about superheroes? Does it have dragons? Not exactly superheroes or dragons, love. Though you could say Harriet Tubman was a superhero in her own way. This is about slavery, and it's a very, very long time ago, but sadly, it’s something that happened to lots of people. Do you know what slavery is, Rosie? No. Is it like when I have to tidy my toys? Not at all, sweetheart. It was much, much worse. It meant people were owned by other people. They were forced to work, often very hard, and they weren't free to go home or even choose what they wanted to do. They weren’t treated with kindness or respect. Can you imagine that, Finn? Not being allowed to choose what you do, or where you live? That's…rubbish. Daddy lets me choose which game to play sometimes. Exactly! And it’s rubbish. It’s wrong. Harriet Tubman lived in America, a long, long time ago – before your grandparents were even born. She was born into slavery herself but eventually escaped, and then she helped other people escape too. How did she do that? Did she have a magic wand? No magic wand, but immense bravery. She was part of something called the Underground Railroad. It wasn't a real railroad, silly! It was a network of people, secret routes and safe houses, that helped enslaved people escape to freedom. She was like a conductor, guiding them. Was it dangerous? Very dangerous, Finn. If the people who owned them caught them trying to escape, they would be punished terribly. Harriet had to be incredibly clever and brave to lead people to safety. She went back again and again, risking her own life. Were they scared? Oh, I'm sure they were, darling. Being ripped away from your family and forced to do things you don’t want to do is terrifying. But they were also desperate for freedom. They wanted to be treated with the dignity they deserved. It’s much like people feel when they are at war. What’s war, Miss Emily? War... well, it’s when countries or groups of people fight. It's a very sad thing, Finn. People get hurt, homes get destroyed, and families are torn apart.

Honestly, that “Love Island” is just utter tosh, isn’t it? Absolute drivel. But Mum's glued to it, and you, Amelia, you're always asking about it. I know, I know, Dad. It  is  a bit silly. But it’s a nice mindless distraction, you know? And the fashion is sometimes surprisingly good. Who’s your favourite this year, Gran? Oh, I don’t care who's favourite! It's all that sun and glamour. Makes me remember holidays in Majorca back in the day. David and I used to walk along the beach… such a lovely place. Such a shame about the prices now, though. Majorca’s gone completely over the top, hasn't it? You’re right, Dad. Remember when a week there was practically a bargain? Still, the biscuits are ready. Anyone fancy a ginger nut? I made them from scratch, you know, like my mum used to. Ginger nuts? Now you're talking! Thanks, Sarah. You’re always thinking of us. Though, speaking of thinking, did you see that article about the rising cost of… Dad, please, not politics again at lunchtime! I’m trying to relax. Did you hear that Piers Morgan’s doing another show? Piers Morgan? Good heavens, no. Won't be watching that. All shouting and nonsense. Can’t abide him. Too loud. Used to love a good chat show with Terry Wogan, mind you. Proper clever fella, he was. Made a brilliant cup of tea, apparently. I used to hear it when I worked at the old hotel. Terry Wogan… a proper legend. Speaking of legends, I saw a lovely piece about Dame Judi Dench the other day. Still going strong at her age, isn't she? Inspiring. Absolutely. A remarkable woman. Though, I wonder if she ever regrets some of the roles she’s taken on. You get to a certain age, and you start to reflect, don’t you? Like, did I do enough? Did I say enough? I think that's just a human thing, regardless of fame. I'm occasionally plagued by thoughts about career paths. Should I have gone into graphic design instead of copywriting? Oh, Amelia. You’re always overthinking. Copywriting suits you. You’ve been doing brilliantly. Remember that campaign you did for the local animal shelter? Amazing work. Thanks, Dad. They got so many adoptions. It was really rewarding. Speaking of animals, has Buster been behaving himself?

Right, nearly finished. Honestly, this dishwasher is a blessing and a curse. It does the washing, but then I’m still unloading it! Mummy! Are we going to read about dragons now? Not just yet, sweetheart. Mummy was just finishing up the dishes. But, you know what? We were talking about inventions the other day, weren’t we? Inventions? Like…magic? A bit like magic, actually, sometimes. Think about the dishwasher! Someone had to invent that, didn’t they? It wasn't always around. But what  did  people do before dishwashers? Wash everything by hand? Exactly! And that makes me think of someone else who invented something really important, ages ago. Have you ever heard of George Stephenson? George… who? Sounds like a grumpy old man. Well, he  was  an old man when he finished his work, but he wasn't grumpy, I don't think. He invented the railway engine! A train engine? Like the ones we saw last weekend at the museum? The really, really big ones? The very same! He didn't invent the  very first  train, but he made them much better and really started the whole railway system we know today. Can you imagine travelling long distances before trains? Taking weeks to go somewhere that now takes hours? Weeks?! That’s forever! I couldn't even stay away from Mummy for a week. Exactly! George Stephenson's trains made travel much faster and easier for everyone. He built the 'Rocket' – a really famous engine. It was incredibly fast for its time. Was he a wizard then? Because making things go that fast seems like wizardry! Not a wizard, darling. A brilliant engineer! He understood how steam could power a machine. It's a bit complicated to explain, but basically, he figured out how to build a strong engine that could pull carriages full of people and goods. How did he know how to do it? Did someone show him? He experimented a lot. He tried and tried again. Things didn’t always work the first time – or even the tenth time! But he kept on trying, and learning from his mistakes. That's important, you know. Even if you fail, you can still learn something. My dad used to say, “Failure is just learning in disguise.” That’s a good saying, Mummy. Like when I tried to build a tower of blocks and it fell over.

Right, so I’ve nearly got this Thai green curry sorted. Think it needs a bit more fish sauce, yeah? Definitely. You can't ever have too much fish sauce, Liam. It's the secret weapon, innit? Seriously though, smells incredible. Are you still obsessing over Words With Friends? My streak is properly getting demolished. Obsessing is a strong word. Just…strategically engaged. Brenda from Accounting is  ruthless . She knows how to block my vowels. It’s a personal attack, I swear. Brenda from Accounting? You're playing Words With Friends with someone from your office? That's... dedicated. I'm still trying to get my café's website looking less like a Geocities throwback. Absolute nightmare. Geocities, eh? Feels like a lifetime ago. You know, back in Australia, we were all about MySpace. Brutal. These rosemary potatoes are coming along nicely, by the way. A little salt, a little pepper... simple but effective. You’re always so calm, Finn. My sourdough starter nearly exploded this morning. Total disaster. It was everywhere! Oh, bless. Speaking of disasters, I had a nightmare with the health inspector last week. Turns out, because I use a  vintage  fridge, it doesn’t meet the current regulations. Apparently, antique appliances aren’t welcome in the food business. Seriously? A vintage fridge? That’s ridiculous. Sounds like they’re just trying to make life difficult. Yeah, bureaucracy bites, doesn't it? Reminds me of trying to get a license to operate a food truck in Melbourne. Paperwork, fees, inspections… it’s exhausting. Was it expensive to replace, Chloe? Thankfully, my cousin's dad is a refrigeration engineer. He got me a really good deal. But I'm considering hosting a little supper club on Sundays to bring in some extra cash while I'm dealing with it. Small group, set menu, nice atmosphere. You all in? Absolutely! Sounds amazing. I’ve been wanting to try something new. Maybe I can contribute a dessert? That exploding sourdough could be repurposed into something delicious, I’m sure. I'm in too. I could do some cocktails. Though Brenda from Accounting might criticize my shaking technique. Count me in. I can bring some extra herbs from the market. This rosemary is just the beginning. Always love a good culinary adventure. Say, Liam, don’t you have that friend, Ben, the lawyer? Is he still helping out with that ridiculous intellectual property dispute your friend had?

Honestly, this coronation chicken is exactly what I needed. Been a hectic morning already, hasn’t it? That new batch of GCSE papers needed collating  twice  – someone clearly wasn't paying attention when they printed. Tell me about it! The network was being particularly grumpy this morning too. A whole load of print jobs just vanishing into thin air. I think Mr. Henderson was about to have a full-blown meltdown. He’s got a deadline on those student prospectuses, you know. Oh, poor Henderson. He does put immense pressure on himself. It’s a wonder he doesn't age ten years a week. Are the prospectuses looking good this year though? I saw a sneak peek earlier, the photography is lovely. Yeah, they’re fantastic. We even managed to get some decent shots of the robotics club – that was a challenge, getting them to cooperate! What about your kids? Have they broken up for half term yet? Not quite, thankfully. Another week until the blessed relief. Little Emily wants to build a full-sized fairy house in the garden – apparently, it needs a moat. A moat! In our postage-stamp-sized garden. It’s going to be... interesting. How's Anya settled in at primary school? She’s doing really well, actually! She's made loads of friends. It’s just… the homework. Honestly, it’s a battle every evening. Reading schemes, maths worksheets, everything’s in English, of course. It's hard on her sometimes, I think. It is, isn't it? The transition can be tough. Mine were the same, especially with phonics. Did you look into getting any extra support for her through the school? They’re usually pretty good at identifying any potential issues. I have, but they said she’s progressing normally, just…a bit slow. But I do think sometimes it’s the language barrier and the sheer volume. Do you ever feel swamped with paperwork at work? Swamped is putting it mildly! It’s a constant juggle, especially with the cover rota. Trying to find qualified staff to fill the gaps is like pulling teeth sometimes. I often wish I had more time for my pottery. Remember I showed you some of my pieces last year? Oh, yes! The little hedgehogs! They were so cute. You're so talented. I've been meaning to get back into my photography. I used to spend ages editing photos in university.

Right then, are we all strapped in properly? Honestly, this Preston traffic is a right nightmare. Shoulda left earlier. Yep, all good here, Dad. Just wish we’d gone to Mothercare on Saturday, like you said we would. Well, Saturday was a bit mad wasn’t it, love? Remember that farmer's market? Couldn’t even get near the fruit stall. Besides, we needed to get the cot bedding anyway, right? Think they had a few new colours in. Yeah, but now we're stuck in this crawl, and I've got that essay to finish for college. It’s due Monday, and Mrs. Davies is being extra strict this year. College, eh? What's the essay on this time, love? Something historical, I bet. You always did like your history. Wish I'd done a degree, instead of just… well, customer service. Never regretted it  entirely , but… Don’t be like that, Steven. You’ve always been the rock of this family. Speaking of families, did the surveyor make any interesting observations about the damp in the downstairs bathroom? They said it's ‘manageable’… which translates to ‘might cost a pretty penny and a bit of hassle’ in surveyor-speak. Apparently, that old Victorian brickwork doesn't breathe very well. We need to get someone in to look at the pointing, and potentially consider some damp-proofing. Ugh, more money, more hassle. Can’t we just slap some wallpaper on it? Wallpaper won't fix damp, lass! You'll just be peeling it off in a few years, along with chunks of plaster. Reminds me of Gran's house, always peeling wallpaper. She used to say, "A bit of Sellotape fixes everything!" Bless her. Gran was a legend. Remember her crocheted blankets? The one with the little sheep? I used to drag that thing everywhere when I was little. Still got it, actually. Yeah! And you used to make me wear it, even in summer. You said it was 'lucky'. It was! It brought me good luck. I wonder if Mothercare have any nice knitted blankets now. Something soft for the baby. They probably do. Reckon we should stop for some water too? Been a bit parched since we left. This heat's doing nowt for the traffic either. Definitely water. And maybe a packet of those chocolate buttons? I’m starving. College life, you know. Ramen noodles and instant coffee, mostly.

Honestly, this new update for 'Aetherium Knights' is a complete mess. They've totally broken the balance. The new mage class is ridiculously overpowered. Overpowered? Like, seriously unbalanced? My Valkyrie is useless now. I spent ages leveling her up! Oh, that game again? You two get so absorbed in that thing. What’s a ‘Valkyrie’ anyway? Sounds… dramatic. It’s a warrior class, Nan. She’s got a big axe and a shield and does a lot of damage. But now, apparently, mages can just… zap everything and everyone. Exactly! And they've introduced this ridiculous resource system too. It's all about 'mana wells' now and you have to constantly be farming them. It’s just tedious! It feels like they’re trying to push people towards microtransactions. Microtransactions? More money grabbing, then? Honestly, modern technology... It’s all designed to take your pennies, isn’t it? Remember when Christmas was about, you know, Christmas? Not clicking on things to buy virtual bells and whistles? Well, it  is  a bit sad, isn't it? Like, I was really enjoying it, and now it’s just a chore to play. I’m starting to feel a bit… down about it. It's weird, isn't it? How a game can make you feel that way. It’s psychology, actually. Dopamine loops and reward systems. The initial enjoyment triggers a release, and when that's disrupted, you can feel a bit… disappointed. It’s why companies intentionally make games addictive. Addictive. Sounds about right. You kids and your screens. Still, feeling down about a  game ? You should try Christmas shopping.  That's  a truly harrowing experience. Remember that awful queue at Argos last year? Practically a riot! That was mad! But I'm serious. It’s like… the anticipation of playing was better than the actual playing now. It’s kind of a bummer. Maybe I should just quit. Don’t quit entirely! There’s a community forum for the game. I've been trying to rally people to complain to the developers. Maybe we can get them to revert some of the changes. Good for you, love. Standing up for yourselves. You remind me of me, fighting for decent bus fares in Liverpool back in the day. Though I doubt anyone will listen to you online. Maybe not. Still, it’s worth a try. Have you been practicing your knitting, Nan?

Right, so, diamonds are obviously the best, aren't they? Everyone says so. But I was thinking… Netherite. It’s so much rarer, and the protection it gives… honestly, it feels like cheating! Diamonds are sparkly! But Netherite's purple! Purple is better. Netherite’s  stronger ! I used it to make my dragon’s armour. He fought a Wither! He did a fantastic job, didn’t he? A Wither's no small feat. Though, remember what Grandma Elsie always said, a good shield, even made of iron, is worth more than a fancy sword. Grandma Elsie? Did she fight a Wither too? Not a Wither, love. She fought squirrels in her garden for the best tomatoes. Said they were strategic enemies. Speaking of strong… what about materials  outside  of Minecraft? Like, in real life? Did you know silk used to be so valuable they were practically worshipped in ancient China? Worshipped? Like, gave it flowers? Something like that! Only really important nobles could wear it. It was a sign of incredible wealth and power. It’s amazing, isn’t it, how things we take for granted - like cotton even - have such a crazy history? What about wool? I like woolly jumpers. They’re cozy. Absolutely! Wool's brilliant. Sheep are pretty clever, you know, producing all that stuff. Better than digging for diamonds, I’d say! Though, I need to remember to order some more vitamin D for you two. It’s getting a bit gloomy outside, and you need to stay strong for all your Minecraft adventures. Are vitamins like iron armour? They keep you strong? A bit like that, yes. They help your bodies work properly, like making sure you've got enough energy to build amazing things and fight scary monsters. Like this! I’m building a castle! It needs a moat! And a dragon! A brilliant castle. Absolutely needs a dragon. And what about the materials for your castle? Stone, obviously, but any special accents? I'm going to use redstone for a secret passage! And… and I’m making up a legend about it! Oh, do tell! A legend? That sounds wonderful. Okay. Long ago, there was a wizard who lived in the castle, and he  loved  redstone. He used it to power all his spells, but one day, a sneaky goblin stole his best redstone crystal! So, the wizard built a secret passage, lined with redstone, to trap the goblin.

Honestly, Liam, I'm still reeling from that documentary last night. About, you know… the safeguarding thing at the youth club. Gut-wrenching. Aye, it were. Proper sickenin’. I switched off about halfway through, couldn't hardly watch it. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About kids and trustin’ people. It does. My mum volunteers there, you know. She’s been doin’ it for ages. Seems daft to even question it now, but… you can’t be too careful, can you? Did you hear about little Thomas? Thomas Miller? Yeah, saw somethin’ about it on the news. Dreadful. Right on our doorstep, isn't it? Makes you look at people differently, even folk you’ve known for years. Exactly! It’s unsettling. Anyway, trying to forget about that horrifyingness, what have you been up to with the guitar? You said you were trying to learn “Smells Like Teen Spirit”? Yeah! Progress is slow, mind. My fingers are bleedin’ somethin’ awful. But it’s gettin’ there. Found a chord diagram online, and I think I’ve finally got the intro down. Sounds a bit… wonky still, but better than nothin’. Wonky's good! That's progress. Remember when you tried to play "Wonderwall" and it sounded like a strangled cat? Don’t remind me! Dad nearly threw his telly remote. He’s got no ear for rock music, that man. He just wants me playin’ folk songs and singin’ about sheep. Ha! Classic Dad. Still, sheep songs are nice for a change. Speaking of music, have you been listenin’ to 'The Crimson Echoes' new single? Nah, haven’t had a chance. Are they good? They've gone a bit… different haven’t they? From their earlier stuff. I liked their first album, loads. They are. It's a bit more atmospheric, less of the shouty guitar stuff. I reckon they're experimentin’. Might be a grower, you know? It took me a few listens, but I’m gettin’ into it now. What else have you been doin' recently? Anything besides fightin’ with your fingers on that guitar? Not much, really. Trying to finish that essay on Victorian literature. Absolute killer. Honestly, the stuff’s drier than the Sahara Desert. I’d rather be learning guitar solos. Have you started your project yet? The one on post-modern architecture? Just started! It's… daunting. So many buildings to choose from! I was thinkin’ about the Hepworth Gallery in Wakefield, but it feels a bit obvious, doesn't it?

Seriously, another half-term already? It feels like we just got back from Christmas. This EPQ is eating my life. Tell me about it. I'm drowning in research for mine. Trying to justify why the history of juggling is… significant. Who knew it was so complicated? Juggling’s fascinating actually. It's about coordination, rhythm, cultural significance... loads of stuff you can connect. You're being dramatic, Leo. It’s half-term, relax! Easy for you to say, Chloe. You’re doing something seemingly straightforward, right? What is it again? The impact of street art on gentrification? Pretty much. It’s trickier than it sounds, actually. Finding reliable sources is a nightmare. And the ethical stuff... it's a bit heavy. Ethical? Juggling just requires balls, doesn't it? Though, thinking about it, historically, circus performers were pretty exploited… there's a poverty angle there, isn’t there? Access to training, fair wages… See? Everything connects! You’re giving me ideas for my conclusion. It’s about the impact of globalisation on artisanal crafts, and I can definitely link it to the precariousness of traditional skills. But I'm currently stressed about finding a decent cafe for a break. I'm starving. There’s that little place just around the corner, Bean There. They do amazing veggie wraps. I could go for one. I'm trying to cut down on meat. Veggie? Seriously? You know I’m trying to get you into a proper Sunday roast, Chloe. Full English, the works. Don’t even. My mum’s a vegetarian, used to drag me to protests against farming. I'm pretty set in my ways. Remember that trip to Montenegro last summer? All that grilled meat… my face was a picture of polite suffering. Montenegro was amazing though! Didn’t realise how gorgeous it was. Those beaches… and the… the… what were those little pastries they sold everywhere?  Burek ! You’re thinking of  burek . Cheese, meat, spinach… Meat, Leo. Always meat with you. Makes me think, have you guys thought about where you want to apply to uni? I'm leaning towards Bristol. They have a really good sociology course. I’m still oscillating between Oxford and Cambridge. The humanities departments are ridiculous. I’m trying not to think about it too much, to be honest. It’s just… a lot of pressure. My parents are constantly asking. They keep mentioning the postcode factor.

Honestly, this fridge is a joke. My yogurt's gone all weird again. Like, actively weird. Aw, not again, Liam! You'd think they'd fix these things. Lancaster Uni’s supposed to be top-notch, innit? Feels more like a glorified boarding school sometimes. Tell me about it! My radiator's been clanking all day. Sounds like a dying robot. Landlord’s left a message saying he'll "get to it eventually." Eventually could be Christmas, for all we know. Well, at least you have radiators. My room is perpetually Arctic. I'm pretty sure I saw frost on my window this morning. Right near the bottom. Right, that’s grim. Frost! I'm telling you, I’m investing in a hot water bottle for life. Still, beats splitting bills with my mum, I suppose. She’s been on about my spending habits again. Oh, the classic mum lecture? What’d she say this time? Something about needing to budget for a house and a cat when I graduate? Pretty much! Said I was “being frivolous” buying a new swimsuit for Cornwall next week. Like, hello? Sunshine, sand, a decent pasty… it’s practically a vital part of my mental health. Cornwall's nice. I went there last summer. Got stung by a jellyfish. It was awful. Ouch! That doesn’t sound ideal. Listen, speaking of families, my auntie Priya just messaged me. Apparently, my cousin Rohan’s getting married! Blimey, Rohan? I thought he was still chasing girls and trying to learn the guitar. Apparently, he met someone at Uni. A girl called Chloe. Turns out Chloe's a doctor. My mum’s already planning the whole wedding, naturally. It'll be massive. Like, peacock feathers and Bollywood dancing massive. Oh, wow! That’s proper exciting for him. Rohan always seemed a bit... chaotic. A doctor, eh? That's a whole new level. Will there be a buffet? Because I’m in if there’s a buffet. Definitely a buffet, Liam. Probably ten different food stations. My mum’s already harassing me for addresses to send out invites. She wants me to make sure everyone’s coming. Your mum’s the best. Always organising. So, Chloe... what’s the gossip? Is she nice? Does she like curry? Essential questions. That's what I was trying to find out! Auntie Priya was being all cryptic. Said she's “lovely, very intelligent, and a great cook.”

Honestly, Mum, this whole Christmas thing is just… a lot, isn't it? Especially with little Leo running around, wanting to decorate the tree before Halloween’s even over. Oh, you’re telling me! Remember when you were that age, darling? You’d be covered in tinsel and demanding carols in July. It’s wonderful, though, isn’t it? The excitement. It’s a bit chaotic, certainly, but it’s… Christmas. Chaotic is an understatement. I’m trying to be organised this year, though. I've actually made a list – colour-coded, naturally. Presents, food, decorations… It's grown to a document longer than my TEFL lesson plans. Colour-coded! Oh, you always were a practical one. Though, you know, sometimes the best Christmases are the ones where absolutely nothing goes according to plan. Remember that year with Uncle Barry and the exploding mince pies? Don't remind me! The kitchen looked like a bomb had gone off. And Aunt Carol was furious. She took  hours  to make those mince pies. She did, didn't she? But Barry was mortified, and everyone was laughing. That’s what Christmas is about, really – making memories, even the messy ones. I'm thinking of suggesting we keep some of that chaos this year. Less pressure, more fun. That sounds lovely, actually. I’ve been trying to channel this ‘perfect Christmas’ image, feeling like I need to tick every box. But Leo doesn’t care about perfectly arranged crackers, does he? He just wants to be surrounded by people he loves. Precisely. Speaking of people, how's Mrs. Henderson doing? I saw her at the farmer's market last week, looking a bit down. Said her arthritis was playing up. Oh, bless her. I pop in every week with a little something. She's been feeling lonely since George passed. I'm taking her over for Christmas dinner this year. It'll be good for her, and Leo adores her stories. He’s obsessed with her tales of growing up in the fifties. That's lovely, darling. Really lovely. You’re a good friend. It's wonderful that you're incorporating her into the family. It feels like she's always been part of our world. She has been, hasn’t she? She was practically a second mum to me when I was little. I remember she used to give me a wee Welsh cake every Saturday after my ballet lessons.

Wow, Crayford hasn’t changed  that  much, has it? Still all the same terraced houses. Feels…surreal being back, to be honest. Two years is a long time. Welcome home, then! Surreal for me too, seeing you all grown up. You were just a kid last time you were in this car. Bit heavier now, aren’t we? Just kidding! You look good. Really good. Thanks, Dad. Yeah, well, teaching twenty-odd teenagers all day does something to your metabolism, I suppose. All that pizza and sugary drinks they try and bribe me with. Speaking of…Have you seen the new Costa that's opened up near the station? It's completely taken over. Costa? Fancy. Used to be a decent little bakery there, Mrs. Patel's. She made the best Eccles cakes. Everything's just getting more…corporate, isn’t it? Still, at least they’re finally fixed that speed camera on the A2. Nearly lost my license a couple of times because of that thing. Seriously? I completely missed that. You’d think they’d warn people! So, how's work going? Still dealing with the joys of customer complaints? Same old, same old. People shouting about late deliveries and wrong orders. Keeps me on my toes, I suppose. Had a nasty bout of flu last week though, knocked me for six. Nearly called in sick, but couldn't be bothered to explain it all. How's the teaching going? Brighton must be a different world, eh? It is. Completely. Much more…alternative, let's say. The students are great, actually. Really diverse bunch. We're planning a massive board game night next week – Settlers of Catan mainly, it's become surprisingly popular. Remember how we used to play Monopoly for hours when I was little? Blimey, yes! You'd always try and bankrupt me. Those were the days. Remember that Game of Thrones marathon we had? We were arguing about who would sit on the Iron Throne right up until three in the morning. Oh god, those were some intense nights. Still can't believe how good that show was. Although, the ending…let's not go there. Anyway, about Brighton…I was thinking, once we’ve sorted out the logistics of you moving down, we could all go back to Tanzania. Remember that trip? Tanzania! Goodness, that feels like a lifetime ago. The Serengeti…the markets…the food!

Honestly, the lighting in that Anthropologie was  criminal . I went in for a new cushion cover, came out feeling like I needed sunglasses. And they’ve rearranged everything again! It's like a retail obstacle course now. Anthropologie, eh? You and your cushions. They  do  have a knack for shifting things around just to confuse you. Did you find anything vaguely resembling what you wanted? Almost. I saw a gorgeous velvet one, deep teal, but it was £65! For a cushion cover! I nearly choked on my own laughter. I mean, I appreciate the craftsmanship, but…still. Sixty-five pounds? That’s…ambitious. Maybe you could attempt to make one? You're surprisingly crafty when you put your mind to it. Remember that macrame plant hanger you did? Don't remind me. It looked like a spider had exploded. Thankfully, we gave it to Aunt Mildred. She seemed to like it. Anyway, less about cushions, more about your day. You looked a bit frazzled when you got in. Big class? Bigger than usual. We had that group of international students who are… enthusiastic. They’re incredibly keen, bless them, but their understanding of post-structuralism occasionally requires a significant amount of, shall we say, clarification. I spent most of the hour gently steering them away from completely wild interpretations of Derrida. It was exhausting. Oh, the joy of trying to explain notoriously obscure theories to people who haven't had the benefit of years of academic indoctrination. It's a superpower, really. Did you manage to keep the conversation on track? Eventually. I think. I ended up using a very convoluted analogy involving a broken biscuit. Apparently, that resonated. I felt a bit silly, but hey, they got it. Speaking of resonating, I’ve been listening to that new Phoebe Bridgers album. What do you think? Oh,  Punisher ! It’s exquisite. Absolutely gut-wrenching, but exquisitely beautiful. I’ve had it on repeat all week. The production is just…perfect. That single guitar line in "Kyoto" gives me chills every time. She's something special. Agree completely. It’s the kind of album you need to listen to when you’re feeling a bit… introspective. Which, clearly, I was after wrestling with post-structuralism all afternoon. I was thinking we might need to go out for dinner tomorrow evening to decompress. Somewhere with decent wine and less existential dread, perhaps? Sounds like a plan.

Honestly, David, I’m starting to think this lentil stew will be the only thing finished tonight at this rate. The beanbag is taunting me. It’s just… a pile of yarn currently. A very colourful, slightly lumpy pile of yarn. Well, Rome wasn’t built in a day, love. And lentil stew  is  essential sustenance for a serious knitting project. Are you making progress on the main body at least? I thought you said you’d got the first couple of rows done. I did, briefly. But then I realised I’d miscalculated the tension. It’s going to end up a bean  chair  at the rate things are going! I’m going to have to frog it all, which is the most depressing part of knitting, you know? Unravelling hours of work. Depressing, but necessary. Better to fix it now than have a misshapen monstrosity in the living room. Speaking of which, have you had a chance to look at that new shower curtain I ordered? Remind me. The… geometric one? Honestly, I’m having serious second thoughts. It’s very… bold. Bold is good! It'll liven the bathroom up a bit. It’s been that beige floral thing for far too long. Remember when ANON insisted on that? Said it reminded her of her grandmother’s guest room. Oh, goodness, yes! And we all pretended we loved it to avoid a full-blown debate. But honestly, David, beige florals in a bathroom? It needs a bit of…oomph. Exactly! And the geometric pattern is surprisingly calming. It’s not garish, just… modern. Think of it as a visual palate cleanser after a long shower. I suppose. It’s just… everything feels so connected now, doesn't it? The bathroom needs a new curtain, and suddenly I’m thinking about new towels, and then maybe a different mirror… and then I'm back to the beanbag, feeling overwhelmed. It's a domino effect of home improvement. It is, isn't it? It's the price of having a home, I guess. It needs constant tending. Though, you’re doing a admirable job. Are you going to add any more carrots to that stew? It looks a little bare. Definitely need more carrots. And maybe some chopped celery. You know, I was thinking… while trying to wrestle with that beanbag… perhaps we should just repaint the bathroom altogether? Something light and airy.

Honestly, I still can’t quite believe it, can you? After all this time – decades, really – they’re finally doing something about the housing situation for folks like us. A new development down by the river, they're saying, specifically for retired, low-income residents. “Specifically,” she says. That’s what they always say, innit? Sounds a bit too good to be true, Margaret. Remember that promise about the new bus route? Never materialised, did it? Spent a whole year waiting for that blasted bus. Don't be so pessimistic, Arthur. This feels different. I spoke to Councillor Davies yesterday, had a brief chat. He seemed genuinely enthusiastic. Apparently, there's a decent budget allocated, and the plans are quite well thought out – accessible, green spaces, support services… the whole lot. Well, that  is  encouraging, John. Accessibility is vital. My knees aren't what they used to be, you know. Being able to get about without too much trouble would be a blessing. And a garden... a little patch of my own! I miss having roses, terribly. Roses, eh? Fancy that. I’d be happy with a bit of lawn, somewhere to put the deckchair. Being cooped up in this little flat… it’s not doing my joints any good, that’s for sure. Damp gets right in them. The main thing is, it’s a chance for a fresh start, isn't it? No more worrying about escalating rent, no more feeling like a burden. I know it’s been tough, both of you. It has. Though I’ve always enjoyed looking after the children, even when it was all a bit much. But the solitary nature of it, you know? Getting old on your own... It’s hard. Aye. Hard. . I’ve just... I’ve just not been one for change, I suppose. Been here for forty years now, in this flat. Plenty of memories. Mostly not good ones, mind you. I understand, Arthur. But memories are just that – memories. This is about building new ones. A place where you can relax, have some peace and quiet, and actually enjoy your retirement. Think of all the walks you could take along the river! He’s right, Arthur. No more worrying about the heating bill, no more struggling to reach the top shelves. We could even have a little book club, maybe? I’ve always fancied that. A book club?

Honestly, this Christmas shopping is mental. Everyone's just panic-buying, aren't they? I spent ages in town today, and it was like Black Friday all over again. Tell me about it, love. I popped into Boots for a bit, just to grab some bits for mum, and the queue was snaking halfway down the street. Honestly, makes you wonder why we don’t just buy vouchers. Vouchers are a cop-out, Sarah. Christmas is about giving something  thoughtful . Something that shows you've put in a bit of effort. Besides, the look on their faces when they unwrap it… that's priceless. Effort is right, John. Though I'm half-tempted to just get everyone experiences this year. Like, day trips. Or a pottery painting session. Less clutter, you know? Ooh, I like that! We could do a Christmas market! There's a lovely one in Canterbury, apparently. Canterbury? Bit of a trek, isn’t it? Especially with the traffic. And parking... don’t even get me started. Well, we could always use the train. Less hassle. But Canterbury's getting very popular. It’ll be rammed, I reckon. True, but it would be festive. Thinking about it, a trip somewhere different would be nice. We always do the same thing – Mum's roast, endless board games… It's comforting, though. Familiar. Exactly! Keeps things nice and… well, sane. I'm not sure I’m up for a huge adventure this year. I’ve been working ridiculous hours at the ward – three extra shifts last month alone. My feet are killing me. You deserve a break, love. A proper one. Perhaps we could just do something smaller, closer to home. A nice pub lunch somewhere? A pub lunch sounds good. Less… chaotic. We could go to The Bull in Wye. They do a great Sunday roast, and it’s only a short drive. The Bull's nice. Remember last year when the power went out and we ended up singing Christmas carols by candlelight? That was a right laugh! Oh, goodness. Absolutely bonkers. The landlord was trying to stop us, bless him. Said we were disturbing the neighbours. He was a grumpy one, wasn't he? Still, it  was  memorable. Speaking of memorable, have you all seen the price of petrol lately? Highway robbery, I tell you. I filled up yesterday, and it cost me a fortune. Don't remind me!

Honestly, this is just breathtaking, isn’t it? I still can’t quite believe we’re here. Northern Cyprus – it feels so… removed from everything. Aye, it is. Quiet, that's what it is. A world away from Bushey, that's for sure. Didn't expect to find myself this far out, to be honest. The adverts made it sound like paradise, and well...it's got the weather for it. Well, the weather  is  undeniably lovely. And the people are so welcoming. I was chatting to Eleni at the bakery yesterday – she insisted I try her boureki. Have you tried it yet? Boureki? Sounds foreign. Haven't been out much since we arrived. Been trying to... settle in, you know? It's a bit overwhelming, all this newness. I understand. It absolutely can be. I felt a bit adrift the first few days. What were you doing before you came here, if you don’t mind me asking? Oh, not much really. Never had a proper job, to be truthful. Supported by... well, let's just say I’ve had some assistance over the years. Always dreamed of somewhere warm, though. Somewhere peaceful. This seemed… doable, with the right help. What about you? You seem awfully… put-together, for someone new to the area. Thank you. It's a bit of a facade, I assure you! I'm a teacher. I used to teach primary school in Dorchester. Lovely place, but... well, let's just say bureaucracy and staffing shortages were rather wearing me down. Looking for a bit of a change, a fresh start. My husband, David, he’s convinced it's the best thing we’ve ever done. He's off exploring some ancient ruins today – obsessed with the Roman period, he is. Romans, eh? They were good builders, I’ll give ‘em that. Built some proper roads. You know, they say the Romans were the first to invent central heating. Really? That’s fascinating! I hadn't heard that. Do you know much about Roman history, then? A bit. Read a few books. Always been interested in history, you see. Never got the chance to study it properly, though. Life got in the way. Still, wishing I had now, looking at all these old stones. I can imagine! So, you've been here a while then? Longer than us, at least? Oh, a few months now. Coming up to six, I think.

Honestly, I don’t think I’ve ever breathed air this… thick. It clings to your throat, doesn't it? Even with the mask. It does. I’m starting to think these masks aren’t doing nearly enough. Remember when we first came here, and I thought it was just a bit of seasonal smog? I was so naïve. Naïve is a kind word. I was actively optimistic. Now, I just feel… resigned. Did you manage to get through to Professor Chen about the revised syllabus for next term? Almost. He seemed receptive to the changes I suggested regarding the Contemporary Chinese Literature module, particularly the inclusion of more female authors. But then he launched into a twenty-minute explanation of why traditional Marxist interpretations are still vitally important. It was exhausting. Oh, Chen. Always a pleasure. You’d think after five years here, we'd be used to it. Still, it’s good you're pushing for those changes. The students deserve a more balanced view. Sarah mentioned in her email she’s struggling to find relevant female perspectives – it’s heartbreaking. Exactly! And she’s a brilliant student. It shouldn’t be this difficult. I showed him a few articles I’d found; he claimed the ‘cultural context’ was irrelevant. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if he’s purposely trying to be obtuse. Did you have any success with the postgraduate applications? A little. I finally managed to convince Mrs. Li to look at the portfolios properly. She'd initially dismissed them as "too experimental," but after I pointed out the connection to early modernist styles, she seemed to soften. I’ve got two promising candidates for next year’s cohort – one’s a brilliant sculptor from Chongqing, the other’s a digital artist. That’s fantastic! We really need to bring in some fresh blood. The department’s been feeling a little… stagnant lately. I miss proper debate. Back in London, even just grabbing a coffee with Giles and Anna would spark some ridiculous intellectual firestorm. Remember that time Giles started arguing about the semiotics of breakfast cereal? I swear, I nearly choked on my bagel. I miss them too. Have you heard from Emily? It feels like ages since she was last in touch. I messaged her last week. She's swamped with the wedding preparations. Apparently, her mother's been trying to convince her to wear a traditional Mongolian gown.

Right, I’m thinking we need a bit more rosemary in this. Don’t you think, David? It’ll give the chicken a lovely flavour. Mmm, could do. Though I think it’s already smelling rather nice, Sarah. You've been busy, haven't you? That's a mountain of potatoes you’ve got there. It does smell good, actually. What are we having exactly? And is there going to be room for dessert? I'm starving. Roast chicken, roast potatoes, carrots, and peas. And yes, there  will  be room for dessert. I’m making that apple crumble you like, Chloe. Remember when we all tried to make it last year and it ended up looking like a volcanic eruption? Don’t remind me! That was a disaster. You nearly set off the smoke alarm, Chloe. Thankfully Sarah managed to salvage it. It was epic! Honestly, my hair was covered in flour. But it tasted…interesting. This year will be better, right? You've got a new recipe? Yes, I’ve found a proper one this time. Less experimentation, more following instructions. And David, have you seen the photos from Aunt Mary’s birthday? I put them on the shared drive. Not yet, no. Been a bit busy sorting out those reports for the board meeting. Dreadful business, those meetings. Always so much jargon. I swear, sometimes I think they deliberately try to confuse people. Tell me about it. At least Aunt Mary looked happy. She seemed to have a lovely time. Though, Uncle George looked a bit lost, bless him. I saw them! They’re brilliant. Aunt Mary looks amazing, doesn't she? And someone managed to catch Uncle George trying to eat a whole sausage roll in one go! Oh, he’s a character, that one. Always has been. Reminds me of me when I was a lad, gobbling down anything I could get my hands on. Speaking of eating, do you think we should set the table now? Chloe, could you pop the napkins and cutlery out? Sure thing. So, what are you both up to tomorrow? Any plans? I was thinking of heading into London for a bit. Maybe check out that new exhibition at the Tate. Tomorrow? I’m planning on tackling the overgrown roses in the garden. They're a menace. And then, after that, I might just collapse in front of the telly. There's that new detective series everyone’s talking about – “Shadows of the Past”, or something like that.

Right, so that new bus route… honestly, it’s a disaster. They’ve cut the 7 every Saturday morning! Every Saturday! How am I supposed to get to the Press bookshop now? It's the only place I can reliably find those niche linguistics journals. You’re still on about the bus route? We talked about this. It’s efficiency, apparently. The council claims hardly anyone uses it on Saturdays. Hardly anyone? Loads o’ folks use it! Students going to the market, people visiting family… and me! I'm trying to keep up with current research, like. It's not like Sunderland had a thriving scholarly bookshop on every corner, you know. I’m grateful for the Press one. I know, I know. I just… they did a study. Apparently, the numbers don't support your argument. Besides, aren't you close to the train station anyway? You could just get the train into town. The train is extortionate! Honestly, it’s daylight robbery. So, about that student protester outside the Senate House yesterday... did you see her? The one with the banner? Vaguely. I was rushing to a meeting. Something about tuition fees, I presume? Cambridge seems to have a permanent student protest going on. Aye, she was passionate, though. Proper railing against the whole system. Reminded me a bit of the demos back home, back in the day. Less… polished, maybe, than some of the Cambridge lot. All very polite arguments and academic papers. Cambridge students do like to intellectualize things. It’s just the environment, I suppose. It's a research university, after all. A lot more focused on academic rigor. Different from, say, a polytechnic where you might find a more visceral, less theoretical approach to protest. That’s puttin' it politely. It's a bit stuffy sometimes, isn’t it? I mean, back at Sunderland University… it was a lot more… real, you know? People worked harder, but it felt less about personal prestige and more about actually  doing  something. Perhaps. I always felt that's the downside of a prestigious institution. The pressure to conform, to maintain the reputation... It can stifle a certain kind of… directness. Plus, everyone here is so intensely focused on their own field. It's hard to get a broader perspective. Exactly! I was talking to Sarah from the linguistics department the other day. She’s doing her PhD on… wait for it… the semiotics of eighteenth-century gardening.

Honestly, the portion sizes here are ridiculous! I swear, this ploughman's lunch could feed a small family. I'm going to be rolling home. Tell me about it. I specifically asked for “light” on the chips, and they gave me a mountain. Though, chips are chips, aren't they? I’ll probably still eat them. You’ve seen me. It's a Cumbrian tradition, I suspect. Everything comes in larger quantities. You'd think they were trying to compensate for something… like the weather! Speaking of something, did you hear back from Liam about visiting next month? The kids are beside themselves waiting to see him. Not yet. His work is absolutely manic at the moment. Apparently, the new quarterly reports are a nightmare. He did send a quick text saying he'd call later tonight, though. Fingers crossed. Poor Liam. It just doesn't seem fair, does it? He's working himself ragged. Children need their fathers, especially at that age. Little Finn wants Liam to teach him to build a birdhouse. It’s heartbreaking he can’t. Finn is obsessed with birds now. He even named them all. There's Reginald, Penelope, Bartholomew... it’s quite charming, actually. What's Maisie into these days? Still the ballet? Still the ballet! She’s even talking about auditioning for a summer performance. I’m slightly terrified. She’s got the passion, definitely, but the competitiveness… it seems a bit much for a nine-year-old. Oh, children and ambition. A dangerous combination! But do let her try, Sarah. Let her experience it. Even if she doesn't get in, the disappointment will be a lesson in itself. When I was teaching, I always used to tell my students, the journey is more important than the destination, even if it sounds cliché. That’s wonderful advice, Mary. It’s just… I worry. Isn't that what mothers do? I’m also trying to convince David to start learning some Italian. We’re planning that trip to Tuscany next year, and no amount of phrasebooks will prepare him for real conversation. Oh, God, David and languages. That's a hopeless cause, isn't it? Remember when he tried to learn Spanish for our trip to Barcelona? He just kept saying "Hola, cerveza!" Exactly! He’ll end up ordering pizza in Italian and declaring himself fluent. You know, it's funny how a simple desire to communicate can be so frustrating.

Honestly, isn’t this lovely? Just strolling along like this. Feels a million miles away from transcribing endless council meeting minutes. It is peaceful. Though that O2… still seems a bit…much. A giant, shiny golf ball plonked down in the middle of everything. I know! It was quite the controversy when they built it. Remember all the arguments about the lighting? But you have to admit, it's become a landmark. A very  modern  landmark. I wonder how many people actually go inside? Probably more than we think. Still, I'd rather a proper view of the river, wouldn't you? This stretch is nice, though. Walking toward Greenwich. Think we'll make it to the Cutty Sark? Definitely. My feet aren't complaining  too  much yet. It’s good to get out and about, you know? Especially without having to battle for a parking space. Honestly, I don't know why anyone bothers owning a car in London. It’s just a source of stress and expense. Preach! I remember when I lived in Edinburgh, car ownership was practically a necessity. Here... utterly pointless. Public transport, cycling, walking… much better. More exercise too, naturally. Exactly. Though sometimes, when I see everyone else hauling their suitcases onto the tube after a holiday, I do briefly regret not having a car. Remember last summer? Trying to pack everything for the kids into those tiny holiday totes? A nightmare! And all the arguments about who got which colouring book. Don’t remind me. The sheer volume of snacks required for a week with those two is astronomical. Like feeding a small army. I was trying to explain to someone the other day about soup – I was describing a 2-cup portion. They looked at me like I was speaking Klingon. Apparently, everything in America is measured in cups. It's absurd, isn't it? We’re so used to millilitres and grams. It's like… a different universe of measurement. It makes baking a recipe from an American blog utterly terrifying. "1 ½ cups of flour…" Oh dear. I always end up making something impenetrable. You and your precise teaspoon measurements! It's admirable, though, that striving for accuracy. Though, sometimes… …doesn’t it all feel a bit pointless? This pursuit of precision, this organisation… we’re just tiny specks on a planet hurtling through space. You’re getting existential on me, aren’t you?

Honestly, Mum, this rain is just relentless. It’s been chucking it down all morning. Sports Day is going to be a mud bath, isn't it? Don't be so pessimistic, love. It might clear up. Though, I’m not holding my breath. Little Leo’s been so excited about the egg-and-spoon race. You know how much he loves those little plastic spoons. He has, bless him. He's been practicing with the ones from the takeaway all week. Honestly, the amount of food he’s dropped trying to balance an egg... It's a wonder he hasn't broken anything. He’s a whirlwind, that one. Speaking of whirlwinds, have you seen my phone anywhere? I'm sure I left it here last night. I need to check if the school’s sent out a reminder about the PTA bake sale. Didn't you have it in the kitchen while you were showing me that new air fryer? Remember, you were saying how brilliant it is for chips. Oh, you’re right! I was showing you how it works, wasn’t I? It  is  brilliant. Crispy chips without all the oil – genius! Still, I can’t find it. Did either of you move it? Nope, haven’t touched it. Little Maisie’s been glued to her teddy, Barnaby, all day. She’s having a right emotional crisis because he’s lost an eye. Apparently, Barnaby needs sewing up. Oh, dear. That’s rough for her. You know, Build-a-Bear used to do little repair kits? Might be worth looking into. It’s a good way to involve her in fixing him. That’s a brilliant idea, Mum! I’ll have a look online. Remember when we used to go to Build-a-Bear when we were little? We spent all our pocket money on those things. I do! You were obsessed with that little pink unicorn you created. You named her Sparkle, didn’t you? And you took her  everywhere . Even to swimming lessons. Honestly, I did! Mum, do you remember how you used to dry Sparkle off with a little towel after swimming? Of course I do! You were so worried about her getting cold. It's funny, isn't it? How children attach themselves to those cuddly toys. Maisie’s just like you were. It's a crucial stage, though. It helps them feel secure.

Right then. Sun’s up, birds are chirping. Feels ridiculously idyllic, doesn't it? Especially considering we’re supposed to be figuring out our lives. Ridiculously idyllic is a good description. More like a distraction, maybe? Because, yes, figuring out our lives is still massively on the agenda. I was thinking about what you said last night, about wanting to properly scale up the consultancy. Yeah. It feels like I’ve been treading water for a bit, you know? Good income, steady… but not exactly pushing the boundaries. I need a project that properly excites me, something that feels like it has real impact. Beyond the quarterly reports, you know? The AI ethics training is a start, but… It is a start. And it's important, genuinely. But you’re right. You need the passion project. Have you, I don’t know, been doing any more digging into that sustainable agriculture initiative you mentioned a while back? The one in Malawi? A bit. The initial research was promising, but it needs serious investment. And frankly, pulling that together from this side of the world is a bit daunting. I was looking at partnering with some impact investors. It’s just… a big leap. Everything worthwhile is, isn’t it? Listen, about the investment, maybe we could brainstorm with Liam and Sarah next week when they visit? They've got that network, that legal brainpower... It wouldn't hurt to have their perspectives. Speaking of which, are they definitely confirmed for the long weekend? Pretty sure. They’re rather keen to escape the London rain. So are we, honestly. A few weeks with friends, proper relaxation, a bit of sanity before we dive back into the madness. It's brilliant we're all able to make it work. Definitely. And it’s a good reminder to check in with ourselves, too. I've been thinking about my own career progression, and I'm starting to feel a bit… stuck. Head of Year is good experience, but it’s not moving me anywhere particularly exciting. I’ve started looking at some online courses in educational leadership, specifically focused on personalised learning. That’s fantastic, love! You should absolutely do that. You're brilliant with the kids. Seeing you work with them, you’ve got an innate ability to understand their needs. Leadership is just about amplifying that, right? It feels that way. I just… I’m also thinking about, you know… the bigger picture.

Honestly, I swear Liam's accent's gotten thicker. I barely understood him when he was talking about that new Pokémon game. It was like he was speaking a different language! Aye, he always has, hasn't he? Wigan's a world of its own. It’s proper thick, innit? But he’s got a good heart, our Liam. Don’t be ribbing him too much. You're being harsh, El! It’s endearing, really. Reminds me of Grandad. Remember when he tried to order a latte at Costa? The poor barista was completely lost. Oh, aye! That was gold! My Uncle Barry did somethin' similar at a service station once. Tried to ask for a “butty” and the woman looked at him like he’d grown a second head. "A what, love?" she asked. He just ended up pointing at a cheese and onion sandwich. Right, that’s a classic. Speaking of classics, remember that camping trip we did when we were kids? The one where Dad tried to build a fire with wet wood and nearly set the tent alight? Don't remind me! I was terrified! Full flight mode activated; scrambling for safety! I remember Mum telling him off something fierce, but he just kept saying he was "nearly there." Aye, he's always been a bit… optimistic. I reckon it’s why he’s always tryin’ new things, even when they go disastrously wrong. Like that time he tried to fix the leaky tap with a rubber band. He means well. He's just… Dad. You wouldn't trade him for the world. He's a comfort, isn't he? Even when he's being utterly chaotic. He is, isn't he? A proper one-off. Listen, I'm absolutely starving. Anyone fancy popping to the shop for some crisps and chocolate? I could murder an After Eight. Oh, please! Yes! I'd love an After Eight. Liam, you're nearest, fancy a quick run? It's just down the road. Yeah, sure. Give us five. Gotta finish this level on Pokémon first. It's a tricky one. Hold on a sec. Mine's nearly charged, I could go. Always good to stretch the legs. You wouldn’t believe how many steps my Fitbit measured today. That’s brilliant, thanks! Whilst you lot are doing that, I'll see if I can get someone's attention at the bar.

Right then, so, the football. Honestly, did you  see  that tackle in the first half? Absolute carnage. Carnage, you say? Well, I 'ad a look. Bit too much running about for me these days, mind. Give me a nice bowls match any day, calmer, you know. Less… commotion. My knees wouldn't stand for that sort of bumping and shoving. Bowls. Lovely. Less likely to need a plaster, that's for sure. Though, I do love a bit of excitement. Remember when Norwich were doing so well a few years back? Kept expecting them to go all the way! They did have a good run. Though, relying on Liam Brady forever wasn't a sustainable strategy, was it? Anyway, back to the football. Anyone else think the ref was having an off day? Absolutely. Several dodgy calls. But, honestly, I'm mostly distracted by the catering tonight! This shepherd's pie looks  amazing , Anon. Seriously, top-notch. It is, isn’t it? Proper good, it is. Proper hearty. Reminds me of me mum’s, she used to make a cracking shepherd’s pie. Used to grate the carrots right in, she did. Nowadays, they put purée, don't they? Ruins it, really. Oh, your mum's shepherd's pie  was  something else, Arthur. The best! I tried to replicate it once, but it never quite tasted the same. Secret ingredient, I reckon. Probably the love, Brenda. Hard to quantify, that. Speaking of ingredients, has anyone kept up with the price of avocados lately? It’s outrageous. Don't even get me started, David. The students are complaining constantly. They're basically a staple of student life, you know? Can’t survive on ramen alone. I had a lecture yesterday actually, about the ethics of avocado production. Turns out, there’s a  lot  of water usage involved... Ethics of avocados! Fancy that! Never thought about it. Always just enjoyed 'em with a bit of salt and pepper on toast. Simpler times. Avocados. Foreign fruit, that. Never needed 'em when I was a lad. We had apples and pears, and we were grateful for 'em! Though a good pear crumble…  now  that's something. We  could  have pear crumble for dessert. If Anon’s up for it. What do you think? Pear crumble sounds wonderful. We could even have custard! Anon: Rest assured, it’s all in hand. And you're right, a crumble would be perfect.

Honestly, this place is a tip. You'd think living with two people would mean someone actually tidies up a bit! And look at these shoes, covered in mud. Proper state. Tell me about it. I swear, if I find another stray sock under the sofa... Anyway, mud's the least of my worries right now. Seriously thinking about speaking to the uni about dropping out. Dropping out? Blimey, Liv! That's a big decision. What’s brought that on? You were buzzing about your course at the start. I was! But it's just... a lot. The workload’s insane, the lectures are rubbish, and I feel like I'm just going through the motions. I'm spending more time stressing about it than actually  doing  it. Everyone else seems to be coping, though. Or at least, pretending to. I know the feeling. Sixthform was like that for me, innit? Just felt completely lost, like I was supposed to be doing something different. My mum kept saying, "Just stick it out, love, it'll be worth it in the end." Proper cliché, but... sometimes she's right. My Nan used to say that too. “Pull yourself together, lass! You’re a McGreggor!” Like being a McGreggor is supposed to magically make you succeed in life. It’s the name of an old Liverpool shipping family, you know? Loads of pressure. Not that I’m going to become a shipping magnate, obviously. Right, a shipping magnate from Liverpool. That’s a laugh. McGreggor, proper posh name though, isn't it? My name's all over the place, actually. "Penhale," It's Cornish. Means 'head of the peninsula'. Fancy, eh? But we've been normal folk in Falmouth for generations. Mostly fishermen and surfers. Not exactly seafaring royalty like your McGreggors. Falmouth! I went there once for a holiday. Beautiful place. My grandad used to take us to the seaside every summer. We'd build ridiculous sandcastles – they never lasted five minutes with the tide, mind you. Keepsakes of our efforts, buried in the sand. My dad used to do that with me. He was hopeless at building sandcastles though. Always ended up just dumping a big mound of sand and declaring it a 'tower'. Still, the memories are good. We used to spend hours searching for sea glass, too. Sea glass! I remember that! We used to collect shells mostly, and try to convince ourselves they were treasure.

"Honestly, this place is lovely, isn't it? I’ve been meaning to come here for ages. So much better than that awful chain place we used to haunt back at uni.” "Oh god, The Greasy Spoon! Don't remind me. The questionable chips and even more questionable coffee...My stomach still shudders at the memory. This is a serious upgrade. What are you thinking of having?” "I'm torn between the butternut squash risotto and the sea bass. Both sound amazing. What about you? Still obsessed with anything involving avocado, I presume?” "Always! Although, I'm feeling a bit adventurous. I might actually go for the lamb. It smells incredible. So, spill! What's been happening? It feels like forever since we last properly spoke. Last time we properly chatted was...what, Gemma's leaving do, wasn't it?" "It was! Feels like another lifetime ago. Work’s been…intense. We’re finally launching the 'Green Futures' project, the one I was telling you about. It’s been a nightmare of spreadsheets and stakeholder meetings, but fingers crossed it’ll actually make a difference.” "‘Green Futures’? Sounds ambitious! Is it as stressful as it sounds?” "Massively. But rewarding, hopefully. The team's really dedicated. What about you?
