Pearson must be keeping you on your toes with all their marketing campaigns.” “It is! We’re pushing the new online learning platform at the moment. Lots of social media stuff, which is fun. I’ve got a team working with me now, which is a huge responsibility but I love it. Actually, that’s part of what I wanted to talk to you about - I'm thinking of doing a management training course. It’s a bit pricey, but it could really boost my career.” "That’s brilliant, El! You absolutely should. You’re a natural leader and I'm sure you'd smash it. Seriously, you’d be amazing. Have you looked at any yet?" "Yeah, a couple. There’s one at Henley Business School. It’s a bit of a trek, but the reviews are good. I was wondering if you might be free to grab drinks sometimes during the course, for a brain dump?” “Absolutely! I’d love to. You know I'm always happy to be a sounding board. So, are you seeing anyone at the moment? Last time we spoke you were complaining about dating apps.” "Don’t remind me!

Honestly, love, it's just bamboozling, isn't it? This whole online shopping lark. I spent ages last night looking for a new tea cosy – simple request, you'd think – and ended up with seventeen tabs open! Seventeen! Seventeen? For a tea cosy? That IS a bit much, Nan. What were you doing? Aye, well, started on Amazon, naturally. They’ve got everything, don't they? But the search results… goodness gracious. ‘Novelty tea cosies,’ ‘tea cosies for oversized teapots,’ ‘tea cosies with cat faces’… none of which I wanted! Then I went on to eBay, thinking I’d have more luck with secondhand. But eBay's its own world, isn't it? All auctions and “slightly used” descriptions that don't tell you half the story. eBay's mental. You’ve just got to be careful. My mate, Liam, tried to buy a skateboard on there. Said it was “like new.” Arrived looking like it’d been through a war. See! Exactly! That's what worries me. It’s all fine and dandy when you're getting a bargain, but what if it’s dodgy? I mean, I bought a set of measuring jugs from Amazon last week - barely used them, the spout cracked the first time I poured water. Amazon’s usually pretty good at returns though, isn’t it? They sorted my Xbox controller out for me when it started glitching. Sent me a brand new one, no bother. That’s true, they are generally alright with returns. But it’s the faff of it all! Packaging it up, printing off labels, trekking down to the Post Office… I'd rather pop down to Mrs. Higgins' little shop on the high street, even if it does cost a bit more. At least then you can see what you’re buying. But you get things delivered to your door, though! That's the best bit. I got a new graphics card last month, huge thing. Would've been a nightmare lugging that around. I know, I know. The convenience is undeniable. That’s what pulls you in, isn’t it? But then you get adverts popping up for things you barely considered, and suddenly you're filling your basket with things you didn't need in the first place. It’s manipulative, it is! Yeah, they’re good at that. They know what you’ve been looking at. Liam’s mum was showing me her Amazon page the other day, it was just full of dog beds!

It’s lovely here, honestly. You’ve really made this place your own, Anon. All these little ornaments… Where did you even  get  that ceramic badger? Oh, that? Flea market in Rye. Years ago now. Good find, that was. Five quid I paid for it. Thought it'd look nice with the ferns. You wouldn’t believe the things you find in those markets, you really wouldn't. Five quid! That’s a bargain. I'm always looking for stuff for my flat, but I never seem to have the time to trawl around markets like that. Work has been absolutely mental, you know? Production schedule’s gone completely haywire. Work, eh? Still that factory job then? Always seemed a bit… noisy to me. It is. Loud and stressful, but, you know, it pays the bills. This new order from that tech company is proving to be a nightmare. They want everything yesterday. And they keep changing their minds about the specifications! Sounds like a right carry-on. Used to hear stories like that about the City boys, back in the day. Always in a rush, never satisfied. Never even took the time to properly learn what they were doing, some of them. Tell me about it. I’ve had to practically rewrite the entire production plan three times this week. My boss keeps saying it’s “market volatility.” Honestly, it just feels like disorganisation. "Market volatility," they call it. Fancy words to hide a lack of planning. Back in my day, we had a plan, and we stuck to it. That’s what was wrong with the world, you see. Everyone chasing after this… this new thing, without thinking. You sound like my grandfather. Though, I can appreciate where you’re coming from. It  is  chaotic sometimes. What are you reading in that paper, anyway? Still the racing pages? A bit of this and that, love. Nothing particularly gripping. There’s a piece about the rising cost of… well, everything. It’s getting silly, isn’t it? Can’t hardly buy a cup of tea without breaking the bank. Tell me about it! My rent’s gone up again. I swear, living in London is going to bankrupt me eventually. Have you thought about maybe looking into… I don’t know… investments? Investments? Me? Don't you worry your pretty head about that, love. I’m not one for gambling.

Right, so, Christmas Day flying. Seriously, Elodie, are you  sure  about that? Seems a bit… bonkers, innit? Bonkers good! Honestly, Finn, it's the only way I’m seeing my family in Perth this year. And think about it – Christmas Day in the air, watching the sunrise over the Indian Ocean. Beats a soggy Boxing Day sales rush any day. I’m just jealous. I'm stuck here, running the café. Boxing Day is brutal enough, I don’t need the run-up to it! Though, I am looking forward to hopefully a quiet Christmas Eve evening. Quiet? You’re dreaming, Liv. Christmas Eve is the busiest night of the year, isn't it? Everyone wants a last-minute hot chocolate and a mince pie before the chaos begins. Speaking of which, these mince pies are bloody brilliant, Elodie. Seriously. Thanks, Ash! Years of practice. My nan’s recipe, you know. Though, I’m experimenting with adding a bit of orange zest this year. What about you, Ash? Any big Christmas plans beyond keeping the caffeine flowing? Nah, not really. Just the café. Mum and Dad are coming over for Christmas dinner though, that'll be nice. We'll probably roast a turkey, do all the usual stuff. It's a bit lonely without the family back in Oz, but what can you do? Turkey! Right. My mum's insisted on a goose this year. Says turkey is  so  last year. I'm not sure I’m a fan. It’s always a bit… greasy, isn’t it? You’re telling me! My mum does a goose too. It's a serious operation. Hours of prep and then the smell lingers for days. But you know it wouldn't be Christmas without it. See? Tradition! It’s all about the traditions. That’s why I'm doing the seventeen-hour flight. Seeing my family is tradition. I get it. Still seems mental. It's just... Christmas Day. Shouldn’t you, you know,  be  with people? Not above them? Finn, you’re such a romantic. She'll be wishing she was on the ground with us all later, trust me. Turbulence and dodgy airline food aren't exactly festive. Speaking of dodgy things… did anyone see that poor deer on the A40 this morning? Absolutely terrible. Oh my god, no! Seriously? That’s awful. It was. Just lying there. I had to swerve to avoid it.

Right, that was…surprisingly smooth. I was bracing myself for Cambridge traffic to be a nightmare, especially on a Friday. Yeah, got lucky, I think. Though, I’m still not entirely convinced this little hatchback can handle the M11 properly. Feels like I’m driving a tin can sometimes. A tin can with incredible fuel efficiency, Liam. Don't knock it. It got us here, didn't it? And it’s a lot better than my dad’s ancient Rover. Oh god, don’t remind me of your dad’s Rover, Ben. The upholstery alone could trigger a sensory overload. Seriously, does he ever clean it? It has…character. Let's just say it’s acquired a certain vintage charm. Anyway, so, about the accents, remember we were joking about that earlier? I reckon everyone in Cambridge sounds vaguely posh, even the students. It's subtle, isn’t it? Not like full-on RP, but definitely more…clipped than what I’m used to back in Brum. Everyone sounds like they're trying to subtly imply they went to Eton. Exactly! I noticed it too. There’s a sort of studied casualness about the way people talk, like they’re deliberately downplaying how educated they are. Though, I did overhear someone with a genuinely lovely West Country accent ordering a coffee. A proper gem. See, that’s the thing! Cambridge is a melting pot. You get all sorts drifting in and out. I overheard two Americans arguing about baseball just as we pulled up. Complete with full-blown regional accents. Speaking of drifting in and out, are we still good for picking up Aunt Carol from the station on the way back? Absolutely. I messaged her, she’s expecting us around seven. Should we grab something to eat before we go? I’m starving. Definitely. I’m thinking that little Italian place near the market square. Remember that one we went to last year? Amazing pasta. Yeah, that was good. Though I’m still not convinced it wasn't a tourist trap. Delicious, but still. We should probably factor in extra time for Aunt Carol’s inevitable wander around the shops. She’ll want to buy something ‘charming’ for the sitting room. Oh, I can picture it now. A tiny porcelain duck or a miniature watercolour of a punter on the River Cam. She's a champion. And don’t forget the inevitable lecture about the declining state of British craftsmanship.

Physics. Honestly. Why does Mr. Davies insist on making us understand quantum entanglement? It’s actively making my brain hurt. Tell me about it, man. I spent the whole lesson trying to figure out if a cat could  actually  be both alive and dead. It's mental. Least music's a bit of a release, yeah? Definitely. I almost drifted off during the bit about superposition. Seriously, it’s like he’s trying to deliberately make us fail. But yeah, need a good tune to wash it all away. What are you listening to these days, Liam? Been obsessed with that new Arctic Monkeys stuff. 'The Car' isn't exactly bangers, is it? A bit... jazzy? But I'm digging the vibe, you know? It's proper chilled. What about you, Finn? Still stuck on grime? Nah, kinda phasing out of grime. It’s good, don’t get me wrong, but I’m getting into this producer, Obongjayar. He’s got this… weird, funky sound. Really experimental. You should check him out. He's proper clever, layering all these different sounds. Obongjayar, right? Yeah, I’ve heard of him! My cousin sent me a track. It’s a bit much for a Tuesday afternoon, though, isn't it? Give me something a bit more mellow to recover from physics. I was blasting some Khruangbin earlier. You guys into Khruangbin? Khruangbin? Never heard of them. What’s the deal? Instrumental mostly. Thai-funk vibes. Super chill, proper good for zoning out. Their guitar work is insane. It’s like... they’re painting pictures with their instruments, you know? Paintin' pictures, eh? That's a good way to put it. I might have to have a listen. Been needing some stuff like that. Everything's been so high energy lately. I'm always up for something chill. Although, after trying to grasp quantum physics, maybe I need something actively  depressing  to match my mood. Anything good in that department? You and your dark playlists, Liam. Always going for the existential crisis. Check out this new film, 'Everything Everywhere All at Once'. Heard it’s wild. Michelle Yeoh is incredible. Oh man, I saw that! Absolutely bonkers. But brilliant. The Daniels are geniuses. It's like, spaghetti thrown at the wall, and somehow it’s all art. And the physics in  that  film... completely different kind of physics than Mr. Davies tries to teach us, obviously.

Right, so, Balanceability practice went well this afternoon, didn’t it, Maisie? You were zooming around the park! Zoom! Zoom! I went really, really fast, Mummy! Faster than Theo! No, I didn't! I was going extra-fast! Alright, alright, you both were impressively speedy. It's brilliant to see you both progressing so well. Remember what we talked about – looking where you’re going and keeping your balance. It's all about that, isn’t it? Like… like learning to read properly, really concentrating. Like school! Lily said Mr. Davies is giving us a big test on fractions next week. Fractions are hard! Are they? Well, we can practice, can't we? It’s just like dividing a pizza into slices, really. Maisie, you want half a pizza, Theo, you want a quarter… So, what's half plus a quarter? Hmmm... more than half! Three quarters! Correct! See? You're already getting there! Lily's got a new house, hasn’t she? Her mum sent me a picture. It’s gorgeous, but a complete building site at the moment. They’re putting in a swimming pool! A swimming pool! Can we go swimming? With a slide? Possibly! But remember what we said about diving? No diving into anything unless you’re absolutely sure it’s deep enough. It’s just not worth hurting yourself. We talked about that at school, didn’t we? Mrs. Peterson told us a story about someone who… Lily said her dad is building a man-made waterfall! A waterfall? How amazing! They're really going all out. Do you think it’ll look like a proper rainforest? It needs monkeys! And a parrot! I think Lily's garden might be pushing its luck if it gets monkeys! It sounds like it's going to be wonderful, though. It made me think, actually, about assessing progress. Trying to see how much the children have truly taken in. It's not just about tests, you know, is it? It’s about showing me they understand, not just memorized something. Like cat facts! Cat facts? What cat facts? Lily told me! It’s National Cat Day in Japan! And cats can sleep a lot! My cat, Mr. Bigglesworth, sleeps all the time! Even when I’m drawing him! Mr. Bigglesworth sounds like a very important cat indeed. Mmm, almost ready. You know what would go really well with this?

Right, so, this Pilates thing. Honestly, it’s…it's a workout, innit? I thought it’d be all gentle stretches and breathing, like a nice lie-down. Ended up looking like a confused pretzel! Oh, bless you! I warned you, didn't I? Pilates  does  look deceptively gentle. It’s all about those tiny movements, engaging your core. My instructor keeps yelling at me to "squeeze your glutes!" It’s mortifying. Squeeze me glutes? I felt like I was gonna pop something! And the lady running it… proper intense she was. All, "Engage your power house!" Power house? I felt like a damp noodle, that’s what I felt like. Did you join that new gym in town? Nope, sticking with the Pilates for now. It’s actually helping my back, you know? Being a Production Controller means I'm at a computer for, like, twelve hours a day. My posture's a disaster. Plus, I’m trying to get back into running. Remember I was training for that half marathon last year? Oh aye! Fell apart, didn’t you? Something with your knee, wasn't it? Yeah, a little niggle turned into a proper issue. Doctor said I needed to build up my strength and stability before I even  think  about lacing up those trainers again. Hence, the Pilates obsession. So, how's the dating scene in Doncaster? Still sifting through the lads on Tinder? Don’t even get me started. Honestly, it’s a lottery. Most of ‘em seem to think their profile picture should be a selfie in the gym, or a blurry one holding a beer. Where's the personality? I swiped left on a lad yesterday who’d only put pictures of his car. A  beige  car, mind you. What's that about? Beige car? That  is  bleak. London’s not much better, to be fair. It's just a sea of the same sort of faces, all vying for attention. I’ve been focusing on work, to be honest. Less time for the dating app madness. Wise choice. Gets right tiring, doesn’t it? Remember Liam, that lad from the pub? Utter nightmare. Thought he was God's gift to women. Oh, Liam! The one who kept talking about his "exceptional entrepreneurial spirit" even though he worked at a vape shop? Heard he's still dating a girl half his age. Aye, some things never change.

“Right then, that was a grand night for the Domino Drive, wasn’t it? Though Elsie did nearly lose her marbles when Maureen’s bingo card was called out two numbers early. Honestly, you'd have thought it was the end of the world.” “Aye, it were mad. Elsie were proper fuming. But that pizza’s champion, though, Auntie Carol. Best Domino’s we've had in ages.” “Champion indeed! Spent near enough an hour gettin' here after that snow. Nearly lost the load of lambs I were bringin' back from Middlesborough, the roads were that slippy. Lucky I've got me winter tires, eh? Wouldn't have wanted to be skidding around like a log out of the fire, would we?” "Don't even  mention  the log! I'm still pickin' bits o' soot off the carpet. Honestly, John, you'd think you were trying to demolish the place with that thing. Tidied up somethin’ awful after your last attempt. Want another slice, love?" “Please! Extra pepperoni this time, if you don’t mind, Auntie." “Now, seein' as we're on the subject of slippin’ and slidin', I saw young Billy Thompson down the Miners' Arms earlier. Had himself a right trim, he did. Looks like a sheepdog now. Trying to be all trendy, the lad is.” “Billy? Oh, goodness. He always had a daft haircut. Remember when he tried to dye it blue? That were a sight, that was. Still, he's got more hair than some of us, I reckon!" She pats her own hair playfully. “He looks like he’s about to audition for a boy band. Honestly. But my mate, Liam, got a proper fade the other day. Looked pretty sharp. Thinking of gettin’ one myself, actually. Think I'd suit it?” “Now, you are a bit skinny, aren’t you, lad? You need to eat more! All that football and not enough proper food. A fade might show off your head a bit  too  much, you’d need a good bit of beef on your bones first. Have you been getting enough to eat recently?” "He's alright, Carol. He plays a mean game of footie, though. Heard he scored three goals on Saturday. Proper star he is, that lad. Speaking of star, did you see the Newcastle game last night? Disaster! Utter disaster! Should've just stayed home and watched the telly, I reckon."

Right, then. Earl Grey it is. Standard, eh? You didn’t fancy a builders today? Feels a bit much, honestly. No, Earl Grey's perfect. Nice and calming. Needed something calming after that disastrous attempt at a soufflé earlier. Seriously, it looked like a volcanic eruption. A volcanic eruption! Oh, no! Did you manage to salvage any? I mean, you coulda mixed it into a soup, couldn’t ya? Think of the texture! I did  not  mix it into a soup. It went straight into the bin. I’m starting to think cooking isn't my forte. I’m more of a research-things-and-interpret-them kind of bloke, not a whisk-things-and-hope-they-rise kind of bloke. Well, you're brilliant at the research bit, that’s for sure. Though, fancy that you’re doing a PhD. What’s the latest drama with your thesis? Still wrestling with the Victorian sewer systems, is it? Pretty much. It’s fascinating, don’t get me wrong, but wading through endless archives and trying to make a coherent argument out of it... It’s a slog. They really didn't keep good records back then, did they? Like, a single drawing of a pipe labelled ‘drainage’ doesn’t exactly scream groundbreaking research. Aye, sounds like a nightmare. Still, you'll crack it. You always do. Speaking of groundbreaking… did you see what Millie Bobby Brown wore to that premiere last night? Honestly! Like something out of a sci-fi film. Millie Bobby Brown? I’m vaguely aware of her. Is she… an actress? I mostly stick to documentaries about Victorian plumbing, you see. My celebrity knowledge is a bit patchy. You are unbelievable! She’s from Stranger Things! The massively popular TV show! Anyway, the dress… it was all silver and shimmering, like liquid metal. Absolute statement. It made me want to chuck a massive pile of sprouts into a fancy silver bowl. Sprout-based haute couture? Now  that  would be groundbreaking. Though, I’m not sure there's a market for it. Speaking of vegetables, your mum’s leeks are fantastic this week. Did you manage to grab some at the farmer's market? Aye, did! Got a right bumper crop. Massive things, they were. Proper posh ones, too. I’m thinking of doing a proper Welsh Cawl, you know, with all the trimmings. Just need to find some good celeriac.

Right, my turn then. Hmmm… “Platypus.” Oh, this is a tricky one. Alright, everyone, listen closely - "A semi-aquatic mammal endemic to eastern Australia.” Bit of a mouthful, Dai! You're trying to win with a dictionary definition, aren't you? Just providing context, Seren! Can’t have you all floundering, can I? Bryn, you’re looking particularly puzzled. Are you lost, boyo? No, no. Just… focused. Trying to think of something clever. "Platypus... a furry puzzle." "A furry puzzle!" Bryn, you're killing me! That’s brilliant in its utter absurdity. Though, realistically, it probably won't get you very far. Oh, Bryn, you always were one for the silly ones. Still, it brought a laugh, didn't it? Your grandfather would have loved that, you know. Reminded him of his own attempts at Articulate. Always trying to squeeze in a Welsh word nobody understood. He did, didn’t he? Tried to explain ‘hwyl’ to everyone for ages. “Intense joyful excitement.” And nobody ever got it. My grandma just used to say, “Just say ‘happy,’ Bryn!” Speaking of rules, Dai, are you allowed to use that level of detail? Because it  does  feel borderline. Borderline what, Rhys? Borderline brilliant? I'm merely clarifying. It’s Articulate! It requires a bit of… intellectual heft! Now, now, Dai. Don't get your waistcoat in a twist. It was a clever one, even if a little wordy. Seren's right though, you can't just read from Wikipedia. It needs to be a description, not a full article. Exactly. It needs a  connected  description. Something that makes people think, “Aha! Of course!” Not, "Let me have a quick Google search.” So, like… “Platypus. A duck-billed wonder, laying eggs and possessing venom.” There you go, Bryn! Much better! Concise, intriguing, and vaguely memorable. Alright, alright. You're a harsh crowd. Fine, I’ll dial it back. Next word… "Parsley.” Oh, this is easy! "Parsley… a vibrant green herb, commonly used to garnish dishes." Perfect, Mairwen! Right on the money. Next! My turn... "Quokka." This one's a good one, I reckon. "Quokka… a small marsupial known for its perpetually smiling face." "Quokka... the happiest animal in the world." Very good, Bryn! See? You are getting the hang of this! A bit less ‘furry puzzle,’ a bit more… wit. Your grandfather would be proud. Right, let’s see what I’ve got… "Sassafras." Oh dear… Anyone know anything about sassafras?

Right then! Full house! Beat that, boys! Show me some competition! Honestly, Mum! You’ve been cleaning us out all afternoon. It's not fair, you've got a photographic memory for these cards. Don't be such a sore loser, Rhys. She's just experienced! Though, I must admit, your poker face is a bit rubbish, love. You give yourself away immediately. It's the twitch above your left eye, Rhys. A tiny, almost imperceptible twitch. Gives you away every time. It does  not ! It's just…dust. There's a lot of dust in this cottage, isn’t there, Alex? A bit, yes. Though I'm choosing to interpret that as exasperation, not a genuine observation about the housekeeping. Tell me, Gareth, are you even paying attention? You’ve been staring at that crossword for the last hour. Just giving my brain a rest. Watching you all bicker is entertainment enough. And I'm winning at the crossword, by the way. ‘Seven-letter word for ‘beguiling’…starts with ‘s’…'spellbinding' doesn’t fit, that's too obvious. You and your crosswords. You’ll be trying to solve the secrets of the universe next. Honestly, Gareth, sometimes I think you have your head in the clouds. Alright, alright, enough about crosswords. Let’s get back to decimating Mum’s winnings. Alex, you in? Always. Though I’m not feeling particularly confident after that last round. You brought your A-game today, Mum. Years of experience, darling. Years! It’s not just about knowing the cards, it's about knowing the people playing them. Rhys, you bluff too much. Alex, you overthink it. Gareth... you're completely oblivious. A useful skill, actually. Sometimes ignorance is bliss. Especially when playing cards with someone as ruthless as you, Nesta. Okay, I'm calling your bluff, Mum. I think you’re holding something better! Aha! You called it! And I win  again ! It’s becoming a habit, isn't it? You're relentless! I'm starting to feel sorry for Rhys. I officially resign. Restoring my dignity is beyond my capabilities. What's the prize this time, Mum? Another round of your legendary Welsh cakes? You know me too well. But first, Gareth, show me that crossword! Let's see if you truly are a genius. Though, I bet I can solve it faster. Oh, it's a tricky one. But I'm nearly there…and the answer to ‘beguiling’ isn’t ‘spellbinding’…it’s…'seductive'!

Honestly, this Christmas special of "The Crown" is a bit… much, isn’t it? All that royal drama. Bit predictable, really. Predictable, yeah, but I'm still hooked. I mean, it's Christmas! We need some proper soapy drama to go with the mince pies. Besides, I'm fascinated by how they make it all look so authentic. I'm actually more into the new season of "Bridgerton." The costumes are  amazing . Think you could write a dissertation on the materials alone! Anyway, I’m starting to think about uni applications properly now. Feeling the pressure a bit. Pressure? You’ve been talking about Cambridge since you were ten! Don't tell me  you’re  getting cold feet. I'm just trying to decide between finance and accounting. My apprenticeship is good, but… I still wonder if uni would open more doors long term. Uni's not for everyone, you know. I'm pretty certain I don't want to go. I mean, working at River Island is alright, and I'm thinking of doing a retail management course. Still gotta pay the bills somehow! See, that’s sensible, Liv. Respect. University's a massive investment, and not just financially. Time, stress... it’s a lot. It did pay off for me, naval engineering and everything, but it wasn't always easy, especially later on. I remember pulling all-nighters fuelled by instant noodles. Well, it  is  Sarah’s dream, isn’t it? All that talk about ancient history. Imagine, wandering around Roman ruins for a living? Sounds incredible. Though, proper expensive. It is my dream! And I'm working my butt off to get there. It’s just… all my friends are stressing about course choices, personal statements and all that. It’s infectious. My gran keeps asking if I’ve thought about Oxford...she thinks it sounds more impressive. Don’t listen to her about Oxford. Cambridge is better. Just kidding! . Seriously though, pick what  you  want to do. And don't compare yourself to anyone else. It’s your path. Exactly! Plus, if you're clever enough, you can get a good job regardless. My cousin left school early and he's doing really well in construction. Good point. It's about finding something you enjoy. Speaking of, anyone else feeling a bit run down? I think I'm coming down with something. My throat’s a bit scratchy.

Lovely dinner, Anon. Really lovely. You’ve outdone yourself, dear. Though, honestly, I could eat another three of these. Mum, you always say that! You’ve already had a mountain of food. You'll be comatose for the rest of the evening. Comatose? Sounds peaceful. Less stressful than trying to figure out the bus route. Don't be daft, love. Stressful? What’s stressful about a bit of fresh air? I used to walk miles every day when I was a girl. Proper rambling all over Essex. Used to love it. Cycling too, had a little Raleigh racer, bright pink it was. Chimed like a bell when you pedalled. Right, Mum, back to your glory days. I’m just saying, getting around here isn’t exactly a breeze. Driving’s the only reliable option, really. Unless you fancy an hour-long wait for the bus to go anywhere vaguely interesting. Driving's not for me. Always felt a bit... anxious about it. Too many variables. And parking! Don’t even get me started. That's why I rely on the bus, even if it is slow. Sometimes I just sit and watch the world go by, you know? See? There’s beauty in that, isn’t there? Just watching the world go by. Not everything needs to be rushed. Though, I have to admit, getting a ring around my legs from sitting on that bus seat isn’t exactly pleasant. Speaking of getting around, Anon said we’re all going for a walk in Grantchester Meadows tomorrow? After lunch? Oh, that'll be lovely! Fresh air, a bit of sunshine… as long as it doesn't rain, eh? Been a dreary couple of weeks. Grantchester Meadows. Sounds nice. Flat, hopefully? My ankles aren’t what they used to be. It’s pretty flat, yeah. Mostly grassy paths. I can even bring my bike if you want, Uncle David, you can try it out a bit. Me? On a bike? After all these years? That’d be a miracle. Probably end up face-planting in the river. Don't be silly, David. A little gentle cycling never hurt anyone. It's good for the circulation. Remember when your father used to take you out on that little scooter? You loved that. That’s… a long time ago, Mum. Different times. Anyway, I was thinking, Mum, after the meadows, we could cycle along the river into Cambridge?

"Honestly, this coffee is…ambitious. But it  is  Alumni Day, so I suppose we should be grateful for the sustenance." "Tell me about it! I was hoping for something a bit more robust after navigating the crowds. I'm Eleanor, by the way." "Olivia. Nice to meet you, Eleanor. Are you an alumna yourself then? Or here with someone?" "Just an alumna. Did my postgraduate here – fascinating research on dialectal variations in East Anglia. Pretty niche, I admit.” "No, that's brilliant! I did my grad degree in sociolinguistics. A slightly broader scope, but still all about the wonderful weirdness of how we communicate. I’m in research administration now - a bit less boots-on-the-ground research and more keeping the trains running, essentially." "Excuse me, ladies, am I interrupting a lovely chat?" "Not at all! Please, join us. I'm Eleanor, and this is Olivia." “Arthur Davies. Retired lecturer from the History Department. Lovely to see so many returning. This Law Faculty is already busier than I recall from my own days!" “It is quite hectic. I was just talking to Eleanor about languages. What were you lecturing on, Arthur?” “Mostly medieval European history, particularly the Iberian Peninsula. Fascinating area, full of linguistic and cultural layering. Did you know Basque is entirely unrelated to any other known language? Extraordinary, isn't it?” “Absolutely! I find the isolation of Basque incredibly compelling. It’s such a link to a deep past. I’ve been looking into its influence, however slight, on surrounding Romance languages. It's a long shot, obviously." Olivia: “I did a module on Basque once. The grammar… it was a beast! It put my attempts at Spanish to shame.” "Spanish is lovely though, isn't it? I spent last summer in Seville. Just wandering through the Alcazar gardens…magic. I’m desperate to go back and explore further north, into the Basque Country itself. The Guggenheim in Bilbao looks amazing, from the photos at least." "Bilbao is lovely. Quite modern, but they haven’t forgotten their roots. You should go. I spent a year in San Sebastián back in the 60s, teaching English. Marvelous pintxos, the food's incredible." "Pintxos! I'm drooling already. I love Spanish food. I’m trying to learn, but my attempts at paella are consistently… disappointing.” “Oh, paella is tricky! It’s all in the socarrat – the crispy bit on the bottom.

Honestly, seeing you all again is just… chaos! Two years! It feels like a lifetime ago we were all squashed on the sofa watching terrible Christmas films. Mum's house is still the same, isn't it? Exactly as you leave it. Pretty much. Though the floral wallpaper seems to be mocking me a little more these days. I swear it’s brighter. And the smell of lavender potpourri is overwhelming. You’re just not used to a proper English home, Finn! It’s comforting, innit? Reminds you of being a kid. Besides, Mum does put a lot of effort in. Did you see the traybake she made? Chocolate orange, Finn – your favourite! Don't tempt me! I'm trying to be good. Teaching a room full of teenagers about proper grammar kind of makes me hyper-aware of my own diet choices, you know? All that talk of ‘healthy living’… it just sticks. Healthy living, eh? You and exercise are like oil and water, Finn. Remember that time you tried to join the gym and lasted, what, a week? Don’t remind me. It was a dark time. Besides, I’m walking around all day, correcting essays about the passive voice. That’s exercise, right? Intellectual exertion? You're impossible. Anyway, did you see anyone’s doing the ice bucket challenge? Loads of people posting on Facebook. Even old Mr. Henderson from down the street! I did! Aunt Carol’s doing it next week for that animal shelter. It’s lovely, but Sarah’s been moaning about being soaked all over Instagram. Typical teenager. I’ve been thinking about donating to a charity, actually. There's a local one that supports foster families. I’ve been reading up a bit, and it's just heartbreaking, you know? Thinking about kids moving around, never really feeling settled… That's lovely, Finn. Mum’s always been big on supporting local charities. Remember when she organised that bake sale for the school trip? That was a right palaver. Oh, the bake sale! Half the cakes looked like they were attacked by a badger. But everyone chipped in. We should do something like that again, maybe. A little fundraiser? That's a great idea! We could choose a cause everyone cares about. Speaking of which, how’s Sarah doing? Still obsessed with those K-Pop bands? Always. She’s also starting to talk about university.

Honestly, this coffee machine is a menace. It's been spitting out lukewarm, half-brewed coffee all week. I think it’s finally given up the ghost. Everything seems to be giving up the ghost these days, doesn't it? Though, I suppose that's the natural order of things. Retirement brings a certain…awareness of entropy. Entropy is right! This lot of boxes is proving a right pain to move. I swear, the removal company’s quote has tripled since they saw the sheer volume of stuff we've accumulated. Tell me about it! I’ve been getting the quotes. It's utterly extortionate. And then the storage? Don't even get me started on the storage costs in Hunsonby. They’re practically daylight robbery! It's like they know we're desperate. Hunsonby is lovely, though, isn't it? Quiet, peaceful. A world away from the bustle of Dublin. I'm glad we decided on this place. A bit remote, perhaps, but… restorative. Restorative for  you , maybe. I’m worried about the cost of everything. We need to be realistic. Is it sustainable, this move? Look, we’ll manage. I’ll revise the budget. We can cut back on… well, everything, really. But we’re here now. It’s done. Besides, think of the hiking! You’ll be busy enough, dragging yourself up those fells. I’m quite looking forward to a bit of gentle walking. And the scenery… just breathtaking. It reminds me a bit of the Wicklow mountains, in a way. Though, considerably more rugged. Speaking of things that are a bit rough around the edges... did you see what Sunak said yesterday? Honestly, the man is just…out of touch. Don’t even get me going! He's completely detached from reality. The cost of living crisis, the NHS… it’s like he's living on another planet. It makes me angry. It's disheartening, isn't it? I always believed in the power of reason, of evidence-based policy. But it seems reason has gone out the window. That’s why I'm cautiously optimistic about this Labour leadership contest. Someone's got to shake things up. Starmer's alright, but… not quite the spark needed, is he? I'm torn. I think he’s trying, but he needs a bolder vision. Something to really inspire people. Remember when Blair came in? The sheer  hope  that filled the air?

Honestly, Mum, I’m already feeling a bit overwhelmed with Christmas plans. It’s barely November! Oh, don't be daft, love. It's the most wonderful time of the year, isn't it? And a little planning never hurt anyone. Besides, you’ve got a mountain of students to teach, you need something to look forward to. That’s true, but… Aunt Brenda wants us to come to her again this year. You know how she gets, wanting everything ‘just so’… the Yorkshire puddings have to be a certain shade of brown, the carols have to be sung in the exact order, and the cat  must  be off the furniture. Ah, Brenda. She’s always been a stickler for tradition. But family is family, isn't it? Though, I can see why it might be a bit much. Remember last year when she insisted on playing that recorder solo again? Oh god, how could I forget? The cat hid under the sofa! I was trying so hard not to laugh, but she gave me the look. You know  the  look. The one that says, "You are disrespecting the sanctity of Christmas." Still, are the grandchildren keen to go? Little Leo loves Aunt Brenda’s garden. He does. That’s the thing that's pulling me. He'll be thrilled to see all the fairy lights and, of course, Aunt Brenda does spoil him rotten. I was thinking, maybe we could suggest we just pop over for the main meal on Christmas Day and then head back to Totnes for Boxing Day? Less Brenda-managing that way, don’t you think? That sounds sensible to me, dear. A compromise. Let me have a word with her – I’m surprisingly good at diffusing Brenda's… enthusiasm. What about your friends? Are they doing anything special? Sarah mentioned she might be going to the Scottish Highlands for New Year. Sarah’s bonkers! Hiking in the snow? Brrr! No, I think I’ll stick to a nice cosy Christmas here. Liam's booked a table at The Angel Inn for Christmas Eve – a proper roast dinner and a few pints. Just lovely. It's nice to have a bit of normalcy, you know? This teaching thing is taking it out of me a bit. I know, love. It's rewarding, but it's hard work. So, you’re thinking about maybe trying for another contract next year, then?

Right, so, Liam's still going on about this snoring situation, isn't he? Honestly, you'd think he was battling a walrus. Aye, he is, isn't he? Every time I see him, it's, "It’s like a freight train, Rach, a  freight train !" Like we haven’t heard it a million times. It  is  bad, though. I slept over at his place last week. I practically bounced out of the bed at 3am. Couldn't get back off, mind. Just lay there all wired. Sleep deprivation's a cruel mistress. It's getting worse too, apparently. He was saying last night it's like he's sawing logs. Logs! Poor Liam! Maybe he needs a new pillow? My mum swears by those memory foam ones. They’re supposed to be good for snoring. We’ve tried everything, El. Different pillows, propping him up, nasal strips… you name it. He just says it's the way he’s built. Men and their excuses. ‘Just the way I'm built.’ Like that explains a rumbling earthquake coming from your face. Did you lot go to Waterfields yesterday? Did we ever! Needed a treat after Liam’s noisy night. Got a Victoria sponge. Brilliant. Waterfields are the best, aren't they? Their Eccles cakes are unparalleled. Seriously! And those Richmond sausages… oh my god. I had two this morning. Just two, mind you. Trying to be healthy-ish. You’re a saint, El. I could’ve eaten a whole string. They’re just… perfect. Salty, meaty… proper. You get those pale imitations now, don't you? Absolutely nothing like the real thing. True! It's the same with everything, innit? Quality’s gone down the drain. My gran used to make the best handkerchiefs. Thick cotton, embroidered corners... proper little luxuries. Handkerchiefs? Who even uses handkerchiefs anymore? Tissue’s so much easier. Don't be daft, Leo. A proper handkerchief is  classy . Tissues just feel… rough. And you can wash them! Gran used to keep a whole drawer full, all neatly folded. My grandma had a box full too. Floral patterns, mostly. I remember trying to steal one when I was little. Got caught, of course. She gave me a stern look, but then she slipped me a Werther’s Original. They always do, don't they? The guilt trip followed by a sugary bribe. Classic grandma move. Exactly! You know, talking about memories… did anyone see that thing on telly about the old Riley’s factory in Runcorn?

Honestly, Dad, that was  such  a lovely Sunday roast. Best you’ve made in ages. Now, now, don't you go buttering me up! It's just a bit of roasting, love. Years of practice, that’s all it is. Glad you enjoyed it though. Didn't think you'd make it back in time after that pottery class. It was worth rushing for. The class was… interesting. Really interesting. Not entirely sure I'm cut out to be a potter, though. Everything kept collapsing. My little bowl looked more like a melted ice cream cone. Pottery, eh? Always fancied a go myself, you know. Back in school, we had a little workshop. Never had the time to pursue it properly. All this farming stuff takes over, doesn't it? I can imagine. So, what did you get up to today then, aside from creating culinary masterpieces? Anything exciting on the farm front? Not particularly exciting, no. The combine harvester finally coughed its last – needed a bit of tinkering, but she's purring again now. Young Tom’s already complaining about the silage needing to be done. He’s got a nose for trouble, that lad. Always does. Is he still talking about leaving and going to New Zealand? Aye, still on about it. Keeps going on about the sunshine and open space. Says it's a proper adventure. He'll soon find out adventure means long hours and hard graft, same as anywhere else. Though, I can't say I blame him for wanting a change of scenery. Been a tough few years for everyone. It has. Everything’s so unpredictable these days. Still, at least the weather’s been decent, hasn't it? Better than last year’s deluge. Aye, can't complain about the weather this week. Though, don't get too comfortable. The reports are saying there’s a cold snap coming next week. Typical. Just when we thought we were out of the woods. Oh, brilliant. Just what we need. More layers. Actually, I was thinking… have you managed to book those tickets for the theatre yet? The one I mentioned last week – ‘Wicked’? ‘Wicked’? Right, right. The musical. Aye, I've got 'em. Got the balcony seats, though. Not quite the best view, but they were the only ones left. Thought you wouldn’t mind, knowing you. Balcony seats are absolutely fine! I'm just chuffed you remembered.

Honestly, this is  lovely , Anon. Thank you for having me. It’s so nice to actually sit down and chat without a classroom full of teenagers staring at you! Of course, Liv! Wouldn’t trade a bit of relaxin’ with friends for a lesson plan any day, would ya? I’ve missed proper catch-ups. How’s everything going back at the school? Still battling with the Year 10s and their insistence on speaking entirely in slang? You know it! It’s a constant battle. I’m trying to incorporate more authentic texts - news articles, short stories - to show them the richness of the language, but convincing them Shakespeare deserves their attention is proving… challenging. What about you? Still enjoying the primary school vibe? You always were better with the little ones. I am, actually! It's a different kind of challenge, though. More… logistics, I reckon. Trying to wrangle twenty six-year-olds into doing anything remotely educational. But they’re brilliant, honestly. Little sponges. I’ve got a particularly keen one, Leo, who's already asking about past participles. Wow! Leo sounds amazing. My Year 10s can’t even consistently conjugate ‘to be’ in the present tense. It’s bleak. Seriously though, it makes me consider, doesn’t it? Why  do  people struggle so much with languages? I mean, it's all just a system, isn't it? Rules and patterns. It is, innit? I think it’s fear, mostly. Fear of looking daft. And sometimes, the way they teach it at school doesn't help. All grammar rules and conjugations, no actually  using  it. I'm trying to incorporate more games and roleplay with the kids, just to make it feel less… intimidating. Have you ever considered teaching something a bit different? Like, conversational Spanish for tourists? I have, actually. I’ve been dabbling with Duolingo myself, trying to brush up my Spanish. It’s surprisingly addictive. Though I feel like I’ll be able to order a paella but unable to ask for directions if something goes wrong! That’s the way of it, isn't it? I've been giving Italian a go, you know. Keeps the brain ticking over, I suppose. Little Maisie’s got a naturally musical ear. I'm hoping she’ll pick it up without even realising. Maisie’s gorgeous! So, how’s parenthood treating you? You seem a lot calmer than I  expect  parents to be, actually.

Blimey, look at that nest, Arthur! Absolute marvel, innit? Biggest I’ve seen in years. Wonder who’s built it. It is a bit of a whopper, isn't it, George? Could be a family of robins trying to cram in. Or maybe a blackbird having a go. They’re getting bolder, these blackbirds. Used to be scared of a thing, they were. It’s beautiful. Makes you wonder about the effort, doesn’t it? All that gathering, all that weaving… reminds me a bit of the puppets I used to make for the children. Layer upon layer, you build something special. Puppets, eh, Mary? Remember those little fellas. Doris loved ‘em, didn't she? Always wanted to be a pirate or somethin’. Got a whole box of 'em, somewhere... though I expect they’re covered in dust now. Remember you tried to get her dressed up as a mermaid, George? She wouldn’t have it! Said mermaids had tails and she had legs. She was a spirited little thing, Doris. She was. She was a delight. Though, goodness, the sugar rush after tea parties with those puppets! I used to worry about their little teeth, I did. Though, of course, even  I  had a bit of cake myself. Cake's the business, ain't it? This Victoria sponge looks right lovely, Mary. Did you put extra jam in this time? Just a touch more, George. Doctor says I need to watch the sugar, you know. Diabetes, it's a nuisance. But a little somethin' never hurt anyone. And you, Arthur? How’s your blood sugar been? Pretty much the same, Mary. Up and down like a yo-yo. These walks are the best thing, though. Keeps me moving. Better than just sitting about moping. Keeps the head clear, too. Sometimes I think about… about the old projects. The bridge over the River Wensum, you know. Felt quite proud of that. Aye, you were good at that civil engineering lark. Always had a head for numbers, you did. Me? I struggled with a simple adding-up. Never really understood it. Happy as Larry, though. Didn’t need to much to keep me content. Contentment is a blessing, George. Something these youngsters seem to forget, rushing about. They’re all obsessed with bigger, better, faster… forgetting what really matters. It's the same with the birds, really. They just want a good nest, a bit of food, a safe place to raise their young.

This is lovely, isn’t it? Such a vibrant atmosphere. I’m starving – I think I’ll have the grilled halloumi with the salad. What about you, David? Halloumi, eh? Sounds good. Though, I might go for the kleftiko. That slow-cooked lamb always hits the spot, especially after a morning wandering about. Are you finding it a bit loud in here? My ears aren’t what they used to be, you know. A little, yes. I kept thinking someone was shouting, but it’s just the general bustle. You’ll need to keep fiddling with that hearing aid, I suspect! Reminds me of Aunt Millie and her constant complaints about her contraption. Remember her, trying to convince everyone she could hear spirits through it? Millie! Always a character. Though, you know, there was something about her. She was always convinced the dowsing rod she kept in her handbag led her to the best bargains in the market. I used to tease her mercilessly about it, naturally. Of course you did! Such staunch skepticism. But didn’t you ever consider that maybe, just maybe... there was something to it? I mean, she always did get the ripest tomatoes. Tomatoes ripen naturally, Philippa! It’s called sunshine. Though… I must admit, that incident with young Timmy and the lost kitten… Oh, don't even start! The way she just wandered around the orchard, rod in hand, and suddenly led us straight to that little ball of fluff stuck in the branches... Honestly, it was uncanny. Makes you wonder about destiny, doesn’t it? Destiny's a strong word. Coincidence, perhaps. Still, it's a more pleasant thought than considering old Margaret’s situation. Poor woman. The doctor confirmed it is indeed the pancreatic cancer. Oh, David, I’m so sorry. That's dreadful. I just saw her last week – she seemed so…portentous about bringing us some mezes when we’re back in England. It’s just no fair. Does she… is she comfortable? As comfortable as she can be, I think. The morphine helps, but she spends most of her time sleeping. It's her spirit that's troubling, I feel. She keeps talking about seeing lights, and yearning to return to the 'old ways', about shepherds and healers... I’ve never believed in that shamanic nonsense myself, openly at least, but she's quite insistent. She wants someone to light a fire for her, to send her spirit on its way.

Honestly, Mum, this is lovely. Just… lovely to be back. Feels like ages since we all properly sat down like this. Don't you start making me feel old! It  has  been a while, love. Work’s been a complete whirlwind, as you know. Those GCSE results... honestly, never a dull moment. How's the project going, then? Still coordinating chaos? Pretty much! It’s a new marketing campaign for a sustainable fashion brand. Loads of moving parts, but it’s actually really interesting. A bit stressful though, deadlines are looming like… well, like looming GCSE results, I suppose. Sustainable fashion, eh? That sounds a bit… idealistic for the real world. Though, good on you for tackling it. Likely got plenty of young whippersnappers involved? Dad! Exactly! Loads of interns. It’s good experience for them, and keeps me on my toes. Speaking of young whippersnappers, have you heard from Chloe and Tom? Did they manage to get those rugby tickets? Oh, they did! Got them for Saturday. Tom's absolutely buzzing. Said he's roped his mate, Dan, into coming too. Promised to send us a postcard, bless him. Remember postcarding? Postcards? Back in my day, a proper letter was the standard! Now it’s all emojis and fleeting messages. Where's the substance, I ask you? Grandpa’s stuck in his ways! Honestly, you’d think a phone call was a technological abomination. Don’t wind him up, darling. He's just being... Grandpa. He's more interested in the cows, hasn't he been trying to get them to wear little hats for Christmas photos? It was a fleeting thought! Optimising the Christmas card appeal! A cow in a Santa hat... it's marketable! Right. Well, I was thinking, while I'm here, we could properly discuss that extension plan. I’ve been looking at some quotes, and if we coordinate properly, we might be able to get it started in the new year. Oh, that's good to hear, love. I've been looking at some wallpaper samples. Something light and airy, wouldn't you think? No dark colours in that room, please! As long as it doesn't disrupt the view of the garden. I need to keep an eye on those squirrels. They’re plotting to raid the bird feeders, I’m telling you. Always the squirrels. Dad, you worry too much. Mum, I think light and airy is a brilliant idea.

Right, so I’ve been doin' some proper deep divin’ online this week, haven’t I? And honestly, it's just… unsettling. Unsettling how? You on a new TikTok rabbit hole again, Elara? Last time it was competitive vegetable sculpting. Nah, this is serious, Liv. It’s about catfishin’. Like, properly convincing catfishin’. I was readin’ about this woman… she fell for a guy she met on a dating app, thought she’d found ‘er soulmate. Turns out, he was a Nigerian prince stole her life savings. Proper heartbreakin'. Oh, aye. There's loads of 'em stories goin' around, innit? People pretending to be someone else online. It's awful. Saw somethin' about it on… what was it? Jeremy Kyle, ages back. Jeremy Kyle! Blimey, that’s a throwback. I'd almost forgotten about that show. They always had a few catfish episodes, didn't they? Remember that one with the bloke claiming to be a fitness model? Turns out he was a retired accountant who bought a load of protein powder. Aye, that was a classic. But it’s more than just a laugh, isn't it? It’s people's lives, their feelings. It makes you wonder how some people can be so… devious. I mean, how do you even  do  that? Build a whole fake persona? I reckon it's got somethin' to do with bein’ lonely, probably. Or lookin’ for attention, even if it’s negative. Like, buildin’ someone up, then just knockin’ 'em down. It's a weird need, isn't it? My nan keeps sayin' ‘a blank canvas is all they are tryin' to fill, darlin’’. That's a bit deep, Chloe! Your nan's wise, as always. But yeah, I think you’re right. It's a desperate kind of action. It makes you wonder about trust, doesn't it? How do you know anyone is who they say they are online? That's exactly it! I’ve been lookin' at profile pictures on Instagram, y’know, just normal people. And you start thinkin’, ‘What if that’s not really them? What if they’re using someone else’s pictures?’ It's enough to make you delete all yer social media! Don't do that! Don't let the weirdos win. Just be a bit more savvy, I reckon. Reverse image search, look for inconsistencies in their stories… the usual stuff. My mate’s brother got caught out by a fake profile once.

Right then, Nan, dig in. I made a bit too much, as usual. Hope you like it, it's got those fancy figs you were on about. Oh, darling, thank you. Figs are always a delight. You're a good boy, always thinking of me. It’s lovely to have you home for lunch, especially with all the chaos at the university. How’s the Classics course going? Still wrestling with Cicero? Wrestling might be a strong word, but yeah, it’s… intensive. I’m giving a presentation next week on his views on rhetoric - it’s drier than the Sahara, honestly, but fascinating in its own way. Makes you appreciate a good, juicy novel, doesn’t it? Speaking of which, remember you were saying you wanted to talk about Paris? Paris! Yes, indeed. I was reminiscing about my time there, you know, back in the sixties. So different then. Much more… bohemian. Less… polished. I was exhibiting at a small gallery near the Sorbonne. Remember I told you about the "Chromatic Shadows" series? Vaguely. You’ve shown me so many series! Was it the one with the layered acrylics, almost like stained glass? Yes, precisely! And I met a rather charming gentleman there - a linguistics professor. He was helping me with the French translations for the exhibition notes. My French was… let’s just say, enthusiastic but flawed at the time. He was wonderful. Fluent, of course, and incredibly patient. I picked up quite a bit from him. My German's still better, though. German’s always been impressive. You’re practically fluent. Better than my French, that’s for sure. I’m struggling a bit, to be honest. My Duolingo owl is constantly judging me. Duolingo! Oh, the tyranny of the owls. It’s a good start, but you really need to immerse yourself. Have you considered going abroad? Maybe a summer course somewhere? Italy, perhaps? Italy would be amazing. I’ve always wanted to see the Roman ruins properly. You went there a lot when you were younger, didn't you? Oh, yes. When I was first starting out, I'd escape Vienna and head south. Florence, Rome, even down to Sicily. The light! The colours! It completely changed my artistic perspective. And the food, of course! I learned to make the most divine pasta ragu from a Nonna in Bologna. Secret ingredient was a tiny pinch of nutmeg.

Honestly, Dad, you were  that  close to clipping that van back there! What was that all about? Are you even looking where you're going? Now, now, love, don’t go getting yourself in a state. Bit of a squash on the M3, innit? Had to make a quick manoeuvre. Besides, I've been driving longer than you've been alive. Robert, please. Millie’s right. You were a little close. Let’s just stick to the speed limit, shall we? Dorset’s lovely, but not if we arrive in an accident. And the traffic's bad enough as it is. Tell me about it. Sat Nav says another forty minutes, minimum. Forty minutes of this… grey. It’s depressing. I was hoping for sunshine! Sunshine, eh? You'll be lucky if we see a single ray. Dorset's always a bit drizzly. Remember that holiday we had there when you were little, Millie? Raining solid for a week. We ended up playing cards in the caravan all day. Ugh, vaguely. I remember being bored out of my mind. And Mum complaining about the damp. Still, at least we’re all together. Though, I really need a day off after this. This essay on Post-Structuralist architecture is killing me. Honestly, trying to understand Derrida...it's like trying to build a shed with Windows 8. Derrida, eh? Sounds complicated. You know, my cousin Derek tried to install Windows 8 once. Nearly blew his computer to smithereens. He’s back on Windows 7 now, happily. Are you still working on that model for your project? The one of Battersea Power Station? Yeah, it's coming along, but I need to get the proportions right. I'm thinking of going down to London next week to take some more measurements. It's such an iconic building. Though, I'm terrified of the solicitor's bill for the family history stuff. Dad said he'd cover it, but… Don’t you worry about that, love. I promised, didn’t I? Though, finding out about those branches of the family… some of 'em were a right bunch of rogues, weren’t they? That Aunt Dot, down in Ipswich... Robert, please. Let’s not bring up Aunt Dot's escapades right now. It’s a long drive, and Millie's stressed enough already. Have you had your checkup with Dr. Lewis, Robert? They said to book it in, didn't they?

Honestly, Arthur, I’ve been thinking about it all day. About what Mrs. Peterson said at the village fete. Mrs. Peterson, did? She's got a tongue like a whippet, that one. What was it this time? Complaining about my prize-winning marrow again, I expect? No, not the marrow, though she  did  remark it was "monstrously large." It was about the community centre. She said, and I quote, "It’s a lovely facility, but it’s hardly being utilised to its full potential. And some of the… residents, well, they could benefit from a little more engagement, couldn't they?" "Residents." Fancy way of saying folks like us, don't you think, Betty? "A little more engagement." What’s that supposed to mean? Me joining the WI and knitting tea cosies? I’ve got a crossword to finish, I'm perfectly engaged, thank you very much. Don't be daft, Arthur. She didn’t mean tea cosies. She meant… activities. Something for people to  do . They’ve got those pottery classes, and the line dancing, and that new ‘digital skills’ thing. But nobody from here seems to be going. Pottery? Line dancing? Betty, you know I’d rather wrestle a badger than attempt line dancing! And digital skills? I can barely work the telly sometimes! What good would a computer do me? It's not about what  you  want to do, Arthur. It’s about keeping busy. Keeping connected. It’s getting a bit… quiet, around here, isn't it? Since Margaret and George moved away. Quiet's peaceful, Betty. Peaceful is what I’ve worked hard for all these years. No rushing about, no fuss. Just a bit of telly, a bit of crossword, a bit of peace and quiet in my own home. But don't you ever feel… a little bit out of things? The world's moving on, Arthur. Those youngsters with their phones and their… TikToks. I saw a young man trying to show me how to use the internet the other day. Nearly gave me a headache! But still... it's there, isn't it? A whole world out there. Look, Betty, I appreciate your concern, I truly do. But I'm seventy-three years old, near enough. I've lived a long life. It’s a bit late in the day to learn a whole new set of skills just to… impress Mrs. Peterson and the rest of the village busybodies.

"Aye, this is reet good, love. Proper hearty. You've outdone yerself, again." "Thanks, Elara. Glad you like it. I was trying to incorporate those parsnips you mentioned. Found a beautiful bunch at the market this morning." "Ooh, parsnips! They do have a lovely sweetness, don’t they? Makes a change from just carrots and swede, eh?" . “Speaking o’ markets, did you see that post from Liam and Chloe? They're having a little acoustic set tonight at The Old Mill. Reckon we should pop along?” "Liam and Chloe? The couple who just moved from Bristol? I've heard their music is quite good, a bit folky, right?" "Aye, that's 'em. Chloe's got a voice like an angel, honestly. Liam plays the guitar like he was born doin’ it. It’ll be a laugh, gettin’ out. Been a bit grey and gloomy lately, hasn’t it? Proper November weather." "It has been. Though I do appreciate the rain for the garden. Everything seems to have perked up. The roses are finally starting to put on a show. Did you manage to get those bulbs you wanted planted?" “Almost! Just need to get round to it. Life’s been a bit hectic at work. That funding proposal needs agonizing over, and the team are chattering away like magpies, as usual. Loads o' last-minute requests." “Research Management, eh? Sounds…stressful. What’s the proposal for this time?” "It's for a project exploring the impact of social media algorithms on younger populations – proper heavy stuff. Trying to convince them it’s vital research, you know? Funding bodies can be right fickle." "I can imagine. Academia's the same, constantly battling for grants. My PhD's on bio-mimicry in architectural design – apparently, bringing bird nests into modern buildings is  crucial  for sustainable living. Go figure." "Bird nests! That’s brilliant, though. Proper innovative. You always were good at thinking outside the box. Still seeing much of your mate, Daniel? He seemed a bit down when I last spoke to him." "Yeah, he is. Things didn’t really work out with Sarah. It’s a shame, they seemed to have such a good thing goin’. He’s trying to stay positive, focusing on his pottery, but it’s tough, you know? He's coming over next weekend, actually. We’re having a proper roast and trying to cheer him up." “Good on you.

…Honestly, it’s just mental, isn't it? Three months. Three whole months since I left that job. And still nothing. I’m staring at a screen all day applying for things, tweaking my CV until I reckon it's practically a work of art, and getting automated rejection emails. It's draining, Liam. Proper draining. I understand. The job search is a black hole of hope and despair. It’s tough, especially when you’ve got your skills and experience. Don't downplay your experience, Elara. You were a brilliant Research Manager. Easy for you to say, you're knee-deep in your doctorate! Surrounded by books and lecturing opportunities, probably getting your brain stretched and challenged every day. I'm just… sending a lot of words into the internet void. It's not  all  lecturing and brilliance, you know. There are days I feel just as lost, staring at a particularly stubborn data set, thinking, "What am I even doing?" But I  am  earning, albeit a pittance, and the fees are… Well, they’re manageable for now. Which brings me to something I was thinking about. Oh? Don’t tell me you’re eyeing up a second part-time job. I can't compete with you PhD students and your side hustles. I’m already feeling like a professional application sender. No, no extra jobs. I was thinking, since you have so much time at the moment, would you be interested in helping me proofread my dissertation? I’m drowning in jargon and I’d appreciate a fresh pair of eyes, especially one as sharp as yours. I could pay you, obviously. Not a fortune, but it would be something. Seriously? You’d let me? That's actually... brilliant, Liam. I’d love to! A bit of actual work, something tangible. Beats endlessly scrolling through LinkedIn. And it'd be good to feel like I'm using my brain for something other than tailoring bullet points. Plus, it'd be good to see you. I miss our chats, outside of stressed-out Christmas cards and brief phone calls. Exactly. It'd be nice to catch up properly. So, dissertation help it is? We could designate a few evenings a week. We’ll need copious amounts of tea and biscuits. Absolutely. And we’ll need to de-jargonize the whole thing. Seriously, some of the language academics use is baffling.

Och, this is lovely, isn’t it, Elspeth? "The Little Wren Who Lost Her Way." Quite charming. Though, the colours are a bit…loud, for my taste. Rather more vibrant than I remember children's books being when I was teaching. I thought so! I wanted it to be really eye-catching for little ones, you know? Liam's got a bit of a short attention span. I’m trying to think about what would really grab him. What do you think of this illustration of the forest? Too dark? No, no, not too dark. Just… atmospheric. Reminds me a bit of the woods behind my auntie’s house in Aberdeenshire. We used to collect wild berries there. Though, you have to be  very  careful which ones you pick, you know. Taught the bairns that at school. Safety first, always. I’ll make sure the little wren learns that lesson! I’m trying to weave in little life lessons, without it being too obvious, you see. Liam’s father, Mark… well, he’d say it’s all waffle. Men, aye. They rarely see the point of a good story with a moral. Being a teacher, I know better. Stories are how we pass down wisdom. More effective than lectures, I’ve found. Exactly! It’s just...Mark's busy being, well, Mark. He's rather preoccupied with his own things these days. Not much time for stories about lost wrens, I suspect. He’s just started seeing someone, you know? Oh, is he? That’s… good, isn’t it? For him? Though, it does complicate things with Liam, I imagine. It does. But I'm trying not to dwell on it. He's a good boy, Liam. Wonderful, truly. Funny how family comes in all shapes and sizes, isn’t it? I mean, he considers Mark’s stepson, Finn, practically a brother. They’re always building Lego castles and getting into mischief together. Aye, family... It's not always about blood. My sister Moira, she never had children of her own, but she was a mother to so many of her pupils. They’d flock to her after school, for a cup of tea and a biscuit. That’s lovely. I wish I could be more like that. Sometimes I feel like I’m just… existing, you know? Just looking after Liam and trying to keep my head above water. It’s tiring.

Right, finally home. That lecture on Victorian literature felt like it lasted three days. Honestly, all that earnest talk about symbolism… my brain’s mush. Oh, you poor thing! Victorian stuff can be a right drag sometimes, can’t it? I just finished my seminar on post-structuralism. Equally mind-numbing, but in a slightly different way. Fancy a cuppa? I brought some of that Yorkshire tea you love. Yorkshire Tea! You’re an angel, lass. Seriously, that's exactly what I need. So, how's uni going in general? Still surviving the fanciness of Cambridge? Surviving, mostly. It’s… a lot. Everyone’s so incredibly… polished. But I’m finding my feet. Though, I did have a rather mortifying moment in the library yesterday. Managed to knock over a whole shelf of first editions. Mortified doesn't even cover it. Oh, no! You didn't! Were they alright? First editions are serious business! Remarkably, yes. Thankfully, they were mostly hardback and bounced rather than shattered. The librarian just gave me  the look  though. The one that says, "You're a barbarian." Aye, I know that look well. My gran gives me that anytime I drop something. Speaking of slightly embarrassing things… I was thinkin' about somethin'. Don't laugh, alright? I promise, I won't. What is it? You seem a bit… hesitant. Right. It’s about… well, body hair. Okay… go on. It’s just… I'm sort of questioning the whole thing, innit? Like, why do we feel pressured to shave everything? It’s just… hair. And I’ve been trying to, like, embrace it a bit more. I haven't shaved my legs in ages, and I'm not rushing to start again. I get it. It’s a totally valid thing to question. I’ve been thinking along similar lines myself, to be honest. It's weird, isn't it? The societal pressure. Like, if a man has a beard, it's seen as rugged and masculine, but if a woman has arm hair... suddenly it’s a problem? Exactly! It’s double standards galore. And it’s tiring, honestly. All the time and effort and money just to conform to some arbitrary standard. Do you…? You know… do you do much shaving? Not really, no. I shave my underarms, purely for comfort in summer, but that’s it. I've been letting the rest go for a while now.

Right, so, alphabet game. My turn. B… badger. Easy peasy. Your go, Liam. And try and beat me this time, aye? Last round you were struggling, love. Badger, alright. Good one. Let’s see… C… Cambridge. Bit obvious, I know, but it’s right here, innit? Are you keeping score properly, by the way? I think you cheated a bit last time with those obscure Scottish words. Cheated? I was expanding our vocabulary! It’s a learning experience, isn’t it? Besides, technically, a “shinne” is a word. Look it up. Anyway, don't change the subject. Letters, remember? You nearly choked on that last one. I was just concentrating! And don't pretend you didn’t squint suspiciously at the dictionary. Look, D… drum. Simple, effective. Your turn. Drum? Seriously? That's a bit…beige, isn't it? Right, E… eagle. A bit more impactful. You’re playing safe, Liam. You’re always so… considered. It’s boring sometimes, honestly. Considered is good! Trying to avoid falling off the stool after three pints is also considered, by the way. And I’m trying to be strategic! You’re just throwing out random animals. So, F… football. Naturally. Football, eh? You know I can’t talk about football without getting proper riled up. Especially with what’s been happening. Yeah, I know. The Rashford abuse was disgusting. It’s vile, isn’t it? Honestly, the level of racism some people spew online… it's just shocking. I keep thinking, how can people be so… ignorant? Ignorant is an understatement. It’s got to be actively malicious. And the clubs aren't doing enough about it, are they? Just lip service, most of the time. It’s like they’re more worried about their brand image than actually tackling it. Absolutely. It’s not just online either, is it? Remember that game last season, the chants they were singing? It’s still happening in the stands. And the police need to do more to identify and ban these people. Actually, talking about impacts… you remember that Tyson Fury fight a few years back? The reaction to that was intense. Oh, aye. Fury. Bit of a divisive character, isn't he? All that shouting and the boxing. It's intense to watch. I wasn’t really a boxing fan before, but there’s something captivating about it. The power… the drama... although I do worry about the long-term damage.

Honestly, Penelope, this St. Edric's proposal is… ambitious. Beautiful, yes, but ambitious. The structural report came back with some concerning points about the south-facing wall. Damp ingress, significant cracking… you’ve seen it, of course? I have, dear. Quite the challenge. St. Edric's has always had a precarious relationship with the elements, hasn't it? Damp being its constant companion. I remember old Mr. Davies, the previous village historian, used to say it was built on a weep hole, designed to drain the marsh. A charming notion, but not terribly helpful in the 21st century, is it? Charming, yes. Practical, decidedly not. The funding application needs to address that head-on. I'm trying to frame it as ‘stabilisation and sympathetic restoration’, but the Heritage Lottery Fund can be notoriously picky. They tend to favour projects that have a clear community benefit, beyond simply preserving a lovely old building. You’re right to be cautious. They sniff out anything resembling a vanity project a mile off. Do you have any plans for community engagement? Workshops, guided tours, something that gets the locals invested? A few initial ideas. I was thinking of a series of talks about local crafts - stonemasonry, stained glass repair... something to highlight the skills needed and the building’s reliance on them. And potentially a photographic archive project – getting the community to share old photos and memories of the church. Excellent. That's the sort of thing they love. Showing a genuine connection to the building and the wider history. I did a similar project with the old mill in Little Puddleton. Started with a village bake-off using traditional recipes, then moved on to oral history recordings. People responded amazingly. It generated a real buzz, and we secured a substantial grant. A bake-off? Really? Don't discount the power of a good scone, darling! It drew people in, made them feel connected. The historical significance became tangible, not just something in dry reports. But back to St. Edric’s... that south wall is a major hurdle. Have you considered a cavity wall tie replacement? It's disruptive, expensive, but necessary if the cracking is structural. We’ve factored it into the budget, but it’s a significant chunk. I’m worried it'll make the overall cost look… prohibitive. They’ll be less likely to consider it. Look, you need to demonstrate a considered approach.

Right, that’s a proper brew, then. Strong enough to stand a spoon in, like me mam used to make. You still prefer yours like dishwater, don't ya, Liam? It's not dishwater, Elara! It’s…refined. Less likely to give me palpitations before I’ve even had breakfast. Besides, all this research talk needs a calming influence. How’s the data diving going? Still wrestling with those sentiment scores? Aye, still wrestling. It’s a nightmare, actually. You know how I was saying about trying to track changes in public opinion about renewable energy? It’s just…so messy. People are saying contradictory things! One minute they’re all for wind farms, the next they’re moaning about the birds. And the language they use… it’s just  wild . So much slang, so much sarcasm... it's a linguist's dream and a research manager’s absolute torment! That  is  the challenge, isn't it? The richness of everyday language. It’s what makes it so fascinating, but also so difficult to quantify. Are you coding for sarcasm at all? That’s usually where the real shifts in meaning hide. I’m  trying  to. I’ve got a few keywords, obviously, like “yeah, right” and “as if”. But it's the subtle stuff, you know? The implied irony. My algorithm keeps flagging genuine enthusiasm as sarcasm because someone used an exclamation mark. Trust me, it's a disaster. I spent half an hour yesterday arguing with it about whether “Absolutely brilliant!” was sincere or sarcastic. Sounds familiar. The perils of automating human nuance. It’s a bit like trying to teach a computer to appreciate poetry, isn’t it? You can break it down into metrical patterns and rhyme schemes, but you’ll lose the soul of it. How's your coding going otherwise? You mentioned playing with some new NLP techniques. That's the light at the end of the tunnel, that is. I'm bringing in some contextual embedding models. They're supposed to be better at understanding the meaning of words based on the surrounding text. Still feels a bit black box, though. Like I'm just throwing stuff at the wall and hoping it sticks. You wouldn’t have any clever suggestions, would you, professor? "Professor" now, are we? Well, I've been looking at something interesting for my own research – discourse markers. Things like "you know," "like," "basically."

Right then, operation ‘School Lunch Logistics’ begins. Honestly, it’s a minefield, isn’t it? Poppy, Leo, how was the school dinner today? Anything vaguely edible? Spaghetti and meatballs! And there was pudding! Chocolate! Meatballs were squishy. Squishy? Oh dear. That doesn’t sound promising. Poppy, did you eat it all? Yeah! It was yummy. But Billy said his was cold. Billy’s always saying his food is cold. He’s a dramatic boy. Leo, you’re awfully quiet. Did you have any? Nope. Leo! Honestly. You know you need to eat something. Are you going to be one of those kids who subsists entirely on crisps? Remember what Granny says – you need your vegetables to grow big and strong! We're going to Granny's on Sunday, you know, and she'll have a roast, all the trimmings… Granny makes the best roast potatoes! All crispy on the outside! Can I have extra gravy? Of course, you can have extra gravy. But that doesn’t excuse skipping lunch! Right, so, the school dinner situation. Are we sticking with packed lunches then, or are we trying the canteen again next week? Packed lunch! Definitely packed lunch. I like my sandwiches. Yeah. Packed. Alright, alright. Packed lunches it is. That means I need to make sure I’m not completely forgetting about fruit and veg again. Last week's apple slice incident was a bit embarrassing. You both turned your noses up at it. It was brown! Brown apples taste funny. Lesson learned. Right, speaking of things you like, the tennis tournament is coming up. Poppy, are you still wanting to play? I’ve signed you up for the under-nines. Yes! I’m going to win! I practiced! That's the spirit! Leo, you’re not interested then? Too much running. Fair enough. Although, you do love pretending you’re a lion chasing things around the garden. Roar! You’re a silly lion! Right, well, tennis is sorted. Now, about money. I need to get some spending money for the school fete next month. They’ve got a clown this year. A clown! With balloons? Possibly! They usually do. Would you like a bit of spending money, then? Just a pound or two? Please! Can I get a balloon animal? A giraffe! Circus! Circus? Where’s that coming from? I want to be in the circus. A strong man! Lifting big weights!

Honestly, that film was a bit much, wasn’t it? All that CGI… I felt like I needed a lie-down afterwards. Though, I did appreciate the historical detail, even if it was a bit… exaggerated. Exaggerated? My dear, history  is  always exaggerated, isn't it? It's just a matter of who’s doing the exaggerating. Though I agree, all those flashing lights... used to get headaches like that in the sixties. Too much television, you know. Exaggerated in the service of entertainment, Dad. That's the key. It’s not meant to be a documentary. Though I did find the portrayal of the political machinations a bit simplistic. It reminded me of that Cambridge debate last week - the one about how much emphasis we should put on rote learning versus critical analysis. Oh, that was fascinating! I was at that, actually. The one at the Guildhall? Mrs. Abernathy made a very compelling point about the need for a solid foundation of dates and events before you can even  start  to critically analyse them. Otherwise, how can the children assess the information? Dates! Yes, dates are important. I remember my history teacher, Mr. Higgins, he could rattle off the entire Norman Conquest timeline backwards and forwards. Utterly brilliant. Though, I do wonder if remembering the date of the Battle of Hastings truly informs understanding of its impact… Exactly! It's the  why  behind the dates that’s crucial.
