Real happiness comes from things like being with people you love, doing things you enjoy, and feeling grateful for what you have. Like this cosy living room, this warm blanket, and all of us being together. I like being with you! I like being with you both too, more than anything. Listen, let's make up a little rhyme about happiness. You help Mummy, okay? Okay! Right. “Happiness is…” ... sparkly rainbows! Perfect! Now you try, darling. What about you? What does happiness sound like? ...Building a tower. Fantastic! So, “Happiness is sparkly rainbows, and building a tower…” ...and ice cream! Of course! "Happiness is sparkly rainbows, and building a tower, and ice cream every hour!" That’s a very happy rhyme! You’re both brilliant poets. Can we have ice cream now? Well, maybe not  every  hour, little one! But we can definitely have a small treat. Although, I think a snuggle and a story might be even better, don't you? After all, those are amongst the things that make  us  happy. Right? Snuggles!

Honestly, Mr. Davies’ lecture on patents was drier than week-old toast. Like, who actually  gets  excited about the intricacies of intellectual property? Yeah, it was a bit…dense. But I did find that bit about Edison and the lightbulb interesting. Apparently, he held like, a thousand patents! A thousand! That’s insane. A thousand! Really? I thought he just…  had  the lightbulb. I never considered the whole patenting process. Think about it, though. If he hadn’t patented it, someone else could have just swooped in and taken all the credit. Exactly! It's about protecting your ideas, innit? Like, what if you invented something amazing, a game-changer, and then someone else just ripped it off? Wouldn't that be infuriating? Furious! Absolutely. It makes you wonder, though, about the bigger picture. All this protecting of inventions… does it stifle creativity? Like, are people afraid to propose something radical because they’re worried someone else will patent it first? Hmm, good point. I guess there’s always that balance. But think about the Chinese tech boom. They’re innovating at a crazy rate, buying up patents and churning out new gadgets. Makes you think about where the future's heading. China, yeah. It’s completely shifted things, hasn’t it? My uncle works in logistics, and he’s always going on about how their supply chains are so efficient. They've got the manufacturing down to a science. It’s a bit worrying, actually. Are we falling behind? My mum says the same thing. She keeps saying we need to invest more in STEM subjects, get kids interested in engineering and coding and stuff. More like China, she says, always comparing us. Classic mum move. But she's got a point. Do you reckon we should be investing in… like, what? AI, obviously. But what else? Renewable energy, definitely. Solar, wind, stuff like that. Looks like it’s where the money's going anyway. My older cousin’s into Bitcoin and crypto stuff – apparently, those are big investments now. Bitcoin! That's so volatile though. My dad’s terrified of it. Says it’s a bubble waiting to burst. He's all about property investment. "Solid as a rock," he keeps saying. Solid as a rock, yeah, until the housing market crashes! My mum’s trying to get me to look into ethical investing. Companies that are doing good for the planet, you know?

Honestly, Rach, I’m still buzzing from that black run this morning. Absolutely exhilarating! Didn't think I’d have the nerve to try it, but you were right to push me. Good, good! I knew you'd love it, sis. You’ve been talking about wanting to challenge yourself, and those slopes are definitely a challenge. Though, I nearly had a heart attack watching you at the top! You were wobbling something fierce. Well, the wobble was more of a strategic lean, thank you very much! And I recovered beautifully, didn't I? So, have you heard anything from Mum and Dad? They were supposed to call this morning. No, not yet. I tried ringing them just after breakfast, straight after my lesson, but it went straight to voicemail. Hopefully, they're just having a late start. They tend to sleep in on holiday. I did text, though, just a quick ‘Having a lovely time, thinking of you!’ sort of thing. Good thinking. I hope they’re enjoying themselves. Poor Dad, he looked so determined to get back on the slopes after his little tumble last year. How are his knees this time? He said they’re much better, although he's booked himself onto a gentler slope today. No ambition to conquer the black runs this trip, that's for sure! He mostly wants to soak up the atmosphere and have a few pints in the bar, if I’m honest. Sounds like a plan. Speaking of bars, are we going to try that fondue place tonight? I’ve heard good things. I was thinking about it! I looked at the menu online; it looked fantastic. We should probably book a table, though, shouldn’t we? It's quite popular, I read. Definitely. Let’s do that now, then. Could you? I’m still feeling a bit wired from the skiing. My brain feels like it’s doing cartwheels. Absolutely. I'll grab my phone. It’s just a shame Emily and Tom couldn't make it. It would have been wonderful to have them here. Tell me about it. Tom would have been in his element, carving up those slopes. Emily would probably have been strategically positioned in the spa! Typical. Are they having a good Christmas back home? They are, from what I hear. Tom's been sending pictures of the kids building elaborate snowmen in the garden.

Honestly, Bernard, this is the fifth racket this month! It's just the strings snapping, isn't it? It's getting ridiculous. And replacing them every week is eating into our... well, everything. It is, Penelope. It’s the sheer force of it all. Those primary school children are surprisingly enthusiastic. Remember little Timmy last week? Near broke  his  arm trying to hit a smash. Oh, don't remind me. We need a solution, something that'll actually last. I was thinking... what about cable ties? Cable ties? To reinforce the strings? Penelope, darling, that’s… a tad unorthodox, isn’t it? Well, think about it! They're strong, inexpensive, and you could weave them in amongst the strings, wouldn't you? Of course, you'd need to experiment with the size. Too thick, and they’d interfere with the play, too thin, and they’d snap just as easily. Maybe a 2mm nylon tie? Hmm. The dimensions are crucial, you're right. And the placement... you wouldn't want them directly across the string bed, would you? It'd throw off the balance. Perhaps weaving them diagonally, at strategic points where the tension is highest? We'd need to test it, naturally. Exactly! We could even use different colours, to make it look… intentional. A sort of design element! Imagine "Fleet Rackets," that’s what we should call them. “Fleet Rackets”? A rather presumptuous name, wouldn’t you say? Implies we have a whole fleet of them! Though, I must admit, I like the alliteration. It’s got a ring to it. It’s certainly more memorable than "Penelope & Bernard's Badminton Racket Repairs." It’s catchy! And think about it – secondary schools might be interested too. They’re less precious about their equipment, you know. They'd be willing to try a solution that's cheaper and more durable. True. The price point would be key. Using cable ties, even at a few pence each, is significantly cheaper than re-stringing with proper string. We could offer different tiers - a basic reinforcement, a premium with coloured ties... Oh! Speaking of tiers... ANON, are you alright? You're awfully quiet. ANON: Sorry, just thinking… I don’t like this fringe. It’s all uneven. You accidentally cut a little stripe in my hair, Bernard! And my ear lobe! Heavens above! I did? Oh dear, Penelope, I am  so  sorry.

Honestly, Dad, this Hockney is rather brilliant, isn't it? The way he captures the light… it's just extraordinary. Hockney, you say? Aye, it's alright. Bit bright for me, mind. Give me a Constable any day. Something proper, with fields and cows. Not all this… abstractness. Oh, Arthur, you and your Constable! There’s nothing wrong with a bit of Hockney's sunshine. It's cheerful, isn't it? And ANON has good taste, choosing it. There's a reason it's so celebrated, Mum. It's not just bright colours, it’s his perspective. He really played with the idea of vanishing points, especially in his later work. Look at how he layers the perspectives, creating a sense of depth. It’s a lot more complex than it initially appears. Vanishing points… Sounds like something they’d teach you at that fancy university of yours, doesn’t it, Eleanor? Back in my day, we just called it ‘a picture’. It’s about understanding  how  he creates the effect, Dad. He wasn’t just throwing paint at a canvas. He was consciously manipulating the viewer's eye. He even used polaroids - lots of them - to figure out the composition before he even started painting. Remember that exhibition we went to, Arthur, years ago? The one in Ipswich? They had some of his preparatory sketches there, it was fascinating to see how he worked things out. Ipswich… That was a long trek. And all for pictures that looked like someone’d spilled a box of crayons. But ANON likes it, so I’ll not complain. It's brighter than that gloomy Turner they showed at the gallery last year. Always painting storms and shipwrecks. Depressing stuff. Turner’s brilliance is in the atmosphere, Dad. He captured the sublime – the feeling of awe and terror in the face of nature. It's a completely different artistic goal than Hockney's celebration of everyday life and sunlight. Exactly. And both are valid! That's what's so amazing about art, isn't it? There’s so much variety and different perspectives. I recently gave a lecture on the impact of photography on landscape painting… it’s all interconnected. Hockney started experimenting with digital painting later in his career, using iPads! Imagine! An iPad? Painting on a tablet? Goodness me! That's quite something. Technology... it's all gone mad, hasn't it? Back in my day, you used brushes and oils.

Honestly, Chloe, I could scream. This project is actively trying to kill me. Let me guess, Brenda from marketing decided "synergy" needs to be incorporated into the quarterly reports… again? Worse! Apparently, the stakeholders want a "dynamic visual representation" of the user journey. Which, translated from corporate speak, means a sparkly, animated infographic that I have to design, even though I’m literally a project coordinator, not a graphic designer. Oh god, that's brutal. You should just send them a dancing banana. That's a dynamic visual representation, right? You're probably right. But Brenda would say it lacks “gravitas.” Gravitas! It’s a flowchart! And let's not even  start  on how she keeps using "impactful" to describe absolutely everything. Impactful. It’s become a linguistic parasite, hasn’t it? Like, when did we become so obsessed with being impactful? I swear, half the ward rounds are just nurses casually dropping “impactful interventions” into conversations. Exactly! It’s exhausting. It's like, communicate clearly and effectively, why use ten words when three will do? Remember when we were kids and Mum used to tell us off for using “like” every other sentence? Oh yeah! She'd go absolutely ballistic. "Use precise language, Emily! You sound like a teenager!" Which, I guess, I was. I’m still pretty much a teenager. Don’t I know it! Speaking of teenagers, did you see Millie's Instagram story? The one where she’s posing in front of that ridiculously expensive handbag? Millie?! Oh, don’t even. She's constantly flaunting stuff. I mean, she's literally still living at home. Where's she getting the money? It's just… showing off. I know! And the captions! Something like, "Feeling blessed ✨". Blessed to be spending your parents’ money, maybe. It's just... a bit much. It is. It's not even just the money, it's the performative aspect of it all. Everything has to be documented, curated, and presented perfectly. Makes you want to smash your phone sometimes. Totally. You know what would be really impactful? A day without social media. . Now  that  would be a statement. So, project death trap aside, how's everything else? You still avoiding cleaning the bathroom? Don’t remind me. It's a biohazard at this point. I  swear  that mould is multiplying exponentially. Seriously. We agreed we’d split it on Saturday. No more procrastination.

Honestly, that meeting this afternoon was a masterclass in pointless. Mr. Harding just… kept going on about synergy. Synergy! As if anyone in that room knew what he actually meant. Sounds about right. Harding seems to think everyone's a mind-reader these days. So, how was the rest of your day? Did you manage to sneak in a proper coffee break? Eventually. Had to stage a fake crisis involving a misplaced spreadsheet to get five minutes of peace. It’s exhausting, you know? All the juggling. Sometimes I wonder if being a PA is less about being organised and more about being a highly skilled liar. There's definitely a performance element to it. You're acting all the time. Though, I do occasionally feel a bit like that with clients. Reassuring them the server isn’t going to spontaneously combust, even when… well, you know. Nicotine helps with that kind of thing. You’re relentless. Still clinging to those things, are you? Honestly, you'd think after all these years… It’s a vice, love. A comforting ritual. Besides, I’m not exactly going to line up for a celebratory juice cleanse, am I? Far too much effort. Speaking of effort, did you see that article about the feminist group protesting outside that tech convention? The one about the lack of women in leadership? Yes, I did. It’s infuriating, isn’t it? They make these grand pronouncements about equality, and then… look around. It's all men. And not even particularly bright men, often. That’s what I was thinking. It’s not just about getting women  into  those positions, is it? It's about having genuinely capable people, regardless of gender. I mean, intelligence and common sense don’t have a gender, do they? Exactly! And I think there's this assumption that feminism is somehow inherently about intellect, some high-minded academic debate. But for so many women, it's just about the basic right to not be interrupted in a meeting or to be taken seriously when you voice an opinion. My grandmother battled for that stuff. It feels like we're still fighting it. My mum always said common sense was more valuable than a degree. Smart people can overthink things to death. Give me someone who can fix a leaky tap and knows when to shut up. You sound just like her! But there's truth in that.

Right, well, that was quite the day, wasn’t it? Absolute chaos, but a good kind of chaos! The piggies! The piggies were  so  muddy! I pet one, Mummy! I fed the sheep! Baa! Baa! You did, didn’t you? You were brilliant with the sheep, darling. Very gentle. Leo, off the chair, please love. It’s a bit wobbly. And the cows were big! Bigger than me! They certainly were, sweetheart. Much bigger. And what about the tractor ride? Did you enjoy that? I like the bumpy bits! It went  vroom vroom ! It did, didn't it? It definitely went  vroom vroom . Honestly, I think they wore you both out. You've been remarkably well-behaved since we got home. So, less bouncing off the walls than usual! We didn’t break anything! That’s true, a definite victory. Although, I'm still finding bits of straw in my hair. Right, tea anyone? I want apple slices! Me too! And grapes! Alright, alright, apple slices and grapes it is. Let's get those sorted. I was actually chatting to Mrs. Davies at school today… Mrs. Davies! She has a funny hat! She does, doesn’t she? A rather… striking hat. Anyway, she was saying that Leo's been a little bit disruptive in class this week. Not  terribly , but a bit restless. I wasn’t! No, darling, you weren't  terribly  disruptive. Just… a little bit distracted. Did you have fun building with the blocks? Yeah! I made a really tall tower! That’s lovely! See, I know you're clever and can concentrate. Maybe if you just try a little bit harder while Mrs. Davies is teaching? Poppy’s drawing is really good! She drew a rainbow! That’s fantastic, sweetheart! Poppy’s very talented. Maybe you could ask her to show you some of her techniques? Do you want to watch  Paddington  tonight? I think we could all do with a bit of calm after today.  Paddington ! Yes! With marmalade sandwiches? Of course, with marmalade sandwiches. Absolutely. Though, perhaps just  one  each. We don't want a marmalade-covered explosion. Me and Paddington like marmalade! We all do! It's a very British treat, isn’t it? Makes me think of my grandma's kitchen. She always had a jar of it. And do you know what? We could maybe even take a few marmalade sandwiches with us next time we go to the farm.

Right, then. Earl Grey it is. Standard, eh? You didn’t fancy a builders today? Feels a bit…celebratory, doesn't it? Like it should be strong enough to stand up to a whole roast dinner. Builders seems a bit much for a Tuesday, doesn't it? Earl Grey’s nice. A little calming. Speaking of celebrations, have you seen what Gemma Chan’s doing with that textile art project? Absolutely stunning. Gemma Chan? No, tell me! I’ve been totally immersed in this report on stakeholder engagement, it’s been a right palaver, honestly. I’m knackered. Stakeholders! You wouldn’t believe some of the opinions flyin' about. Anyway, what's she been up to? Textiles, you say? Yeah, she's collaborating with a weaver from the Lake District, creating these huge tapestries. Apparently, they're inspired by ancient Celtic knotwork, but with a very modern, almost digital aesthetic. I saw a preview online – the colours are incredible. Very immersive. Like stepping into another world. Dead set! Gemma Chan, doing weavin’? That’s brilliant! She’s always had such fantastic taste. Remember when she said she admired Grayson Perry’s pottery? Proper clever girl. I’ve been trying to pick up knitting again, you know. Proper slow progress, mind. I'm still mostly producing wonky scarves that look like they've been attacked by a badger. Badgers have discerning tastes, I’m sure. Knitting’s harder than it looks. My mum used to be brilliant at it; could whip up a jumper in a weekend. I tried once, and ended up with a pile of tangled yarn and a profound sense of failure. Aye, it’s fiddly, isn’t it? I'm trying a cable stitch, which is laughin' at me something fierce. Speaking of things that are fiddly, did you catch any of the Olympics last night? Those divers... honestly, my stomach was twisting just watchin' them. I saw bits and pieces. The synchronized swimming was mesmerising, though. So much precision. It requires incredible control. Almost an artistic performance as much as a sport. Reminds me a little of the art I’m studying, actually – this whole idea of control and structure, but also allowing space for improvisation. Aye, I can see that. It’s like, you need the rules to make it interesting, but you also need someone to break them a little bit to make it beautiful, don’t you?

Right then, Arthur. That was… something, wasn’t it? The Natural History Museum. Absolutely rammed, though. Felt like Piccadilly Station on Christmas Eve! Aye, it were a bit busy, weren’t it? Though, I did like the dinosaurs, love. Always did. Brings back memories of visiting the Science Museum with me dad as a lad. Proper impressive, those skeletons. Aye, the dinosaurs were good. Though, I’m not sure little Finn would’ve appreciated them as much as we did. He was more interested in that giant blue whale model, bless 'im. Kept saying it was a 'big fishy'. Little 'uns, eh? They’ve got their own way of seeing things. Did you see that new exhibit on the insects? Absolutely massive some of 'em were! I did! Crikey, a stick insect longer than my forearm! Gave me the shivers, it did. Reminded me too much of those creepy crawlies we used to find down the garden back home in Liverpool. Oh, for a bit of peace and quiet, eh? True enough. Mind you, getting here wasn't exactly peaceful either. The Tube… honestly! Stranded at King's Cross for half an hour thanks to a signalling fault. Proper chaos. Oh, don't even start! I knew we should’ve taken a bus. It would've been slower, but at least we’d have known where we were, and avoided those crowds. I swear, the last time I used the Tube during rush hour, I thought I’d be flattened. A bus? Love, you know how I feel about buses. Rattling around, stopping every other minute, and you’re never sure if you’re going to get a seat. The Tube's quicker, normally. Just a bit unreliable today, that’s all. Quicker until it breaks down, and you're stuck like sardines! Honestly, Arthur, they need to invest in better infrastructure. It’s not like London hasn't got the money. They do, alright. Wasting it on those silly cycle lanes, if you ask me. Posh people on shiny bikes, whizzing about while the rest of us are crammed into carriages. Now, don’t start on the cyclists again! They’re trying to encourage people to be more eco-friendly. And they pay road tax, you know. Road tax? Through their registration, aye? That’s not the same as a proper licence and insurance! And don’t get me started on them weaving in and out of traffic.

Right then, so Christmas dinner… logistics. I was thinking we stick with a traditional roast, yeah? Turkey, all the trimmings? It’s just… feels right, doesn't it, even out here? Aye, seems a bit daft not to, doesn't it? Doing a full-blown Cantonese spread at Christmas just feels... wrong. Turkey it is. Are we doing sprouts this year? My niece, little Maisie, has a pathological hatred of them. Sprouts? Absolutely. But we're doing the honey-glazed ones. Apparently that makes them almost palatable, even for sprout-averse children. Though, no promises. How’s your sister coping with the time difference? She's usually the one orchestrating everything. She's doing alright, I think. A bit frantic, truth be told. Keeps sending me messages at three in the morning about cranberry sauce versus quince jelly. Honestly, the woman! Still, she’s determined to make it feel like Christmas, and I appreciate that. I had a proper laugh when she sent a picture of her attempting to decorate the tree with fairy lights while the cat was attacking them. Classic. You know, speaking of movies, I’ve just re-watched ‘Love Actually’. Always gets me. Utterly cheesy, but undeniably comforting, especially now. Need a bit of familiar warmth, don’t we? ‘Love Actually’… Hmm. A bit too saccharine for my taste, to be honest. I’m more of a ‘Die Hard’ man at Christmas. It’s a Christmas movie! Fight scenes, explosions, Bruce Willis being sarcastic… What’s not to love? You’re pulling my leg, aren't you? 'Die Hard' is hardly festive. Although, I suppose it’s an excuse for excessive amounts of eggnog. Exactly! Festive eggnog fueled action. It’s brilliantly ridiculous. Have you heard from Ben and Sarah? I haven't seen them in ages. They were meant to be coming to visit us in Chengdu last Spring, remember? No, I haven't. I messaged them a couple of weeks ago about Christmas, just to see if they were free. They said things were a bit hectic at work for them both, but they're trying to get flights sorted. Apparently, getting to China during Christmas is an ordeal in itself. Plane tickets are through the roof. Tell me about it! I swear, airlines are laughing all the way to the bank. Still, it would be brilliant to have them here. It wouldn't be Christmas without a bit of Ben's terrible jokes and Sarah's expertly crafted cocktails.

Right, official winding down time. Just scrolled through Twitter, and honestly, some people are just… relentless. Did you see that thread about that restaurant getting five-star reviews for, I swear, serving lukewarm water? You’re kidding! People will complain about  anything , won't they? I had a proper nightmare customer today. Wanted a gluten-free, vegan, sugar-free, nut-free cake… for a five-year-old's birthday. And then proceeded to tear into it, saying it was “bland.” Bland! It had beetroot in it for the colour, giving it a natural sweetness! Honestly, some people shouldn’t be allowed near cake. Oh god, the entitlement. Don't even get me started. Last week, someone left a one-star review for the café saying our cappuccinos were "too frothy." Too frothy! Like, what even  is  that complaint? They’re meant to be frothy! Too frothy! That's peak internet absurdity. Reminds me of that design blog I follow – someone left a scathing review of a cafe's interior design because they thought the colour palette was "too beige." Beige is the safest bet, innit? Can't offend with beige. Though, speaking of design, I've been looking at some stuff for a possible renovation of the bakery. Thinking a bit more Scandi, you know? Lots of light wood, clean lines… less chintz. Ooh, I love that! It would look amazing. Have you seen that place in Margate, 'The Cornerstone'? That’s exactly the vibe I was going for with the café, if I'd had a bigger budget. Simple, but really thoughtful. Their website is gorgeous, too. Margate, huh? You planning a trip? I've been meaning to go. Always hear it's having a bit of a renaissance. Escape the London madness. I'm actually thinking of it! I'm looking at renting a little space there to open another café. Smaller, more focused – just good coffee, pastries, and maybe some light lunch options. Less faff than here. Seriously? That’s amazing, Maya! That’s brilliant news! You’d kill it. Margate needs a good cafe. Are you nervous about it, though? Leaving the café here? A bit, yeah. It's a lot of risk. But this one's kind of…stagnating, you know? I need a new challenge. And I’ve been looking at these vintage enamel signs online—perfect for the coastal vibe. Plus, I reckon the internet reviews will be better with a fresh start.

Right then, everyone! Dig in. Fresh from the garden this morning. Oisin, darling, do you want some raspberries? Raspberries! Yes, please! They look absolutely lovely, Sarah. You've got a real knack for gardening, you know that? Much better than my attempts! My tomatoes were a disaster this year. Just tiny, sad little things. Oh, they’re easy once you get the hang of it. Plenty of sunshine and water, that's all they need. Unlike toddlers, who seem to require constant supervision and an endless supply of snacks! Mum always says I need to eat more greens. This broccoli’s… well, it’s broccoli. You know, broccoli isn’t so bad! Remember when we went for that walk down by the river last weekend, and we saw those bird eggs? Absolutely fascinating. It makes you think about all the little creatures out there, all needing their greens too! Absolutely! And remember how we saw that little robin hopping about? He was probably searching for worms! Speaking of natural things, Liam, did you have a good bike ride after school today? Yeah, it was alright. Went round the park with Finn. Saw Mrs. Henderson's gerbil again. It's gotten really big since last time! Is it? Gerbils do grow quickly, don’t they? I used to have a gerbil when I was a kid - Pip. He chewed through everything! My mum was furious with him, but secretly, I think she found it quite funny. Those little critters! Oisin, more raspberries? Don’t fill up on those before your dinner though, sweetheart. You need your carrots. Carrots boooo! Oh, come on, Oisin! They’re good for your eyes. You’ll be able to see even  further  on your bike! Can we have ice cream after dinner? Pleeease? We’ll see, Liam. After you’ve finished your broccoli. Promises? Fine. But chocolate ice cream. Definitely chocolate. Chocolate is always a good choice. It’s a treat, but in moderation, of course. Although a massive bowlful after a long day teaching… well, that’s sometimes exactly what’s needed! Hear, hear! You’ve earned it, Emma. You’re working so hard with those exams coming up for your students. How are things going? Chaotic, as always! Year 11s are particularly stressed. The pressure is just immense. I’m trying to be as supportive as possible, but it’s hard to see them so anxious.

Honestly, Mum, your place always smells so lovely. Is that lavender you’ve got simmering on the stove again? Aye, love. It does calming, doesn’t it? Needed a relaxin’ day after Mrs. Peterson's, bless her heart. She’s makin’ such a fuss about that fallen tile in the bathroom. Honestly, you’d think the world was ending! Tiles, tiles! Back in my day, we were lucky to  have  a bathroom. We used the outside privy, rain or shine. Now  that  was a worry! You’re a marvel, Mum. Always bringing things into perspective. Speaking of perspectives, I was at the supermarket earlier, battling the crowds. They’re putting those fancy pre-prepared meals on special again, and it’s tempting, isn’t it? But then I think of you and your lovely roast dinners… Oh, I do love a roast, don't I? Though my knees weren’t keen on all the standing yesterday. I’m thinkin’ of gettin’ one of them standin’ desks for the kitchen. Seems a bit silly, but... A standing desk? That  is  silly! But I understand, wanting to ease the strain. I’ve been meaning to book myself in for a haircut, you know. It’s getting wildly unruly. Sarah's been having such trouble getting in somewhere decent; even  she  says it's a nightmare now. Sarah’s got that lovely young man cutting her hair now, hasn’t she? The one with the… the purple hair? Seemed a nice lad. Though I’m stickin’ with Brenda. Been going to Brenda for sixty years! Wouldn't trust anyone else with my eyebrows, you know. Getting them done is the highlight of my week. Brenda's a legend. You and Brenda go way back, Mum. Remember when she used to sneak you a packet of sweets after your appointment? Don’t you go tellin' tales, girl! It was a treat, a little somethin' to brighten my day. Back then, everything was a treat. Now… Now you've got us, Mum. And we’re here for you. I was thinking, we should all go out for a meal next week. Somewhere nice, like that Italian place down the street? They do a lovely risotto. That sounds lovely, love. I’ll have a nosey at the menu tonight. Shame about your Auntie Carol, though. Still feeling poorly, is she? Yes, poor thing. She’s back to needing help with her shopping and everything.

Honestly, this weaning process is something else, isn't it? Little Arthur seems to think carrot is a personal affront. He’s just making the most extraordinary faces. Tell me about it! Maisie had a similar phase with broccoli. Green everywhere. It was like a tiny, vegetable-induced Jackson Pollock painting. Though, to be fair, he  does  look intensely unimpressed with that carrot. He does, doesn't he? It's a really thoughtful disapproval, if that makes sense. You'd think he’d have something constructive to offer instead of just… scrunching up his nose. How’s Maisie handling all this baby chaos? Seems like a lot for her too, being an aunt. She's absolutely charmed. She keeps trying to teach Arthur silly words – “wiggle worm” is currently his favourite. She’s been a massive help, actually. Offered to come over Saturday and entertain him while we run errands. Said she’s finally freed up a bit of time. That’s lovely. Saturday would be perfect. We need to get nappies and more purees. I swear, he gets through them like they’re going out of fashion. And your mum and dad... are they still planning on coming down next weekend? Yes, they are! Dad’s already boasting about how he’s perfected his ‘baby-whispering’ technique. I’m slightly terrified, to be honest. He tried to make Arthur wear a miniature tweed suit last time. Oh, your Dad. Bless him. He means well. We should probably hide the tweed. Seriously though, it’ll be good to have them here. We could all go for a walk in Sutton Park. Arthur needs fresh air, and frankly, so do we. Definitely. I was thinking we could have a little barbecue on Sunday if the weather holds up. Keep it casual. Just a few people. Aunt Sarah and Uncle David, of course. Sounds wonderful. I’ll let Sarah know. Speaking of keeping busy… how are the sign language classes going? You were so excited about those. They’re brilliant, actually! I’m really enjoying it. I can already sign a surprising amount. It’s so useful for Maisie at school; lots of the kids have communication differences, and it’s making a real difference. It feels good to be able to support them. That’s fantastic, love. I’m so proud of you for pursuing that. It's brilliant you can use it with the children, it’s a really valuable skill to have.

Honestly, isn't this just  divine ? I needed this. London has been… well, London. All grey and deadlines. You say that every time we escape. And every time, you're right. Though, I'd argue Norfolk’s grey can be pretty spectacular too, especially on a drizzly day. Think the sea mist rolling in. Don’t you dare tempt me with drizzle! Sunshine and rolling hills are what I ordered. See that dip over there? It looks almost… deliberate, doesn't it? Like a little bowl carved out of the landscape. You've got a good eye. It's probably just erosion, centuries of rainwater carving its way down. Norfolk isn’t exactly known for dramatic geological formations, you know. It's mostly flat. These little undulations are the exception. That’s precisely what I find so charming about it. London is all sharp angles and imposed order. Here, it feels… organic. So much quieter. Did you see that signpost back there pointing to Little Barningham? I did. Tempting, isn’t it? We could swing by for a cream tea if you're feeling adventurous. Though, Little Snoring wasn't exactly thrilling last time. You purposefully bring up the most ridiculous village names, don't you? Little Snoring! It’s wonderfully absurd. It makes you wonder what the story behind it is. I bet there's a fascinating history. These small villages... They've held onto centuries of stories. Probably a shepherd with a fondness for, well, snoring. Or maybe a particularly noisy flock of sheep. Seriously though, you're right. They're like living museums. Each one carries its own little narrative. My grandfather used to tell stories about his childhood in a village like this one. Completely different world. That's what I find so restorative about coming here. It puts things into perspective. All those anxieties I’m carrying around... suddenly seem a bit… trivial against a landscape that’s been here for millennia. It does that, doesn't it? Makes you remember what really matters. It's also a welcome break from grading papers on the French Revolution. I'm starting to feel like I  lived  it. Oh, please. You’re brilliant at that stuff. You can make Robespierre sound dashing. Although, I still think you romanticize the Reign of Terror just a little… I merely appreciate the complexities of the period! A little drama never hurt anyone.

Right, I’m officially declaring myself emotionally exhausted. Another day wrestling with spreadsheets of tagged language. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m speaking in code. Sounds… glamorous. Far more exciting than dealing with stress calculations for bridges. At least yours has a slightly more human element. Human element? You’re cracking me up. It’s analysing the frequency of the word “however” in political speeches! Thrilling, I tell ya. What about you? Bridge crisis averted today? Mostly. Had a slight issue with a load bearing strut. Nothing catastrophic, just needed a bit of… adjustment. You know, standard stuff. How's Mark doing, by the way? Last I heard he was interviewing for that data analyst role at "Innovate Solutions." Oh, Mark? He was proper chuffed! Said the interview went brilliantly. They seemed really impressed with his Python skills. He reckon’s he’ll hear back next week. Fingers crossed for him, eh? He really needs it. Rent's killin' him. Absolutely. He's a good lad. Deserves a break. "Innovate Solutions" is a decent place, from what I hear. Not the most exciting company name, admittedly. No, they’re not exactly burstin’ with creativity. But a job's a job, and better than livin' on beans on toast every night. Speaking of things that are a bit… stressful, have you seen the state of the roads today? Cyclists everywhere! Tell me about it. I nearly took out a bloke in Lycra on the A1 earlier. He was weaving in and out like he owned the place. It's getting worse, innit? Aye, it is. Don't get me wrong, I'm all for people bein' active, but some of 'em are absolutely reckless. No lights, jumpin' out in front of cars… it’s a recipe for disaster. It is. Maybe they should have compulsory cycle safety training. Or at least make them wear ridiculously bright colours. I’m thinking neon pink. Oh, that'd be brilliant! Imagine tryin' to explain that to 'em. "Sorry, sir, but your fluorescent orange is a public safety hazard.” Exactly! Right, changing the subject slightly. Been meaning to ask, did you ever get around to watching "Everything Everywhere All at Once?" Everyone's raving about it. Oh my god, yes! I finally saw it last week. Honestly, it blew my mind. It was absolutely bonkers, but in the best possible way. Michelle Yeoh was incredible.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Just… fields and sky. London felt like it was closing in on me this week. You'd think after all these years, you’d be used to the bustle. Still, Norfolk’s a good medicine. Look, there's a proper clump of poppies there. Reminds me of those old farming calendars my mum used to have. Poppies are gorgeous, aren’t they? Though, I was reading something fascinating about the economics of flower farming the other day. Apparently, the cut flower industry is incredibly complicated, with a massive reliance on imported labour and a ridiculous amount of pesticide usage. Right, cheerful stuff. Always a hidden cost, isn’t there? Though I suppose it’s similar to what's happening with these cash crops around here. Beetroot, mostly, isn't it? Big sugar factories sucking up all the water. It's horrifying the impact on the local ecology. It is. I was looking at some research out of Cambridge on hydrological shifts in the Fens, actually. Really quite alarming projections. It makes you question the sustainability of it all, doesn’t it? Especially when it’s all driven by global commodity prices. Exactly. They call it 'optimisation', don't they? Optimising for profit, regardless of the consequences. Reminds me of that paper I read on comparative linguistics – how even seemingly neutral language structures can be used to subtly reinforce economic power dynamics. Oh, do tell! I'm always fascinated by that. Which language were you looking at? It was a study of Swahili trading dialects. The way certain phrases are employed to subtly favour the seller, the way verbs are constructed to imply a contract is more binding than it actually is. It's all in the nuances. Clever, really, in a rather Machiavellian way. That’s brilliantly put. It's always the subtle things that get you, isn't it? Like the way they use certain terminology in financial reports to obfuscate losses. It’s a case of linguistic camouflage. Precisely! Speaking of camouflage… Did you see that hare dart across the field just now? Speedy little thing. I missed it! I was lost in thoughts of economic exploitation. Typical. Though, you know, it’s funny. We spend so much time dissecting these complex systems, and then you come out here and see a hare, and you're just… momentarily present. It’s the crux of everything, isn’t it?

Right, so, parking at Wimbledon. You  swear  it's not going to be a nightmare? Last time we went, I thought I'd aged a decade just battling for a spot. Relax, love. I booked it weeks ago, remember? Premium parking, right by the South Entrance. No queuing for hours, no dodging rogue pushchairs. It’s sorted. You were stressing about it last week, kept bringing it up. Aye well, I’m a worrier, aren't I? And it's Federer’s last Wimbledon, ya know? I don’t want to miss a single rally dealing with a territorial parking dispute. Speaking of, did you see Newcastle played brilliantly yesterday? Proper battering, that was. Yeah, saw bits and pieces. Genuinely impressive performance. They looked sharp. Though, I’m still slightly terrified about their chances against Man City next week. They’ll need to be at their absolute best. You reckon they’ll have a shout? Honestly? A shout, yeah, but a win? Maybe wishful thinking. But they've got the spirit! And the new manager's done wonders. It’s a bit like going back to when Bobby Robson was in charge, innit? Gives you a bit of hope. Exactly. Speaking of hope, what about the flat situation? Still looking at those places near Richmond? Aye, still looking. Found one yesterday, a little one-bed, decent location. But the parking is… well, let's just say it involves a lot of praying and hoping someone’s leaving. Absolute chaos down there, it is. Much better than Sunderland, where you could park anywhere - just had to dodge a few seagulls! Remember that trip we took up to see the Angel of the North? How could I forget? You nearly tripped over a sheep trying to get the perfect picture and I was trying to explain the engineering of the thing. You just wanted a good selfie. Hey! It's a majestic sculpture! And it looked brilliant with the sunset behind it. I’ve got a picture framed, you know. It reminds me of home. I miss the open skies sometimes, even with all the rain. This London smog… it’s not the same. I get that. But you enjoy living here, don't you? The job’s going well, you're getting on with everyone... Aye, the job's grand, the people are sound. It’s just… the  fuss , ya know? Everything’s so expensive.

Right then, that’s the kitchen sparkling as usual, isn't it? Lovely cuppa, thanks ever so much. Bit chilly today, innit? It certainly is. Feels like autumn’s really decided to make itself known. You've done a brilliant job, as always, Sarah. I appreciate you popping over. It's nice to have a proper chat. Oh, you're very welcome, love. Been thinking about that trial, haven’t you? The whole Depp and Heard thing. It's been going on forever. It has! Absolutely bonkers. I find the whole celebrity trial spectacle quite unsettling, actually. So much public scrutiny, dredging up all sorts of… well, not pleasant things. Though I have to admit, I did find myself following it a bit too closely. Tell me about it! Everyone at the shops' been talking about it. You can't avoid it, can you? All those fancy lawyers, twisting things around. My niece, Maisie, she's convinced he’s entirely innocent. It’s hard to know, isn't it? There’s so much conflicting information. Anyway, it’s a bit of a distraction from more important things, I think. Like, have you noticed the geese are already gathering? Oh, yes! I saw them down by the river this morning. Massive flock. Honking their heads off! They're starting their migration, aren't they? It's a sight to behold, it is. Used to see even bigger flocks when I were a girl, living closer to the Fens. Millions of ‘em, they said. Covered the skies. Not like this now though, mind you. That’s incredible! I’ve only ever seen them in smaller groups. It's fascinating, the way they navigate, isn’t it? Thousands of miles, instinctively knowing where to go. It really is amazing. My granddad used to tell me stories about the wild birds he'd spot in his garden. Sparrows, robins, you name it. He knew everything about ‘em. Said they were a good sign of things to come, if the birds were thriving. Used to have a robin that visited every morning, perched on the bird bath. Name of him was Percy. Bold as brass, he was. Would hop right up to my window. Oh, how lovely! I've been trying to encourage more birds into my garden. Put up a bird feeder, but the squirrels are very clever at getting to the seeds. They are, aren't they?

Honestly, this quiche is  divine , Anon. You’ve really outdone yourself. Proper comfort food. Glad you like it! It's Mum's recipe, you know. She'd be furious if I messed it up. So, how was the journey up from Hitchin? Traffic as bad as ever, I expect? Dreadful. Seriously, the M40 was a parking lot. Had to listen to a podcast about the history of bread just to stay sane. Wildly inappropriate for a lunch focused on… well, actual quiche. You and your language teacher brain! Always seeking knowledge, even in gridlock. Tell me, how are things at the school? Still battling with the Year 8's obsession with TikTok? Don’t even get me started. It's a constant war. They use "sus" in every single sentence. I’m trying to explain the nuance of Shakespeare, and they’re worried about whether their teacher is being “sus.” I swear, one day I'll just stage a TikTok ban and see what happens. Oh, believe me, I understand the struggle. Year 3 are currently convinced that glitter glue is a legitimate form of currency. Trying to explain fractions while dealing with a five-year-old offering me a sparkly masterpiece for a quarter… it’s draining. Exactly! And it’s not just the kids. The pressure on teachers these days is insane. I've got a candidate interview later this week for a head of department position. Absolutely terrified. Oh, wow, that’s huge! Head of department? You’d be brilliant. You're so organized and dedicated. You'll smash it. Don’t be nervous. What’s worrying you specifically? It's just... the panel. They're all seasoned veterans, you know? Years of experience. I feel like I’m still learning and I'm just… me. A language teacher from Hitchin. It’s a bit intimidating. Nonsense! Your postgraduate degree, your experience… That proves you are more than capable. Think of it like teaching a new class. You do your prep, you know your material, and you just go for it. The panel just needs to see your passion. Remember that time you practically single-handedly organised that French trip to Paris? You managed to quell fifteen teenagers' sugar rush during the Eiffel Tower visit.  That  is leadership! You’re right. That was chaotic brilliance, wasn’t it? A near-disaster averted by a well-timed bag of croissants.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. A proper catch-up and a cuppa. Cambridge is lovely, isn’t it? So much more relaxed than Lewisham. It really is. Anon’s flat is a haven. And yes, a catch-up is definitely needed. It feels like ages since we last properly spoke. So, production controller, huh? Sounds intense. How’s that going? It  is  intense. More than I anticipated, actually. It's not really the creative stuff I was hoping for after my postgraduate. Lots of spreadsheets and making sure the right bolts are going into the right widgets, you know? But the pay's decent, and it’s giving me a grounding in… well, everything. It's just… I keep thinking, is this it? Am I destined to be spreadsheet-adjacent for the rest of my days? I get that feeling. I have it about the admin job sometimes, too. Filing and photocopying… it’s not exactly revolutionising the world. Though, to be fair, someone's gotta do it, right? Do you ever think about what you  really  want to be doing? Without the practicality of needing to pay rent and eat. All the time. I used to fantasize about being a documentary filmmaker. Travelling the globe, telling important stories… But then I remember how competitive it is and how much equipment costs! It feels ridiculously out of reach. What about you? Any secret dreams of being a marine biologist or something equally unlikely? Not a marine biologist! Though I did consider pottery for a while. I’m terrible at it, mind. My attempts resemble abstract lumps more than bowls. No, I think… I think I want a bit more stability, maybe. A proper house, a garden, a dog… Not necessarily a flashy career, but something that feels…rooted. Maybe something in interior design? I’ve always had an eye for it. Interior design? That actually suits you! You always had amazing taste, even back in school. Much better than my chaotic, mismatched aesthetic. Have you looked into courses or anything? A little bit. There are online ones, and some local colleges offer evening classes. It’s daunting, though. Leaving a steady job, even one I sometimes question, to retrain… it’s a big leap. My parents keep saying, "Are you sure? It’s such a risk!" Your parents. Always the pragmatists. Mine are the same. “Get a sensible job, save your money, buy a flat.”

Honestly, I'm  fuming . Absolutely fuming. Ooh, what now, Liv? What’s set you off this time? Him again? It's not just  him , Rach. It’s… everything. He was all over Chloe at the market this morning. Like, genuinely. Chatting her up, laughing at her stupid jokes… I could practically feel my eyeballs popping out of my head. Chloe? Chloe who works at the bakery? The one who dyes her hair bright pink? Aye, that’s her. And don't you start with the "he's only being friendly" nonsense. I know what I saw. He even offered to carry her bag. My bag he  never  offers to carry! Liv, you’re being ridiculous. He’s just being polite. You’re being a right drama queen. Easy for you to say, you’ve been single since… well, forever! You don't know the sting of being stood up for, Rach. It’s not about politeness, it's about respect. And he’s not showing me any. Rach's got a point, Liv. Men are generally… less demonstrative. Especially when they're trying to be agreeable to everyone. Remember when Tom kept complimenting Sarah’s earrings at your cousin's wedding? Didn't mean he was leaving you. Tom was a creep. And this is different. This felt… intentional. He was deliberately trying to wind me up. I swear, if he does it again... I might just chuck his phone in the Seine. Now  that  would be entertainment! Don't do anything drastic, Liv. How about we just forget about him for a bit? Paris is lovely. Enjoy the macarons, the sunshine… live a little. I’m trying! But it's hard when you’re constantly thinking about being replaced by a woman with neon pink hair and a passion for pain au chocolat. You're not being replaced, Liv. You're overthinking. He probably just likes chatting to people. Remember what my mum always says? "Don’t sweat the small stuff, and everything else doesn’t matter." Your mum also says that floral wallpaper is  always  a good choice. Her advice isn’t always golden, Izzy. She does have a point, though, doesn’t she? Besides, haven't you been moaning about wanting a bit of excitement in your life? This is your excitement. My excitement shouldn’t involve feeling like I’m competing for a bloke's affections! Honestly, I wish I'd stayed home and watched reruns of 'Coronation Street'.

This shepherd's pie is absolutely lovely, isn't it? Honestly, Mark, you’ve outdone yourself. Cheers, Sarah. Glad you like it. Tried a new spice blend this time, a bit of smoked paprika. Figured it needed a bit of a kick. It  is  good, Dad. Really good. Though, I reckon a bit more gravy wouldn’t go amiss. Yeah, more gravy would be brilliant! I’m still starving. Hockey’s made me ravenous. Hockey? How did your game go, Liam? You seemed pretty fired up when you left. It was intense! We lost by one goal, though. Heartbreaking, really. We were leading for most of it, but they scored from a penalty in the last minute. Absolute agony. That's rough, son. These things happen. Did you play well? I think I did okay. Got a couple of decent tackles in. Coach said I was covering a lot of ground. So, yeah, not too bad. Did you see that save from Ben? Amazing! He practically pulled it out of the air. Oh, Ben’s the goalkeeper, right? He's always been a good one. Remember that time he saved that penalty in the regional finals? Ah, yes! Good times. Speaking of good times, Sarah, we should finally book that trip to Cornwall. Remember we talked about going last summer? Cornwall! Absolutely! I’ve been looking at some cottages online. There's a gorgeous one in St. Ives, right by the harbour. It’s a bit pricier, but the pictures are just stunning. Cornwall? Can we go surfing?! Please, Dad, please?! We'll see, Jamie. Surfing depends on the weather, and your enthusiasm! But it’s definitely on the cards. We could even visit the Eden Project. Eden Project? Sounds…educational. I’d rather go climbing somewhere. There are some fantastic climbing spots in Cornwall, love. The south coast is riddled with them! Maybe we can factor that in. Right, so Cornwall it is then. Let's look at dates. Sarah, when are you free in the next few months? Let me check my diary… Hmm, June looks a bit tight with that marketing project, but July looks good. Or even late August. July! That's when the new FIFA game comes out! I’ll need internet access for that, obviously. Naturally. The world revolves around FIFA, doesn’t it? It does! And I need to practice my new skills. I've been trying this new formation… It’s lovely to see you all so enthusiastic.

Honestly, this is breathtaking, isn’t it? I didn't realise trees could get  this  big. It feels… prehistoric. Like something out of Jurassic Park. It really is. Though, I'm not sure a T-Rex would appreciate being hemmed in by all this greenery. My neck hurts just looking up! Did you see that tiny little hummingbird earlier? It was zipping about. Yes! Absolutely incredible. I managed to snap a photo, though I doubt it does it justice. So, about Sarah… Did you hear back from her about the wedding? She's been so vague. Nope, still nothing concrete. She mumbled something about "logistics" and "venue availability." You know Sarah – she specialises in making things unnecessarily complicated. I suspect it's because Mark still hasn’t fully committed to learning the tango. Oh, Mark. Poor Mark. He looks like he'd rather wrestle a bear than attempt a tango. He insists he’s “rhythmically challenged.” Rhythmically challenged is putting it gently. Remember his attempt at karaoke at Liam’s birthday? He tried to sing Bohemian Rhapsody and… well, let’s just say the microphone deserved a medal. Oh, bless him. He’s got enthusiasm, I'll give him that. But the actual singing? Definitely not his forte. I feel sorry for Sarah, though. She’s always wanted this big, romantic wedding. I do too. She deserves it. She’s been working so hard. What about your mum? Has she booked her flights yet? I know she was dithering about the cost. She’s booked! Surprisingly. She used those frequent flyer miles she's been hoarding for years. Apparently, she managed to snag a decent deal. She’s already planning all her outfits, naturally. Five, she says, "one for each day of the celebrations." Typical Mum. She’ll be bringing enough floral prints to single-handedly brighten up the entire Californian coast. Are you worried about Uncle David and his… tendencies? Let's just say I’ve briefed Mark on the "Uncle David protocol." Which is, essentially, keep him away from open bars and strategically positioned to be near someone who can discreetly steer him towards water. Wise move. Remember that incident at Christmas with the inflatable reindeer? Still gives me nightmares. Although, I have to admit, his rendition of “Silent Night” after several glasses of sherry was… memorable. Memorable is one word for it. I’m mostly just relieved Grandma isn’t going to witness it this time.

Ah, these are good. Proper dunkers, these. Not like those flimsy ones you get nowadays. Did you lads enjoy the Kievs? I think I might’ve gone a bit heavy on the garlic, myself. Yeah, they were alright, Dad. Bit garlicky, maybe. But better than last time, when they were dry as dust. They were lovely, actually, Liam. Really lovely. You put a lot of effort in. Though, Leo, must you chew with your mouth open? Honestly! She's got a point, Leo. A bit of table manners wouldn't go amiss, would they? Especially when Granny’s coming to visit next week. She'll be watching you like a hawk. I know, I know! But it’s just… comfortable here. Granny's always going on about posture. And the way you hold a knife… ridiculous. Leo! Don’t you backchat your father! He's worked hard to make this a nice dinner. And your Granny deserves respect. Remind me again, are you looking forward to seeing her? Sort of. It’ll be boring. Just lots of questions about school and, you know, “Are you seeing anyone?” She just cares, Leo. She's worried about you, like any granny would be. Besides, you’ll get a few stories out of her. She’s finally tackled that mountain of old photo albums, apparently. Maybe you'll find something interesting. I reckon there'll be Wallies in there somewhere, that’s a certainty. Liam, please don't bring up Wallies! It’s been years. And Leo’s far too young to understand. Ah, come on, Sarah. A bit of history never hurt anyone. Brings back a few memories, doesn't it? Remember those nights down the pub…? Liam! Focus. We're talking about Granny and Leo. Did you check on the Dropbox folder for the photos I sent over of the toddler? I need to show Granny when she's here. And could you remind Leo to back them up on Flickr as well? I hate losing photos. Flicker? Dropbox? Mum, you’re such a tech head. Honestly. Can't you just print them? See what I mean? Leo needs to learn about cloud storage. Essential in this day and age. It’s like having a safety net for your memories, isn't it? Speaking of safety, did you see that rugby match yesterday? Absolutely brutal! Those lads are taking some serious hits.

Honestly, David, I’m still buzzing about that set of Shelley cups and saucers I snagged on eBay. Can you believe the price? Fifty quid! For Shelley! Fifty quid? You're having me on. Shelley's usually commands a far higher price, even with imperfections. Let me see a picture. Right here. See? A tiny hairline crack on one saucer, but otherwise, they’re exquisite. The floral pattern is just...  chef’s kiss . Think of the afternoon teas we can have! Right, right, fair enough. A hairline crack does make a difference. Still, a steal. You’ve got a knack for finding these things, you know. Like that Royal Worcester teapot last year. It's a talent! Though it does occasionally require a small fortune in postage. Speaking of finding things, I’m thinking of trying that buckwheat bread recipe I saw. You know, the one with the sunflower seeds? Buckwheat bread? Sounds…interesting. Not usually my go-to. Is it very difficult? My baking skills are, shall we say, rudimentary. Not at all! It's surprisingly easy, and supposedly very good for you. Plus, I need something to go with that lovely Stilton I picked up at the market yesterday. It'll be a proper treat. You and your markets! You come back laden with cheese and antique china. I swear, you could open a little shop. And I'd be stuck washing up mountains of teacups. Don’t be such a grump! It’s the community spirit, David. You should join me more often. It's brilliant for meeting people and finding all sorts of interesting things. I'm happy weeding the garden, thank you very much. Besides, I've got that leaving do to organise for Sarah next week. It’s proving to be rather more complicated than I anticipated. People have  opinions  about music and food apparently. Oh, yes, Sarah’s leaving. It's no good to her, is it? She deserved a promotion. You'll get it sorted though. You're a master organizer. Have you decided on a venue? We’re leaning towards The Old Mill. It’s got a nice atmosphere, and they do decent canapés. But securing the space on a Friday evening in this town is like pulling teeth. Everyone wants a party. You’ll manage. Just delegate! That’s what you’re good at. Don't try to do everything yourself.

...and honestly, the paperwork alone for this latest client is enough to drive a person mad. It's all about offshore accounts these days, isn't it? Seems everyone wants to… shield themselves. Shield themselves, aye? Sounds a bit dodgy, don't it, Uncle Dave? I’m studying law now, remember? We’re learning about money laundering and all that. It’s proper scary stuff, innit? Don’t be dramatic, Maisie. It's complicated financial regulation, not necessarily criminal activity. There’s perfectly legitimate reasons for international banking. My business operates across several borders, you know. Requires a bit of careful structuring. 'Structuring'… yeah, that’s a good word for it. Keeps things neat. Liam’s got a point. It  is  complicated, Lucy. And there’s always a grey area. My job is to navigate that grey area. Legally, of course. Mostly. Look, this client… he’s a property developer. Big developments in Spain, some in Dubai. He’s paying hefty fines over in France for some building code violations. Seems he cut a few corners. Proper mess, really. Fines? Like, how much? And building code violations... sounds like someone got greedy. Greedy’s a harsh word. Sometimes ambition clashes with bureaucracy. It happens. What sort of fines are we talking about, Dave? And what’s the structure you’re setting up to help him? Don't get too technical, though, I'm not a chartered accountant. Well, the fines initially totalled over €500,000. We’ve managed to negotiate that down to around €350,000, but it still stings. The key is moving assets… intelligently. We’re using a series of shell companies in the Cayman Islands, moving funds through various brokerage accounts... it’s a delicate dance, really. Has to look… organic. Shell companies, eh? Like, invisible companies? That’s clever. Liam! Don't encourage him. Uncle Dave, are you absolutely certain this is… wise? We’ve talked about your conscience before. Remember that trip to the Lake District and the guilt you felt after that newspaper article about those dodgy tax schemes? Lucy, darling, that was years ago. I'm much more discerning now. Besides, this is a service I’m providing. He's paying very well for it. And I’m very good at what I do. I wasn’t involved in the initial violations, I’m just cleaning up the mess. That’s a very important distinction.

Honestly, this weather is mad, isn't it? One minute sunshine, the next a proper downpour. The kids were gutted - we’d planned a nature walk this morning, but it was just a soggy mess. Tell me about it, love. I was hoping to get a bit of gardening done, but it’s been on and off all day. At least the rain's good for the garden in the long run, I suppose. Though I am starting to miss decent sunshine. It’s typical, isn’t it? Just when you think you've got a nice spell of weather, the heavens open. Still, beats a snowstorm, I reckon. Remember that one a few years back? Couldn’t get out for days. Oh my god, the traffic was insane! I was stuck on the A38 for, like, three hours. I was bringing back a huge delivery for the store, and everything just ground to a halt. Absolute chaos! We finally got it through, but it was touch and go for a while. Speaking of chaos, how's the store doing, Chloe? Still busy? Ridiculously busy. It’s the run-up to Christmas, you know? Non-stop. Honestly, the energy levels are draining. But the team’s pulling together. We’re trying to keep spirits up with hot chocolate breaks and cheesy Christmas music. Well, you've got to embrace the madness, haven't you? Is it all geared up for the big day then? Decorations and all? Absolutely! We’ve got the full works. Giant inflatable reindeer, flashing lights, the whole shebang. It’s a bit much, maybe, but people seem to like it. Too much, definitely too much. My ears are ringing already just thinking about it. All that tinsel… Oh, don't be such a grump, David! Christmas wouldn't be Christmas without a bit of over-the-top festivity. Anyway, changing the subject slightly… I've been thinking about signing up for that sign language class. Really? That's lovely, darling! Where is it, then? It’s at the community centre down the road. It's a beginners' course, so hopefully, I'll pick it up quickly. I thought it'd be useful, you know, especially with the baby coming. It could be useful for communicating with her if she’s upset, or something. That’s a really good idea, Amy! I reckon it’s brilliant. Plus, it's just a really useful skill to have.

Honestly, this quinoa is aggressively bland. Did they just… steam it? Cambridge catering. What can you do? It's more about the atmosphere than the culinary delights, isn't it? Good to see you all actually managed to find a table, though. It’s usually a battle. Tell me about it. I nearly had to wrestle Sarah from Accounts for this spot. She was guarding it like a dragon. At least the natural light’s decent. Sunlight is a precious commodity in this place. It’s not  that  bad, the quinoa. It needs a bit of seasoning, maybe some lemon. And you're not wrong about the light, Elin. I swear I turn paler by the day just working here. So, did anyone manage to get through the proofs for the Dickens biography? Tried. But honestly, the footnotes alone are a beast. Professor Harding expects  everything  documented to the nth degree. I think I aged five years just reading one chapter. Oh, Harding! He's a force of nature. My team’s been working on a corpus analysis of his recurring themes and his language usage is… complex, to put it mildly. It's fascinating, though, in a deeply frustrating sort of way. Are you finding anything particularly interesting, Chloe? Just a lot of minor factual errors. Dates don’t quite match, places are misattributed… the usual. It’s tedious but someone’s gotta do it. The sheer volume of material he dealt with is staggering, though, isn't it? It's wild to think about how much went into all those books. All the editing, the proofreading, the typesetting… and now, everything’s digital. It feels… impersonal somehow. Like there’s less care. I disagree slightly. I think the sheer speed means there’s potentially  more  care, just spread out differently. We catch things digitally that would have slipped through a typist in the Victorian era. It's just a different kind of rigor. Plus, think of the trees we're saving! That's a solid point, Mei. Though, there’s a certain romance to the physicality of a well-crafted book that’s hard to replicate. That feeling when you open a first edition and the smell… pure magic. You sound like you’re about to write a poem about old books, Amelia. Don’t tempt me! It’s a very real phenomenon. It's why my research focuses on the evolution of language in printed texts.

Right, so, Mongolia. Still feels a bit mental when I say it out loud, doesn't it? Like, Wigan to Mongolia... that's a fair bit of dosh, innit? Tell me about it. I’ve been wrestling with this visa application form for the past hour. It's a beast. They want your great-aunt Mildred's date of birth and favourite colour. Seriously. Aye, they do love making things complicated, don't they? Did you get that passport photo sorted? I went to that Boots place down the road, the one near the market. They made me do three takes, 'cause apparently, I was "not smiling enough." Like, I  am  smiling! It’s just… a very North West smile. Subtle. I know that smile! You look like you just remembered you left the oven on. Mine were awful too. I ended up just using one where I’m half-blinking. Better than looking like a right moody git, I reckon. So, visa... I'm stuck on this bit about 'intended duration of stay’. Should I be honest and say 'as long as we can keep the bikes running'? Don't you dare. Put, like, "30 days." Sounds official. We’ll just… extend it if we have to. Reckon we'll get a right grilling at customs, though. Have you heard back about any donations yet? Mrs. Higgins from down the street promised a fiver. Little bit of effort that, for her. Aye, she’s a star. Got a few promising leads on Gumtree for the rally - someone offering to print some flyers. But I'm a bit wary about posting too much detail publicly, ya know? Don't want to attract the wrong kind of attention. Need to make sure it's all secure. Good point. Maybe just a simple poster - "Charity Rally to Mongolia, all proceeds go to...” – and a website link. I can design something on Canva later. I did a decent poster for me mum's bingo night a few years back. Got quite the reputation for it, actually. Really? So, you’re a design guru now? Fantastic. On the subject of design, what about the bikes? You've been quiet about them. Are they patched up alright? I'm still having flashbacks to that time on Park Lane when yours started smoking. Don't remind me. They're  mostly  alright. I got that bloke, Barry, over at the garage to have a look.

Blimey, this room is still a state. Did you honestly sleep in your clothes again, ANON? Don’t judge, Willow! My brain shut down last night. Literally. All I remember is flashing lights and a nurse asking me which arm hurt. A LOT. Oh, Liv, you poor thing! Are you actually feeling any better today? You were so pale at the hospital. Did they figure out what caused the… the impingement? Not really. They poked and prodded, said it was probably a weird sprain, gave me some paracetamol and sent me on my way. Apparently, throwing myself across the dance floor wasn’t the best idea. Should've listened to you, Maisie, about pacing myself. Pacing yourself? Liv? That’s a new concept. It was brilliant though, wasn’t it? Seeing you absolutely  own  that dance routine. Until... you didn't. It  was  brilliant! Until gravity decided to remind me it exists. My shoulder feels like someone’s used it for target practice. Honestly, I practically crawled back here. And then the nausea hit... Here, drink this. It’s ginger and lemon, should settle your stomach. You look knackered. Seriously, you need to chill. University isn't a race to see who can be the most perpetually exhausted. Easy for you to say, Ms. ‘Always Gets 8 Hours of Sleep and Eats a Balanced Diet’. I’m living the student dream, which is apparently fuelled by instant noodles and questionable decisions. You're priceless, you are. Speaking of questionable decisions… did you see Ben from my seminar last night? He was trying to chat me up at the bar. Proper persistent, he was. Kept saying my eyes were like the sea. Really? Ben? I thought he was all study, study, study. Sounds like he's got a bit of a romantic side. What did you say? I gave him a bit of a laugh and said the sea was awfully stormy last time I looked. Then I conveniently disappeared behind Sarah. Honestly, the drama. You’d think he'd never spoken to a girl before. Oh, the tragedy! A girl rejecting your cheesy compliments. The end of the world! I had a slightly different experience last night. Remember Tom, from my chemistry lab? Vaguely. The quiet one with the messy hair? That’s the one. He… he actually started a conversation with me. Like, a  proper  conversation, not just about titration curves.

Right then, love. That was quite the do, wasn't it? Twenty-five years! Can you believe it? Seems like just yesterday we were squeezing into that little pub in York, weren't we? Yeah, it was good. Loads of people. Auntie Carol nearly knocked over the cake with her handbag, though. Aye, she did! Nearly gave your dad a heart attack, she did. He was fussin’ over that cake all afternoon. Honestly, twenty-five years and she’s still keepin’ him on his toes. Did you see Uncle Barry tryin' to join in that line dancing? Briefly. He looked like he was fightin' a losing battle against the music. Proper awkward. But he tried, I'll give him that. Did Grandma remember to take her medication? She seemed a bit… off at one point. I did keep an eye on her, petal. Gave her a little reminder when she was chattin’ with Cousin Emily. She seemed alright after that, though. Just a bit overwhelmed, I reckon. Twenty-five years is a long time for everyone to celebrate, isn’t it? I felt a bit weary myself by the time we cleared up. It was a lot. I felt bad about leaving early, but I had that revision to do for the History mock. Mr. Henderson's really piling on the pressure. Oh, aye, I know how it is. Those History teachers. Always a tough crowd. But you did well stickin' to your studies, love. It shows you're serious about your A-Levels. It’s important, isn’t it? Your future. Don't let a bit of line dancing and cake distract you from that. I know, I know. It just felt a bit weird leaving while everyone was still celebrating. Your mum kept asking when I was coming back. She did. She's got a big heart, your mum. She loved the effort you made to be there in the first place. And she understands about the revision. She's always said education's the key, hasn't she? Just like your dad. He was so chuffed to see you properly engaged, you know. Not just standing in a corner on your phone. He was. He kept telling me I was a credit to the family. Corny, but nice. So, what about the speeches? Did your dad give a good one? Last time he tried to be funny, he just ended up blushin' bright red.

Are we nearly there yet, Dad? My bum’s numb. Now, don’t start that, love. We've only been driving for, what, three and a bit hours? Cornwall’s a fair old trek. Got your water bottle, haven’t you? Don’t want you flagging. Yeah, yeah, got it. But three and a bit hours feels like forever when you’re squished in a car. Do you think we could stop somewhere for a proper break soon? Not just a petrol station. We will, love. I’m keeping an eye out. There's a Holland and Barrett just past Exeter, remember? I could pick up some liquorice root – good for the digestion, you know. Settles the stomach. Dad, please, don't bring up digestion. You know I get a bit... sensitive... sometimes. Especially when we’re travelling. IBS, remember? It's not exactly riveting conversation. Right, sorry, love. Just thinking. Want a coffee? I could pull over. Actually, yeah, that would be nice. And maybe a chocolate bar. I’m craving something sweet. Proper Milk Chocolate, not that dark rubbish. Always with the chocolate. You’re just like your Auntie Maureen. She'd eat a whole bar in one sitting. Speaking of Maureen, she's still moaning about the move, hasn’t she? Don’t remind me. The stress of her sorting out all her china... Honestly, moving house is the worst. Remember when we moved from that little flat in London to this one? I was so upset leaving my friends behind. Aye, that was a bit of a wrench. But look at us now, aren’t we lucky? This house is lovely. And think about Cornwall – sunshine, beaches, and no packed examiners breathing down your neck. You've earned a good break after those A-Levels, lass. I suppose so. I still can’t believe I got into Sixth Form. I was terrified I’d mess up the exams. You know, I read somewhere that the Egyptians used hieroglyphics to keep track of taxes. Like, seriously advanced bookkeeping, thousands of years ago! You always did have a knack for pulling random facts out of nowhere. Like that time you started lecturing me on Scandinavian folklore, the Moomins specifically, while we were stuck in traffic on the M6. Remember? They're brilliant! Have you ever seen the Northern Lights in Norway? Apparently, they're amazing. Like, shimmering green and purple streaks across the sky...

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that speech. Professor Davies really pulled it out of the bag, didn't she? Quite the passionate defense of the revitalisation project. She did. Though, I must say, I found her figures a little…optimistic. Revitalisation often promises more than it delivers, wouldn't you agree, Moira? Optimistic? Colin, darling, she was realistic! You younger generation are so cynical. When I started teaching, we built entire schools from the ground up. There was hope, a genuine belief in making things better. This project, bringing the old library back to life…it’s a symbol of that. A symbol of investing in our community. Aye, a library. Good, that. Though, I’d rather see them spend the money on the community centre roof. Leaks like a sieve, that does. My grandkids can't even use the badminton court when it rains. Gareth, you always bring it back to practicalities, don't you? But the library  is  important. Think of the access to information, the reading groups... It’s more than just a building, it’s a hub. And Professor Davies made such a compelling case. A hub that'll mostly be used for book clubs and dusty archives. I'm not dismissing the idea entirely, but the projected cost-benefit analysis seemed…stretched. Where's the money coming from, really? They glossed over that bit, didn’t they. Money always has to come from somewhere, Colin. But think of the wider impact! Increased footfall for local businesses, a sense of pride in the town… and education, of course! A vital resource for the children. We can’t lose sight of that. You know, when I was Headmistress, I fought tooth and nail for every extra book, every new computer. Education is the bedrock of everything. Bedrock's fine, so long as the roof doesn't cave in. My sister's doing a bit of volunteering down at the library now. Says it's full of people complaining about the lack of decent wifi. Fancy a library not having decent wifi. That’s a fair point, Gareth. It  does  need to be modernised, not just preserved. Perhaps Professor Davies didn’t address that enough. It needs to be a library  for  the 21st century, not a museum piece. Exactly. A digital library, integrated with online resources, that would be genuinely useful. This restoration seems more focused on aesthetics than function.

Right, so, Mother’s Day. We need a plan, don’t we? It's creeping up fast. I was thinking… Forest School seemed like a really lovely idea this year, actually. Fresh air, a bit of exploring, a picnic… what do you both think? Forest School! Can we build a fairy house, Mummy? A  really  big one! Will there be muddy puddles? I want to splash in really big muddy puddles! Absolutely, darling. Fairy houses are a must, and yes, I suspect there  will  be muddy puddles. You'll be covered head to toe! Perhaps we can bring your wellies, specifically for puddle splashing? I was picturing a little hamper with sandwiches, fruit, and maybe some cupcakes? Cupcakes  with  sprinkles! Lots and lots of sprinkles! And cheese sandwiches! Please, Mummy, cheese! Sprinkles, and cheese sandwiches it is. Right then. Okay, let's logistically work this out. Forest School usually gets busy on Mother’s Day, so we’ll need to book a slot. I’ll have a look online tonight. Do you think your Grandma would like to join us? Grandma loves fairies! She always tells me stories about them. Can Grandma splash in the puddles with me? I'm not sure Grandma would appreciate the muddy puddles quite as much as you do, sweetie, but she’d certainly love to see you having fun. Let’s check with her. It might be a bit tricky getting her there, though. She’s been feeling a bit stiff lately. Maybe we should make her a card! With glitter! LOTS of glitter! I can draw a picture of a puddle! A really,  really  big one! Perfect! Glitter and puddle pictures – brilliant ideas. I’ve started thinking about a little something for myself, too. It's silly, but I saw a tea towel with a rather amusing idiom on it. An idiom? What’s an idiom, Mummy? Well, it’s a phrase, see, that doesn’t mean exactly what the words say. Like, "raining cats and dogs." It doesn't  really  mean cats and dogs are falling from the sky, does it? It means it’s raining really,  really  hard. But… why cats and dogs? That’s a very good question! Nobody really knows for sure. It’s one of those old, funny sayings. The tea towel had “Let the cat out of the bag” on it. What does  that  mean? That means to accidentally reveal a secret.

Honestly, Sarah, I’m just… drained. Completely drained. It’s been a week since we got the news about Dad, and I still feel like I’m wading through treacle. I know, love. It’s a lot to take in, isn't it? It feels surreal, doesn't it? Even though we both knew… we’ve  always  known it was a possibility with his history. That’s the thing. He always said it would be a ‘good innings’… you know, fought so hard after Mum. And then this… this aggressive thing just… appears. It feels incredibly unfair. Mark’s taking it harder than I am, I think. He’s just retreating into himself. Mark is always more outwardly emotional. He wears his heart on his sleeve. But he's processing it, you can bet on it.
