Did you talk to him about getting some professional support? There's no shame in it, is there? Especially with everything he’s been through the last couple of years with the business. I mentioned it. He just mumbled something about needing to ‘sort things out’ and went back to staring at his phone. Classic Mark. Stubborn as an ox. I’m worried about him, though. He’s not sleeping. He’s snapping at the kids for the silliest things. That’s a definite sign he needs to talk. I’ll have a word with him. Maybe just a casual mention, you know? No pressure. I could say I was reading about mindfulness techniques and found some good resources… something like that. Distraction, maybe. That would be brilliant, thank you. What about Emily? She’s been so quiet. She tries to be strong for everyone, but I can see it’s hurting her too. She put on a brave face at the hospital, didn’t she? All smiles and reassurances. Teenage girls are good at that. But she'll need to talk eventually. Perhaps you and she could just… have a girly afternoon? Manicures, a bit of gossip… somewhere away from the house? I was thinking of taking her to that new café in Barton. They do those amazing milkshakes. I think a bit of normality might be good. It's just so hard to remember normal while everything’s like this. It is. Remember that time Dad tried to build that birdhouse for Leo when he was little? It fell apart the minute a robin landed on it.

Right, that’s the last of the grammar exercises marked. My brain feels like scrambled eggs. Fancy a coffee? Please! Absolutely. I’ve been wrestling with this bibliography for ages. It’s a nightmare, honestly. Professor Davies expects everything in MLA format, and I swear, I’ve changed the citation for this one article about five times already. Davies, eh? He's a stickler, isn’t he? I remember struggling with him on my undergrad. So, what’s the article actually  about ? Something exciting, I hope, to justify all that bibliographical angst. It's on sociolinguistics, actually – looking at the differences in politeness markers between Korean men and women. It's fascinating, really. Did you know that in South Korea, men often use very formal language even with close female friends, whereas women tend to be more casual with men? No, I didn’t! That’s brilliant. So, it’s a cultural thing, definitely, rather than purely linguistic? Heavily influenced by culture, yeah. It’s tied up with the whole power dynamic and the concept of ‘nunchi’ – you know, reading the room, understanding unspoken cues. Apparently, getting it wrong can be seriously embarrassing. Wow. That makes me think about how frustrating it is even here when people misunderstand nuances of language. Still, Korea sounds incredible. Have you ever thought about travelling there? Oh, desperately! I'd love to go to the Chuseok festival. All that food! And the traditional clothing… it looks so beautiful. I’m trying to learn some basic Korean, but it’s a beast. The grammar is completely different to English. Tell me about it! I started Duolingo for a bit, but it just felt like memorising random patterns. I think actually  speaking  with someone is the only way to really get it. Thinking about it, my Korean student, Ji-woo, mentioned a fantastic traditional market in Busan… Maybe we could plan a trip sometime? Seriously? That would be  amazing ! Although… could we afford it? Tuition fees are already swallowing a large chunk of my savings. And that new textbook I need for next term… Don’t remind me. It’s outrageous, isn't it? I'm considering looking into doing some extra tutoring on weekends to try and buffer it. Maybe even selling that old copy of  The Witcher 3  on eBay. You know I hardly ever play it anymore. Oh, you should! It’s a classic.

Ugh, this is exactly what I needed after that disastrous physics tutorial. Honestly, Professor Davies just…lectured at the board for ninety minutes straight. No questions, no engagement. Like we're robots! Sounds about right for Davies. Remember last year when he literally just wrote ‘E=mc²’ fifty times? Aye, and then just stared at us expectantly. Like we were supposed to spontaneously understand the universe. I nearly fell asleep. This pizza  is  good, though. Thanks for ordering, Maya. It's gorgeous! I’m starving. I spent the afternoon trying to wrestle with that Statistics module assessment. It's like they invented it just to make us suffer. Seriously! I’m convinced some lecturers just enjoy inflicting pain. Did anyone catch the Big Fat Quiz of the Year last night? I did! Jack Whitehall was killing it. The round about obscure facts was brutal. I felt genuinely stupid. He’s brilliant. My mate, Liam, is obsessed with him. Remember when he tried to do that impression of him at Christmas dinner? It was… something else. Speaking of Christmas, did anyone get any truly awful Secret Santa presents? I’m still traumatised by the scented candle shaped like a pug. Oh god, don't remind me! My aunt gave me a sequined boxing glove. A  sequined  boxing glove! What am I supposed to do with that? That's genuinely amazing! I got a “motivational” poster with a picture of a kitten hanging onto a branch that said “Hang in There.” That’s classic. Awful, but classic. Right, has anyone been to Sugarhouse this week? Heard anything good about the lineup? Chloe went on Tuesday, said it was rammed. Apparently, there were some decent DJs on. Thinking of heading down Friday. I’m still recovering from last week. Turns out flavoured vodka isn't a good idea when you're trying to dance. Tell me about it! I ended up attempting a karaoke rendition of Charlie Simpson's ‘Photograph’ and I don’t think I’ll ever live it down. Oh my god, really? You and Charlie Simpson? Legendary. Moving on, has anyone been following the flooding situation here? It's getting pretty serious. It is. My mum keeps sending me updates; she’s worried sick. Luckily, we're up on the hill, but some of the lower areas are awful. We should probably stock up on supplies, just in case. Remember the camping trip last summer?

Honestly, this drive feels like it's lasting a lifetime. Are we nearly there yet, love? My neck's killin' me. Nearly, yeah. Just another fifteen minutes or so. You alright? You seemed a bit quiet back at your aunt’s. Everything okay with her? Aye, she’s fine. Just… a lot, you know? Aunt Brenda’s grief is still proper raw, even after all this time. Holding onto those photo albums and cryin' over every single picture. It’s pullin’ at me, seein’ it. Reminds me of me Mam, a bit. It must be hard. She clearly adored your uncle. Did she say anything specific that struck you? Nah, not really. Mostly just talkin' to the photographs, like they’re actually listenin’. 'Remember that holiday, George?' or 'You always did love a good roast dinner, didn't ya, pet?'. Proper heartbreaking. I tried to be useful, offered to make her a cuppa and tidy up a bit, but she just kept sayin’ "leave it, lass, leave it.” Some people want to be left to feel, you know? It’s their way of processing. It's a bit like when I had to present my dissertation findings after Dad... well, you know. I remember just wanting to disappear. Aye, I remember that. You weren't yourself for weeks. Did your thesis suffer? It did a bit, to be honest. I kept second-guessing myself. My supervisor was really understanding, though. Said it was perfectly normal. Still, presenting all that work, knowing Dad wouldn't be there to hear it... that was tough. Was there anything funny at your aunt’s? A bit of a lighter moment to balance out all the sadness? Actually, there was. Your cousin, little Thomas… bless him. He was runnin' about, pretending to be a superhero, and kept yellin’ "I'm Captain Brenda-Saver!" at the top of his lungs. Oh, Thomas! That’s classic. He's got a heart of gold, that kid. He always cracks me up. He probably just wanted to cheer her up. Aye, I think so. It did give everyone a bit of a laugh, even Aunt Brenda managed a wee smile. It was needed, definitely. It's just... hard to see someone you care about hurting so much. It makes you think, doesn't it? About your own lot, your own people. It does. It puts things into perspective. Reminds you what’s important.

Honestly, this rain is relentless. It's been chucking it down for days now. Feels like Norfolk is permanently under water. Aye, it's a bit of a soggy business, innit? Remember '78? Now  that  was a summer. Sun blazin', barely a cloud in the sky. You youngsters wouldn't believe it. Don’t start reminiscing about '78, Arthur. You’ll go on for hours and we'll all be cold. It  is  awful though, raining like this. My knees are playing up something fierce in this damp. You know, weather apps are getting surprisingly accurate these days. They predicted this downpour down to the minute. Apparently, it’s not letting up until at least Tuesday. Well, thanks for that lovely bit of information, Daniel. I was hoping for a miracle. My students are complaining they can’t concentrate with the gloom pressing in on them. Bit hard to talk about Shakespeare when it feels like the apocalypse outside. Shakespeare? Fancy that. Used to have little Timothy, bless him, asking me about Shakespeare. He was a bright little tyke. Couldn’t get the hang of the language though, poor love. Always wanted stories about dragons and knights instead. Dragons, eh? Used to tell young’uns stories myself, back when…well, never you mind. Still, the football's on tonight. Norwich are playing Ipswich. Should be a good match, even in this weather. Ipswich? Really? Figured Norwich would have a better chance. Any bets? Absolutely not. I have lectures to grade and a research paper to finish. I can’t afford to get emotionally invested in something as unpredictable as football. Besides, Daniel would just bore us all with stats. Hey! I just enjoy analysing the probabilities. It’s…intellectually stimulating. Oh, Daniel. Always with the big words. You and your fancy degrees. Still can’t boil an egg properly, though. That’s a blatant exaggeration. Don’t let her wind you up, lad. Women and their cheek. Reminds me of my Doris…always nippin’ at me. Still miss her, though. I know you do, Arthur. It's been a long time. Have you been taking your medication regularly? You seemed a little…out of sorts last week. Aye, I’m alright, love. Just a bit of a creak in the old bones. The doctor says it's the rain, plays havoc with the joints, he says. Nonsense, I reckon. More likely it's this dreadful tea.

Honestly, this week has been mental. Mr. Henderson wants  everything  redesigned for the new brochure. Everything! Feels like I'm living on coffee and adrenaline. Tell me about it. Administration is a constant stream of requests, most of which are completely unnecessary. Apparently, changing the font on a single email is “vital to the company image.” Vital! Oh god, you guys always manage to find the most ridiculous things. I’m dealing with spreadsheets and targets all day. At least  my  ridiculousness is financially rewarding. Though, don’t get me wrong, the pressure is on. Big sales push next month. Sales, spreadsheets… sounds easy comparatively to Mr. Henderson's artistic whims. Remember last year when he decided all the corporate colours needed to be ‘evocative of a sunset’? Don’t remind me. I spent three days choosing the precise shade of burnt orange. And then he didn’t like it. So, speaking of big things... how are the wedding plans going, Liv? Has anything changed since the last time we spoke? Actually, yes! He finally booked the band! A local one, called 'The Renegades'. Apparently, they're really good, and they play all the cheesy 80s stuff I love. Dad's not thrilled, he thinks they’re too… energetic. Energetic is good! Dad's just being a dad. Let him be. Remember my dad's face when I told him I wanted neon green accents in my flat? He nearly had a stroke. Right? Parents. They're just… there to worry. So, when’s the actual date? Any narrowing down? June 15th! Feels so real now. Although, I’m starting to get a bit… twitchy about the whole “marriage” thing. It’s just… a big commitment, you know? Of course it is! It's terrifying, isn’t it? But a good one is wonderful. My aunt and uncle have been married for… goodness, 45 years? They're still ridiculously in love. My nan always says the secret is separate bathrooms. Wise woman, your nan. Seriously though, Liv, you seem happy. That's the most important thing. I am. Mostly. It’s just… people keep asking about kids. Like, it’s the next logical step. Do you guys want kids? Eventually, maybe. Definitely not right now. I'm still figuring out how to keep a houseplant alive. I'm firmly in the “absolutely not” camp. Too much responsibility. I like my freedom and my sleep.

This newfangled kettle, eh? Whirls about like a fairground ride it does. Never had one like it in me life. Too complicated, I reckon. Give me a good old gas stove any day. You remember those, Marjorie? Proper heat you got! Oh, I do, Arthur. Though, honestly, I preferred electric. A bit less faff, no soot everywhere. Though yours  was  always a bit temperamental, wasn't it? Remember that time it nearly blew the lights out at Christmas? Your Maggie nearly had a heart attack! I remember! I was just a teenager then, visiting for the holidays. It was quite the scene. Speaking of Christmas, my workload before retirement always peaked around that time. Marking essays, planning nativity plays... it was relentless. Did you ever have many children at yours, Marjorie? Oh, bless you, David. Loads! I ran a childminding business for years, just after Matthew left for university. A constant stream of little ones. Some were absolute angels, some… well, let's just say they kept me on my toes! Little Rosie, bless her, used to try and feed the goldfish toast. Every. Single. Day. Kids, eh? They’re a wonder, ain’t they? Maggie’s got three now, you know. Liam’s at university, Sarah's doing her A-Levels, and Tom… well, Tom's got a fascination with them computers. Spends all his time glued to that screen. Don't know what's to become of 'im. Technology, isn't it? It's moving so fast. I spent hours teaching my Year 8s about cybersecurity last term. You’d think they’d be naturally adept, but persuading them not to share their passwords was a constant battle! Do you get much technical bother, Arthur? Technical bother? Don’t even get me started! Tried to order somethin’ online the other day. Took me three hours, and I still didn’t get it. All these passwords and logins... It's a head-scratcher, it is. Young Tom tried to 'help' me. Just made it worse, the little scamp. It can be daunting, Arthur. But they  are  helpful sometimes, aren’t they? Matthew’s quite good, actually. He sets up my printer every six months, because I always manage to mess it up. It's not all doom and gloom! Absolutely. I used to feel like a tech support hotline for my colleagues, constantly fixing their printers and helping them with email.

Honestly, Arthur, it’s lovely to see you. It feels like ages since you popped over! How are you keeping? Alright, alright. Can’t complain, Annie. The bones creak a bit more these days, you know, but the mind's still ticking, thank goodness. This tea’s lovely, by the way. Proper builder’s brew. Haven’t had this good in ages. Glad you like it! I’m trying to be more disciplined about my tea-making. Last week it was all herbal infusions and I felt like I was drinking scented water. So, what have you been up to? Still battling the squirrels in the garden? Those rascals are relentless! They've started digging up the patio looking for nuts. I swear, they’re organized. I put down those bird-deterrent spikes, but they just sidestep ‘em. They’re learning. What about you? Still charming young minds with the French language, are you? Absolutely! I've got a new cohort starting next month – a real mixed bunch. Bit of everything, really. One young lad is desperate to learn so he can impress a French girl, naturally. And another wants to brush up for a holiday. It's always entertaining, seeing their different motivations. The French, eh? Lovely language. Always wanted to learn it properly myself. Never had the time, of course. Being a Managing Director tends to gobble up all available hours. You wouldn't believe the hours I used to put in. Used to practically live in the office. I can imagine. It sounds incredibly demanding. Did you ever get to travel much for work? Oh, yes. All over Europe, mostly. Germany, France, Italy… even a few trips to the States. But you know, it was always about the deal, the bottom line. Never really had time to  look  at the places, if you catch my drift. Just airports and conference rooms. That's a shame. Travel is so enriching. I always try to encourage my students to think about the culture, not just the grammar. Last year, I took a group to Paris. It was amazing to see them actually engaging with the language in a real-world setting. Ordering croissants, asking for directions… they blossomed! Sounds lovely. Honestly, I probably wouldn’t have been much use on a cultural excursion. I'd have been worrying about the exchange rate and whether the Wi-Fi was reliable. Habits, you see.

Honestly, Chloe, Valentine's Day. What even  was  that? Felt more like a social obligation than anything romantic, innit? Tell me about it, Liv! My mum went on and on about how I needed to be all dressed up, ready for a ‘potential suitor,’ as she put it. Like I’m back at school dances. It was a bit much. Did you have anything… exciting happening? Nah, not really. Liam got me some chocolates. Nice chocolates, mind, posh ones from that place near Covent Garden, but still. Chocolates. On Valentine’s. Bit predictable, yeah? Predictable but… appreciated, hopefully? My mum’s idea of romance is a massive bouquet of roses and a fancy restaurant. I told her I’d rather have a pizza and a movie night. She looked at me like I’d sprouted a second head. Oh, mums. Always the same, yeah? I reckon Liam’s mum was probably pushing for diamonds. Didn’t he mention anything about, like, proposals or anything mad? Nope. Just a lot of him saying how much he liked my new jumper. Which, fair enough, I did spend ages hunting for it in Oxford Street. Nearly got trampled by a group of lads though. Honestly, the crowds! Oxford Street on Valentine's? You're brave, girl. I stayed firmly within the confines of my flat, avoiding the drama. Speaking of which, are you going to that new cinema in the city centre? The one with the velvet seats? The Everyman? Yeah, I was thinking about it. What’s showing that you fancy? I’m still on the fence. There’s that new rom-com everyone's talking about, but it looks a bit cheesy. I know, right? Everything feels a bit… forced, doesn’t it? I was actually thinking about seeing that action film, the one with the explosions. Need to switch my brain off a bit after all the Valentine’s Day cheese. Ooh, that sounds good actually. Sometimes you just need a massive dose of action. Speaking of switching off, I’m absolutely starving. Fancy grabbing some chips from that chip shop down the road? They do a wicked gravy. Gravy chips? You’re speaking my language! Proper comfort food. But seriously, you didn't have  any  romantic gestures planned? Not even a little bit? Absolutely not. I openly declared my anti-Valentine's stance to everyone. Including Liam. He just laughed and said I was "brutally honest."

This broth is actually incredible, isn’t it? So much better than that place we tried last week. Seriously, how can a simple noodle place get it so right and some fancy restaurants miss the mark? It’s the attention to detail, I reckon. And fresh ingredients, obviously. Though I’m still wondering why I agreed to this spicy level. My mouth is already on fire. You always go for the inferno option. Reckon it's a subconscious desire for drama. Maybe! Speaking of drama, did you see that article I sent you about the council estate redevelopment in Hackney? The way they're displacing all those families… It's infuriating. I did, yeah. Absolutely infuriating. It feels… deliberate, doesn’t it? Like they're just pushing out people they deem 'undesirable' to make way for luxury apartments. Gentrification at its finest, or rather, its most cruel. Exactly! And the rhetoric they use! ‘Regenerating the area,’ ‘enhancing the community’… it’s all just code for ‘get rid of the people who can’t afford to be here anymore.’ My auntie Fatima lives nearby, and she’s terrified she'll be next. It’s the same pattern everywhere, isn’t it? London’s becoming completely unaffordable. My parents are constantly talking about how Watford's becoming a commuter town, and even  that  feels expensive now. I keep thinking about buying a flat, but it feels like a pipe dream. And if I do manage to save up, the interest rates... ugh. Don’t even get me started on the interest rates! It's just… the whole system is rigged. Capitalism, right there in action. Built on the exploitation of housing, for profit only. People should have a  right  to a decent place to live, not just those who can afford it. You and I have had this conversation a million times, haven't we? It’s just… it feels hopeless sometimes. Especially when you read about the Conservative party’s planning proposals. It's all about deregulation and encouraging developers to build whatever they want, regardless of actual need or community impact. It  is  disheartening, but we can’t just give up. I'm trying to get involved with a local housing collective. They're organising protests and putting pressure on the council. Interested in joining? It would be really helpful to have you – you know, the architect’s perspective. I don’t know… my work’s been pretty intense lately.

Honestly, love, I’m a bit of a nervous wreck about little Leo starting nursery next week. It feels… momentous, doesn't it? Like a real chunk of my life is changing. Yeah, I know what you mean, Mum. It's definitely a big step. But he’ll love it, won’t he? He’s so social. Remember how quickly he made friends at the baby group? That’s true. He did latch onto little Poppy straight away. Still, relinquishing him to strangers for most of the day… it's a strange feeling. Are you alright with him being away from me that much? You've been spending so much time with him lately. Nah, I'm good. Uni's been pretty hectic anyway, so I haven't been able to dote on him  quite  as much as I wanted to, to be honest. Plus, a bit of time to myself isn’t going to hurt, is it? Though, I'll miss him loads, obviously. Will they do loads of messy play? He loves getting covered in paint and pureéd carrots. Apparently so! They sent a list of things he’ll need - wellies, waterproof coat, spare clothes… it’s a whole new level of preparation compared to when he was a tiny baby. And the cost! Good grief, the cost of everything. Have you been looking at holidays? Something to look forward to after all this settling-in madness. Speaking of cost, I've been looking, yeah! Somewhere sunny. I was thinking Spain maybe, or Portugal. Somewhere with nice beaches. We could do a proper family trip. What about Greece? I’ve always wanted to go to Greece. Greece would be lovely. Bit more expensive though, wouldn’t it? We need to be sensible. Although, a week away somewhere warm sounds utterly divine. Maybe next summer then? Right now, I’m more focused on getting back to work. I’ve had a few emails from the office. Oh yeah, that’s daunting, isn’t it? Going back… it’s going to be a big adjustment. Are you worried about balancing work and Leo? Absolutely. That's a huge part of the nerves. I don't want to feel like I'm failing at either. I’ve been trying to figure out weaning too. He's getting so big now, stage two baby food. Is it a nightmare trying to get him to swallow lumps?

Honestly, this day has been… something else. I feel like I've been wading through treacle. Tell me about it. The charity gala was a nightmare. Half the donors cancelled last minute, and the caterers almost forgot the canapés. Typical. At least the food here looks decent, love. It smells amazing, actually. Mum, you look knackered though. What happened? Was it about the police thing? It was. They wanted a statement. A full one. Apparently, there’s been a… disagreement, let’s say, at the office. It's tedious, really. Legal quibbling over something so minor. But I had to go in and give it. Annoying afternoon. A disagreement? What kind of disagreement? Is everything alright? You seemed really stressed earlier. Oh, don’t worry, darling. Nothing to do with  you . Just corporate nonsense. Honestly, the lawyers involved are making a mountain out of a molehill. It’s already been passed up to senior management and they are dealing with it. I didn’t want to bring it up, but Emily kept pestering, so… Emily, you shouldn’t pry into things that don’t concern you. Some things are better left unsaid, eh? Oh, come on, Dad. She’s allowed to be concerned. Mum’s been looking like she’s aged ten years today. So, what WAS this disagreement about? It's about a marketing campaign. A rather disastrous one, to be honest. Let’s just say someone made a rather questionable decision regarding influencer selection. And now we’re facing… repercussions. Influencer selection? Seriously? The things people focus on. Anything truly serious? No, no, not at all. Just… paperwork. And lawyers. Lots and lots of paperwork and lawyers. Well, you’ve done your duty. Gave your statement. Let the higher-ups sort it. Now, forget about it. Have some more gravy! Speaking of things that are stressful, has anyone seen my EE phone bill? They’ve charged me for roaming again, even though I haven’t been abroad! I swear, those companies are just ripping people off. I think I saw it on the kitchen counter earlier. I tried to call them about my data allowance the other day, it was a joke. Waited on hold for an hour and then got disconnected. Honestly, customer service is dreadful these days. It used to be something they prided themselves on. Tell me about it. Trying to get anything fixed is a mission.

…Honestly, this Earl Grey is exactly what I needed. Travel’s knackering, isn’t it? Especially all that flying. Though, you’d think with Luton so close, you'd have popped over more often! Luton ain't exactly a hop, skip and a jump when you’re wrestling with brambles all day. And honestly, celebrating your marriage felt like a proper occasion, needed a trip to Bedford. Good to see you, mate. This place looks… comfortable. Very you. Cheers. Comfort’s the key, isn't it? I like to think it has a vaguely Roman vibe, you know? All the… earthy tones. Been obsessed with Spartacus recently, actually. Watch it on that streaming platform. Properly brutal, but fascinating. Did you know they used to… well, you probably know all about Roman history, you're always reading. I do dabble. More focused on the practical stuff, really. Military campaigns, siege tactics, the stuff that involves building things, moving things. Not so much the poetry, though I appreciate a good epic now and then. Spartacus – yeah, brutal is putting it mildly. Makes you appreciate modern plumbing, doesn’t it? I’ve been thinking about trying to grow some chickpeas myself, you know? Could dry them, make some houmous… Chickpeas! Brilliant idea. I’ve got a whole shelf of herbs and spices. Paprika, cumin, coriander… everything. Speaking of food, your wife – how’s she finding British cuisine? Remember that time we tried to convince her to eat a full English? She nearly had a heart attack. Oh, she’s adapting. Slowly. She’s a fantastic cook, mind. Really gets into it. She bought this mortar and pestle the other day – proper authentic, volcanic rock, she says. We've been experimenting with lots of different spices. Trying to recreate some Cypriot dishes. Speaking of adapting, I brought you something. Ooh! What's this? Stunning! It's beautiful embroidery. Where'd you get this? China! I was in Beijing last month for a landscaping job - some posh hotel, ridiculous expense account. Had a week to kill, so explored. Thought you'd appreciate the craftsmanship. Reminded me of mosaics, really, the way the threads are laid down. China! Wow. Did you get bitten by anything exotic? Malaria risk, wasn't it? You’re mad, going off-piste like that! Got the jabs. More worried about the sea lice, to be honest. Nasty little blighters. And the crowds.

Honestly, this English test felt like it was designed to make us fail. Did you see how many quotes they wanted? Like, recite Shakespeare from memory! Tell me about it! I spent ages trying to remember the one about, like, "the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune." I think I got the fortune part right, but the rest was just a blur. Mr. Davies seemed to be enjoying watching us panic, though. He totally was! He had that little smirk. It's so annoying. And the essay question! "Discuss the impact of setting on character development." Seriously? I wrote about the moor in  Wuthering Heights , but I'm pretty sure I rambled on about the weather for half of it. Ugh,  Wuthering Heights . So bleak. I much preferred our art project – that abstract landscape. I actually felt a bit proud of mine. Miss Davies said my use of colour was ‘particularly evocative’. Remember? Evocative? That's a fancy word for 'a bit messy,’ isn't it? Seriously though, I’m glad we’re not doing that again tomorrow. French is already hard enough. Madame Dubois looks like she's going to explode if anyone mispronounces ‘le chat’ one more time. Oh, I know! I nearly died when I said “la table” as “le table” last week. It was mortifying. At least the wind band is less stressful. Rehearsal was good, wasn't it? Mr. Finch reckons we’re finally getting the hang of that tricky bit in the second movement. Yeah, that's brill. I think the flutes are finally holding their own against the clarinets. Though, Beatrice keeps forgetting to breathe. It’s a bit of a disaster sometimes. She’s convinced Mr. Finch thinks she’s hopeless. Beatrice? Oh, poor thing. She needs to toughen up a bit. Remember when Liam tried to trip her last week? She totally ignored him. That was actually quite impressive. Yeah, he's such a tool. Honestly, some people. Speaking of people, have you seen Chloe with Josh lately? They're practically glued to each other. I know! It’s so sudden. I thought she was still seeing Ben. Ben’s quite gutted, apparently. I heard him talking to his mum. He's withdrawn from the debating club. Oh, that’s awful for him. Chloe can be a bit fickle, to be honest. She does whatever's trendy, doesn't she? It’s just… weird.

Och, look at that rain. Proper miserable, isn't it? Makes you want to curl up with a biscuit and a good book, doesn't it? Aye, it's chucking it down. Thought you’d be moaning about the football, Miss Thompson. How did the Magpies do, then? Don't start with me, lad. They were hopeless. Absolutely hopeless. Lost 3-1. Honestly, you'd think they were playing in boots filled with sand! Still, at least we can’t get much worse, can we? Sorry I'm late! The buses were a nightmare. This rain, you know...it just slows everything down. Lovely to see you both. Can I get a latte? No worries, Brenda. Take a seat. Always the buses, aren't they? Right, lad, put your phone away and tell your Auntie Brenda about what you were saying on the phone the other day. Something about coding? Right, well, Mr. Davies – he’s the tech teacher – he set us this project. We’ve gotta design an app for the school. He says it’s a good way to get ready for university. An app! Fancy that! What kind of app? Is it complicated? It’s not  that  bad. It’s supposed to be a timetable and notification app. So you can see your classes, reminders, the whole shebang. I'm thinking we could add a section for lost property too, that’d be useful. Good idea, that. The amount of jumpers they lose, it’s scandalous. You're getting clever, aren't you, lad? Bet your Grandad would be proud. He always said education was the key, didn’t he? Aye, he did. He didn't get much himself, though, did he? He was always saying how he regretted not sticking with school. Absolutely. Although, I always think experience counts for something too. All those years working in the old Harris factory…he learned a lot, he did. Practical stuff you don’t pick up in a classroom. True, but if he’d had a bit more… well, it might’ve opened other doors. Don’t you think, Brenda? These kids now, they've got so many more opportunities. It’s fantastic, really. Though, a bit daunting, isn’t it? All that technology… sometimes I feel like I'm living in the Stone Age. It's easy enough to learn, Miss Thompson. YouTube's your friend. Mr. Davies showed us a few tutorials.

Honestly, this discussion about genetics has taken a really odd turn, hasn't it? We started on driving, and now we're debating whether my inherited allergy to shellfish is a direct result of my great-aunt Mildred's penchant for pickled onions. Well, family history’s important, love. Me dad always said, “You are what your ancestors did, magnified.” Though, I reckon he meant that in a more general sense about character, not allergies. Anyway, speaking of multiplyin' things, look at ANON’s portions! Bit generous, ain't they? Oh, don't you start, Arthur! He needs to eat. He’s always burning the candle at both ends with that lecturing job. And he’s got that operation coming up, hasn’t he, dear? Needs to keep his strength up. Mum, I appreciate the concern, but I’m perfectly fine. And I’m sticking to the recommended portion size, thank you. It’s just…everything looks smaller on the plate than it did when it was served! Besides, I need the energy for the jigsaw later. We’re making progress on that landscape, aren’t we, Eleanor? Always bringing it back to the jigsaw, do you? It’s the one constant in this family, isn't it? But seriously, about the operation… are you nervous, ANON? It’s a big thing. It is, but the surgeon seems confident. They say it’s routine, really. Though I’m not entirely convinced about their insistence on me doing all that post-op physiotherapy exercises. Feels a bit like they're passing the buck, if you ask me. Routine, eh? Don’t let ‘em fool ya. Operations are always a gamble. I’ve seen a thing or two in my time fixing cars – people trying to cut corners, ignoring warnings... it ends badly every time. Same principle applies to bodies, I reckon. Don’t listen to Arthur, love. He’ll have you worried sick. Doctors know what they’re doing. Back in my day, you didn’t question a doctor, you just did what they told you. Things were simpler then. Less fuss. Simpler, maybe, but also less informed, Mum. We have access to so much more information now. It's crucial to be an active participant in your own healthcare. Though, I do agree, Arthur tends to lean towards the pessimistic side. You need to be more supportive. Supportin' means bein' honest.

Honestly, Moodle is trying to actively sabotage me today. I spent a good hour trying to upload these practice quizzes, and it just kept giving me error messages. Random ones! "Invalid file format" when it was a perfectly good .docx. Sounds about right. Moodle’s a beast. What's it doing now? Still throwing a wobbly about the quizzes? Yes! And I can’t figure out  why . I’ve checked the format a hundred times. It’s driving me completely bonkers. I feel like I'm speaking Klingon to it. You wouldn't happen to have any magical Moodle whispering skills, would you? Maybe a few. Though 'whispering' is generous. It’s more like furious shouting until it does what you want. Let me have a look. Where are you at? Are you trying to upload directly, or using the 'add activity' option? Add activity, definitely. I’ve always found that’s more reliable, although clearly not today. I've selected quiz, set up the general settings, and then it gets grumpy when I try to upload the actual quiz file. It’s… it’s almost like it's deliberately choosing the most obscure reasons to fail. Right. Let’s see... Okay, interesting. It's saying it's encountering an issue with the file size. How big is it? Not huge! It's only about 2.5MB. I’ve got lecture slides on there that are bigger than that. Exactly! That's the problem, isn’t it? Moodle’s become ridiculously sensitive. It’s probably something to do with their latest update. Remember last year when it refused to accept any image files that weren't .jpeg? It was a nightmare. Don't remind me! I spent a weekend reformatting every single diagram. So, what's the solution this time? Shrink the file? We could try. Sometimes compressing it helps, but I suspect it's more to do with the underlying code. I had a similar issue with a group discussion forum last week. Turns out, Moodle was freaking out about a particular character in the title. A single asterisk. Can you believe it?! Absolutely ludicrous. They really do fight you every step of the way. I'm starting to think I should just print everything out and hand it to the students. Much less stressful. Tempting, I know, but think of the trees! Look, let’s try this. Instead of uploading the entire Word document, could you save it as a .txt file?

Oh, my goodness. I genuinely thought I’d feel a little better by now. This jetlag is brutal. I feel like I’m running on fumes and the faint memory of a decent cup of coffee. You look it. Honestly, I thought you’d bounce back quicker, being you. I’m still pretty hazy myself, but at least I managed to mostly function in the toddler wrangling department this morning. How was grappling with Leo? Grappling is the perfect word. He decided the living room floor was a prime location for an archaeological dig involving all his cars and a significant portion of my houseplants. I think I unearthed a small dinosaur along the way. He didn’t want to be parted from it, naturally. Sounds about right. The tenacity of a two-year-old armed with a plastic T-Rex is a fearsome thing. Right, so, about Saturday. Did you manage to sort out tickets for  The Importance of Being Earnest ? I did! Got them. Excellent seats, apparently – row G, centre. Apparently, it’s a really clever production. The reviews were fantastic. Are you looking forward to it? It’s been ages since we’ve had a proper night out. Absolutely! I'm desperately craving some culture. And honestly, the prospect of sitting in a comfortable seat, listening to witty dialogue, and not having to simultaneously break up a Lego war is… luxurious. We should book a table at that little Italian place on Elm Street beforehand, shouldn’t we? It's been a while. That’s a brilliant idea. I’ll book that now, actually. While I'm still vaguely awake. What time should we aim for? Dinner around seven, curtain up at seven-thirty? Sounds perfect. Just promise me you won't fall asleep halfway through. I don't want to have to nudge you awake during Algernon’s monologue. I’ll do my utmost. Though, I can't guarantee anything if the jetlag truly wins. Maybe I should pack a travel pillow and a blindfold. Don’t be ridiculous. You'll be fine. Just a little bit of caffeine and a solid night's sleep tonight should do the trick. Did you see the message from Mum? She wants to come round on Sunday for lunch. Oh, yes! I replied. That would be lovely. Sunday lunch at ours - sounds idyllic. What were you thinking of making? I was thinking a roast chicken, maybe?

Blimey, this Earl Grey’s proper good, ANON. Thanks for having me over. So, you were saying about your cousin, Rana? Still in Erbil, is she? Yes, still there. It's... complicated. She wants to come over, properly settle here, but the visa situation is a nightmare. You know how it is, eh? Paperwork layered upon paperwork. She’s got a good job, teaching English at the university, really bright girl, but… Aye, I can imagine. The bureaucracy's a right pain in the backside, isn't it? My sister, she’s trying to get her Estonian fella over here, and it's been a saga. Years, practically. Politics, eh? Always getting in the way of decent folk. What's holding Rana back, specifically? Is it financial requirements? Partly that, the financial proof is a sticking point. But it’s more than that, I think. It’s the perception. They look at Kurdistan, they see instability, they see its proximity to…well, you know. Syria, Iran. They paint everyone with the same brush. And they don’t seem to understand the realities. It's not all chaos, you know? They’re building, they're developing… Exactly! And all those headlines about oil...it completely blinds people to the nuances. It's like, 'Kurdistan = Oil = Trouble.' It's a dangerous oversimplification. It's the same with Libya, isn't it? They forget the people, the lives, the desperate need for stability. You see a lot of talk about Wahhabism creeping in, compounding issues… it’s a constant worry for families. Absolutely. It's a constant worry. My parents, they still have relatives in Sulaymaniyah. It’s hard. Trying to explain the situation to people here, who just see headlines… it's exhausting. My niece, she’s fascinated by Western culture, wants to be a fashion designer. But she worries about the future, you know? What will it be like for her? It’s that generational shift, isn’t it? The young folk, they’re so much more globally aware, more connected. They want opportunity. They see what’s possible elsewhere. My own students, half of them are children of immigrants, second or third generation. They're not defined by outdated prejudices. It's just... getting them  there  can be a challenge. I’ve been thinking about moving a bit myself, actually. Oh? Where to? Out of the city. Got a bit knackered of the hustle and bustle, really.

That was absolutely delicious, Anon. Honestly, the best roast lamb I’ve had in ages. You’ve really perfected it. I agree completely. Though, I must say, I think you managed to steal a large chunk of the Yorkshire pudding, didn't you, love? Guilty as charged! They were just so good. It's silly, isn’t it? Such a simple thing, a good Yorkshire pudding, but it can make or break a Sunday roast. You know, I always say a good roast is a testament to the cook’s soul. And yours, dear, is a very contented soul indeed. Back in my day, at the school, we'd have roast dinners every Friday. Not quite as good as this, mind you, but the children always looked forward to them. Speaking of looking forward to things... Anon mentioned something about a cruise earlier. Are you seriously going through with it? I am! We booked it last week. A Mediterranean cruise. Seven days, lots of sunshine, hopefully very little rain. Oh, how lovely! Where are you going? We’re starting in Barcelona, then hitting Mallorca, Sicily, and ending up in Naples. Should be quite an adventure. Sounds dazzling. Are you taking the dog? Sadly, no. It’s too long, and the heat would be awful for him. We’ve arranged for Mrs. Higgins next door to look after him. She's an absolute angel with dogs. A good neighbour is worth their weight in gold. I was so fortunate to have neighbours at the school who were always willing to lend a hand. Though, I confess, dealing with landlords was never a pleasant experience. Tell me about it! This place we’re renting… the landlord is a character. Promised me a new washing machine six months ago. Still waiting. That's dreadful! It's so frustrating when they don't follow through with repairs. Are you pushing him again? I wrote a strongly worded email yesterday. Don't hold your breath, though. He's always got some excuse. You have to be firm, dear. Document everything. Keep copies of letters and emails. That’s what I did when the heating kept breaking down in one of the boarding houses. Eventually, they had to replace the entire system. Solid advice. It's amazing how things haven't really changed much over the years, has it? Both in terms of landlords  and  the importance of a good Yorkshire pudding.

"Right, I’m starving. Anyone else feel like they could eat a horse?" "Coming, coming! Just finished washing up. What about we order a pizza? My student loan’s just landed, so I can treat." "Aye, a pizza’d be champion. Pepperoni and mushroom, like always?" He shifts uncomfortably on the sofa, avoiding eye contact. "Pizza sounds good. Though, honestly, I’m still getting used to proper takeaway food. Everything in Germany was… different. More sophisticated, I guess." She gives a small, slightly sad smile. "Sophisticated like sauerkraut and sausages? Don't knock it 'til you've tried it, Elodie! Although, a pepperoni pizza is a pretty solid choice. Right, Chloe, what toppings are we thinking?" "Yeah, pepperoni and mushroom is a classic. Maybe add some jalapenos for a bit of a kick? And definitely garlic bread – vital pizza accompaniment." "Jalapenos are a bit too much for me. Makes my mouth go all tingly. Just keep it simple, eh?" He picks at a thread on the sofa cushion. “Alright, alright, Mr. Simple. No need to be difficult. So, Elodie, you settling in okay? It’s been a couple of weeks now, hasn’t it? Still missing home a bit?” "It's… an adjustment. Everyone’s been lovely, really. But it’s strange not having my family just down the road. And the food… oh, I miss Mum’s apple strudel something awful. It's not the same here, even though I tried to make it – total disaster, honestly." "We can order some German bits online for you. I'm sure there are shops that import things. I've got loads of links. You'll be baking strudel in no time." "Yeah, I’ll have a look too. Listen, how's the college stuff going, Chloe? Are you enjoying your A-Levels?" "It's alright. History's brilliant – obsessed with the Tudors at the moment – but Maths is proving to be a nightmare. I swear, I’m going to have an aneurysm before the exams. Honestly, sometimes I think I should just chuck it all in and open a bakery." "Bakery'd be good. You're good at baking. Better than me, anyway. I tried making scones the other day. They were like bricks." He manages a weak chuckle. "See? That’s your problem, Liam. You lack patience. Proper baking takes time! Speaking of which, Liam, any movement on the job front? Still nothing?"

Right, so the sugar’s in, flour’s in… this Victoria Sponge needs to be perfect for Year 3, doesn't it? They’re doing ‘The Great British Bake Off’ theme in literacy, remember? Is it pink, Mummy? Will it be pink? I want pink icing! Vroom! Pink racing stripes! Pink icing, alright, darling. We’ll do pink icing. But first, we need a cake! Now, Tom, please don’t race the car into the flour. Remember what happened last time? Sorry, Mummy. It's alright, sweetie. So, Year 3. I’m planning on letting them decorate their own mini-cakes. Think it'll be manageable? Or will it descend into a flour-covered chaos? A flour tornado! Exactly! A flour tornado. I did try a similar thing with Year 2 once, and it ended with half the class wearing buttercream on their noses. Buttercream noses are funny! They are, aren’t they? Though not particularly hygienic. Anyway, what do you two think? Should I give them little pots of icing and sprinkles, or just a basic buttercream? Sprinkles! Lots and lots of sprinkles! Rainbow ones! And gummy bears! Can they have gummy bears, Mummy? Gummy bears might be pushing it a bit, Tom. We’ll stick to sprinkles, I think. Now, speaking of pushing it… did you guys see what I found in Morrisons? A whole box set of "Paddington"! Remember how much you both loved those? Paddington! He eats marmalade everywhere! He's a bear! A silly bear! He is indeed. It was a bargain, so I grabbed it. Should be perfect for story time. It's almost time for your half birthday later, isn’t it? We were thinking of having a little party, just the three of us. With cake? A pink cake? Of course, with a pink cake! And balloons! We could even have a little Tomodachi Life party on the tablet to celebrate. Remember how you both liked creating your little characters? My Tomodachi is a robot! He goes  beep boop ! A robot, is it? Fancy that. Right, back to the cake. Do you think the children will appreciate all the work I’m putting in? I'm worried they'll just shove everything on and not care about presentation. They'll love it, Mummy! Because you make it so yummy! Yeah! Mummy's cake is the bestest! You two are the bestest. Now, Tom, can you go grab the vanilla extract from the cupboard for me, please?

Honestly, Mark, I still can’t believe you traded your perfectly good Golf for a… a Tesla. A  Tesla ! Perfectly good? It was ten years old, darling. And needed a new exhaust. And the sat-nav was prehistoric. The Tesla is a revelation, honestly. You just  have  to try it. The acceleration… it’s like being on a rollercoaster. Rollercoasters and cars shouldn’t be in the same sentence, really. I prefer something a bit more… grounded. Reliable. My little Fiat 500 is a workhorse. Gets me from A to B without the need for a software update every Tuesday. It's more than just acceleration, though. Think about the environment! You know I'm trying to reduce my carbon footprint. Plus, the tech is incredible. The autopilot is genuinely impressive – though I'm not letting it drive me everywhere yet. Still keeping a hand on the wheel, you know. Safety first. Autopilot? Sounds terrifying. I saw something on Facebook about a Tesla malfunctioning and ending up in a ditch. Don’t tell me you haven’t seen that. Facebook, Elodie. Facebook. You know how reliable that information is. There are millions of Teslas on the road. A single incident, blown out of proportion. And they’re constantly improving the software. They pushed an update last night that fixed a minor issue with the lane-keeping assist. It’s amazing. See, that's my point! A  minor  issue with lane-keeping assist! Shouldn’t it be perfect  before  you’re relying on it to not drive you into a hedge? And software updates? I’d rather a mechanic with a wrench, frankly. It's the future, love. Everything's connected now. My watch syncs with the car, I can pre-heat it from my phone… it's convenient! And the charging is surprisingly easy. There's a rapid charger just down the road from my office. Convenient until the grid goes down. Then you’re stranded. My Fiat runs on petrol. Petrol is  reliable . And you’re spending a fortune on electricity! It's cheaper in the long run. Lower running costs, less maintenance. Plus, I get government subsidies. It’s a win-win. Besides, I’ve recently been trying to reduce my overall online footprint. I've been clearing out old Facebook groups, you know? So much pointless clutter. Good for you. I've been a bit overwhelmed with algorithms lately.

Right, that was… unexpectedly bizarre. Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs. Honestly, I haven’t seen anything like it since I was, like, ten. It’s proper mental, innit? But I like it! I like Flint and Sam. They're brave. Brave is one word for leaping into a river of spaghetti. Though, you have to admit, the animation is pretty decent. And the concept… it’s got a weird message, doesn’t it? About, like, consumerism and overproduction? Nah. It’s about making the best of things, I think. Even when all you get is pudding. And pies. Loads of pies. You’re probably right, love. Simpler explanation is always better. Still, that whole factory churning out food… bit dystopian, yeah? Like, we’re creating too much, and it’s all going to go wrong. It's just… funny! See, when the meatballs fall, they make a big splash! They do, don’t they? Right, fancy another drink? I’m proper parched after that shift. Absolute chaos at the garden centre today. Goths wanting gnomes. Honestly. Can I have a lemonade? Please? And can you stop talking about gnomes? They're creepy. Alright, alright. Lemonade it is. Blimey, whose remote is this? It feels like it’s got a million buttons. Do you know how to turn the volume up? You press the one with the plus sign, silly. It's right there. Crikey! Right, got it. Sorry. Bit loud. You know, it's funny, I was thinking about work today. It's just… repetitive. Like, I'm selling plant pots and gardening tools to people who clearly haven’t got a clue what they’re doing. My history teacher said work's always repetitive. But it’s how you make it fun. She's really into feminism, you know. She says we need to prove that girls can do anything boys can do, but like, better. She does, does she? That's a strong message. It's good to hear young people talking openly about that stuff. I think things have changed a lot since I was your age, even. Although, there are still some proper silly attitudes out there. Like what? Oh, you know... people who think girls shouldn't be interested in science or maths. That kind of thing. It’s ridiculous. Like, look at Sam in the film. She’s inventing stuff, problem-solving… She’s brilliant!

Right then, Barry. So, you managed to snag a cab all the way out here to Joensuu for this conference? Bit of a trek, even for a seasoned Liverpool driver, eh? Aye, Dr. Schmidt. It were. But ANON's paying, so can't complain. Plus, always good to get out of Liverpool for a bit, see a different place. Finland’s…well, it’s a bit quieter than I'm used to, that’s for sure. Heard you were giving a talk on the influence of post-war anxieties on Eliot’s work. Sounds heavy! Heavy is one word for it. Trying to unpack the layers of disillusionment, isn't it always? Speaking of disillusionment…what’s your take on things over home? The politics, I mean. It's become rather… fractious, hasn’t it? Fractious? That's putting it mild, mate. Absolute shambles, to be honest. Remember when New Labour were in? Tony Blair, seemed like he knew what he was doing. Kept things relatively stable. Now? Don’t even get me started on this current lot. Indeed. There was a certain optimism, wasn’t there? A genuine feeling of progress. Blair’s legacy…it’s complex, of course. But the sense of purpose, the belief in possibility… it’s largely evaporated, isn’t it? Do you think Brexit played a significant role in all of this? Massive role. Huge. Blamed it on the politicians, I did. None of 'em were honest about what it'd actually  mean . Promised everyone the world, then… well, look where we are now. Prices going up, businesses struggling, and everyone shouting at each other. My fares are higher, that’s for sure. People are grumbling more. Used to be, folk would just chat. Now, they're staring at their phones, worrying about bills. A sadly familiar narrative. I’ve noticed the same sort of… resignation, in my students. They no longer possess the naive faith that things can be improved with sheer willpower. They see the system as rigged, impenetrable. Rigged is a good word for it. It's like, the richer they get, the more rules they make to keep it that way. They're all in it together, aren’t they? Politicians, big businesses...same old story. You know, it's fascinating how a shared sense of disillusionment can transcend class boundaries. I’m lecturing on modernist literature, analysing the existential angst of the privileged, while you’re driving fares and witnessing the anxieties of working-class families.

Right, so I’ve been going through some of these BNC recordings… Honestly, it's fascinating how much regional variation still pops up, even in seemingly standardised spoken English. I found one from the 80s where a bloke from Norfolk was practically unintelligible to me. Norfolk, eh? My nan used to holiday in Norfolk. Always said they spoke a different language. Are you doing it for work, then? This language research stuff sounds proper interesting. Yeah, it is. We're trying to visualise language change over time, and the BNC’s a goldmine. Though, I’m trying to get my head around using LinkedIn for recruitment side projects – feels a bit… corporate, doesn’t it? I’m not sure I'm selling myself properly. LinkedIn's a necessary evil, love. Just treat it like a professional peacocking platform. Flash your feathers, you know? Easy for you to say, ANON! You've never had to write a professional summary. So, what's been keeping you busy? Still editing away at those travel blogs? Yep, still editing away. It’s a bit repetitive sometimes, but I got a really good write-up on this small island in the Maldives. Apparently, the sunsets there are life-altering. I’m ironically jealous of all these people travelling. Maldives! Ooh, amazing. I've never been. Flying is still my nemesis, you know? The thought of being that high up… makes me sweat. I completely get it. My cousin’s terrified of flying. But she ended up going to see the whales in Iceland a few years ago and absolutely loved it. Said it changed her perspective. Maybe you could start smaller? A quick hop to France? France sounds sensible. Actually, I've been thinking about a trip to Spain. I haven't been since I was a teenager and I really need to just… disconnect. No work, no research, just paella and sunshine. Spain’s brilliant. Seville's got to be done. And tapas, of course. Don't forget the tapas. Seville! Good shout, ANON. I actually did a little freelance work for a company based there last year. The vibe was lovely. Have you seen those Pug accounts on Instagram? They're hilarious. Oh my god, yes! Little Winston is my absolute weakness. I spend far too much time scrolling through pug photos, I admit. It's a much better distraction than thinking about flight paths.

Right, so, I’ve finally booked in for the sleeve. Full sleeve, yeah. Proper commitment. Full sleeve, eh? You're really going all in, aren't you, Liam? You haven't mentioned a single reservation about your student loan repayments lately. Seems like body art’s taking priority. Don't start, Mum. It’s a bit of a well-deserved treat, alright? And it’s really thoughtful, actually. The design has loads of meaning. Birds, branches... represents moving on, growing, all that. Bit cheesy, innit? Cheesy and expensive, I imagine. What are you having for dinner tonight? Smells amazing. You’ve finally mastered a decent Pad Thai. Yeah, I watched a load of YouTube tutorials. Think I've got the hang of it. You bringing anything over? I was thinking we could crack open that bottle of Pinot Grigio you bought last week. Absolutely. I'll grab some mangos from the market as well, they’ll be perfect. So, moving on from your lavish tattoos... how are things at uni? Still drowning in essays? Less drowning, more… gently bobbing. They’ve thrown the interns at us now, though. A nightmare, honestly. There’s this one girl, Bethany, who thinks she’s the next Zadie Smith just because she wrote a mildly clever short story in sixth form. Oh, dear. I know that type. They exist in abundance in my world, darling. Keen to impress, zero actual skill. Just remember, everyone starts somewhere, even if they’re irritating. Easier said than done when she’s asking me to fact-check her prose about the existential angst of house plants. That’ll be Chloe. Right on time. Liam, could you get that and keep the door open, please? Cheers. Chloe! Come in, come in! You’re looking… festive. I am! I went a bit mad at the Christmas market, I'll admit. Thought I'd bring you both some early festive cheer. Gingerbread scented everything! And some ridiculously twinkly fairy lights. Chloe, you’re a lifesaver. I'm completely behind on Christmas prep this year. The house renovation ate all my free time, you know. Seriously? How's the renovation going? Still a chaotic mess? A considerably more chaotic mess than anticipated, actually. The plumbing's decided to stage a revolt. It's costing a fortune. But nearly there, hopefully. Just needs the kitchen tiling. You're a saint, Mum, putting up with all that.

"Right, nearly there! I think this Korma needs just another five minutes. Honestly, ANON’s kitchen is lovely, isn’t it? So much brighter than mine. I'm still battling with that hideous wallpaper in the hallway." "It is nice. A definite improvement from the last owners, I hear. And the light is amazing. Though, you know, I'm not entirely convinced about this Korma. Are you sure it’s not a little… creamy?" "A little? It's practically swimming in coconut milk! But that's the point, isn't it? It's supposed to be rich. I was trying to recreate that dish from that little place we went to in York last year. Remember? The one with the ridiculously good naan bread?" "Oh, absolutely! The 'Spice Merchant' wasn't it? Yes, divine. I’ve been trying to find a decent curry house in Birmingham that comes close, but no luck so far. Everything’s either too spicy or tastes suspiciously of tinned tomatoes." "Exactly! Which is why I’m attempting culinary greatness at home. It’s a disaster waiting to happen, probably, but at least it's  attempted  culinary greatness. Have you been managing to get to those Pilates classes you mentioned?" "Actually, no. Life’s been a bit hectic at work. The editor's on the warpath about something or other, deadlines are looming… the usual. I’m feeling rather stiff as a result. I did manage a quick walk around Cannon Hill Park last weekend, though. Perfect for a bit of fresh air." "Cannon Hill’s lovely. I should really make more of an effort to go. I've been so caught up in lesson planning and grading papers. It’s all terribly dull, isn’t it? Particularly the A-level grammar rules. Honestly, they'd rather be on TikTok." "Tell me about it. Maintaining engagement with teenagers is a universal struggle. Speaking of which, I saw this amazing article about sustainable travel. It was highlighting eco-friendly resorts in Costa Rica. Completely sparked an urge to escape." "Costa Rica! That sounds incredible. I've been dreaming of somewhere tropical. My sister went to Bali last year and sent the most gorgeous photos. Though, the flights... honestly, the carbon footprint is a bit worrying, isn't it?" "That’s what the article was focusing on! They were suggesting offsetting carbon emissions, choosing direct flights, supporting local businesses...

Honestly, I’m still reeling from Marcus's email. Saying he’s 'taking a sabbatical' to learn pottery in Jingdezhen? Seriously? Marcus always was a bit…eccentric. Pottery, though? I didn't peg him as having a creative bone in his body beyond writing academic papers. Exactly! I thought he was going to declare he’d joined a monastery or something. Jingdezhen! It's like the pottery capital of the world. He mentioned something about really seeking 'inner peace' through the molding of clay. Inner peace through clay? That's a new one. Remember when he couldn’t even figure out how to properly load the dishwasher? Oh, don't remind me. It was a constant source of minor aggravation. Still, good for him, I suppose. Taking a leap. Though I do wonder how he’s going to explain it to his parents. They’ll be horrified. They’ll probably assume he’s having a mid-life crisis and bought a motorcycle. Which, knowing them, they'll then lecture him about the dangers of. Precisely. I’ll have to send them a carefully worded email myself, explaining that he’s engaged in artistic and spiritual exploration. Ugh, the language alone… You’re far too diplomatic for that. I’d just tell them he’s finally lost it. Did you manage to finish marking those essays? I was drowning in them yesterday. Just about. That student, Liam Davies, really pushed me to the limit. His argument about post-structuralism in Chinese poetry was… ambitious, to put it mildly. Utterly impenetrable, actually. Always a challenge, isn't it? Trying to decipher what students  think  they’re saying versus what they are actually saying. Absolutely. Though, on a completely different note… my toe nails are a disaster. Seriously. I’ve been neglecting them something fierce with all the marking. A disaster? That's a new crisis to add to the Marcus/pottery situation. I know, it's ridiculous. But they're thick and rough, and I just haven't had time to do anything about them. I’m thinking a proper pampering session this weekend. Possibly involving a foot soak and a lot of cuticle oil. Sounds divine. You deserve it. Speaking of friends, did you hear from Chloe? She sent me a postcard from Nepal. The mountains were incredible, apparently. Oh, fantastic! I need to write back. I was so worried she’d be miserable trekking alone.

Honestly, Mark, I still can't believe you actually  bought  into that documentary about lizard people running the government. Come on, Eleanor, you're a language teacher! You deal with people believing all sorts of things. A little conspiracy never hurt anyone, does it? It’s just… entertaining. Besides, they had some serious "evidence." Evidence presented by a guy who looks like he hasn't slept in three weeks and quotes ancient Sumerian texts! It was sensationalist fluff, Mark. Pure, unadulterated fluff. I watched it with Dad, and he was shaking his head the whole time. Dad’s a bit of a cynic, isn't he? He'd dismiss the moon landing as CGI if you gave him half a chance. Look, it just got me thinking. All these powerful people… don’t you ever wonder if there's something… more at play? Of course, I wonder about complex power dynamics. It's part of teaching history! But I'm not going to attribute it to reptilian overlords. Speaking of powerful people, did you see what happened with Leo DiCaprio and that new actress? The tabloids are having a field day. Oh, the gossip rags. Trying to avoid those. Honestly, the relentless scrutiny celebrities face is appalling. Remember when Kate Middleton’s sister, Pippa, was everywhere? It felt brutal. It did. But a lot of it is self-inflicted, isn't it? Choosing that level of visibility. Though, I do feel sorry for them. I’d never want that level of attention. I prefer my quiet life teaching French to slightly grumpy teenagers. Grumpy teenagers? Sounds idyllic compared to dealing with quarterly reports and boardroom politics. My week has been a nightmare. We're trying to merge with a smaller tech company, and the due diligence is a beast. It’s all spreadsheets and projections and… ugh. Sounds stressful. You need a holiday. Somewhere far, far away from spreadsheets. Have you even thought about going anywhere? I’ve started looking. Somewhere with sunshine, definitely. Thinking about Greece. Sarah and I were talking about visiting Crete. Though, finding a decent childcare arrangement while we're away is proving tricky. Thomas is at that age where leaving him for more than a weekend feels like pulling teeth. I completely understand. Lily's the same. It's funny, isn't it? You spend years wanting a bit of peace and quiet, and then you feel guilty for wanting it.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? This motorway’s just grey. Everything's grey! Even the sky's a bit grey. Now, now, Elara. We've only been on the road a few hours. Cornwall's a fair distance. And it ain't all grey, lass. Look at those wildflowers by the verge, see? A bit of yellow there, a bit of purple... It’s not exactly Jamaica Inn weather though, is it? All dramatic and stormy. Jamaica Inn? You’re gonna make me read that, aren't you? I'm already dreading it. All that smuggling and fog. It sounds bleak. Is it better than The Wizard of Oz? I’m still obsessed with Dorothy and the ruby slippers. Better? Different, love. Think about it – one's a fantastical adventure, the other's a bit more grounded in reality, albeit a dark one. Though, I reckon both have a bit of magic about 'em. Did you know Daphne du Maurier, who wrote Jamaica Inn, lived not far from here back in the day? Really? That’s a bit creepy. Speaking of things a bit creepy, remember that Sherlock Holmes story you read me when I was little? The one with the… what were they called? The speckled band? Gave me nightmares. Aye, the Speckled Band. A good ‘un, though. Clever stuff. Reminds me a bit of Lewis Carroll, really. Both twisting logic and having a bit of fun with it. You ever read  Alice in Wonderland  properly? Not just the bits at school. I’ve tried. It's... weird. All riddles and nonsense. Like, what does a rabbit have to do with anything? I prefer something a bit more straightforward. Maybe a fairytale? Like Cinderella? Fairytales are good, lass. But even they have their layers, don’t they? All those subtle instructions… Do this, or the fairy godmother vanishes! It's all about following rules, isn’t it? Similar to how they used to send messages. Remember when they used telegrams? Telegrams? You’re dating yourself, Dad! What were they like? Did they do emojis? Emojis? No, love! Just words. Very few words. You had to pay by the letter. It was all about brevity, see? Like Morse code. My granddad used to be a telegraphist. Says he could tap out messages in his sleep. Morse code! Blimey. How did they even do that? And braille, too? It’s amazing how people communicated before phones and texts.

"Aye, this is a right grand place, Anon’s home is. Proper cosy, isn't it? Feels a world away from Sunderland, that's for sure. Never thought I'd see Somerset, truth be told. What did you make of the drive, Dad?" "The drive? My dear girl, the drive was an event. All these new bypasses! When I was a lad, you’d be pottering along for hours, dodging lorries. Timperley to London used to be a full day’s trek. And the petrol stations! They had bell pushes you'd ring to get someone to serve you. Fancy that, eh? A bell push! None of this self-service nonsense." "That's fascinating, actually. The history of service stations is quite a niche area of transportation studies. They evolved from basic roadside stops catering to horse-drawn carriages, obviously, but the shift to self-service really accelerated with the rise of the motorway network in the 50s. It was all about increasing throughput, you see…" “Throughput, eh? Sounds a bit like managing a corpus, doesn’t it? Just different kinds of data. Though I doubt I'll be dealing with bell pushes any time soon!” "Corpus? What's a corpus, lass?" “It’s, well, it’s a large collection of text or speech used for linguistic analysis. Think of it as like, a massive database of words. I check it to make sure everything's consistent, you know, spelling, grammar. Tedious work, but someone’s gotta do it.” "It's incredibly important for natural language processing - powering things like chatbots and translation software. Very relevant in my field, actually. We use corpora to train algorithms for simulating materials behavior under stress. It’s…a surprisingly similar principle, really - understanding patterns within a large dataset.” “Simulating materials… Sounds a bit like inventing things, doesn’t it? When I were with BT, we weren’t inventing much. Just connecting people. Though in the war, of course, everything was about communication. Morse code. It was critical! I remember those blackout curtains...you couldn't see a thing if you looked out the window at night.” “We were just learning about rationing in school. It’s hard to imagine being without so many things. Did cinema prices go up a lot during the war?” "They did, significantly. But cinema was a vital escape during those years. It was one of the few mass forms of entertainment available.

Right, Mum, I think I’m finally starting to feel less like I’ve been run over by a truck. Jet lag is a beast, isn't it? Three coffees and still battling it. Oh, love, you look dreadful. Sit down, sit down. Have a biscuit, they’re shortbread - your favourite. And don't worry about the jet lag, it’ll pass. Honestly, coming all the way from Japan, you’re a marvel. So, you managed to get everything sorted with the flat, then? Did you remember to pack the photos of Grandad? Nearly sorted. The landlord’s doing the final inventory check tomorrow, so fingers crossed. And yes, I’ve got the photos! They're safe and sound in my carry-on. I was a bit panicky about leaving them behind, you know? It felt...wrong. Are you sure you don't want me to give you a hand with that horrifying pile of boxes in the spare room? We could make a decent start. Oh, don’t you bother about that, pet. That’s my project for the next few weeks. It’s mostly old Christmas decorations and things I swore I’d use. Honestly, I'm surprised the floor hasn't collapsed under the weight of it. Speaking of projects, have you thought any more about… well, about you and Liam? Mum! Must you? It’s far too early for the 'wedding talk' again. We're happy as we are, you know. Besides, jet lag makes me susceptible to emotional manipulation. Oh, don’t be daft. I’m not manipulating you! I'm your mother. It's my job to subtly pressure you into finding a suitable life partner and producing grandchildren. It’s in the job description! Seriously though, Liam seems lovely. You’ve been together for ages now and I adore him. Just...think about it. I  am  thinking about it. Honestly. I’m just… thinking about a lot of things right now. Moving, work, jet lag, you badgering me about marriage… It's a bit much. By the way, remember Uncle Barry telling that ridiculous story about catching a weaver fish on holiday in Cornwall? Honestly, it was wild. Apparently, it tried to bite him! Oh, bless him! Barry and his tall tales. Yes, I remember! He always did have a knack for embellishing things. You know, he went on about how it nearly took his finger off.

Look at ‘em, eh? Just munchin’ away on those leaves. Proper zen, innit? Makes you wish you could just photosynthesize instead of dealin’ with petrol prices. Absolutely. Though I'm not sure my complexion would handle a purely chlorophyll-based diet. And speaking of dealing with things… did you see that article about the A-Level reforms? Honestly, it's just more instability for the kids. Aye, I did. Mad, isn’t it? They’re changin’ the goalsposts again. I remember when I was doin’ A-Levels in Sunderland, the pressure was already intense. This just adds another layer of stress. It feels like they’re constantly tinkering with the system without properly considering the long-term effects. Exactly! Especially considering the disruption of the last couple of years with the pandemic. It's hardly fair to pit them against each other after that. I was reading about how universities are already struggling to assess applications properly. Right? It's gonna be a right mess. Speaking of struggle...have you heard anything about the NHS? My nan was in hospital last week, just for a routine check-up, and the waiting times were ridiculous. She were proper fumin’. I have. It’s bleak, isn’t it? I feel so guilty, I’m using a private GP when I can just to avoid the waiting list for simple things. It shouldn't be a privilege, should it? It really highlights the cracks in the system. Funding, staffing shortages… it's a perfect storm. It is. And it’s terrifying, to be honest. What’s gonna happen if somethin’ proper serious happens? I mean, look at this documentary – nature's got its challenges, sure, but at least it’s not actively engineered for chaos! A fair point. On a slightly lighter note… what do you think of my new haircut? I got it trimmed this morning. It looks… shorter! Nah, seriously, it’s better. It suits you. You were lookin’ a bit like a professor, you know? This is a bit more… approachable. Though, maybe invest in some gel if you wanna keep it tidy. That’s the plan! I’m trying to channel a slightly less academic vibe. Actually, I was thinking about experimenting with different styling products. What do you use for your hair? You always look so effortlessly stylish. Oh, stop it! It’s mostly just sea salt spray, honestly.

Right, I’m officially declaring myself a nicotine addict. Uni life is just…stressful, innit? Especially with that history essay looming. Black Plague, honestly? Who even  chooses  to write about the Black Plague? Aye, don't make me start on the essay. Professor Davies is mad, dead mad, for setting it. Black Plague! Like there wasn’t enough misery in history to write about. And you, Sarah, lighting up like a bonfire. You promised you were cutting down. Honestly, Sarah, you’re making the room stink. And cutting down? You've been saying that for a month! Look, I get it. Essay stress, lectures…but that’s not a sustainable solution. Think about your lungs! Tell her, Chloe. She’s going to be wheezing by Christmas at this rate. Though, I sympathise. My economics readings are just as bleak. It’s all supply and demand curves and… I don't even know what half of it means. Makes me want to join the Plague victims, frankly. Less complicated. Easy for you to say, Gemma, you're practically a genius at economics. I tried explaining derivatives to my mum the other day, and she looked at me like I’d grown a second head. Anyway, what about  your  budget, Gem? Heard you were complaining about being skint last week. Don't remind me! Rent is ridiculous in Leeds, and I’m working at the coffee shop like, ten hours a week. It’s barely enough to cover the essentials. I’m seriously considering raiding my gran's emergency biscuit stash. Tell me about it! I'm picking up extra shifts at the bakery, but between rent, books, and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, I’m living on beans and toast. At least the biscuits are homemade! It's just so unfair, isn’t it? We’re all working our socks off, and it still feels like we're constantly running on empty. Do you guys ever feel like… the system is rigged? Like, corporations are raking in billions while we’re all struggling? Now you're talking. That's why I was reading that article about intersectional feminism the other day. It's not just about equal pay anymore; it's about dismantling the whole power structure, isn’t it? It  is  rigged, Chloe's right. Just the way it's built. Aye, proper set up to keep us down.

It’s just… stunning, isn’t it? Makes you feel quite small. It does. Though, I’m having trouble appreciating the vastness right now. I've been thinking about something, actually. Something a bit… heavy. Oh? Everything okay? You’ve seemed a bit preoccupied all morning. California sun usually works wonders for mood, you know. It usually does. It's just... I’m starting to feel like I need to… I don’t know… scale back some of my friendships. Scale back? You mean like, less frequent coffees? Not a particularly radical idea, honestly. Lots of friendships ebb and flow. It's more than that, I think. There’s this one in particular… Chloe. We’ve been friends since university. And she's... exhausting. Every conversation is a competition, a complaint, or an attempt to one-up me. I feel drained after even a short phone call. Oh, I know that feeling. It's like constantly needing to recharge your batteries  after  seeing them. With people like that, it's hard to build anything meaningful. Exactly! And the thing is, I feel guilty. We've got years of history. And I know she’s going through a tough patch, which makes me feel even more awkward about wanting to distance myself. Guilt is a tricky thing. It's a natural response, especially when long-term friendships are involved. But you have to ask yourself, is maintaining this friendship  for her  or for you? It shouldn’t be a purely altruistic decision. That's what I’m struggling with. Everyone keeps saying, "Just be honest!" But being blunt feels… cruel. What do you even  say  without hurting her feelings? You don’t necessarily need to lay it all out. Grey rocking is a good technique. You become utterly uninteresting and unresponsive to her drama. Short answers, no emotional engagement. It’s surprisingly effective. I used it with a particularly demanding relative once. It withered the conversation quickly! Grey rocking… I like that. Sounds a bit like a storm-weathering strategy! But what if she brings it up? What if she asks why I’m being so distant? That’s where you have to be prepared with a simple, vague response. Something like, "Life's been pretty hectic lately, and I've been focusing on my own priorities." You don’t need to offer elaborate explanations. Keep it about  you , not about her shortcomings.

Right, so Professor Davies really laid it on thick this morning. Said my dissertation proposal was ‘intriguing, but lacked demonstrable rigor.’ Demonstrable rigor!
