Like I’m supposed to conjure it out of thin air while I'm chowing down on beans on toast. Oh, academic pronouncements. Always a drama, aren't they? Don’t let it get you down, darling. They love to sound important. What's the topic again? Something about Victorian social reform and the theatre, wasn’t it? Yeah, exactly. Focusing on how the music hall challenged societal attitudes. It's good stuff, I think! I've got a mountain of primary research—playbills, contemporary reviews, even correspondance from some of the performers. But he wants…more. He wants a spreadsheet outlining influence per performance. Seriously! A spreadsheet? Heavens. They weren’t thinking about spreadsheets when these brilliant artistes were captivating audiences. Sounds terribly…dry. Remember when I used to get those sorts of battles with the gallery owners? “The colour palette is too bold, Anya! It needs more… beige.” Beige! That’s brilliant. I'll have to write that down. It's just... frustrating. I feel like I’m doing all this work and it’s just never enough. Especially when I'm trying to balance it with Grandma Elsie's birthday coming up. Did you book the table at The Ivy for her? I did, dear. Saturday, as requested. She’s been going on about their soufflé for weeks. Honestly, sometimes I think she enjoys the pretence more than the actual eating. Though, I must say, their soufflés  are  rather exceptional. Have you spoken to your Aunt Clara recently? Not properly, no. She’s still in Florence, isn’t she? Finding inspiration for her… pottery? Is it still pottery? Last I heard she was experimenting with bronze. Bronze now, yes. She texted me a picture this morning. A rather abstract sculpture of a pigeon, apparently. She says it’s a commentary on urban displacement. Right. Classic Aunt Clara. Remember that clay gnome she made for Mum’s birthday? It looked like it was actively trying to escape. Oh, that horrific gnome! It did have a certain… pathos about it. But that’s what I admire about Clara. She’s not afraid to be… unconventional. You should go visit her, you know. A few weeks in Italy would do you good. Get away from Professor Davies and his spreadsheets.

Right, so, we’re still aiming for Tarnow by, what, six? That's a pretty good chunk of driving still. I’m starting to feel peckish, actually. Should we grab something before we hit the gym? I was thinking maybe a pierogi place. Six sounds…ambitious. But yes, something to eat would be lovely. My stomach’s been grumbling for hours. Though, I do worry about stuffing ourselves before a workout. You know, it’s really quite counterproductive, isn’t it? Counterproductive maybe, but delicious is a pretty powerful motivator. And hey, a little extra fuel never hurt anyone. Besides, haven't you been saying you need to build muscle? Pierogi aren't exactly protein shakes, granted, but… You're incorrigible, you know that? Alright, fine. Pierogi. But just a small portion. I don’t want to be lumbering around the gym like a walrus. I'm finding this whole journey surprisingly exhausting, you know. So much  doing . Yeah, I get it. Travel is tiring even when you’re not, you know, wrestling with a campervan half the time. And are we still on for the weights class? I looked online, it’s mostly guys, ironically. Ironically? Why? Well, it just seems…particularly in strength training, it’s mostly fellas. I was thinking, it would be nice to be in a class where there are a few more women. It's often intimidating, just surrounded by all those big muscles and grunts. It is, isn’t it? That whole culture – the emphasis on sheer power, the competitiveness… I remember when I was younger, attempting to join a weightlifting club… it was rather… unwelcoming. I was constantly being given unsolicited advice, most of it rather condescending and, frankly, laced with a bit of patronising sexism. I gave up pretty quickly. Oh, that’s awful. Did they… did they treat you badly? I hate the thought of anyone feeling like that. It's just so unnecessary. Not overtly, no. Nothing blatant. But the cumulative effect was…discouraging. It's subtle, isn't it? The assumption that you're not  serious  because you're a woman. The constant need to justify your presence, to prove you belong. It's a tiresome performance, really. Yeah, it is. I've noticed it too, even in smaller gyms. Like, a guy might offer advice with a wink, like he's doing you a favour. Or just…making a show of lifting heavier than you.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s glorious sunshine, the next it’s spitting again. Right proper muddle, it is. Could be anything down there now, the slugs'll be havin' a field day. Aye, lass, you’re right about that. Always is unpredictable round 'ere. Remember that summer of '68? Never saw rain like it. Flooded right down from the moors, it did. Remember Mrs. Higgins’ prize roses? Gone in a blink. I’ve only got photos of the 68 roses, nan. Not the living articles! Though the delphiniums are blooming lovely this year, aren't they? I did get a new batch of those hand-thrown mugs in from that potter in Haworth. Thought you’d like one. They’re good for a proper cuppa, you know, keep it warm. Ooh, they’re lovely! Really sturdy. Like they could survive anything. A bit like me, eh? I’ll take the blue one, please. Always did love blue. Reminds me of the cornflowers we used to pick as kids, down by the canal. Course, nan. Fancy a top-up? I've got oat milk today. You alright with that? The cow’s milk seems to give you a bit of trouble, doesn’t it? Oat milk's fine, dear. Better than nothing. Used to get proper milk in the mornings. Delivered by Mr. Farnsworth in his electric float. Remember them? Big, blue things, they were. Now it’s all self-service, isn’t it? Just not the same. No, it isn’t. Everything’s rush, rush, rush these days. Still, at least we can sit here and put our feet up. Did you see that article about the Footlights Festival? They're having it in Saltaire again this year. Might be worth a look. Footlights… oh, those amateurs! Saw some of ‘em last year. Bit loud, they were. Though that young lad playing the trumpet… he had something about him. Reminded me a bit of young Michael. That’s right! You used to tell me about him. He lived down the road from you, didn't he? Reckon he ever got anywhere with that trumpet? Never did, love. Ended up working at the council offices down in Bradford. A good lad, though. Always helped an old woman across the street. Speaking of which, did you hear about poor Elsie Beaumont? Fell down the stairs the other day.

Right then, let's have another look at this – Cornwall, it is? Honestly, Geoff, you're so set on the Southwest Coast Path. Doesn’t anywhere else appeal? We could have gone to the Lake District, seen some proper mountains. Mountains? Eleanor, lass, you know I need the sea air! My lungs practically demand it. Besides, the Lake District’s a bit… well, a lot wetter this time of year, isn’t it? Cornwall’s got sunshine, craggy cliffs, and plenty of pubs with decent fish and chips. What’s not to love? Fish and chips  and  surfing? You said there were surf schools, Dad. Please tell me we’re actually going somewhere I can actually  do  something. School's been relentless. See, Geoff? Even Maisie wants a bit of excitement! And she’s right, there  are  surf schools. Polzeath is apparently excellent for beginners. Though, honestly, I’m more excited about the cream teas. Cream teas? Eleanor, don’t you start. Maisie’s got a point. We need some action. I’ve been too cooped up practicing my ukulele. A good long walk, salty air filling your lungs… that’s what I need. So, are we doing the whole Southwest Coast Path thing, or what? Because if we're just sitting on a beach sipping tea all day, I’m going to stage a revolt. Oh, you dramatic thing! We’re not just sitting on a beach. We'll do a few sections of the Path. I’ve marked a few shorter loops – nothing too strenuous, right, Geoff? I'm not exactly built for cliff scrambling. A few shorter loops. Perfectly reasonable. We’ll start gentle, build up the stamina. There’s a lovely section near St Ives, I think… dramatic scenery… and a little cafe with excellent pasties. Pasties  and  surfing? Now you're talking. Have you looked at those photos of Fistral Beach? It looks amazing! Are there any cool shops in St Ives? Like, vintage clothes or record shops? Let's see... They do have a few independent shops in St Ives. I found one that sells locally made jewellery and another with antiques. Not sure about record shops, love, but I can have a proper look later. I sent you a link to the surf school website earlier, didn't I? Yeah, I glanced at it. It’s pretty expensive though. Are you sure we can afford it?

Ugh, history is  killing  me. Seriously, Mr. Davies thinks we actually want to know about the agricultural revolution in minute detail. Like, who cares about crop rotation? You're being dramatic, Chloe. It's not  that  bad. Though, I do get where you’re coming from. I’m drowning in equations for physics. Mr. Henderson expects us to be Einstein already. Einstein? Please! I can barely remember which date Henry VIII got married. It’s all just… dates and names! Why can't we learn about something interesting? Like, after we watched 10 Things I Hate About You last night, I googled Shakespearean insults.  That's  interesting! Oh my god, you did? Tell me! Did you find any good ones? "Thou art a boil, a plague sore"? Classic. Heath Ledger was amazing in that, wasn’t he? I’m still swooning. Absolutely! And Kat Stratford? Goals. I wish I had her wit, honestly. But yeah, the insults were brilliant. “Art thou a monster?” I’m planning on dropping that on Mr. Davies if he asks me about the enclosure acts again. Caution advised. You'll get detention. Seriously, though, it’s funny how much of Shakespeare  is  infused into modern culture. It was interwoven so well in that film. Did you notice how the whole plot mirrored A Midsummer Night's Dream? I did! That’s what made it so clever. It’s just… school’s so tedious sometimes. I feel like all we’re doing is memorising stuff for tests. I’m dreading the mocks next month. Me too! But at least we'll have London after that. Remember we were looking at those museums? The National Gallery, specifically. All those Impressionists… Oh! Yes! The one with all the water lilies? Monet’s, right? I think it's absolutely beautiful. We  have  to go. Mum said she’d try and book tickets online before we get there, so we don't spend ages queuing. Good thinking. And maybe we can try that afternoon tea place near Buckingham Palace? I saw pictures, and it looked completely posh. Tiny sandwiches, scones with clotted cream... Oh. My. God. Yes! Posh food is a definite must. What about that vintage shop on Portobello Road? You were saying you wanted to find something a bit… unique. Totally! It's been ages since I got something that wasn’t from Primark. It would be really cool to find something proper retro, you know?

Honestly, I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by Facebook. It’s just…constant. Everyone posting about everything, and all the arguments! I saw a proper shouting match erupting about whether pineapple belongs on pizza, of all things. Pineapple on pizza? Cor blimey, that  is  a thing, isn't it? Never seen it myself. Bit much, if you ask me. Give me a good old ham and mushroom any day. Used to get that down the chippy on a Friday, back in the day. Simple pleasures, eh? John's always moaning about Facebook too. Says it's full of nonsense. But he secretly checks it ten times a day to see what the grandchildren are up to. Guilty as charged. Though I mostly use it to organise lectures and share relevant articles with my students, really. It's a useful professional tool, sometimes. Though I do get drawn into the silly debates, I admit. It’s a weakness. Exactly! And the comparison game. Everyone presenting this perfect, filtered version of their lives. It’s exhausting. I’m trying to be more mindful about how much time I spend on it. It’s prompted some thinking about my OCD too, actually. The constant checking, the need for validation…it’s all very similar, isn't it? That’s a really insightful connection, actually, Emily. The validation seeking. I’ve noticed that myself. It’s interesting how those compulsive behaviours can manifest in different areas of life. OCD…poor dear. It must be dreadful living with that. My nephew, little Thomas, he has some anxieties, bless him. Keeps washing his hands constantly. The doctor said it could be a mild form, you know. Anything to do with chicken pox though? We've got that going around the school, apparently. Three children already. Chicken pox! Right little nuisance that was when I were a lad. My mum covered me head to toe in Calamine lotion. Smelled like a chemist’s shop, it did! Never had a proper clean face for weeks. Itches something fierce, doesn’t it? It does. It's funny, isn't it? We try so hard to shield children from everything these days, but they still get exposed to things like chicken pox – and anxieties, too. Sometimes, I wonder if it's better to let them experience those things, within safe boundaries, so they learn to cope. There's a lot of debate about that in parenting circles, definitely.

Honestly, Dad, you’re still going on about that Mini Cooper? It was twenty years ago! Twenty years ago, love! It was  the  Mini Cooper. Black, chrome trim, the works. Absolutely brilliant little thing. Remember, Elsie, we drove all the way to Southport in it, didn't we? Of course, I do, dear. It was a squeeze, though! And you complained the whole way about the fuel economy. Nonsense. I was admiring the scenery. Southport was lovely. Your mum absolutely adored the pier. You two always have a story about a car, don't you? Reminds me of Nan and her Ford Fiesta. She used to say it was “a proper little workhorse.” Workhorse is right. My old man had one too. Bright orange. You couldn't miss it. Used to take me to the seaside in that thing. Still remember the smell of petrol and sunscreen. Reminds me of when I was a teenager and trying to learn German. My dad made me listen to German radio every evening. Said it was important. German radio? Really? What did you listen to? Mostly Schlager music, to be honest. Dreadful stuff. But it did pick up a few words. I even managed to hold a clumsy conversation on a trip to Bavaria once. Though their accents were utterly baffling. They kept asking me where I was from, and I'd just say "England," and they'd look at me like I was speaking Klingon. Oh, that’s brilliant! They all speak German, don’t they? Don’t they ever get confused? Their regional dialects are strong, Elsie. Very strong. It’s like different languages sometimes. It’s why people from the North Sound so different from those in the South and West. It's the same here, isn't it? People from Ashford sound different than people from… well, anywhere else in Kent, probably! That’s true. I remember when your Aunt Maggie moved down from Lancashire. Took her a good six months to understand what anyone was saying! You're exaggerating, Dad. Aunt Maggie's no daft. Were you lot talking about holidays? Remember that disastrous trip to Cornwall we took when I was a kid? The rain never stopped. Don’t remind me! We were huddled in that little caravan, damp and miserable. Your father insisted on trying to build a sandcastle. It  would  have been a good sandcastle! If it had stopped raining.

So, you're  still  slinging pans then, eh? Last time I saw you, you were talking about opening your own place. Any closer to that dream? Nah, not really. The restaurant scene in Exeter's a bit…saturated, you know? And frankly, the capital needed is terrifying. I’m mostly at The Old Mill now, which is actually alright. Good team, decent ingredients. Less pressure than trying to run the whole show myself. How's uni going, Liam? Still immersed in…what  is  it you’re studying again? Postcolonial Literature. Sounds dull, I know, but honestly, it’s fascinating. We’ve been looking at the impact of music on liberation movements - Bob Marley, Fela Kuti… stuff like that. It's made me appreciate music on a whole different level. Wow, that  is  something. I just appreciate it for, you know, being good. I’ve been listening to a  lot  of Royal Blood lately. Simple, but brilliant. Saw them live a couple of months ago – absolutely blew the roof off. Royal Blood are solid! Jamie’s already obsessed. He’s been trying to convince me to pick up the drums again. Remember when we both thought we were the next big thing with that awful garage band in school? "The Atomic Ferrets"? The Atomic Ferrets! Don't remind me. My mum still has somewhere a recording of us attempting "Smells Like Teen Spirit.” Horrendous. You were actually surprisingly good on the drums, though. Shame you gave it up. Yeah, well, A-levels got in the way. What about you? Ever drummed before? Not really. I bang on pots and pans when I'm prepping ingredients, does that count? Seriously though, I’ve always admired drummers. The rhythm section, the backbone of the whole thing. Who's your favourite? That’s tough. John Bonham, obviously. But I’ve got a real soft spot for Dave Grohl. The energy he brings is just insane. You know, Sarah's been raving about this new band, 'Lunar Echoes'. Apparently, their drummer is phenomenal – really complex rhythms. Lunar Echoes? Never heard of them. I'll have to check them out. Actually, speaking of Sarah… have you heard from her recently? She seemed pretty stressed about her internship at that design firm in London. Yeah, I spoke to her last week. It's intense, apparently. Long hours, demanding clients… but she said she's learning a ton. She’s earning good money too, which is a bonus.

Right then, Thomas, this is nice. Proper nice. Needed a sit-down after battling through that crowd at the market. Honestly, it was like Black Friday! Yeah, it’s alright, Mum. Bit noisy though, innit? Loud music. Aye, it is a bit of a din. Still, better than listening to the rain battering against the car window. Speaking of which, did you remember to put the sleeping bags in the boot? We're heading to Durham next weekend, and I don't want to be rummaging about in the dark trying to find 'em. Yeah, they’re in. Packed 'em yesterday. Got the tent too, right? Ooh, good lad! Aye, the tent's ready to go. I've been looking at the weather forecast – looks like we might just get lucky with some sunshine. Think of it, Thomas, a proper walk along the river, maybe a bit of sightseeing… Durham's alright. Not as good as Newcastle, though. You and your Newcastle! Always defending your hometown. But it  is  lovely, isn’t it? I’ve been meaning to visit the Cathedral properly for ages. And that new cafe on the Quayside, ‘Riverside Brews,’ apparently does a cracking scone. Scones are dead boring. Need a proper fry-up. Speaking of which, did you get the bacon and eggs on the shopping list? Of course, I did! Don’t you worry your head about it. And sausages, and mushrooms... Honestly, you’d think I was feeding a regiment! Did you see that story on the news about obesity in kids? It's worrying, isn't it? More and more takeaways, less proper meals. Loads of kids like takeaways. It's tasty. Tasty, maybe. Healthy, not so much. I’m trying to get you to eat more vegetables, you know. I saw that recipe for roasted root vegetables – looks lovely. Maybe we could try it this week? Maybe. Is that Domino's delivering tonight? I'm proper starving. Thomas! We just had a conversation about healthy eating! We're going to Durham, to be out in the fresh air. And you want takeaway pizza? Just thinking. It's Friday. Everyone gets pizza on Friday. Aye, well, not  everyone . I’m thinking we might have a Domino’s deal, aye. There was that promotion online, buy one get one half price. Might as well use it. I've been meaning to look at loyalty programs.

...and honestly, Tom, this is it. Sussex life. A bit quieter than Bedford, that’s for sure. Though, honestly, finding decent post here is a saga in itself. Took three attempts for your parcel to arrive! Tell me about it! I swear, Royal Mail is testing my patience these days. Though, it’s lovely to see you sorted, Finn. Proper nice flat. Much nicer than that student hovel we shared at uni. Don't remind me! The lingering smell of instant noodles… Traumatic. So, good to see you too, properly! It feels like ages. How's everything going with, uh, the Assurance Analyst gig? Still crunching numbers? Yeah, still crunching. It’s… well, it’s a job. Pays the bills, lets me save a bit. Though, you wouldn’t believe the amount of paperwork. Form filling is a significant portion of the job, honestly. You’d think being an analyst I’d  appreciate  spreadsheets, but there's a limit. I can imagine. I'm teaching English – mostly Korean students at the moment. They're brilliant, really keen, though their grasp of colloquialisms is…interesting. I was explaining the phrase “raining cats and dogs” the other day, and their faces! Oh, bless ‘em! That's classic. English colloquialisms are a minefield, even for us Brits sometimes. My mum still uses phrases that date back to the Stone Age, proper Midlands speak. “Nowt wrong with that,” she’ll say. “Nowt at all.” "Nowt wrong with that!" I love it. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? The way accents and dialects evolve and differ. I used to think all accents were just…accents. Then I started studying linguistics, and it's a whole world. Trying to record some examples for my students, actually. That's partly why I wanted to get you down. You've got a distinctly Midlands lilt, you know? Do I? I barely notice it myself. It’s just how I speak. Though, Lizzie does constantly rib me about it. Lizzie! How’s she doing? Still battling with the morning sickness? Honestly, watching her go through the pregnancy has been… intense. She's being incredibly brave. She is. Proper trooper, that one. Absolutely knackered, mind you. Constant cravings for bizarre combinations, like pickled onions and custard. And the tiredness... she sleeps nearly the whole day sometimes. It’s a bit scary, actually, thinking about the whole childbirth thing. It is a lot to take in.

...and honestly, Sarah, I still feel a bit numb. It’s been three weeks since Dad…well, since it happened. Three weeks and it still doesn’t quite feel real. I know, love. It's a weird feeling, isn't it? Like you’re waiting for him to pop round with a silly joke and a gardening tip. It’s not the grief itself that's surprising, it's the  absence  of the familiar. Exactly! And Mum… she’s… she's holding it all together, as she always does. But I can see it in her eyes. That sort of… brittle strength. She keeps saying she’s fine, that she’s busy sorting everything, but… She’s classic Mum, isn’t she? Always putting everyone else first. Did you talk to her about getting some support? Maybe a bereavement counsellor? I tried, gently. I brought it up, you know, ‘Mum, it might be helpful…’. But she just waved her hand and said, "Don't fuss, pet. I've been through worse." It’s like trying to argue with a brick wall. It’s the same with the cancer, isn't it? She just... shut down. Refused to acknowledge the seriousness. I remember your Aunt Carol telling me about that stubbornness of hers. It's ingrained, isn't it? Sometimes, you just have to be patient, eh? Little nudges, not big pushes. How are the kids taking it? Liam’s being his usual self – trying to be strong for everyone, all quiet and serious. But I know he’s hurting. And Chloe… Chloe’s been a proper mess. Crying fits, refusing to eat, the whole nine yards. I feel a bit useless, to be honest. Like I should be able to magic away all the sadness. You’re not useless, love. You're being there. That’s the most important thing. Remember when James’s dad passed? I felt the same way, useless and helpless. You were the one who brought over those shepherd's pies every week, and listened to me rant for hours. That was more than enough. You did, didn’t you? I’d almost forgotten. Actually, talking about it… I’ve been feeling a bit… off myself, lately. Not physically, but… mentally. Just this underlying weight, like I can't quite shake it off. Sleep's been terrible, too. Just tossing and turning, replaying everything in my head.

Right, that was a decent roast, wasn’t it? Chloe, you’ve barely touched your potatoes. Everything alright, love? Just full, I think, Dan. It's been a proper feast. So, Leo, you were saying something about tennis coaching? Yeah! Mr. Davies offered me an extra session this week. Said my forehand’s coming along really well. Seriously? That’s brilliant, Leo! I’m still slicing my serves into the net. That’s fantastic, Leo! You've put in so much effort. It's really paying off. Are you enjoying it, then? It does seem like you're spending every waking hour on that court. It’s good! Especially now the weather's a bit warmer. Though, Mr. Davies is  really  strict about warming up properly. He goes on and on about injury prevention. He's sensible, that's all. Prevention is better than cure, eh? Reminds me of when I messed up my knee playing five-a-side. Never quite the same since. Now I’m all about stretches and proper footwear. Five-a-side’s rubbish, though. Give me proper football any day. Did you see the game on Saturday? Man U played… what was it? Brighton. And they lost! Shocking. Speaking of things that are shocking... Did anyone read much about the referendum results last week? Seems like a lot of upset in the country, doesn’t it. Aye, quite a reaction. It'll take a while for things to settle down, that's for sure. I’m a bit worried about the impact on the business, to be honest. Supply chains could get complicated. That’s what I was thinking. It's concerning. But it does open up potential opportunities too, doesn’t it? Perhaps new markets? Markets? Like… selling things to other countries? Exactly! Although, that's something for grown-ups to worry about. What about you, Jamie? How’s school going? You seemed a bit quiet earlier. It’s alright. Got a mock exam next week for Maths. Not looking forward to it. Maths, eh? Always been my weak point. Never could get my head around algebra. What are you thinking about doing after school, Jamie? Have you had any more thoughts about apprenticeships? I’ve been looking at some engineering ones. There’s one at JCB, which would be pretty cool. They do really good training. JCB! My mate's dad works there. Says it's a good place to learn.

“Right, nearly an hour in, and still haven’t managed to finish that crossword. These scenic bits of countryside are rather distracting, aren’t they?” "They are, definitely. I was trying to get a head start on some admin for next week, but honestly, the rolling hills are much more appealing than spreadsheets. Lancaster’s coming up, I think? See those sandstone buildings?” "Yeah, spotted them. Feels a bit… Norman, doesn't it? Aunt Susan’s going on about Lancaster Castle, apparently. It’s been ages since I’ve seen her, actually. How's your mum doing? She was sounding a bit under the weather last time we spoke.” "Mum's okay, a bit better, actually. The cough’s finally clearing. She's been doing all sorts, trying out new herbal remedies. You know her. It's just the general wear and tear, I think. What about your folks? Still battling the garden?" "Always! Dad spent last weekend wrestling with the climbing roses. Apparently, they've gone rogue this year. Anyway, Lancaster... I'm mostly excited to see Aunt Susan. She's said something about driving us up the coast a bit afterwards? Fancy a look at Morecambe?” "Oooh, Morecambe! That’s a proper day out. Though, remember that cockle disaster a few years back? Felt a bit grim, didn’t it? All that talk of pollution and shellfish… I suppose it’s improved since then.” “Oh, I’d almost forgotten about that! Shocking, wasn't it? Still, a bit of sea air is exactly what we need. And fish and chips, naturally. You know I’m ruthless when it comes to seaside chippies.” "You absolutely are! Okay, fish and chips are non-negotiable. Are you still considering going back to uni for a Masters? You mentioned it last Christmas." “I am, actually. I'm looking at some programmes in Applied Linguistics. It’s a bit terrifying, though. Writing a dissertation… the thought alone gives me palpitations. What about you? Still enjoying the admin side of things?” "It's alright, it's stable. But sometimes I wonder, you know? I'm surrounded by brilliant researchers, and I'm just… filing things. My cousin got made redundant from his marketing job last month. It's a bit of a wake-up call, isn’t it? Makes you think about job security.” "Absolutely. My research co-ordinator has been subtly hinting that a Masters might open up more opportunities.

Right, so you’re tellin' me The Static Echoes are actually  gigs  now? Not just you and Liam in your shed with a broken mic stand? Aye, they are! Booked a couple of small venues in Sheffield, actually. First proper gigs, y'know? Feels a bit mental. Liam finally upgraded the mic stand, too. No more feedback squeals, thankfully. Mental’s an understatement! I always knew you lot were on to somethin', honestly. Remember when you tried to convince me to be your roadie? I nearly choked on me chips. You did! You said you'd rather wrestle a badger. But seriously, it's good. Liam's got this new pedal – a distortion thing – it sounds wicked. We're playing a few originals, and some covers, naturally. Got a bit of Arctic Monkeys in there, just to keep the lads happy. Arctic Monkeys are always a smart move, aren't they? Plays well with the crowd. So, who else is going? Sarah and Josh going to be there? They were proper obsessed with that one song you wrote about the bus station. Sarah definitely, she's already practically bought tickets for both dates. Josh is a bit… unpredictable. Depends if he can get away from his Nan’s bingo night. I sent him a nudge, mind. What about you? You comin' down to support your favourite brother? Ooh, ‘favourite brother’? Don’t let Dad hear you say that! Of course, I’m coming! Wouldn’t miss it for the world. Just need to check my shifts at the café. Mrs. Higgins is a nightmare about cover when there’s a football match on. Tell me about it. Speaking of nightmares, have you heard from Ben recently? He was raving about that pottery class he started. Ben? Nah, not for a couple of weeks. He said he was makin' a penguin. A massive, ceramic penguin. Honestly, I'm picturing something terrifying. I hope he hasn’t gone full-blown artistic and started wearin' berets. Knowing Ben, it's probably a ceramic penguin with a beret. He did send me a photo of it, actually. It's…unique. Kind of reminds me of that garden gnome we used to have at Grandma’s. Oh god, the one with the chipped nose? Don’t remind me! We were convinced it was haunted. What about your sculpting? You said you were thinking of giving it a go.

Right, I’m putting this in Atlanta. Definitely Atlanta. We need a firm foothold in the States, and that's the best strategic point. Strategic, is it? You’re taking this awfully seriously, Rhys! It's a game, lad. A pandemic, admittedly, but still just a game. Rhys has a point, Gareth. We need to contain the outbreaks. I’m adding a specialist to Yokohama – hoping we can slow that red down before it spreads to Seoul. This is quite tense, isn’t it? Tense? It's a full-blown crisis! Watch out for that yellow in Cairo, folks. I swear, it’s like trying to herd cats. And I'm a chef, not a disease controller! I’m putting my operations expert in Cairo – just to try and keep things under some semblance of order. Reminds me a bit of Singapore back in the day, you know. Always something bubbling under the surface, needing a bit of calming down. You’ve got to quarantine the chaos, you see. Think about it. Containment, resilience... it’s good practice for life, isn't it? Now, now, Gwynne, don’t go getting all philosophical on us. It's a game! Though, I suppose having a bit of patience is useful, even against the clever viruses this game throws at you. I'm adding a medic in Madrid - somewhere that needs it. And Eluned, darling, are you even  looking  at the board? I’m assessing the situation, Mum. Strategizing! Don’t underestimate me. This pandemic is ruthless, it demands careful consideration. See, Bangkok is about to flare up. We need to put a researcher there before… Strategizing? You were staring out the window at the sheep for a full minute! They were  very  fluffy sheep, Rhys! And occasionally, a bit of distraction is necessary for optimal cognitive function. Gareth, what’s your plan? Are you just going to keep chuckling your way to global annihilation? Trying to keep the spirits up, love! A little bit of laughter reduces the stress levels. I'm sending a dispatcher to Algiers. Need to move people around quickly. And speaking of stress, does anyone else feel like they're losing this? It’s getting close! Losing? We’re already lost! Look at that chain reaction in South America! It's going to be a domino effect. I think I need a biscuit. Building a research station  and  battling a super-virus is hungry work.

Right then, Operation Birthday Planning is officially underway! Poppy, Leo, are you even listening? I said, should we do a pirate theme this year? Or maybe superheroes? Pirates! Pirates! Arrr, me hearty! Can I be a sparkly pirate princess? Superheroes! I want to be Captain Awesome! He can fly and shoot lasers! Captain Awesome, eh? Sounds formidable. We’ll see. It’s a big decision. It has to be better than the last one, doesn’t it? Remember the dinosaur debacle? The volcano eruption was very messy! Very messy is putting it mildly! Right, so, birthdays... Poppy's is first, naturally. Then Leo's. We just need to solidify plans. I was thinking maybe another CBeebies pantomime? They do such lovely ones. Remember that one last Christmas with the Gruffalo? Gruffalo! He was big and grumpy! He was! But he also had a lovely cup of tea with the mouse. Speaking of tea, Leo, are you going to help me tidy this chaos, please? Can we watch CBeebies first? Please? Just one episode? They’re doing a story about a little bear who loses his favourite scarf. It's really sad. Alright, alright, one episode. But  then  we clear up this mess. You two are like miniature tornadoes! And after CBeebies, we’ll sit down and properly talk about decorating the garden. I’m thinking fairy lights. Do you think we can convince Grandma to help us hang them? Grandma is good at hanging things! Like Christmas stockings! Exactly! She's excellent. Oh, and I was thinking… World Book Day is coming up, isn't it? We need to sort out costumes. I was reading about a lovely initiative at school. They're encouraging everyone to use a funny saying from a book! Like what, Mummy? Well, there’s "Higgledy-piggledy, my black hen." From  Meg and Mog . Poppy, you'd love that one. It's so silly. And for Leo, perhaps something from  The Gruffalo ? “A mouse took a stroll through the deep dark wood…" I want to say, "Roar!" like the Gruffalo! You certainly can, darling. Now, another thing... Mother’s Day is just around the corner. I don’t expect a lot, you know. Just a big hug and maybe a drawing? Though a lie-in wouldn't go amiss. I'm going to make you a really, really nice picture! With lots of colours! And I’ll give you a kiss!

Honestly, this sourdough is incredible, Anon. Where did you get it? It’s way better than anything I’ve found in Hereford. It’s from that little bakery down the road, 'The Crusty Loaf'. They do amazing things. You should check them out, Chloe. You've got a serious bread appreciation, I’ve noticed! They’re alright, yeah. Not quite up to German standards, mind you. My mum used to bake the most incredible rye bread... really dense and sour. This is... pleasant, but not that. You’re always comparing everything to Germany, Liam! I’m starting to think you secretly miss the autobahn more than you let on. Well, it’s just... different. Everything feels a bit... softer here, you know? Not just the bread. I get that. Moving from Hertfordshire to London was a shock initially, even though it's only a short distance. Everything's louder, faster, more… aggressively cosmopolitan. Speaking of moving, Anon, how are the flat hunting adventures going? Still endless viewings of damp bedsits? Speaker_Anon: Don’t even get me started. It’s brutal. I've seen places where the kitchen is literally just a hotplate and a sink in the corner of the bedroom. And the rents! I’m seriously considering just staying here a bit longer, even though it’s starting to feel a bit like a long-term house guest situation rather than a flatshare. You should have brought me. Shared expenses would've been a lifesaver. Seriously, the cost of living here is ridiculous. I’m constantly second-guessing whether I need that extra coffee or not. Tell me about it! Teaching English is rewarding, but it doesn’t exactly make you rich. I’ve been trying out those online tutoring platforms, but the competition is fierce. It’s basically an internet dating site for teachers, but instead of finding a partner, you’re battling for students. An internet dating site for teachers? That’s… fascinating and slightly terrifying. Is it as cutthroat as Tinder? I swear, dating apps have drained all the romance out of finding love. I actually met a guy on Bumble last week who referenced his star sign in the first message. A  star sign ! Dating apps are a necessary evil, aren’t they? I swear, the profiles are all the same: smiling picture hiking, pretending to like dogs, mentioning travel… it’s a carefully curated performance.

…and honestly, the presentation was a disaster. Mr. Henderson kept interrupting with these incredibly pedantic questions about projected ROI. It felt like pulling teeth, the entire time. Oh, bless him. Sounds like classic Henderson. Remember when he tried to convince Dad that a colour-coded filing system was the key to world peace? No! Seriously? Your dad’s filing system was legendary. It was just… piles. Efficient piles. Exactly! Dad would say, “Everything’s in there somewhere, darling. Just requires a bit of rummaging.” Henderson probably had palpitations. He absolutely did. He was a stickler for order. Reminds me, did you ever have a Spirograph, Sarah? A Spirograph! Oh my goodness, yes! I was obsessed. I spent hours making those intricate patterns. I think I single-handedly depleted my mother’s supply of felt tip pens. Did you, Fiona? Oh, yes! I had the one with the little wooden base. And I spent even  more  hours making them than you did, I reckon! All those spirograph patterns covered the walls of my bedroom. Mum wasn’t best pleased. I’m sure I still have a couple of them lurking in a box somewhere. I had a Rainbow Loom! That was my thing. I used to make little bracelets for everyone. Remember that craze? It was intense. My fingers ached for days! Rainbow Loom... that was a bit later, wasn't it? I remember Poppy wanting one. I had more of a Barbie obsession myself. My poor mother. Her bank account suffered tremendously. Barbies. Wonderful things. Though I always thought they had terribly unrealistic proportions. My sister, bless her, was obsessed with Cabbage Patch Kids. She’d name them all and create elaborate backstories. My grandma collected those! Little porcelain dolls. They were all so prim and proper. It's funny, isn't it, how those childhood things stick with you? Absolutely. It’s funny how different our childhood collections were, too. I wonder if it’s a regional thing, a bit. You know, growing up in Lincolnshire, things felt... calmer. Less frantic than, say, living near London. Possibly. Living in Peterborough, you definitely felt the pull of the city, but it's still got that East Anglian heart, doesn’t it? That slow pace. I sometimes think people from the South East rush around constantly, like they’re being chased by something. I think you’re right. Growing up in Essex, it was a mixture.

Right then, where were we? Oh yes, Italy! Honestly, you wouldn't believe the pasta. Absolutely incredible. You were just telling us about the little trattoria in Florence. The one you said had the best carbonara you've  ever  tasted? Best. Ever. No exaggeration. Mum, you remember? It was tucked away down this tiny little alleyway, you could barely see it from the main street. And the aroma… honestly, it pulled us in. I remember! And the owner, that lovely gentleman, Giuseppe, insisted on bringing us a limoncello after dinner. Strong stuff, that! Nearly knocked me sideways. Limoncello! Sounds good. So, Florence – was that your favorite city, Dad? You were rattling off a list of at least five. Difficult to say! Rome was magnificent, of course. All those ancient ruins… mind-boggling. But Florence had a certain charm, didn’t it, love? The art, the architecture… and the food! We went to the Uffizi Gallery, and I swear I could have spent a whole week just looking at Botticelli's "Birth of Venus." Did you manage to see the David? Everyone says it’s a must-see. Of course! We queued for ages, but it was worth it. Absolutely stunning. A bit… large, perhaps, but undeniably impressive. Mum, you were taking pictures like mad, weren’t you? I was! Trying to capture every angle. Your father kept saying I was blocking the view for everyone else. Honestly, he’s impossible sometimes. Sounds like him! So, after Florence, where did you two go? Venice, right? Venice! Oh, Venice was… something else. A bit too crowded for my liking, to be honest. All those tourists jostling for space. But the gondolas… gliding through those canals… it was magical in its own way. Did you do a gondola ride? We did! A bit pricey, mind you. But worth it for the experience. The gondolier serenaded us, too. Though his English wasn't the best, to be honest. He kept trying to convince us to buy a little glass donkey. He did! We narrowly avoided that purchase. Nearly broke the bank with the gondola alone. Well, you deserve to splash out on a holiday. How was the food in Venice, Dad? Different from Florence? Very different! More seafood-focused, naturally. We had some delicious risotto with clams. And Mum had some sort of fried squid that she declared the best she’d ever tasted. You eat  everything , Mum.

Honestly, the sheer volume of celebrity gossip this morning is exhausting. Apparently, that actor, you know, the one from... well, you know,  that  show… is dating a reality TV star. It's baffling. Oh, don't even. I make a point of avoiding that stuff. It’s just manufactured drama to sell newspapers, isn't it? I’m trying to actually  make  breakfast here, contributing something real to the world. Although, these pancakes are looking a little… questionable. Morning, ladies. Something burning? Smells… interesting. And celebrity dating – yeah, a complete waste of brainpower. I was reading this article about new advancements in sustainable concrete yesterday.  That's  interesting. Apparently, they’re incorporating recycled plastics into the mix... Recycled plastics in concrete? Right. You and your engineering marvels, Liam. While I’m hearing about fleeting romances, you’re saving the planet one building block at a time. It's not about saving the planet  one building block , Sarah! It’s about developing more sustainable and efficient building practices. It’s a small part, but everything helps. It's a far cry from my initial research in Germany, though. Dealing with the DACH regulations was… something else. Germany, right? You rarely mention it. Still hold a grudge against that university, do you? Not really a grudge. It was just... intense. Very rigorous. I was rather young, fresh off the boat. I definitely appreciate the slightly more relaxed pace of life here. Plus, the tea’s much better! Agreed on the tea. Though, this gossip is offering a certain… entertainment value. Anyway, speaking of intense, did you see anything about that strike at the port in Felixstowe? Seems like it’s really impacting supply chains. I did. Dreadful. My sister's online clothing boutique relies heavily on imports, so she's freaking out. She’s been moaning about shipping costs for ages, but this is just going to make things worse. Said she might have to put prices up. It’s that domino effect, isn’t it? The price of everything keeps creeping up. Have you been watching the energy prices, Emma? It’s terrifying. I’m seriously thinking about investing in those solar panels I've been looking at. Smart move. My dad is saying the same thing. He's been reading up on government subsidies. It's something we all need to think about, isn’t it? It's depressing though, isn’t it?

Right then! One last pint for this old soldier before I’m off to Jeddah! Feels a bit bonkers, doesn't it? Leaving everyone here. It does, Reg. It doesn't feel real, does it? Especially with everything going on. You’ll be miles away. Jeddah, yeah? Bit of a culture shock compared to Liverpool, eh? You got your satnav sorted? Last thing you need is to be lost in the desert. I’ve had a nightmare with Google Maps lately. Keeps sending me down one-way streets! Google Maps is a joke, mate. Remember when it told me to drive through a farmer’s field? Proper muddy it was. Ended up looking like I’d wrestled a pig. Oh, I remember that, Liam! You looked a right state. And a satnav? Don't you worry about me, lad. Been navigating tougher situations than a dodgy Google route for the last thirty years. Got me trusty Garmin, loaded with all the maps. Plus, I’ll be with a good bunch of lads over there, we’ll look out for each other. That’s reassuring to hear. It's still a huge change though, Reg. Are you nervous? A bit, love, aye. But mostly excited. New experiences, see new places… It’s been a long time since I’ve had an adventure like this. Your mum’s gutted, of course. Kept going on about missing her Sunday roast dinners. Mum will cope. She’s a rock. Anyway, back to the topic of getting lost... Seriously, Reg, take screenshots of the important map bits BEFORE you go. Just in case. Don’t want you ending up befriending a camel. Imagine that! Reg riding a camel across the desert. That’d be a postcard worth sending. What are you doing out there, exactly? Training exercises, mostly. Helping them develop their infrastructure. Bit of everything, really. It's a…sensitive area, best not to go into details. We understand. So, Liam, how's the new job going? I heard you're coordinating some big project now? It’s alright, yeah. A lot more responsibility than I was used to, but good money. Just trying to keep all the contractors on track. Stressful, but it pays the bills. Still miss the lads I used to work with on the building site though. Good times. It’s a world away from roughing it in Peterborough, eh? You’re practically a manager now.

Honestly, this place is just balm for the soul, isn't it? The sheer variety is astonishing. Though, I’m quite surprised to see so many  Rhododendron  'Nova Zembla' blooming so late. Usually, they’ve finished by now. It  is  lovely. Sweden’s doing a cracking job with their botanicals. And you’re right, the 'Nova Zembla' are a bit behind. I did read something about a delayed flowering season across Scandinavia this year – a result of that unusually mild winter and then the colder snap in April. Something about the plants not getting the right cues. Delayed flowering, you say? Fascinating. It's a good reminder of how interwoven everything is, isn’t it? Weather patterns, plant cycles, even our own internal clocks, I suspect. Makes you think about resilience, doesn’t it? Speaking of internal clocks, how are you both feeling, really? This trip has been… a lot. Oh, you're telling me! My allergies have been atrocious. I thought I’d left my hay fever behind in Dorset! I’ve been popping antihistamines like they’re going out of fashion. I'm thinking about trying some of those nasal rinses people rave about. Have either of you ever used them? I have, actually. Years ago, when I was doing that trek in Nepal. It did the trick, reduced the congestion noticeably. Though, the first few times, it’s a bit… unsettling. Like you’re having a very strange shower in your nose, rather than on your body. That's a brilliant description, Liam! I can imagine. You know, I was reading an article about microbiome diversity and allergies. Apparently, having a wider variety of beneficial bacteria in your gut can significantly reduce allergy symptoms. It's a long game, but worth exploring. Probiotics and fermented foods, that sort of thing. Right, well, I'm hardly one for sauerkraut, am I? Though, I do like a good yogurt… perhaps I should focus on  that . It’s easier than sticking a hose up my nose, that’s for sure. Though, Lizzie has been trying to get me into kombucha. Horrible stuff if you ask me! Honestly, Sarah, you’re such a traditionalist. Though, I do agree, kombucha's acquired taste. I’ve been trying to be better about hydrating, on the recommendation of my physiotherapist. Fewer coffees, more water with lemon and ginger. It's actually a surprisingly pleasant thing, once you don’t think of it as ‘effort’.

Honestly, this Wi-Fi is atrocious. How's anyone supposed to get anything done, let alone play Minecraft, with this lag? Tell me about it, Dan. I was just trying to send a quick email to my tutor about the essay, and it kept buffering. It’s ridiculous. Mum, have you even tried using the internet today? Not really, love. Not much need. I’m making a shepherd’s pie. Bit healthier than the usual takeaway, eh? You lot are always glued to your screens. Reminds me of when I was a kid watching ‘The Generation Game’ – that was the peak of entertainment back then. ‘The Generation Game’! Now you're talking, Brenda. Dusty Springfield! I used to try and imitate her voice. Couldn’t quite manage it, mind you. My voice just isn’t built for that sort of… flattery. It's always been a bit… gravelly, innit? Gravelly is putting it kindly, Arthur. Sounds like you’ve been gargling with sandpaper. No offence. None taken. You young'uns with your fancy voices. It’s all about projection these days, isn't it? Nowadays, you can’t even talk to your phone properly. Voice recognition never understands me. Accents are dying out, I reckon. Everyone tries to sound like they’re in a bloody advert. I think accents are just  evolving , Grandad. Like, I hear younger people in London, they’ve got this completely different way of speaking. It’s almost… detached, you know? Hardly sounds like anyone from Gillingham anymore. Though, I still get asked if I'm Australian sometimes, apparently my vowels are a bit… distinct. You and your posh vowels. Don't you go turning into a proper toff on me, love! Speaking of evolving… Your uncle Mark’s called again. About little Lily. It's a right mess, isn't it? That custody dispute. Don't. Just… don’t bring that up now. Honestly, Dad, it’s been going on for ages. And with his drinking… it’s just not fair on Lily. He’s a grown man! He’ll sort himself out. Always has. Remember when he used to build those elaborate Minecraft worlds? He was brilliant at it! Totally absorbed. Waste of time, of course. Waste of time? It was an outlet for him! And it kept him occupied, considering… well, you know. It was better than him staring at the wallpaper, wasn't it?

This is good, Mum. Really good. What’s in it? Loads of cheese? It’s a creamy pesto pasta, love. And yes, lots of parmesan. I tried a new grater actually, one of those rotary ones. Much quicker than the box kind. You know how much time I’ve wasted grating parmesan over the years? It’s practically a monumental waste of time when you think about it. It's just cheese. I don’t get why you’re stressing about grating cheese. It’s not  just  cheese, Finn! It's a metaphor! For efficiency, for strategic time management! It's about applying those principles to everything, even something as simple as pasta. Speaking of which, your cousin Liam is still coming to the Halloween party, right? Yeah, I think so. He said he’s bringing that mate from his gaming group, Alex. Good. The more the merrier. We’re aiming for a proper spooktacular evening. I’m even attempting a Baked Alaska. A Baked Alaska? Seriously? That’s… ambitious. Isn’t that like, incredibly hard to get right? That’s the fun part! It’s a challenge. Reminds me a little of recruiting for my new project. Finding the right people, the ones with the right spark… it's a delicate balancing act. Sometimes you end up with a slightly melted meringue, sometimes it's a glorious triumph. Recruiting? You’re still going on about work. It’s just an analogy, Finn! Relax. It makes me think of Uncle David, actually. Remember when he applied for that management training program, and they basically told him he wasn't 'management material' because he was from a working-class background? Vaguely. He always got really quiet when he talked about that. It was awful. Just blatant discrimination. They expected him to conform to a certain… image. It made me so angry. It still does. Knowing people are still facing that sort of rubbish. It's probably worse online, isn’t it? With all the... you know. Exactly. And it’s not always so obvious. Subtle biases, unconscious assumptions… it's insidious. That's why being aware of it, calling it out where you see it, is so important. It’s also why I’m determined to build a diverse team for this project. I want people with different backgrounds, different perspectives. It strengthens everything. Did you ever… worry about me when I was really little?

…and then young Finnigan just stared, didn’t he? Absolutely gobsmacked. Said he’d never seen anyone so insistent on returning a library book three days early. Honestly! Some people. Right, more toast? You look like you could do with it. Definitely! Thank you, Moira. That's classic Finnigan, though, isn't it? Always a bit flustered. And early book returns are a genuine rarity these days. Speaking of travel, how was your trip to New York? Last time we spoke, you were just gearing up. Oh, it were brilliant, love. Absolutely brilliant. Bit overwhelming, mind, the sheer size of everything. Broadway was a right spectacle, and the art at the Met… well, I could've spent a week there alone. Though, the cost! Good heavens. Makes a holiday in Scarborough seem like a bargain. I can imagine! New York isn't exactly known for its budget-friendliness. Did you manage to see everything you wanted to? And did you finally get that ridiculous hot dog you were threatening to get? I did! A proper New York hot dog, piled high with everything they could throw at it. It were… an experience. Some things are best experienced once, I reckon. But yeah, I saw most things. Honestly, though, I missed the quiet. Missed being able to hear myself think. It’s lovely to be back in Swansea, even if it's a bit… damp. Damp is the Welsh way, Moira. You get used to it. So, you were saying earlier about that flying lesson? How did that go? Oh, marvelous! Absolutely marvelous! I’m properly hooked, I think. The instructor - a fella called Gareth – he were lovely. Explained everything so clearly. Took off, circled round a bit, and then… suddenly I were piloting the thing myself! It’s a frightening and utterly exhilarating feeling, all at once. Seriously? That's fantastic! You always were a bit of an adventurer. I wish I had the nerve. I’m happy just thinking about planning a trip, to be honest. I’ve been meaning to book that pottery class ages. Right, so what are we doing today? Fancy a walk along the beach? The tide’s going out. That sounds lovely, Sarah. Though, I think I need to have a proper look through all me photos first. I've got hundreds from New York. I’ll bore you senseless, I expect. Also, I need to get me bins out.

“Q… seriously? Why do I  always  get the Q?” “Bad luck, mate. Could be worse, you could have a Z. Though you could use a Q, I suppose. Trying for 'quaff' across the double word score? Risky, but could pay off.” “You’re always thinking about points, aren’t you, Liam? It's not  all  about the score, you know. Sometimes it's about the word itself.” "True. I was playing with my niece the other day, and she tried to spell 'orange'. She couldn't understand why it's spelled that way. Apparently, the 'ge' is a weird quirk of the Norman French influence. It's fascinating when you think about it." “See! That’s what I mean. Why  is  ‘orange’ spelled like that? It’s just… illogical. Like ‘queue.’ What’s with the 'ueu'? So pretentious.” "It’s all history, isn't it? Languages are just evolving messes. 'Queue' comes from the Latin 'coda' - meaning tail. Think of a line of people, tailing behind each other. Makes a bit more sense then, doesn’t it?" “I love that! It’s like uncovering a secret about the world. Reminds me of reading Roald Dahl as a kid. 'The BFG' was always my favourite, the way he invented words… 'gobblefunk'!” She laughs. “Makes you wish you could just create new words all the time.” “Speaking of children’s books, did you guys see that new Julia Donaldson one? The illustrations are stunning. It'd be perfect for Elsie, my niece. She’s suddenly obsessed with flowers." “Which reminds me… did anyone catch the Chelsea Flower Show this year? Absolutely incredible. I'm considering trying to plant lavender this summer, maybe a little herb garden.” "Lavender’s a good shout. Easy to grow, smells lovely. Although, knowing you, you'll probably order some fancy hydroponic kit and overcomplicate it." "Hey! I resent that. I’m perfectly capable of planting a simple lavender bush." “Are you now? Remember that time you tried to build a birdhouse and it ended up looking like a miniature spaceship?” "That was a design innovation! Ahead of its time!" He glances at his tiles again. “Okay, okay. Q… U… E… U... Right. No 'queue’ for me today.” “I remember when I was doing A-levels, I really struggled with French. Spelling especially. It felt like a constant battle against random vowels and silent letters. Completely different from cooking, where things are far more concrete.”

Honestly, Arthur, I’ve been thinking about it all day. About what Mrs. Peterson said at the village fete. Mrs. Peterson, did? Blimey, what on earth did she say now? She's always got an opinion, that one. About everything. Probably complaining about my geraniums again, weren't she? No, not the geraniums, though she probably will next week. It was about the new community centre plans. You know, the one they want to build on the old allotments. Oh, that. Heard a bit about it. More concrete, is it? Seems a bit much, don’t it? We've got a perfectly good hall in the village, haven't we? That's exactly what I told her! But she went on about needing space for youth groups, and computer classes, and a new library... All very laudable, of course, but at what cost? The allotments are lovely. The bees love them, the children love picking blackberries there... Aye, you’re right. Used to wander about down there as a lad, I did. Found a dormouse once, I did. Nearly had a heart attack, I did. Little thing, nestled in the roots of a rhubarb plant. You and your dormice. See? That's what they'll lose. That quiet, that connection to nature. It's important, Arthur. Especially for the young 'uns. They’re glued to their screens most of the time, they are. Doubt they even  notice  a dormouse these days. Still… ripping up the allotments... feels a bit harsh, doesn’t it? It does. And the council haven’t even consulted anyone properly. Just a quick survey, a couple of flyers. It's all being rushed through. I bumped into Geoff from the gardening club yesterday. He’s fuming. Says they’re going to lose their prize-winning pumpkins! Pumpkins! Good grief. Geoff's pumpkins were legendary. Could win prizes anywhere, those could. More than just pumpkins, though, innit? It's about tradition. About something that’s been there for years. Changing things just for the sake of it… never sits right, does it? Exactly! I'm thinking of going to the next parish council meeting. To voice my concerns. You are? Do you think it’ll do any good? They tend to have their minds made up already, don't they? Well, it’s worth a try, isn’t it? Someone needs to stand up for something. And honestly, Arthur, I could use the company.

That was absolutely delicious, Anon! Honestly, the best meal of the holiday. You've really outdone yourself with the lamb. Where did you even  find  such lovely rosemary? Aye, it’s cooked right. Bit of a faff, all that basting, but worth it, innit? And the rosemary… I got it from Farmer Giles down the road. Best in Devon, he claims. Doubt it’s  that  special, but it does smell lovely. Been letting it dry out a bit to use it later, really concentrates the flavour, you know. Giles is a character, isn't he? Remember last summer when he tried to sell me a goose that was convinced it was a duck? He was so serious! You’re right, though, the rosemary  is  fantastic. This whole meal feels properly autumnal. It really does. I’m already thinking about winter comfort food. Roasted squash, maybe a really hearty stew… speaking of which, did you see that article in the local paper about the Bramley apples? Apparently, they’ve had a bumper crop this year. Perfect for apple crumble! Oh yes! Read that. Good news for the crumble makers, that. Though, I’m more partial to a good rhubarb crumble myself. Always reminds me of my mum. She used to make it every Sunday. You and your memories of your mum! She sounds like a wonderful cook. I should start posting some of my recipes online. I've been playing around with this new app, 'Spice Route', it's supposed to be brilliant for sharing recipes and finding inspiration. Have either of you heard of it? Spice Route? No, can’t say I have. Is it any good? I’m always hunting for new ideas. My Year 6s are forever asking for ‘food that’s exciting’ and suddenly I'm expected to be a Michelin-star chef! It's surprisingly intuitive. It even lets you filter recipes by dietary requirements. I've been linking up with some other teachers – sharing ideas for healthy lunchboxes, things like that. You can also track your macros, which is good for fitness. I’ve been trying to get back on track with my running after the holiday indulgence. Macros? Sounds complicated. I stick to a good walk along the beach, that's all the fitness I need. Easier on the knees too, you know. Though, I may have put on a pound or two… not that I’m counting!

...and honestly, that seminar on Hamlet last week was brutal. Professor Davies really went for it, didn't he? He spent a good twenty minutes dissecting Gertrude’s motivations. I’m still not sure I'm any clearer, to be honest. Davies, yeah. He’s a legend, in the most intimidating way possible. Remember that time he pretended to faint when someone suggested Hamlet was a simple revenge tragedy? Good times. So, you actually  enjoyed  it, though? Apart from the Gertrude deep dive? Enjoyed is a strong word. I found it… intellectually stimulating? In a deeply exhausting sort of way. It's just, sometimes I wish we’d actually  watched  the bloody play instead of endlessly theorising about it. I saw that Shakespeare on TV adaptation last night, the one with Rory Kinnear. Oh, yeah! I meant to watch that. Was it any good? I'm a sucker for a proper Shakespearean production, even on the telly. Better than trying to follow Davies’ ramblings. It was brilliant. So atmospheric. They filmed it in some old castle, really added to the melancholy. Kinnear was phenomenal, absolutely believable as a man teetering on the edge. Far more compelling than I'd imagined after all the seminars. Speaking of compelling, have you made any progress on getting those tickets for the FA cup game? Don’t even mention it. It’s a battlefield out there. Everyone and their dog wants a ticket. I’ve been refreshing the website every five minutes for the last two days. No luck so far. I’m starting to think I’ll have to bribe someone at the campus sports club. That’s never a good idea. Last time you ‘bribed’ someone, you ended up with a used rugby ball and a week's worth of lukewarm shepherd’s pie. Okay, fair point. Slightly less successful than planned. Still, anything’s better than missing the game. I was thinking after this, maybe we could check out that new Italian place on Cryws Road. Apparently, they do a decent carbonara. That sounds fantastic, actually. I'm starving. And I need something to take my mind off Gertrude and her… complicated feelings. We should probably book, though; it's always packed. Did you hear about Liam’s stag do? Apparently his mates have booked a paintballing weekend in Cornwall. Paintballing? Liam? That’s surprisingly tame for him. I thought they’d be going to Magaluf or something.

Honestly, this Wi-Fi is appalling. I’m trying to clear out a few emails before I head back to the office, but it’s taking forever. So, tell me everything! It feels like ages since you were last down this way. Oxford treating you well? It’s alright, you know. A bit… refined, maybe? It’s nice to escape back to Cambourne though, for a proper catch-up. And the Wi-Fi here  is  better than some places, surprisingly. Work’s… work. Pearson’s still Pearson, you know? Mountains of spreadsheets and meetings about meetings. How's the project coordination going? Still wrestling with spreadsheets of your own, I imagine? Oh, you have no idea! This new initiative – trying to streamline the logistics for the solar panel rollout across the county – it's been a nightmare. So many stakeholders, so many different opinions. I swear, I spend half my day just mediating arguments. At least it's challenging, though. Keeps me on my toes. What's Pearson got you involved in lately? Anything exciting? Not particularly exciting, no. Mostly re-branding a line of textbooks. Exciting for the marketing team, apparently. Loads of focus groups and demographic analysis. I'm starting to feel like an expert on the reading habits of 16-year-olds, which, let’s be honest, isn’t exactly a career highlight. Anyway, speaking of exciting...have you heard from Tom? Tom?  Tom  Tom? No! Seriously? What’s he been up to? I haven't thought about him in ages. Last I heard, he was backpacking through Southeast Asia. Yeah, he's back. Settled in Bristol, actually. Got a job in sustainable energy. Bit ironic, considering your solar panel rollout, isn’t it? He messaged me the other day – wanted to know if you were around. Sounded… nice. Grown-up even. Grown-up, huh? Wow. That's… unexpected. I honestly hadn't considered… well, anything. I’ve been so focused on work and, you know, just getting by. I hope he's well. Do you think he'd actually… want to see me? Honestly? I think he does. He seemed genuinely keen. He said he’d been thinking about you a lot. Don’t let that deter you though, if you're not feeling it. No pressure. But it's kind of lovely, isn't it? After all this time. It is… It is lovely. A little daunting, though.

Right, that's done! Honestly, this thing makes a racket. Fancy a brew, love? I'm making a proper Yorkshire Tea, like you like it. Strong enough to stand a spoon in, you said? Please, please. Yorkshire Tea is a lifesaver after a morning wrestling with recalcitrant data. And yes, strong. Very strong. You've got the good mugs out, too. Not the chipped ones. Well, you deserve a treat after slaving away on that thesis. How’s it coming, by the way? Still convinced that Victorian garden gnomes hold the key to understanding early industrial philosophy? Don't tease! It’s more nuanced than that, I promise. Though, the gnomes  do  provide a fascinating lens through which to view societal anxieties about progress and the uncanny. It's just... getting the proper phrasing right is a nightmare. Professor Davies keeps suggesting I "unpack the inherent symbolism." Seriously, what does that even  mean ? Oh, academics! "Unpack the inherent symbolism." Sounds like something you'd do with a particularly stubborn suitcase. He just means he wants you to explain it, doesn’t he? Strip it back to the basics. That's what I thought, but he says it's not about  explaining  it, it’s about revealing the layers. It's exhausting. Did your mum ring today? I haven't heard from her in a few days. Aye, she did. She’s still obsessed with that prize-winning marrow she’s got growing. Apparently, it’s nearly as big as your head! She's planning on taking it to the village fair. Says she’s got a real rival this year, old Mrs. Henderson and her monstrous pumpkins. You know how competitive she gets. Competitive indeed. Remember that time she and Aunt Carol had that feud over the best Victoria Sponge at Christmas? Absolute carnage. It ended with flour everywhere and a passive-aggressive comment about baking temperatures. Don't remind me! I was refereeing that one. It was mental. Speaking of cooking, I was thinking of having a go at that Thai green curry you showed me last month. The one with the galangal? Oh, you should! It’s surprisingly simple, really. Just got to get the paste right. Don't skimp on the chilies, either - makes a world of difference. Do you have any lemongrass? I think so. Let me just check... Ta-da! Found it. What about these ferns?

Honestly, David, this marking… it’s a relentless tide, isn't it? Seems to swell every weekend. I’ve barely seen daylight. Tell me about it, Alistair! I've got a stack of dissertations that could rival the Leaning Tower of Pisa. It's not just the volume, is it? It's the...effort of trying to build each student up, even when the work isn't quite up to scratch. Did you see young Rhys Davies’ essay on the French Revolution? Bless him, he clearly tried, but it read like a shopping list. Rhys Davies, eh? He's got a father who plays for Cardiff City, doesn't he? These young footballers' children… sometimes I wonder if they even appreciate the value of a good education when they've got a bit of sporting stardom hanging over them. Aye, you’ve a point there. Though, I’ve always found it's a mixed bag. Some are driven, some coast along. Still, Rhys needs a bit of a nudge. Speaking of stars, did you catch that snooker match on Sunday? That young Alfie Carter is something else. Incredible potting skills. Reminds me a bit of a young Higgins, you know? Higgins was a legend, wasn't he? Though I’ve always been more of a Steve Davis man myself, that cool, almost robotic focus. My weekend wasn't all marking, thankfully. Managed to get out into the garden for a couple of hours. The roses are finally starting to bloom – a proper riot of colour. Yours still looking rather… sparse, I recall? Don't remind me. Slugs. Absolute scourge of the Welsh garden. I’ve tried everything – beer traps, copper tape, even those little woolly hedgehogs. Nothing works! Maybe I should just give up and pave the entire thing. What about you? Any battles with the local wildlife? Just the squirrels, trying to pilfer the birdseed. They're remarkably cunning creatures. It's almost comical. It’s a far cry from Cairo, you know. Gardens were rather different there… palm trees, hibiscus… quite exotic! Cairo! You never mentioned that. Quite a difference from Tredegar, wouldn’t you say? This town never changes, Alistair. Still the same old faces, same old pub, same old issues. Speaking of which, did you hear they're having real trouble recruiting for the police force locally? Not surprising, really, with everything that's going on. Indeed.

Right then, let’s just run through this again. Christening’s two weeks away, isn't it, love? And little Poppy’s birthday is just after… so a lot to juggle. Two weeks! Will there be cake, Nana? A big, sparkly cake? Yeah, two weeks. And it’s going to be mad busy. Uni’s kicking off again soon, so I’ll probably only be able to really help with the food shopping, realistically. Sorry. Don’t apologise, love. Anything’s a help. It's just... I want everything to be perfect for Poppy. It’s her first Christening, you know. A big family affair. I’ve been trying to get a proper photographer, but they're all booked solid. Typical. Mum, seriously? You’re stressing about a photographer? It’s a lovely family gathering. Pictures will come out on phones, and that’s perfectly fine. Honestly, you worry about the small things. It's not a small thing to me, El! It’s a memory. I want something beautiful to remember it by. Besides, Poppy will be far too busy exploring to hold still for a phone photo. She's like a whirlwind! I am! I like running! She certainly does. Look, I can ask around at university. Maybe someone’s studying photography and looking to build their portfolio? It'd be cheap, at least. That’s a brilliant idea, El! Honestly, that would be fantastic. Thank you. Now, the cake… I was thinking Victoria sponge. Classic, but everyone loves it. Poppy’s allergic to strawberries, remember? Right, no strawberries. Got it. And what about the buffet? You planning on doing all that yourself? Because that’s a  lot  of food and I'm happy to help with some salads and that if you’re feeling overwhelmed. I was hoping to… it’s just thinking about the number of people coming… Auntie Brenda and Uncle George, and their lot… and your cousins. It's a fair few. I might have to order some things in. Can Lily have cake too, Nana? Lily likes cake. Of course, darling. Lily can have all the cake she wants. It’s a celebration! What about your birthday, sweetie? You turning three soon, aren't you? We need to start thinking about  that , too. Three! Wow, time flies. A little tea party? Are you thinking a princess theme again? Last year's was a bit… intense.

Honestly, this rain is just relentless, isn’t it? I was hoping for a bit of sunshine this weekend. Little Poppy’s been asking about picnics. Tell me about it! I had to deal with a flooded pavement outside the store this morning, nearly took out a customer’s shopping trolley. It's properly gloomy. Poppy’s right though, a picnic would be lovely if the weather cooperates. Though, knowing our luck… Pic…nic! Sunny! Exactly, sweetie! And Poppy, Daddy's making pancakes tomorrow, a little sunshine in a pan! Ooh, pancakes! That's a definite win. Speaking of winning… did you manage to sort out those staff rotas for next week, Gemma? It’s been a bit chaotic with people calling in sick. I did, eventually. Thankfully, Sarah offered to cover a couple of shifts. It's just… running a shop these days, isn't it? Always something popping up. Want to talk about it? Thanks, I appreciate that. It’s just tiring. But it’s alright, it always is. Still... I was thinking, if we  do  manage to get a weekend free, we should really start looking properly at flights to New York, shouldn't we? Poppy keeps asking when she’s going to see the Statue of Liberty. Oh, absolutely. New York would be brilliant! We need to get a move on before the prices skyrocket. I was reading an article that mentioned October might be a good time - not too hot, not too cold, and the autumn colours would be beautiful. October sounds perfect. I’ll have a look at dates and prices this week. We could try for something around Poppy’s half-term, that would make things easier. Remember that dreadful delayed flight we had going to Spain all those years ago? Oh, don't remind me! Stranded in Malaga for twelve hours! Honestly, at the time it felt like the end of the world. Poor little Ben was a nightmare. He was, wasn't he! Throwing tantrums and demanding ice cream every five minutes. You handled it like a saint, you did. Compared to that, this week with the staff shortages feels like a walk in the park! Well, it's good to have perspective, isn’t it? Though, Ben was a handful even  without  travel delays. Remember his obsession with dinosaurs when he was three? He used to roar at the postman! How could I forget?

Right, so, this is…this is the mess. It's the culmination of, honestly, far too much reading and number-crunching. You wouldn't believe the amount of primary source material I had to wade through for this module. Salford's looking lively then? You’ve got more paperwork than a solicitor’s office. What is it precisely? Still that economic history thing? Yep, still the economic history of the Industrial Revolution. But this? This is my dissertation proposal. See, I’ve had to lay out the research question, methodology, potential sources, the whole shebang. It’s basically a promise to the university that I can actually  do  this thing and it'll be worth something. Sounds…intense. So, what  is  the research question then? Don't use too much fancy academic language, yeah? My brain's still recovering from last week's philosophy lecture. Fair enough. Okay, so, basically, I'm looking at the impact of the canal system on the textile industry in Lancashire, specifically around the period of 1820-1850. Seems pretty niche, right? Not massively, actually. Canals and textiles are big chunks of the whole Industrial Revolution story, innit? I remember a bit about that from A-Levels. So, what's new about  your  angle? What are you arguing? That's the tricky bit. Existing scholarship tends to focus on the broader economic impact - trade routes, bigger markets, that kind of thing. I’m trying to drill down into the local level, see how canals affected  specific  mill towns, wage structures for specific types of workers - weavers, spinners, overlookers – and whether it led to increased social stratification. Right, so you’re looking at the nitty-gritty, the people on the factory floor. Clever. Are you using local records? Parish registers, maybe? That's where the juicy stuff is, right? Exactly! I've been digging through the Lancashire Archives for weeks. It’s phenomenal. They've got ledgers, payroll records, even letters between mill owners! It’s a treasure trove. But... ... it's also overwhelming. Honestly, I feel like I’m drowning in data. That's why this proposal's so important – it's supposed to help me focus. So, this proposal is your life raft in a sea of 19th-century paperwork? Makes sense. Have you got a working title yet? Something dramatic? I’m toying with "Canals and Cloth: Labour, Landscape, and the Shaping of Industrial Lancashire".

You know, I had the strangest dream last night. Really vivid. Oh yeah? What sort of strange? Don't tell me you were back in Dartford, dealing with another rogue pigeon. No pigeons, thankfully. But I was… teaching a class full of penguins. Just lecturing them about quadratic equations. And they were all taking notes with little flippers. It was utterly ridiculous. Woah! Penguins! Can I see the penguins, Mummy? They were just in a dream, sweetheart. Sadly not real. Wouldn't be able to mark their homework! Rawr! Penguins don’t know maths! That’s brilliant. You’d fit right in, teaching penguins. I bet they’d be a more engaged bunch than some of my clients. Don't jinx it! I’m happy with my human students, even if they’re occasionally...challenging. What about you? Any wild dreams lately, love? Actually, yeah. I dreamt I won the Lottery. A ridiculous amount. Enough to buy, you know…a proper garden. And a dog. A doggie! A fluffy one! Big one! That licks you! A dog would be lovely. We’ve talked about it so many times, haven't we? But the responsibility…especially with two little ones. Exactly. It’s a proper commitment. But in my dream, I’d already put all the groundwork in. Walkies every morning, training classes…a whole rota. It felt…right. And fantastically easy. So you're living the dream within a dream? Sounds rather complicated. I know, right? It’s silly. But it made me think. It's not just about the money, is it? It's about having the time and flexibility to do things you really want to do. Like spending long afternoons in the garden, or taking the dog for a run in the countryside. Things we barely have time for now. Absolutely. It's the freedom.
