I often dream I’m on holiday somewhere exotic, reading a book in the sun, without a worry in the world. But the reality is a bit more…marking essays and packed lunches. I dream about dinosaurs! Big, scary dinosaurs! They eat all the broccoli! Yes! Rawr! Roar back at them, little man! Maybe your dreams are showing you what you'll be like when you’re bigger - a fearsome dinosaur expert! Or maybe you’ll be a penguin teacher! Who knows? I’m just hoping for a dream about a fully marked pile of coursework.

Och, I’m still achin’, Liam. Honestly, I feel like I’ve been run over by a bus. A very small, very stubborn bus. You’re still complaining about that trip over the cat? Honestly, Maisie, it wasn’t exactly a catastrophe. A grazed knee and a bruised ego. Bruised ego? Liam, I landed right on me hip! Me hip! I thought I’d broken summat, I did. And the cat? He just sat there, lookin' smug like he’d planned the whole thing. Typical. He probably did, the little monster. But the A&E people said it was just a sprain, didn't they? And a decent amount of swelling. They gave you those cold packs, right? Aye, they did. Though the wait was bleedin’ ridiculous. Hours, Liam. Hours just sittin’ in that plastic chair, surrounded by people lookin’ even worse than me. There was this poor fella with a busted hand, and a lass whose ankle was all swollen up. Made me feel a bit daft, to be honest. Just a wee graze. Well, you felt it was bad enough to warrant a trip, didn’t you? And that’s what matters. Look, I’m glad you went. Better safe than sorry. Did they give you any painkillers? They gave me summat, a codeine thing. It’s wearin’ off now, though, and the throbbing's comin' back. Honestly, I feel like me grandma. She used to get hip pains like this. Maybe I’m startin’ to turn into her. Don't be silly. You’re 24, not 84. You probably just did a bit too much gardening yesterday. Trying to wrestle those rose bushes into submission, eh? Aye, they were fightin' back something fierce. But still, a sprain? I’m gonna be hobblin’ about for a week at this rate. I’ve got loads to do next week, important stuff at work… You’ll be fine. Just take it easy. No gardening for a while, definitely. And maybe delegate some of that work. You can’t run yourself ragged, especially when you're nursing a bruised hip courtesy of Mr. Whiskers. He’s gettin’ away with it, that one. He’s curled up on the sofa, purring like he’s earned a medal. Do you think I should get him a little cone? Just to keep him away from me legs. A cone? Maisie, you’re brilliant. Seriously. But maybe just keep a close eye on him.

Dreadful business, isn’t it, Derek? This situation in Sudan… utterly appalling. Makes you feel rather helpless, sitting here in Hove, you know? Aye, terribly sad, Richard. The news is just a constant stream of it, isn't it? You can't escape it. Though, I was reading something this morning about the potential impact on global grain prices. Ripple effect, that. Always a ripple effect. Grain prices, you say? I hadn’t even considered that. Just the sheer human suffering, you see, that grabs you. Do you remember old Mrs. Peterson from the school? She was doing some volunteer work with refugees a few years back. Came back completely changed. Mrs. Peterson! Goodness, yes. A fiery one, she was. Always pushing the kids to think critically. Right, about those prices, apparently significant amounts of wheat come from the region. It's just another layer of complication, isn’t it? Still, I’m more concerned about the price of timber these days. My little project… Ah, yes! The project. You haven’t given up on that, have you? Last time we spoke you were still wrestling with the local council about permits. Wrestling is putting it mildly! It was a battle, Richard, a proper battle. But I’ve finally cracked it. Got all the approvals. The workshop’s practically finished. It’s amazing what a well-placed donation to the local cricket club can achieve, eh? You and your… "strategic philanthropy," as you call it. So, you're truly going ahead with the bespoke furniture business then? A risky venture, Derek, at your age. Risky, perhaps. But I’m bored, Richard! Blasted bored since I retired from the removals business. Needed something to occupy my mind, something… creative. I’ve always enjoyed working with my hands. Remember that ridiculous birdhouse I built for Emily when she was little? How could I forget? It looked like a miniature Victorian mansion! It was a hazard to any self-respecting sparrow. But Emily loved it. Still has it, I believe. Speaking of Emily, how are she and John doing? Heard they're thinking about expanding the physiotherapy practice. Oh, they're doing brilliantly! Absolutely teeming with clients, apparently. John's been working ridiculous hours, but Emily keeps him grounded. Expanding is the plan, yes. They’re looking at opening a second clinic in Worthing. Smart move, that. Worthing’s booming. Have you seen the new development down by the seafront?

You know, this Guardhouse is… surprisingly pleasant. I wasn’t expecting much from a pub right next to the barracks. It's got a bit of character, hasn’t it? Not just your standard sports bar feel. It is. They've done a good job with the décor. That mural on the far wall – the one with the old map of Woolwich? Quite impressive. Much better than that awful Wetherspoons down the road. Reminds me a bit of some of the old pubs I used to frequent in Edinburgh, actually. Though, Edinburgh pubs tend to be a bit… darker. Edinburgh pubs are a whole different beast, aren't they? All low ceilings and history practically dripping from the walls. Right, food. Are we thinking pub grub, or shall we scout out that new Indian place a few streets over? I'm properly ravenous. Pub grub's fine. A decent pie would hit the spot, I think. Though, I must admit, I've been craving a proper curry. Still, let's not overthink it. We can always come back for curry another night. What did you think of last night’s Happy Valley? Oh my goodness, last night! Absolutely brutal. Catherine Cawood is a force of nature, isn't she? I was gripping the sofa the whole time. That ending… wow. Truly gripping. All those twists! Did you predict any of that? Not a single one! I thought I had a handle on it halfway through, then bam – completely thrown off. I rather admire the writing, actually. It doesn’t pull any punches. It’s grim, but it’s also brilliantly observed. Reminds me a bit of the social research I did back at university, actually - just a different kind of investigation. You always manage to tie things back to university, don’t you? You were so serious back then. Trying to save the world with your sociological studies. Someone had to! And besides, it’s all connected, isn’t it? Human behaviour… it’s all fascinating. Speaking of which, how are Whiskers doing? Did you remember to leave him enough food while we were out? Yes, of course! He practically has a personal chef now. He’s gotten so demanding in recent months. Little furry tyrant. I think he was plotting his dominance while I was transcribing those endless legal documents today. Sounds about right. He’s inherited your meticulous nature, I suppose.

Ach, this is the ticket. Proper pint o’ heavy. Needed that after wrestling wi’ young Jamie all afternoon. He’s determined tae break every rule in the warehouse, the wee scamp. Jamie, eh? Still causing mayhem, is he? Sounds like a familiar face. Reminds me o’ my wee nephew, Finn. He’s convinced gravity is a suggestion, rather than a law. Aye well, Jamie's got a bit o’ that about him too. Anyway… you’ve been quiet. Still dreaming about that trip tae Iceland? Last I heard you were drowning in brochures. Drowning is putting it mildly! I've narrowed it down to two routes, actually. The Ring Road, obviously, but I’m seriously considering adding the Westfjords. It's a bit more remote, bit trickier to navigate, but the photography… imagine the landscapes! Those sheer cliffs, the birdlife… Westfjords, eh? Sounds… bracing. I’m no much for the cold, tae be honest. I enjoyed that little jaunt tae the Highlands last summer, though. Ach, that was glorious weather we had. Not a cloud in the sky for a week. You went up to Loch Ness? Did you get any good shots? I saw some of your Instagram. The light on the water was stunning. Aye, Loch Ness and a bit around Glencoe. Got some decent ones, aye. Trying tae get a decent photo o' the monster proved a wee bit difficult, as you might imagine. The light was the key, I think. Early mornings, late evenings. That’s when the magic happens, right? Absolutely. Golden hour, blue hour... it’s everything. That's what's drawing me to Iceland, really. Imagine the Northern Lights dancing over black sand beaches. It’s a photographer's ultimate fantasy. I’ve been studying the aurora forecasts like a religious text. Aurora forecasts… fancy that! I just check the weather app. If it's not raining, I’m happy. I’ve been thinking about getting a new lens, though. Something wider angle. I keep missing bits of the landscape. A wider angle would be brilliant. Have you looked at the Sigma 16-28mm? It’s supposed to be fantastic for landscapes. Sharp as a tack and relatively affordable. I've been eyeing it myself. Sigma, ye say? I’ll need tae do some research. Always a bit hesitant spending a fortune on equipment, ye know? It’s easy to get carried away.

Honestly, Anon, your place always feels so…calm. A world away from the chaos that is my week ahead. Right, where was I? Oh yes, plans. I’m dreading the garden party on Saturday. Mrs. Featherstonehaugh insists on a croquet tournament, and you know how I am with a mallet. Mum, you always say that about Mrs. Featherstonehaugh's parties! It's never as bad as you make out. Besides, it's lovely to see everyone. And a bit of sunshine wouldn’t hurt. How's the paperwork coming along for the village fete? Don't even  mention  the fete paperwork. It's a beast. Endless spreadsheets and risk assessments. Honestly, you’d think we were launching a rocket into space, not selling jam and raffle tickets! And the committee...oh, the committee. Half of them seem to have forgotten how to communicate with anyone under the age of sixty. Sounds familiar. Tell me, have you had any luck with the nursery for Leo? I spoke to Little Acorns today, and they still haven't confirmed if they have a space for him next week. It’s stressful, isn’t it? I’m so worried about leaving him practically a stranger. Leo... Honestly, that's been my biggest worry. Little Acorns are proving remarkably unhelpful. They keep talking about waiting lists and ‘assessments’. I'm trying to be pragmatic, but it’s hard. It feels like I'm failing him somehow. I did speak to Sunshine Daycare, just down the road, and they sounded promising. A lot more… personal. Sunshine Daycare? Really? I’ve heard good things. Mrs. Davies who lives across the street’s granddaughter goes there and she says they’re brilliant. Less structured, more free play, right? Maybe that would be a better fit for Leo. He's full of energy. That’s exactly what they said. They seem to understand that toddlers don’t thrive on rigid timetables. Although, the fees are slightly… robust. Still, peace of mind is worth something, isn’t it? What about you, anything exciting happening this week? Apart from the usual classroom dramas, of course. Well, the Year Two's are putting on a play, "The Very Hungry Caterpillar," on Friday. It's going to be chaotic, I'm sure, but the kids are so excited. I've got to finish marking those reading records, and prepare for parent-teacher meetings next week.

This is really lovely, ANON. You’ve outdone yourself. Yorkshire pudding’s spot on, too. Proper crispy. Aye, thanks, love. Me mum's recipe. Can’t go wrong with a classic. So, Liam, you were saying something about the building site before? Sounds… intense. Nah, it's alright mostly. Bit repetitive, to be fair. Same brick, same pattern, all day long. It’s honest work though, innit? Pays the bills. The foreman's a right grumpy git, though. Keeps shouting about 'efficiency' like we’re robots or summat. Efficiency, huh? Sounds familiar. My boss at the factory, Mr. Harding, is obsessed with that too. Every second counts, apparently. Makes you feel a bit… dehumanised, doesn't it? Tell me about it! At the conference centre, it's all about ‘seamless transitions’ and ‘client expectation management’. Like people are complicated machines you’ve gotta keep oiled and happy. I swear half the time I'm just running around putting out fires. Fires? Seriously? What kind of fires? Oh, you know. Speakers not turning up, vegan options running out, the projector refusing to work, some bloke trying to use a chainsaw to ‘enhance’ the décor… the usual. A chainsaw? You’re pulling my leg! Wish I were. Honestly! It was a very enthusiastic team-building exercise apparently. Thankfully, security intervened. Blimey. Sounds mental. At least my biggest problem is whether to use blue bricks or grey ones. Less exciting, but, you know, safer. Speaking of excitement, did you manage to find anything decent for that wedding next month? It’s quite formal, remember? Uh… not really. I’ve got… this. Thought it might do. Liam! It’s a  wedding . Your Aunt Carol will have a heart attack. You need a suit, at the very least. Or a nice shirt and some smart trousers. Aye, you’re right. You can’t go looking like you’ve just rolled out of bed. Though, to be fair, your fashion sense hasn’t always been top-notch. Remember that Hawaiian shirt you wore to Grandma’s 70th? Don't remind me. I was, like, fifteen. Thought I was being cool. You were definitely  something . Right, I’m going to have a quick look online. Surely there's something affordable somewhere. There's a charity shop near me that sometimes has good finds. Good shout! Failing that, you could borrow me Dad's old suit. It’s a bit… dated, but it’s better than that t-shirt.

You know, I’ve been thinking about tea. Proper tea, I mean. Not that herbal nonsense. There’s a certain comfort in it, isn’t there? A ritual. Brings back memories of school mornings, a cuppa after marking essays… Aye, that it does. I’ve always been partial to a good brew. Mum used to make it just so. Strong, but with a drop of milk, never sugar though. Said it spoiled the flavour. Can’t say I ever got the hang of brewing it quite like she did. Always a bit… weak, mine is. Oh, Arthur, you’ve always been a bit too generous with the water, haven't you? It's not hard, really. It's all about the temperature and the timer. Though, I confess, I experimented with a lot of different blends when I was looking after the children. Some of them were frightfully particular. One little boy, Thomas, absolutely insisted on Earl Grey, with  exactly  one and a half sugars. The cheek! Children  are  particular, aren't they? But it's lovely to cater to that, in a small way. A little bit of comfort in a cup. I always found a cup of tea was the perfect pick-me-up after a particularly challenging class. A good PG Tips, usually. Reliable. You can't go wrong with PG Tips. Reliable? That's a bit… bland, isn’t it, Margaret? Personally, I prefer something with a bit of character. Yorkshire Tea, now there's a proper brew. It’s got backbone, that one. Makes you feel ready to take on the world. Or at least, ready to tackle the crossword. Yorkshire? Bit strong for me, that. Gives me the jitters. I used to try it when my old mate, Barry, would bring some back from visiting his daughter up north. Couldn't manage more than a couple of sips. I can see that, Arthur. It’s definitely a bolder flavour. Although, I did find it went down quite nicely with a digestive biscuit. That’s important, you know. The right biscuit is crucial to the tea-drinking experience. Absolutely, Elsie. It must complement, not compete! A shortbread, perhaps, or a nice, crunchy ginger nut. Something with a bit of bite. Though, for a really soothing cup, I'm partial to a custard cream. Don’t tell anyone! Custard creams? Blimey. You’ve gone soft, Margaret. That's child's play.

Right, who wants seconds of this aubergine? Honestly, I think I've slightly overdone it on the balsamic glaze, but it’s still pretty good. Don't you dare say that, it's delicious, Elodie! You always make the best veggie dishes. I’m starving after that drive up from London. Traffic was horrendous. Aye, London traffic. Nightmare. Reminds me of trying to navigate Cardiff city centre at rush hour – a constant battle. This is lovely, mind. Proper good. So, Anon was just saying they were protesting outside the Senedd yesterday. About… what was it, Rhys? Something to do with health services? Yeah, it was the cuts to the community clinics, mostly. Really affecting people in Caerphilly. Got a bit heated, to be honest. A few raised voices, a couple of arrests, the usual. Nothing major though. Didn't want my mum worrying back home. That’s awful about the clinics. It's so disheartening to see services being chipped away. Reminds me of the debates we have at uni around funding for local arts initiatives. Always the same argument: ‘not essential’. Speaking of essential, I had a funny experience at work this week. We’re rolling out mandatory CRB checks for all our training staff – a new government requirement. And one of my team, poor bloke, was quite distressed because he'd forgotten he’d volunteered to help out at a local dog shelter a few years ago. Apparently, his application was borderline. Really? Helping out at a dog shelter? How borderline is that? Apparently, even though he was just walking dogs, there was a slight technicality about unsupervised access to animals. Thankfully, we managed to sort it out, but it just goes to show how bureaucratic things have become. Bureaucracy's the word, innit? Back home, it's the same story. I’m trying to get a personal license for driving a minibus for the local rugby club. Endless forms, medicals, training… Feels like they're trying to make it impossible. Honestly! Speaking of driving, you wouldn’t believe the near miss I had on the way here. Someone came flying across lanes. I honestly thought they were going to end up in a ditch. I was thinking about putting a dashcam in my car. Good idea. The roads around Norwich can be a bit… spirited, to put it politely. Fancy a pint after this? The King's Head in Wroxham’s not bad.

Right! I'm back! Honestly, feeling like a proper zombie. Sunburn and a serious lack of sleep, but it was  so  worth it. Welcome home! You look… delightfully wrecked. Did you have a good time, then? I swear the house felt weirdly quiet without you barging around. Quiet is an understatement! It was blissfully peaceful, but I missed the chaos, honestly. Cornwall was beautiful, though. Proper windswept beaches, you wouldn’t believe it. We spent nearly every day surfing - well, attempting to surf. I think I swallowed half the Atlantic. Sounds about right for you! Surfing? Really? You and water don’t usually get along. Did Liam teach you? He did! He’s like, a natural. Makes it look effortless. I spent most of the time faceplanting, but he was really patient. It was fun though. Anyway, what's been going on here? Anything exciting happen while I was away? Did the plants survive my absence? The plants are surprisingly alive! I watered them religiously, obviously. Work’s been… work. A few new admissions, which is always a bit intense. We had that particularly difficult case I was telling you about before you left, the one with the anxiety and social isolation? Oh yeah, the one you were really worried about. How's that going? It’s… slowly improving. Small victories, you know? Got him interacting with the group today, just for a few minutes. It felt huge. Honestly, those little moments make it all worthwhile, even when things are really tough. That’s brilliant, seriously. You’re doing amazing work, you know that? I always feel a bit inadequate comparing my spreadsheet wrangling to what you do. Don’t be ridiculous. Your project management skills are essential! Without you keeping everything organised, the whole team would descend into chaos. Besides, everyone’s important. Did you see Marco while you were gone? I did! He surprised me, actually. He sent me a ridiculously cheesy postcard - you know how he is. Turns out he's trying to learn pottery. Pottery?! Marco? That’s… unexpected. Honestly, I never pictured him with anything more artistic than his Spotify playlists. Apparently, he’s surprisingly good. He sent a picture of a wonky vase. It was glorious. Oh! And I bumped into Chloe and Ben - they're doing really well. They're thinking of moving to Brighton! Fancy that. Brighton! That's a nice move for them.

Honestly, this planning application for number seven Willow Creek is ludicrous. They want to add a whole extension! It'll completely block Mrs. Henderson’s light. Willow Creek, eh? Bit ambitious, that. I saw the pictures online. Right on the boundary, isn’t it? They’ll have a fight on their hands. Though, given how quickly houses are selling around here, I can understand wanting to maximise the value. It's not about value, it’s about ruining the village aesthetic. It's charming, that’s why we moved here! And honestly, I find myself thinking about the planning regulations a lot more than I used to. It’s weird. It comes with the territory of owning property, I think. Used to be, I wouldn’t have even noticed. But did you hear back from the Macmillan nurse about Sarah? Not yet. I left a message yesterday, just touching base. I feel… useless, really. Sitting here worrying about building extensions while she’s… you know. Fighting. You're not useless. You’re a brilliant friend. She adores you. And you’re doing everything you can. Remember when she was worried about the garden? You volunteered to weed it for her. That meant the world to her. Small things add up. It feels like treading on eggshells sometimes. I don't want to say the wrong thing, or make things worse. She was being so brave at the garden club meeting last week, smiling and chatting… and then I saw the tiredness in her eyes. It just hit me. It's okay to feel that, love. To acknowledge it. Don’t worry about saying the ‘wrong’ thing. Just be there. Listen. Offer a cup of tea, a shoulder, whatever she needs. She's a tough cookie, you know? She'll tell you if she needs space. I just hope… I hope the latest round of chemo is working. She seemed so weary afterwards. And the side effects… I can’t even imagine. They said it was targeting the cancer cells well in the last report. It’s not a guarantee, obviously, but it’s encouraging. We both know the road ahead is long and difficult. We have to focus on the good news when we can, yeah? You’re right. It's just… I wish there was something more tangible I could do. Something that would genuinely make a difference. Beyond weeding a garden, I mean.

Right, I’m tellin’ ya, Sarah, this new coffee machine? Absolutely useless. Utter waste of space, it is. Makes a cup of somethin' that tastes more like dishwater than coffee. And it takes forever! Like, five minutes just for a lukewarm brew. Tell me about it, Mark. Honestly, it’s been a nightmare since they swapped it out. I tried to make a latte for a student earlier – bless their heart, they were having a right day – and it just sputtered and then produced this… brown liquid. They looked like they wanted to cry. Aye, sounds about right. They probably thought we were actively tryin' to wind 'em up. It's not just the coffee either, is it? It's the noise they make. Sounds like a washing machine gargling. Gives me a right headache after a few hours. The noise is appalling. I had a complaint just yesterday about the rumbling. Some poor girl on the third floor said it was keeping her up. I tried explaining it was the new machine, but she just didn’t believe me. She thought we had a faulty pipe or somethin’. Salford Uni and their fancy new ‘improvements’. Honestly, they spend a fortune on this stuff, and it’s always a disaster. Remember that smart lighting system they installed last year? Took three weeks to get that sorted! Kept switchin’ off in the middle of the night, sendin' students into a panic. Oh, god, don’t remind me. I was on call for that. Spent half my nights wandering around corridors trying to reset the system. To be fair, the contract guys were useless. Couldn't tell a circuit breaker from a biscuit tin. That’s spot on! It’s always the same, innit? Outsourcin’ and contractors. Never get the job done right. Though, honestly, the worst thing I've gotta complain about is the new fire drills. The fire drills? What about them? They're a bit disruptive, sure, but… Disruptive? Sarah, they're chaos! They change the drill routes every single time, without tellin' anyone. Last week, I nearly had a heart attack tryin' to herd a bunch of students down a completely blocked stairwell. They didn’t even know they were supposed to be going that way! Oh, no. That sounds awful. I had a similar situation, actually. I was trying to make sure everyone got out safely from the ground floor, and then realised the designated exit was actually taped off for ‘maintenance’ nobody’d informed us about.

Honestly, seeing that couple arguing in Flemish just now… it was so  English . Like two people having a full-blown row about whether the waffles were properly buttered. It just made me miss home, you know? Aye, you always could pick out the Brits, couldn't you, love? Loud and clear, even when tryin' to be subtle. Package tours mostly, wouldn't you reckon? All bundled together, lookin' lost. Colin, that’s a bit harsh! Not everyone who speaks loudly is on a package tour. And I thought the Christmas market in Bruges was lovely. Just imagine taking the kids there… all the twinkling lights, the hot chocolate… a proper Christmas feeling. Bruges was gorgeous, Mum. But the traffic getting  into  Antwerp was a nightmare. Honestly, it took ages. I kept thinking about Herne Bay shopping – much more relaxed, you know? You can actually wander around without feeling like you're stuck in a queue. Herne Bay? Used to go there with me mum, years ago. Donkey rides on the beach, chips in paper... Simpler times, eh? Antwerp's got character, though. Just needs a bit of clearing out. Reminds me of London these days, really. Everything's busy these days, Colin. Even Brighton seafront is busier than it used to be, though I still love a paddle and a bit of fresh air. Did you see that little puppy in the window of that pet shop earlier? Gave me such a pang. Wish I could have another one. Oh, I did! It was adorable. Reminded me of Buster, when he was a pup. Remember how he used to chew everything? I miss having a dog. University’s a bit… restrictive, you know? I’d love a bigger place to keep one. What’s Mark doing for Christmas, Mum? Is he going to try and get tickets to a market again? Mark's sorting out Jack and Tom's birthdays. He’s really keen to get one of those bouncy castles. They'd love that. He’s also been talking about a little Dorset caravanning trip next summer. Said he wants to take them somewhere different. Caravanning? Bless him. Remember when I thought I’d be travelling the world by now? Retirement was supposed to be all sunshine and long holidays. Ended up mostly staring at daytime telly. Still, beats working, I suppose. You always had a good way of looking at things, Grandad.

Honestly, Mum, it’s ridiculous. All this fuss about the equality vote. It’s just, like, obvious, isn’t it? Everyone should be equal. Obvious to you, love, perhaps. But you'd be surprised how many people  don't  see it that way. It's a deeply ingrained thing sometimes, you know? Centuries of assumptions and…well, just plain prejudice. But it’s Ireland! I thought, like, everyone here was pretty chilled about that sort of stuff. Back in Bristol, it felt… well, a bit more complicated, to be honest. People didn’t always say the wrong things, but you could  feel  it, you know? Ireland is generally very progressive, yes, but even here there’s a lot of history to unpack. And the vote, as you know, isn’t exactly a landslide. There's a decent chunk of people who are...resistant, shall we say. My own sister, God love her, she had a right old rant about it last week. So much rambling about ‘tradition’ and ‘the sanctity of marriage’. Made my head spin! Ugh, seriously? My mate Liam’s dad said something similar the other day. Honestly, it's like they’re living in the Stone Age. Can’t they just see that people should be able to love who they want? It’s not hurting anyone. It's tempting to think that, isn't it? But for some people, it's about their own beliefs being challenged. They feel as though their worldview is being threatened. It's not always malicious, you know. Just…fear. Though, sometimes it is malicious. Your Liam’s dad sounds like a bit of a… well, never mind. He’s got that smug look, hasn’t he? Like he's got all the answers. Remember when you tried to explain evolution to Uncle Barry at last Christmas? He almost choked on his Brussels sprouts! Oh, don't remind me! It was a disaster. He insisted dinosaurs lived alongside humans. I nearly lost my mind. Honestly, some people are just determined to be wrong. It's their hobby! It’s probably why politics are so messy. Everyone’s shouting their opinions, thinking they’re right. Maybe. Though, it's good to argue, isn’t it? As long as people are listening to each other. My History teacher, Mr. Davies, he always says it’s vital to challenge assumptions. Your Mr. Davies sounds like a sensible man.

Honestly, Marjorie, that was a dreadful thing to say about Gerald. A hamster in a microwave! Where does he get these ideas? Oh, leave him alone, David. He's always been a bit… unique. Besides, he wasn’t suggesting he  actually  put a hamster in a microwave! It was a metaphor, I think. A very odd one, admittedly. Aye, a metaphor. About the new turning tools, see. The set I got from that fella in Spalding. Said they'd revolutionise me work. Revolutionise! Like putting a hamster in a microwave’ll revolutionise summat! They’re a right disaster, they are. Just chip the wood, they do. Ruin the grain. Turning tools, Gerald? I thought you gave that up years ago when your arthritis flared up. Gave it up? Never! A man's gotta 'ave 'is hobbies, David. Keeps the brain ticking, it does. Besides, got a commission, I 'ave. Old Mrs. Higgins wants a bird table, see. A proper one. With a little roof and everything. Can’t be giving 'er summat shoddy, can I? Especially not with these dreadful tools. Well, you always were meticulous, dear. Remember the rocking horse you made for little Emily? She adored it. Still has it, I believe. That were a good 'un, that were. Spent a fortnight on it, I did. Now  that  were proper craftsmanship. These Spalding tools… they wouldn’t 'ave lasted five minutes! So, about this ‘hamster in the microwave’ analogy? Any clarification on what it represents specifically? Because I'm genuinely intrigued. Was it a comment on the tools' inherent flaw, their destructive potential? He was trying to say they're too powerful, David. Overkill for the job. Like blasting something with a microwave when a gentle pat would do. It’s Gerald's way of being dramatic, you know. Exactly! Overkill! Like tryin’ to carve a rose with a chisel! These tools are for turning great chunks o’ oak, not for delicate work. They’re bludgeoning the wood to death! And cost me a pretty penny, they did. Should’ve stuck with me old Stanley set. Never did me wrong, those didn't. You know, Gerald, I think I have a few older tools in the shed. Belonged to my grandfather. He was a cabinet maker. Might be worth a look. They’re probably a bit more… refined. Really? You’d be willin’ to let me 'ave a look?

Honestly, John, you won’t believe what I was transcribing today. Someone’s diary entry, and it was entirely written backwards! Mirror writing. Apparently, it was a hobby of some people – Leonardo da Vinci, for instance. It's quite fascinating really, though I can't imagine doing it deliberately. My eyes would ache! Mirror writing? Goodness. That's dedication. Are you sure it wasn't just a very elaborate prank? People do try to confuse transcribers, you know. A prank? Nonsense. There was a time when people did things for the sheer intellectual challenge of it, dear. Not everything is about a laugh, you see. I once knew a boy at the school who could solve cryptic crosswords in  ten  minutes. Absolutely astonishing. Well, this wasn't a crossword, Agnes. It was diary entries. Personal reflections, jumbled up. It made for rather slow going, I can tell you. Speaking of slow, did you see that piece in the news about the cat who got stuck in a drainpipe for three days? Poor thing. I did! They had to use a little camera to locate it. Shows you the ingenuity people are coming up with, doesn't it? Though I must say, technology does worry me a bit. All this data collection… Oh, don't start on that, John. It's progressing whether we like it or not. Much like house prices, I suppose. Absolutely ridiculous, aren't they? My granddaughter, Emily, she's saving like mad, but feels she'll never be able to afford a place of her own. Tell me about it. It's a national crisis. And the banks! They’re practically laughing all the way to the bank, aren't they? Charging all sorts of fees. I keep thinking about consolidating my debts, but then there's the interest… it's a vicious cycle. It is. And don’t even get me started on the American political scene. It's becoming increasingly bewildering. Did you see… John, dear, let’s not descend into a political argument before dinner. Agnes does get a bit flustered. Though, I must say, this charging for plastic bags... It seems to have done the trick, though. Less plastic everywhere. Small victories, eh? Absolutely. It's the small victories that keep you going. Although, I did get a rather stern email from the supermarket the other day. Apparently, I forgot to scan my reusable bag at the checkout.

Honestly, you two. Look at this kitchen. It’s a disaster! Lego scattered everywhere, controllers abandoned... and not a single book in sight. But Mummy, Lloyd’s about to face Morjinn! It's  really  important! I'm almost to the Nether! Almost got diamond gear! Diamond gear? Nether? Morjinn? What about 'The Gruffalo'? Or 'Where the Wild Things Are'? Remember those, do you? We just bought you that beautiful illustrated copy of 'Alice in Wonderland'! I  have  read books, Mummy. I read 'Harry Potter' all last summer. Properly. Minecraft's way cooler than Harry Potter. You can build  anything . That’s lovely, darling. Truly. Building anything is fantastic. But screens all the time… I worry. It's not just about limiting screen time, is it? It’s about sparking imaginations in different ways. Lego  can  spark imagination, absolutely, and Minecraft too, but reading... it's a different kind of fuel for the brain. But the Ninjago series is  amazing ! The characters, the storylines… it’s like a really long, exciting book! It is, in a way. But it's presented in a different format. It’s passively received, you know? Reading, you  actively  create the images in your head, you follow the words. It’s exercising a different muscle. Can I build a dragon in Minecraft? A  really  big one? You absolutely can, sweetie. And you could read a book  about  dragons! Imagine all the descriptions you could use, all the details… making your Minecraft dragon even  better  because you’ve read about them. You think reading about dragons could help me build a better Ninjago temple? Absolutely! You'd get ideas for architecture, for the materials... for the  story  of the temple. Think about it. What's the history? Who built it? What's its purpose? These things are all in books. I need iron and gold… for dragon wings! Right, right. But how about this? We have a deal. For every half an hour you spend on the screens, you spend half an hour reading. Even just a chapter. We can make it a competition – see who can read the furthest. And I’ll read with you. Like a reading challenge? Will there be prizes? Possibly! Maybe a trip to the Lego store… or a new texture pack for Minecraft? We’ll have to negotiate. Can I pick the book? Of course, darling. Any book you want. Even one about dragons.

Honestly, girls, I'm  still  feeling the residual bliss of that holiday. Barbados was just...perfect, wasn't it? The colour of the water, the warmth… I haven't relaxed that much in ages. It was, Mum. Absolutely gorgeous. Though, I did miss my dogs a bit. Even paradise can't replace a good cuddle with Buster and Daisy, you know? Management's been a little hectic this week – a supplier let me down on a shipment of new Christmas decorations, can you believe it? Stressful, but at least I got a tan! Yeah, Barbados was amazing. Such a change from Manchester drizzle! Uni's been intense, though. I'm drowning in essays at the moment, especially this one on post-colonial literature. It's fascinating, but...long. Did you manage to get any good photos of the sea turtles, Mum? I was so hoping to snap a few. Oh, loads! I've got hundreds, actually. I'll have to sort through them. I even managed to get one of a turtle hatching! It was incredible; a proper miracle to witness. I'll show you both later. Listen, what are you two up to today then? Anything exciting planned? Well, I'm working this afternoon, sadly. Two shifts back-to-back. But Anya – my best friend – is coming round for dinner tomorrow night. We're thinking of trying that new Thai place in town. Fancy joining us? Oh, that sounds lovely! I'd absolutely love that. Thai is always a treat. What about you, darling? Any lectures or library sessions looming? Unfortunately, yes. A mountain of them, really. I need to hit the library for most of the day, sadly. But I was thinking… maybe tomorrow evening, after Anya's dinner? We could all go for a walk around Beacon Park? The leaves are supposed to be spectacular this weekend. Beacon Park sounds divine! A walk and a bit of fresh air would do us all good. That’s perfect. You know, I was thinking of finally getting around to sorting out those holiday souvenirs. I've got a pile of little beachcombed things that need a home. Honestly, Mum, your beachcombing skills are legendary. You always come back with the strangest but most charming little treasures. Remember that starfish you found that year in Cornwall? Oh, I do! It was a beauty! I still have it, don’t I? Sitting on the windowsill.

Right, Uno then? I’m calling dibs on being dealer. You two were messing around with the sandwiches for ages. Sorry, sorry! This one from Greggs is actually pretty good, you gotta admit. Way better than the vegan option Chloe was pushing. Chloe's just being…Chloe. Trying to be all virtuous. It’s exhausting. Honestly, you’d think she was single-handedly saving the planet with a carrot stick. Speaking of exhausting, Mrs. Davies giving us Shakespeare next term? I'm already dreading it. All those 'thees' and 'thous'. Ugh, tell me about it. I heard old Mr. Peterson's taking over the history module. Apparently, he’s obsessed with the Napoleonic Wars. Likely to bore us to death, isn't he? Peterson? He just drones on, doesn't he? My uncle did a tour in Afghanistan, and he says history’s important, but not like that. He said you need to understand  why  wars happen, not just the dates. True. It's weird, though. You see all this stuff on the news, about Ukraine and everything… feels so far away, and then suddenly, you're learning about Napoleon's campaigns and it's like, warfare has been going on forever. It's messed up. Remember that documentary we watched last year about the Bosnian War? Absolutely heartbreaking. Made you think, didn't it? It did. And it made me think about Jamal too. The stuff he's been saying lately… What’s he been saying? Some stuff about the new prefects. Mostly about how they’re all “posh kids” and don't understand what it's like for the rest of us. It’s a bit… uncomfortable. It’s more than a bit. He's making some pretty prejudiced comments, honestly. Saying they only got their positions because their parents donate to the school. It’s unfair, and it’s borderline racist. Wow. He’s never been like that before. I thought he was alright. Maybe something's going on? I don’t know. He’s been acting weird in general. Skulking around, listening to angry podcasts… Actually, remember that weird military recruitment thing they had at school last week? He seemed really fixated on that. Ugh, yeah. All those guys with their perfectly pressed uniforms talking about service and duty. It felt…off. My dad said it’s been getting more aggressive, the army trying to get young people.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is  killing  me this year. Physics is just...layers and layers of baffling. I swear, he enjoys making us feel stupid. Tell me about it! My brain feels like scrambled eggs after his lessons. Did he give you that impossible question about projectile motion again? The one with the catapult and the marshmallows? The marshmallow one! Yes! I spent the entire weekend trying to work it out, and I’m still not entirely sure. It’s just… why are we launching marshmallows, Mr. Davies? Shouldn’t we be, like, calculating the trajectory of a rocket or something slightly more impressive? Exactly! It feels like a practical joke. Mrs. Peterson's English lessons are a blessed relief, though. At least she makes reading interesting. I finally finished "Wuthering Heights" – it’s surprisingly intense. Oh, I’ve heard that’s a right downer. I’m still slogging through "Pride and Prejudice." It's…fine. A bit slow, though. Reminds me a bit of Mr. Davies explaining the difference between potential and kinetic energy – endlessly repetitive. Spot on. He’s definitely got a “slow burn” teacher vibe. What did you think of that announcement about form photos tomorrow? I'm dreading it. Ugh, the  absolute worst . I’m already planning my strategic pose. Gotta hide the under-eye bags. Did you hear about Chloe and Liam? Apparently, they were laughing in Mr. Peterson’s class again. He actually sent them to see Mrs. Hawthorne! No way! Mrs. Hawthorne? That's intense. She's legendary for her…quiet disapproval. Liam's going to be mortified. He’s got such a crush on her, hasn’t he? He does! It’s almost painful to watch. Speaking of mortifying, remember when Tom accidentally called Mr. Davies "Dad" last year? Oh my god, I'd completely forgotten! That was brilliant! The look on Mr. Davies' face... pure horror. He didn’t say anything, just paled and hurried away. He practically sprinted! It's still brought up at lunch. It's school folklore now. Anyway, I was thinking… we should watch "17 Again" this weekend. I've seen it a million times, but it’s always a good laugh. Ooh, yes! Definitely! I’ve been wanting to watch it again. It's so silly, but in a good way. Imagine being transported back to school, reliving it all. It’s tempting, isn’t it? Though, thinking about it, I'm not sure I’d want to relive  every  day.

Right, so, Transylvania, eh? You’re actually going? Seriously? Yep! Booked the flights last week. Mum's been on at me for ages to go, said it's incredible, all the history and, you know, vampire lore. A bit cheesy, admittedly, but I'm up for it. You should come! Vampires? Liv, you're mental! It’s October, aren’t you going to be freezing your bits off? And surrounded by bats! It's not just about Dracula, Chloe! They have stunning castles and beautiful scenery. And it's the shoulder season, so hopefully not  too  packed with tourists. Anyway, October’s the perfect time for spooky vibes. Liam, you could use a bit of a break from your dissertation. Dissertation's going well, thanks. But Transylvania… that’s a bit intense, even for me. What about Dan? Is he coming with you? He’s trying to get the time off work, but it’s looking unlikely. He’s really gutted. Says he wants to experience proper Romanian coffee shops. He's obsessed with finding the  perfect  espresso. Mate, tell him he's chasing a shadow! You won’t find a decent espresso in Transylvania. They mostly drink instant, you know. It’s a whole different coffee culture over there. Try everything else, though - the food is bonza! "Bonza?" Seriously, Mark? Still using Aussie slang after all these years? It’s a reflex! Twenty years is hard to shake off, Chloe. Besides, "bonza" applies to pretty much everything good. This Sunday evening, for example, is bonza. Good company, good drinks… Fair enough. So, what are your summer plans, Mark? Still hoping to get back to the coast? Yeah, absolutely. Got a bit of leave lined up. Hoping to surf at Bells Beach for a week. It'd be grouse to get a few good swells. Ooh, jealous! I’m just planning on baking my way through the summer, probably. Trying out new recipes – sourdough is my nemesis at the moment, it's just… wonky. You and sourdough! You’ll conquer it eventually. Speaking of baking, I’m thinking of doing a little pop-up shop thing at the café on weekends. Nothing serious, just a chance to test out some new pastries. Maybe lavender scones? Lavender scones sound amazing! Definitely pop in. Are Sarah and Ben coming over later? I wanted to tell them about this article I read on… They’re running late, apparently.

Right, nearly dinner. And honestly, after battling that muddy obstacle course, I'm starving. How are my little adventurers feeling? AMAZING! I won the log roll! And I didn't fall in the mud puddle, Mummy! I almost won the tyre run, but my shoe got stuck. It was very muddy though. You both were brilliant. Honestly, well done. I’m so glad we did that – a bit of fresh air and a good laugh. Now, about the party… Liam's rang, did you hear? Party! Party! Is there cake? Will there be music? Loud music? Yes, darling, there will be cake. And yes, Liam is putting on a playlist. He said he's going for a bit of everything - some classic 90s, a bit of pop, a sprinkle of... well, you'll hear it! We're going this Saturday, remember? Saturday! Can I wear my sparkly shoes? Absolutely sparkle-shoes-ready! Though maybe not the best footwear for dancing on grass, hmm? We'll think of something. I'm worried about getting decent photos though. Last time, we looked like we'd wrestled a pig. You  did  look muddy, Mummy. Oh, you two are terrible! But you’re right. Speaking of photos... I was thinking about sorting through those family photos I took last summer. They’re all on the hard drive. What do you think? Maybe we could print a few, get some framed? Can we put the one of me with the giant carrot in it? And the one where you were pretending to be the Queen of Hearts! Good choices! Though, the Queen of Hearts wasn't  entirely  flattering, was it? I’m still trying to get my hair back into shape after that photoshoot… it was a  lot  of red dye. Remember when I tried to teach you both about Alice in Wonderland? You read us the story! And you showed us the Mad Hatter's hat! I liked the Cheshire Cat. He disappeared! He did, didn't he? Actually, that reminds me - I saw an aerial hoop demonstration the other day at the village fete. It looked incredible! Think you two would be interested in trying something like that? It's quite a workout. Aerial hoop! Like a princess? Is it very high up? It is high up, but you're safely strapped in! It's surprisingly strong. Anyway, back to reality for now. Dinner’s nearly ready.

Right then, that was a lovely roulade, wasn’t it? Proper posh for a Tuesday! Though I do think a bit more cream wouldn’t have gone amiss. Posh, you say? It was lovely, it was. Better than anything I’ve ever managed, I'll tell you that. Always burnt my attempts to a cinder. You’ve a real knack, Diane. It’s just a recipe I picked up years ago, Arthur. Simple really. But tell me, has Chloe got her results yet? You were expecting them this morning, weren't you? I got them! I did! I got a B in English Lit! And an A in History! She did! She did! Look, she's showing off already. Brilliant, Chloe! That’s fantastic news. A B in English Lit and an A in History? Very impressive indeed. Hard work pays off, doesn’t it? Well done, love. What about the others then? Maths was... tricky. Ended up with a C. And Science… let’s just say I'm glad that’s over. C’s not bad, love. Not bad at all. Plenty of good jobs needed folks with a C in Maths these days. Don't you fret about it. Speaking of jobs, Bethany, have you thought any more about what you're leaning towards? You were awfully quiet during Dad’s rant about needing to think about futures. Dad’s always ranting. It’s exhausting! I’m thinking about maybe doing something with animals. Like a vet nurse or something. That’s a worthwhile ambition. Sounds lovely. You'd need good grades in Science for that though, wouldn't you? You could always retake. Though, honestly, I’m thinking about just working for a year. Earning some money. I’ve started taking driving lessons, you know. Driving lessons, you have? That's smart thinking! I never had a license myself. Never saw the need. Though my sister Doris did, always zooming around in her Morris Minor. Gave me a lift to Ipswich once, nearly had to hang on for dear life! Oh, Arthur, you and your stories. Always something dramatic. Mine's been trying to get a taxi lately, the parents' evening at the school was a nightmare. Queues stretching down the street! You know, I was at parents’ evening too, last week. Found out little Timmy in my class is spending all his time on that… what do they call it now… TikTok?

Right, Dad, you’re sure you want to play another round? I’m still reeling from the last one. Feels like I learned more about strategic retreats than I did in my university lectures. Don't be dramatic, Liam. It was a good game. You're getting better, I’ll grant you that. Though my rook still seems to have your number. Honestly, the noise drifting up from downstairs! Sounds like a miniature war is being waged. Breakfast is ready, everyone. And Liam, put that board down for five minutes and eat something. You'll need your energy. Thanks, Mum. Just reconvening after a…difficult battle. Dad's basically a Chinese chess oracle, you know. He anticipates my every move. Nonsense. Just experience. I've been playing since I was a boy. It's a beautiful game, really. The way the pieces move, the history behind it… it's fascinating. Did you know it’s older than chess? Everything's fascinating to you, Richard. Remember when you were obsessed with the way pigeons communicate? Spending hours recording their coos and trying to decipher them. There was something to it! I still think they're passing on vital information. Perhaps about breadcrumb locations. You're a legend, Dad. Speaking of recordings, I had a student last week, from South Korea, who was fascinated by Winston Churchill’s speeches. She wanted me to explain the rhetoric he used, like his use of metaphor and… Oh, Churchill! Such a remarkable man. Though sometimes his views… well, let’s just say they haven’t aged terribly well. He was a product of his time, wasn't he? Still, his wartime leadership... Quite. It’s interesting how strongly people still feel about him. There was a debate on Scottish independence the other day, and someone brought him up, arguing his resolve should be an example. I think it highlights the appeal of strong leadership, regardless of the era. Makes you wonder how different things would be if he'd had a slightly different perspective on... well, various things. We were also talking about New Zealand – she’d never been. Keeps asking me to describe the landscapes. Easier to show her than to tell, I suppose. New Zealand is stunning. I’d love to go. Though the thought of such a long flight… and the time difference! I’m trying to be more organised with my schedule, you know.

Honestly, this weather’s something else, isn't it? Feels like a perpetual November. Still, beats Bury in November, I reckon. Absolutely. Dampness, yes, but… manageable. Bury in November… well, you know. Glorious grey. A sort of romantic grey, I suppose. Though romantic doesn’t help when your car needs an MOT. I've been putting it off, you know. Just… haven't felt like sorting it. Don’t put it off too long! It’s stressing me out just thinking about it. I've got Mark dealing with mine, thank goodness. Speaking of stressing out, how are your students going? Any particularly bright sparks this term? Some. It’s a mixed bag, as always. I've got a young Korean chap who's incredibly diligent, but his grammar is… creative. And a lovely older woman from Saudi Arabia, determined to learn English to communicate better with her grandchildren. It’s rewarding, but… the pay isn't exactly bolstering my pension prospects. Tell me about it! Postgraduate loan hangs over me like a dark cloud. At least I’m earning, though. Teaching in Poland isn't exactly a fortune, but it's something. Did you see that article about the proposed changes to pensions? It’s terrifying. Saw it, yes. Honestly, it’s just… disheartening. Another thing to worry about. I never really had a proper pension, of course. Let's not go there. I’ve been rather distracted by Netflix. Have you seen 'The Crown'? Oh my god, yes! I’m completely obsessed. Though, it’s a bit unsettling to see the Royal Family playing out like a slightly less dramatic version of reality TV. Speaking of unsettling... I was reading about consent the other day, for a training module we have to do. It’s surprisingly complex, and I feel like we’re still getting the hang of it, even as adults. Absolutely. It's crucial, isn’t it? And far more nuanced than people often realize. It's good that you’re being proactive with that training. Educating people is vital. Though sometimes... sometimes I worry things aren’t changing fast enough. Me too. It’s a constant, ongoing conversation. Right, practicalities. So, are you feeling up to driving back to Krakow tomorrow? Or do you want me to take over? My sat-nav is a bit wonky, but I can usually find our way. Oh, honestly, my dear, driving is… taxing these days.

Honestly, this place is mental. Didn’t realise it’d be  this  busy on a Saturday. Glad we managed to snag a table though. Tell me about it. Booked it online ages ago, practically a miracle. And yeah, good choice avoiding the booze for today, Liam. Sixthform essays aren't exactly improved by a dodgy pint. Dodgy pint? It's responsible decision-making, Ben. Besides, I’ve got a History essay due Monday that's currently staring blankly back at me. Human Sciences applications are stressing me out enough, I don't need the added complication of a headache. True, true. Human Sciences... heavy stuff. What are you thinking in terms of specialisation? I’m leaning heavily towards the Social and Demographic strand, you know, looking at population trends and stuff. I'm still waffling, to be honest. I like the idea of the Cognitive one, but I keep worrying I'll get bogged down in neuroscience and miss the bigger picture. It’s a lot of different things to juggle. What about Maths? Are you sticking with that? Yeah, definitely. Found my groove with it, didn’t I? Applying for Warwick, hopefully. Honestly, the prospect of those problem sheets for the next three years is simultaneously terrifying and… exciting. More exciting, probably. What are your options? Oxford, obviously. But Leeds and UCL are on the list too, depending on how the personal statement goes. Thinking about maybe adding a bit about my cooking, actually. Sounds ridiculous, I know. Ridiculous? No way! You make a mean lasagne, Liam. People rave about your lasagne. That’s a genuine skill! Shows dedication, attention to detail… all the things unis want to see. You think so? I just felt like it was a bit random amongst all the sociological theories and research methods. It's not random! It's… it’s  you . Plus, imagine, a Human Sciences student who can also whip up a decent Sunday roast. That’s a good person to have around. Speaking of food... are you hungry? They do decent burgers here. Actually, yeah. Starving. After that disastrous attempt at making Shepherd's Pie last night, I'm pretty much running on caffeine and despair. Shepherd's Pie gone wrong? Tell me everything. Did you burn the potatoes again? Worse! The lamb was... well, let's just say it resembled something more akin to shoe leather. My mum nearly had a heart attack.

Right, Dad, so you said you wanted to explain this whole… windfall tax situation? Honestly, it all just feels so confusing. I read something in the paper, but it was full of jargon. Well, love, it  is  a bit of a murky business, isn’t it? They always try to make it sound complicated to confuse the average bloke. Let’s see if I can unravel it a bit for you. Now, essentially, the government’s put a tax on the extra profits that energy companies are making. These are… are called ‘windfall profits’. Windfall? Like, lucky wins? Precisely! Though I wouldn't call it lucky for those companies, would I? They're moaning about it, of course. But the idea is, because of the war in Ukraine and all the disruption to gas supplies, energy prices have shot up. These companies, who already make a decent profit, are suddenly making  massive  profits. Higher than they’ve ever seen. So, the government wants a share of that? Seems fair enough, doesn’t it? Everyone's struggling with bills. In principle, aye. It seems reasonable. But where it gets tricky is how it's implemented and the knock-on effects. See, they’re saying it's to help with the cost of living crisis, to cushion those of us struggling to keep warm and put food on the table. The money’s meant to be used to fund benefits and support schemes. Okay, so that makes sense. But I heard they're worried it’ll discourage investment in renewable energy. Is that true? That's what the energy companies are shouting about, innit? They’re saying, ‘Why would we invest in new wind farms or solar panels if the government's just going to nick a chunk of our profits?’ There's some merit to that, I suppose. You don't want to stifle innovation. But then, you’ve got to balance that against ensuring people can afford to heat their homes. It's a balancing act, always is. So, it’s a bit of a gamble then. Hoping they’ll still invest, even with the tax? Aye. And the devil's in the details, as they say. The specific rate of the tax, how long it lasts, all that sorts of things. It's been tweaked a few times already. The latest version, I think, allows for some investment in new energy projects, which is a move in the right direction.

Honestly, Mum, this project is eating my life. It's just… relentless. Deadlines are shifting constantly, and everyone seems to have a different idea of what ‘done’ actually  means . Oh, you young ones and your projects! Sounds a bit like my last Ofsted inspection, actually. Always something unexpected popping up to throw a spanner in the works. What’s it on, then? Something exciting? It’s for a new sustainability initiative for the borough council. Sounds really important in theory, you know? Reducing waste, promoting local businesses, that kind of thing. On paper, it’s brilliant. In practice, it’s a chaotic mess of spreadsheets and stakeholder meetings. Borough council, eh? Bureaucracy central. Remember when your Uncle Barry tried to get a new bench put in the park? Six forms, three meetings, and a year later, it was still just a promise. Did you have a good weekend, at least, away from all that? It was alright. I went to see Chloe and Liam. Liam's finally started walking – it's the cutest thing! He kept trying to crawl towards this rogue sock. You’d have loved it. Oh, I would! Babies are just the best, aren’t they? Growing up so fast. Little whirlwind of chaos, just like you were at that age. Remember that time you painted the cat blue? Oh, Mum! Don't remind me! Dad was  furious . Still, the cat seemed okay, eventually. Chloe’s having a right time with teething though. Constant crying, constant drool… Ah, teething. The bane of all parents’ existence. We went through that with Harry. I swear, I lived on paracetamol and lukewarm tea for six months. Has Chloe decided what she’s doing after uni? She's thinking about going into graphic design. She's got a really good portfolio, actually. Feels a bit daunting though, the whole job hunt thing. The competition’s fierce. It always is, love. But Chloe’s got talent. She’s a bright girl. Just needs a bit of push and encouragement. You're doing a good job of that, I'm sure. How's your flatmate, Sarah? Still raiding your fridge? Don’t even start. She used to just sneak a yoghurt. Now it’s entire takeaway containers. I've resorted to hiding my good biscuits on the top shelf. It’s ridiculous. You’ve got to be firm with them. Otherwise, they’ll walk all over you.

Right, Dad, you’ve been eyeing this up all evening. Fancy a glass? Mark says it’s decent, though he’s rarely wrong about wine, is he? Aye, lass, that’d be grand. Sauvignon Blanc, eh? Fancy, that. Used to be just fruity vine in my day. You’ve got yer knowledge, haven’t you? Corpus Administrator… sounds powerful, that. More powerful than running a lab, I reckon. All them fancy words. It's less about power, John, and more about making sure computers understand language. It's… surprisingly fascinating. And Mark’s palate is quite refined, I’ll admit. He can tell you the terroir of a vineyard just by sniffing a glass. Don’t let him hear you say that, he'll go on for hours. Honestly, he could wax lyrical about grapes for the rest of the evening. Anyway, Mark, you alright? You’ve been quiet. Still going over those job applications? Yeah, a bit. This one in Birmingham is promising – project management for a new sustainable water system. The salary is… let’s just say it would allow me to actually afford a decent flat. Rather than battling for space in shared accommodation. Birmingham, though? That’s a fair trek. Away from home, lad. Away from us. I know, Dad. It’s a big decision. But everything’s in Sunderland, isn’t it? It feels like I'm going to end up feeling stagnant. I need a challenge. And to be honest, with the recruitment market as it is... He’s right, Dad. It’s not like there’s a huge demand for brilliant young consultant engineers here. Besides, we'll come down to visit. Loads. And you can always FaceTime. FaceTime… that’s the modern world for ya. Never thought I'd see the day. Seems like only yesterday I was showin’ you kids how to build a den in the garden. Remember? Used to build 'em right sturdy, we did. Proper weatherproof. None of yer flimsy tarpaulin stuff! Oh, I remember! We spent a week building that one, and it collapsed in the first rainstorm. You were not best pleased. That's a pretty vivid memory, actually. And you were lecturing us on structural integrity, weren't you, John? Aye, I was. Always had an eye for a good design, even back then. It’s in my blood, I reckon. Biomedical science, engineering… all about understanding how things work, see?

Honestly, Lizzie, I’m still recovering. That conference was… a lot. A  lot  more than I anticipated. Oh, don’t tell me! I’m only halfway through planning my presentation, and already the anxiety is building. Which one were you at again? The TESOL one in Bristol? Yeah, Bristol. Thought it’d be a nice little trip, you know? Convenient, close-ish. Turns out, ‘convenient’ doesn't mean ‘relaxing’. It was swarming with people, and the sheer volume of materials they were throwing at you… I swear I’m going to be sifting through handouts for weeks. Ugh, I know that feeling. Remember the IATEFL one in Manchester a few years back? The goodie bags alone were enough to fill a small suitcase! What was the best thing about it, then? Surely there must have been  something  good. There were a few. The workshop on incorporating games for younger learners was actually quite brilliant. I got some really practical ideas for my Friday morning class. And I did meet a lovely woman from Madrid who's doing some really interesting work with refugees. We exchanged contact details. That's good! Networking is always a plus, even if the actual conference feels like an endurance test. Honestly, I'm dreading the presentations. I’ve been wrestling with my topic for weeks now – ‘Leveraging Narrative Storytelling to Enhance EFL Engagement’ – sounds impressive, doesn’t it? It does. A bit… academic, perhaps? Exactly! That’s what I'm worried about. It’s easy to get bogged down in theory, isn’t it? You start thinking about Bloom's Taxonomy and all sorts of jargon, and forget that you need to actually deliver something useful to other teachers. Absolutely. I was nearly tempted to just put up a slide with pictures of cats doing silly things. You know, guaranteed engagement. Don’t tempt me! Though, I suspect my head of department wouldn’t be thrilled with  that  approach. What about the worst bit of the conference? Spill. The plenary speaker. Oh, my goodness. This man... he was talking for an hour about the importance of differentiated instruction – which, okay, fair enough, it's important. But he was using these incredibly complicated charts and graphs, and frankly, he seemed to think we were all PhDs in education. No one was taking notes, everyone looked utterly bewildered. Oh no! The classic "talking  at  you" scenario. I’ve been there.

Right, according to this, we should be approaching Piaseczno soon. You sure this is the best route, Eleanor? It feels…rural. Really rural. Oh, absolutely, darling. It’s much prettier than the motorway. Besides, the motorway service stations are dreadful. Remember that one near Swindon? The coffee tasted like dishwater. You and your opinions on service station coffee. I do. Though, I’m honestly wondering if we’ll even  see  a service station for a while. My legs are starting to feel a bit cramped. I should have done more squats before we left. Squats! At your age, you're obsessed with squats. Honestly, you'd think you were training for the Olympics. I did a bit of gentle stretching earlier, that's all the exertion I'm managing these days. This whole campervan thing is surprisingly tiring. It is! But it’s good tiring, you know? Like, a proper adventure. I'm loving seeing this part of Poland. Tarnow was lovely, but it’s good to be moving. So, what are you reading at the moment? Still tackling that Dickens behemoth?  Bleak House . Yes, still. It's…dense. Honestly, I'm finding it a struggle. I keep drifting off. Perhaps I need something lighter. Perhaps something with a handsome hero. Are you reading anything good? Actually, yeah. I just finished 'Circe' by Madeline Miller. Seriously, Eleanor, you should give it a try. It's mythological, but so beautifully written. And the protagonist is brilliant – strong, independent, finds her own path. It’s completely absorbing. Mythological, eh? Sounds a bit… complicated. I used to love Greek myths, but that was years ago. Everything feels a bit complicated these days, doesn't it? Trying to navigate… well, life. Speaking of complicated, how's that volunteering thing going at the language school back home? Still enjoying it? It's alright. It’s rewarding, seeing the students progress, but the admin is a nightmare. And the pay… well, let's just say it doesn’t exactly cover the cost of all these lovely Polish pastries we’re eating! It’s good practice, though – teaching experience never hurts. Have you been thinking about picking up more TEFL work? I've had a few inquiries, yes. But the thought of committing to a schedule again… it's daunting. It's been a long time since I had a proper routine. I do enjoy it, of course, but the silence, you know?

…and that’s why I think this whole telomere shortening thing is fascinating, isn’t it? It's all about protecting the ends of your chromosomes, delaying the inevitable cellular decay. Though, honestly, the more I read about it, the more complicated it gets. Like, could you actually  reverse  it? That's the big question, isn’t it? It  is  a bit mind-boggling, isn’t it? I mean, the idea of extending life…it feels both amazing and a bit unnerving. Think of the implications! But honestly, when you’re up at 3 AM with a toddler who has decided teething is a competitive sport, immortality doesn’t seem terribly appealing. Fair enough! Priorities shift with the small ones. Still, it’s not about immortality per se. It's about healthy aging. Think, adding decades of  quality  life, not just… existing. Did you see that documentary about the longevity communities in Okinawa? Their diet and lifestyle are incredible. I did catch a bit of it. All that sweet potato and gardening, right? It’s lovely, but moving my entire life to Okinawa isn’t exactly practical with Leo. Though, a long weekend…that’s a different story. You mentioned a weekend away? I did. I was thinking, maybe West Cork? There’s that kayaking place down near Baltimore. Remember we talked about it that time, years ago? Oh goodness, yes! The one with the seals? We were going to do it before…well, before Leo arrived. I’d love that. Baltimore is gorgeous. But kayaking…I’m a bit rusty, to say the least. And the weather can be so unpredictable. Don’t worry about the kayaking; we can take it easy. Plenty of sheltered bays. And we’ll check the forecast. Honestly, a bit of fresh air and sea breeze would do us both good. Something completely different. You and I need a brain recharge. I've been buried in reports about server migrations and legacy systems... it's draining. You sound exhausted! Tell me more about those reports. Legacy systems…that sounds terribly dull. It’s funny, with Leo's delays in speech, I've been devouring information on autism, trying to understand everything better. Suddenly, ancient server architecture seems positively relaxing! I can only imagine. It must be incredibly demanding. The diagnostic process alone…That’s got to be stressful. What have the specialists been saying? They’re saying he's still a bit behind, but making progress.

Right then. So, Anya's got this voucher for that Italian place, Bella Notte, down in town. Fancy giving it a go this weekend? Bella Notte? Really? I've heard they do a mean tiramisu! Is it proper Italian, like, not just posh pizza? It's quite good, Elara. Authentic, actually. I used to go there a lot when I was at university in Manchester. They have a lovely outdoor terrace too, if the weather holds up. Aye, that's the plan. Weather permitting. Though, knowing St Annes, we'll likely be battling a gale! We’d need to book, I reckon. Saturday night? Saturday sounds good. Can we take Nana? She’s been saying she fancies a nice meal out. Of course, Elara. Nana would love that. We just need to check with her if she’s feeling up to it. Good thinking, lass. Now, speaking of spending money, have you seen this coffee maker I ordered? It’s absolute rubbish! Leaks everywhere. Sent it back already. Right pain, that was. Needed a new one for visitors. Oh no, that’s frustrating! Where did you get it from? Maybe you can get a refund. I know a good place in Lytham, “The Bean Scene” - they have amazing coffee and sell proper machines. A bit pricey, but their advice is spot on. Coffee’s alright, but I’d rather have a proper cuppa. Nana’s been going on about needing new sunglasses, too. Says hers are all scratched. We could pop into town later and have a wee look. Aye, we could. Though, with that referendum coming up... I’m right lost with all the arguments, to be honest. All this fuss about Europe… Makes you wonder where we’re headed, doesn't it? It’s certainly unsettling. I feel a bit… disconnected from it all, being Slovakian originally. Knowing both sides, you see the complexities no matter which way you lean. It's a shame people aren't trying to understand each other more. My History teacher was saying it’s like 1930 all over again. A bit scary, to be fair. Don't you go gettin' doom and gloom on me, Elara! We'll be alright. Anyway, back to more pleasant things. Have you had a look at that high chair for the baby yet, Sarah? Little Leo’s growing like a weed. I did! There's a lovely wooden one from John Lewis with all the safety features.

Honestly, love, it's not quite right, is it? Something's missing. Feels a bit…sparse. Sparse? Mum, it looks lovely! You’ve got the lights on, the baubles…you’ve even managed to wrangle those ridiculous reindeer you bought last year. They’re festive! And no, it needs something extra. I was thinking of fairy lights woven through the branches, you know? The ones with the little stars. Remember those from when you were little? Oh, yeah! Those were brilliant. I’m sure the lights would look lovely. Are you waiting for Dad to get back from the shops? He's been gone ages. Did he remember the gingerbread men? Leo’s been asking about them all week. He said he'd try, bless him. Though knowing your dad, he’ll probably come back with fifteen different types of chocolate and forget the gingerbread completely. Still speaks to him, doesn't it? About the neighbours, anyway. Did you see Mrs. Henderson lugging those enormous bags of groceries in yesterday? Poor woman. I did! I offered to help, but she practically snapped at me, said she’s perfectly capable. Honestly, some people... They’re so secretive too. Don’t know much about them, do we? Not a great deal. They keep themselves to themselves. Although, I did overhear her talking to her grandson on the phone last week. Something about needing a 'complicated ancestor tree' sorted. Suddenly sparked my curiosity, I must admit. It led my mind somewhere... have you ever got into genealogy at all? Not really, no. It seems a bit… intense. Though, I’ve been vaguely thinking about my German heritage. Great-Grandma Hilda was from Berlin, wasn’t she? I barely remember her. You were just a tiny thing. But she used to tell the most wonderful stories. About Christmas markets and the Brandenburg Gate. She always wore a little Edelweiss brooch. She used to say it reminded her of home. It's a shame we never learned much about German history and culture from her. I wonder if there’s a good documentary we could watch with Leo? Educate him a little. That's a really lovely idea, Mum! I could probably find something online. I have a project on at work at the moment that's been teaching me a lot about different cultures anyway. It’s about crafting compelling narratives for travel companies – so, you know, making places look  really  appealing.

Right, that’s… that’s a box down. Feels like we’ve moved the contents of Argos in here. Are you alright, Elara? You've been remarkably quiet. Just… taking it all in, I suppose. It’s actually quite nice, isn't it? Smaller than I imagined from the photos, but… cozy. And the light’s lovely. Sussex is a bit different to Gillingham, though. Much greener. Yeah, definitely. Bit of a change from Bedford too, to be honest. Less… brick. Less grey. So, priorities? The internet is top of my list. Can’t teach without the internet, can I? I’ve got the router, just need to sort out a connection. Did you call Virgin? I did! They said they can get someone out tomorrow afternoon. Four to six window. I told them we absolutely needed it for teaching and stuff. They seemed to understand. Is that alright? Brilliant! That’s perfect. Saves me the hassle. Right, food situation. I’m starving. I grabbed a couple of pasties from Greggs on the way, but that’s hardly a sustainable long-term plan. I was thinking we could hit the farmer’s market in Lewes tomorrow. Apparently, they have amazing seasonal stuff. Pears and plums are just coming into season, which is lovely. And proper sausages. I’m craving proper sausages. Lewes, huh? Okay, that sounds good. Less stressful than navigating the supermarket after this carnage. Although… have you figured out the rubbish collection days yet? I checked the council website, and it's a bit cryptic. Vaguely. Green bins on Tuesdays and Fridays, I think? But I need to double-check. And recycling… oh god, recycling. You know how much I hate sorting all that out. Do you remember my flatmate back in uni? He just threw everything in the general waste. Vaguely. Sounds like a nightmare. We'll sort it out, though. No more environmental sabotage from us. Speaking of nightmares, did you hear anything from next door? The nursery? I'm a little apprehensive about that. They popped their heads over earlier, just to say hello. Seemed really friendly, actually. Offered to bring over some biscuits tomorrow. They said they’re used to noise – lots of little ones running around. Biscuits are a good sign. So, not instantly going to wage war on us then? Good. Phew. I was envisioning constant screaming and tiny feet hammering on the floor.

"Liv! Honestly, it’s so good to see you! You look amazing." "Chloe! You too! It feels like ages. Seriously, Peterborough isn’t exactly a hotspot for reunions, is it?" “This place is buzzing, though. Bills is always reliable for a decent lunch, right?” "Definitely. And I was starving. The project I'm coordinating has been absolutely mad this past month. All-nighters, endless meetings… you name it. I needed a proper catch-up and some carb loading." "Tell me about it! My placement at the insurance firm has been… an experience. Lots of spreadsheets. Lots. And the office culture is… well, let's just say beige is a very prominent colour in their aesthetic." "Beige? Oh, dear. That sounds delightful. What exactly are you doing?" "Essentially, I’m assisting with claims processing. It’s not exactly the glamorous world of finance I imagined when I was at uni, but it's giving me a good grounding. What about you? Still loving the project coordination?" "Mostly! It’s challenging, which I like, but it’s a lot of responsibility. Right now, it's a massive redevelopment of a local park. So, lots of stakeholder management, budgets, and trying to keep everyone happy – which, you know, is a special skill." “Remember that disastrous end-of-year student party we organised? Let's never speak of the inflatable unicorn again.” "Oh God, no! That was... a choice! Dad still brings it up, you know. He says it was the most chaotic thing he’s ever witnessed." "My mum would have had a heart attack. She's very much a 'everything must be organised and perfect' kind of woman." "Mine too! They're constantly comparing me to my cousin, Priya. Priya's a doctor. Naturally, I’m supposed to be following in her footsteps. Have your parents been nagging you about 'settling down'?" "Don't even get me started. My grandma's been particularly relentless. ‘You need a nice young man, Chloe!’ Like it’s a shopping list item. What about you? Any pressure to find Mr. Right?" "Oh, the pressure is intense! Diwali’s coming up, and my aunties are already openly planning my matchmaking prospects. Last week, I got shown photos of a software engineer from Birmingham. Apparently, he's 'very respectable'." "Respectable software engineers! Sounds thrilling. Maybe we should just elope to Vegas and become lion tamers." "I'm tempted! Honestly, I just want to travel.

Honestly, this cider’s no’ bad, but it’s not a proper cloudy cider like you get back home. None o’ that proper fruity tang. It’s just… flat. Cambridge isn’t exactly known for its authentic North East beverages, is it? I’m just glad they have something vaguely resembling beer. You’d miss your Newcastle Brown Ale something fierce, wouldn’t you? Don’t even  get  me started. You wouldn’t believe the amount of people here who think bitter’s the only acceptable drink. They’ve never experienced the joys o’ a decent Diet Coke either, seemingly. Anyway, you were saying about your research? It sounds intense. It is. It's looking at the impact of algorithmic bias in hiring practices. Really dry stuff, I know. Much less interesting than your work, actually, managing research. That sounds…dynamic.
