Used to try and explain natural selection to my class, but getting teenagers to grasp the nuances of genetic drift… well, that was a challenge! I can imagine! It's definitely more engaging when you're reading about it in the context of a specific place. Speaking of science, did you see that article about the new potential Alzheimer's treatment? No, dear, I haven’t. Is it promising? I’ve been rather out of touch with the news lately. The internet's become a bit of a labyrinth, I find. So much noise. It’s early days, but yes, apparently there's some evidence it could slow down the progression. They're using a novel approach with… well, I couldn't explain it properly, involved something to do with clearing misfolded proteins.

Right then, so Finn, you were telling us about this… 'Roblox' game? It sounded a bit mad, to be honest. Like, building your own worlds and fighting… what was it, zombies? Nah, not just zombies, Dad! There's all sorts of things. There's obbies – obstacle courses - which are really hard sometimes, and then there's Tycoons where you build businesses and earn money. And Adopt Me! That's the one I've been mostly into lately. Adopt Me? Sounds… gentle. Unlike fighting zombies. Is that the one where you get to look after virtual pets? Yeah, exactly! You hatch eggs, and there’s loads of different animals you can get. Some are really rare, like the Shadow Panther. I’ve been trying to get one for ages! It's about raising them, building them houses, trading with other players... Trading, is it? That’s just like a miniature economy, isn’t it? Sounds complicated for a Thursday evening. It can be, but it’s fun! You have to know the value of everything. I traded a Legendary Unicorn for a Triple-X Dragon the other day. Huge upgrade! A triple-X dragon? You're talking like a little entrepreneur! Your dad's an IT manager, you're already trading in the digital marketplace. It's quite something. She’s got me beat on business acumen, I think. It's rather impressive, to be fair. Though I’m not entirely sure it teaches you how to manage a real budget. Liam’s been building a whole jungle for his dinosaur, you know. He’s got teddy bears, toy cars… all part of the jungle landscape. It reminds me a bit of what you’re describing, Finn, with the building and the… creating. Yeah, I guess it’s kind of similar, just… virtual. See, Liam’s got the basics down already. He's architect and landscape designer, all rolled into one squishy little package. What’s your dinosaur’s name, little man? Roar! Dinky! Dinky! That’s a lovely name. He’s been very focused on his jungle all evening. He even asked me to find him some "green leaves" for the monkeys. So, if you could design your own world in this Roblox, what would it be like? Hmm… Probably a giant theme park. With rollercoasters that go through space, and a haunted house that's actually  scary , not just jumpy.

Right then, who’s got the sat nav sorted for this trek to ANON’s? It’s a bit off the beaten track, innit? I've been looking at the map and it looks like a right maze. Barry, you’ve been saying that for the last half hour! I've got it, dear. It's in my lap. And it  isn't  a maze. It’s a perfectly reasonable route, if you’d just let me get on with it. Used to know a fella… Costessey, he did. Kept horses, ‘e did. Right nice fella. Not the best driver, mind you. Once drove into a ditch trying to avoid a pheasant. Pheasant was fine, car wasn't. Grandad, that’s awful! But pheasants are silly, they just run out in front of cars. Yeah, they do! See, Sarah and Chloe get it. Pheasants are a menace. Anyway, are we even remotely close to ANON's yet? My stomach's starting to rumble something fierce. Christmas dinner is calling, you know. We’re about twenty minutes out, Barry. And stop complaining. You ate half the mince pies already. Mince pies. Reminds me of my mum’s. Always made ‘em, she did. Tiny little things, but packed a punch, they were. Nothing like these shop-bought ones, eh? All air and sugar. Grandma Ken, you're getting nostalgic! Are you thinking about Christmas with your mum? Of course, darling. It's hard not to think of loved ones at Christmas. It's a time for remembering, isn’t it? And it's for enjoying the good food, too! Now, Chloe, are you sketching anything on your tablet? You always have your nose in it. I'm just doing some doodles, Auntie Ken. I’m trying to get the perspective right on a horse's leg… it’s harder than it looks! Horses, you say? My niece, Emily, she's mad about horses. Wants to be a vet. Proper keen. Same! I’m thinking of horse riding lessons next year. Oh, lovely! That would be splendid. Though, remember what your Grandad said about avoiding pheasants! Be careful out there. Aye, be careful. Had a friend down the road, had a Land Rover. Believed he  was  a Land Rover, he did. Always going over bumps. Nearly bounced himself into next week. You're full of stories today, Arthur! That’s brilliant. You should write a book, you know.

Right then, who’s helping clear up after this feast? Honestly, I’m knackered. That was lovely, though, wasn’t it? Absolutely scrumptious, love. Your curries are always a winner. And no, I’m not clearing anything. Consider it a perk of being Head of Department. Delegation is key, you know. Don’t be like that, Dad! I’ll help. There’s loads of plates and… Woah! Leftovers! Can I have some for lunch tomorrow? Of course, darling. Help yourself. She’s right, David. You’re shirking your duties. Remember last year's Christmas dinner clean-up? You nearly needed a crane to get you off the sofa! That's a slight exaggeration, isn’t it, Sarah? I was simply...conserve energy for the Boxing Day sales. A vital task, I’ll have you know. Oh god, Dad, Boxing Day sales? Really? Seriously outdated. You should be thinking about… festival season. Got any plans for that this year? Festival season? At my age? My back protests at the mere mention of standing around for eight hours listening to electronic music. No, I think I’ll stick to a nice, quiet pub and a quiz night. Speaking of which, did you hear about Brenda from accounting finally winning the jackpot at the Tuesday night quiz? No! Seriously? Brenda? She's always been so smug about knowing obscure facts about medieval farming. I always suspected she was cheating. That’s brilliant! Imagine, all that knowledge just for a couple of pints and a plate of chips! Anyhoo, back to festivals. Chloe’s going to End of the Road again. I'm thinking about tagging along. End of the Road? That’s lovely, isn’t it? Quiet, you know. Not like some of those massive ones. Is it expensive though? It’s a bit pricey, yeah, but worth it for the atmosphere. And the food trucks are amazing. I was thinking, might be a nice birthday present for you, Mum? A ticket? Oh, you shouldn’t have! That’s incredibly thoughtful, sweetheart. Though, I’m not sure David would be thrilled with me traipsing off to a music festival. Traipsing? I’d be thrilled! As long as you send me regular pictures, of course. And promise not to come back with any… bohemian piercings. Dad! You’re impossible. Mum, seriously, think about it. It’d be a change of pace. We could all go!

Honestly, the heating bill this month…shocking. Absolutely shocking. I’m starting to think about layering up like it's the Blitz again. Tell me about it, David. Elsie’s been complaining something fierce. Says her knees are aching more than usual, and she puts it down to trying to stay warm. It’s just not right, is it? Especially at our age. Blitz, you say? I remember the Blitz, I do. We were lucky in Costessey, really. Didn’t get hit as badly as some. Though, the rationing… that was a proper bother. Still, at least the weather was a bit more predictable. This mild sort of cold is just…dampening. Predictable? Harold, in my experience, weather is  never  predictable. Running a business in London, you learn to factor in every conceivable contingency. From blizzards to heatwaves, you’ve got to be prepared. Though, I agree, this dampness is rather unpleasant. It's settled right into my bones. Speaking of unpleasant... did you hear about Penelope’s party? Apparently, Derek was flirting something awful with that new gallery owner. Derek and Penelope? Still going strong, are they? I thought he was getting rather enamoured with the florist down the lane. Always bringing her extravagant bouquets. Oh, you don’t mean… Derek? A mistress? Goodness! Penelope will be devastated. They've been together for donkeys' years. Remember when we all went to that summer fete with them, Elsie? Such a happy couple they seemed. I can’t say I’ve noticed anything amiss with Derek. Always seemed a respectable sort. Though, men... you never know, do you? My brother George, always had his eye out for something a bit flashier than what he had. Ended up marrying a woman with a penchant for sequins and a questionable accent. Well, Harold, you know what they say – a rolling stone gathers no moss. Perhaps Derek simply craves a little excitement. Although, no doubt Penelope’s connections will make the gossip travel with lightning speed. You know how she is. It's just so... tiresome. All the drama. I'd rather be watching Big Brother, honestly. At least with that, you  know  you're being exploited for entertainment. This is just… messy. Oh, don't remind me of Big Brother. Elsie's glued to it. Says it's fascinating to see what people will do for fifteen minutes of fame. I just find it rather depressing.

Right, nearly there then! Smells better than it looks, I reckon. How was that documentary you were watchin' earlier, Liv? You were glued to it. Honestly, it was fascinating, Chloe! It was about the making of ‘Paddington 2’ – can you believe how much effort they put into those marmalade scenes? Like, crafting the marmalade itself to look  just right  on camera. It’s ridiculous, but brilliant. Aye, a bit bonkers, isn’t it? But I get it. You lot down south are obsessed with that bear. Still think 'Babe' was the better pig film, mind. Babe was lovely, don’t get me wrong, but Paddington has heart! And the humour is just so… British. Speaking of, how's your Mum doing? Last I heard she was still battling with that leaky roof. Still a right palaver, love. The builder’s keepin' me on hold, says he’s got too many jobs on. It’s drivin' her spare, she keeps muttering about needing a new hat and movin' in with me. Which, I’m not sure I’m ready for, to be honest. Another set of tea cups to wash! I can see that! But she’s your mum, Chloe. You've got to help her out. Maybe having a really firm word with the builder? Right, are you nearly done with the culinary masterpiece? I'm starving. Almost. It’s a chilli, me nan’s recipe. Fair warning, it’s got a kick. You’ll be reachin’ for a glass of water, you will. Reminds me of when I was a kid, I put a whole chilli in my mouth thinkin' it was a sweet. Nan nearly had a heart attack! Oh, please don't tell me that! I’m not a huge fan of spice, actually. So, family stuff… Have you heard from your Auntie Maureen lately? She's been a bit quiet. Nope. She's probably off doin' something wild. Remember that pottery class she signed up for last year? Ended up selling all her mugs online for twenty quid a pop, apparently. She said she was gonna be a professional potter. Honestly, she’s a whirlwind. What about your family? Are you going down to see your nan for Christmas this year? Yeah, definitely. She's been asking about you, actually. She wants to know if you're free to come down too. It would be lovely if you could.

Cor, this rain's relentless, innit? Sat in here all day marking GCSE papers, and now this. Makes you want to wrap up in a blanket and just…forget about the world. Aye, it’s proper miserable out. Speaking of forgetting about the world…did you see what’s happening with Scotland again? The referendum’s back on the table. Aye, I did. Been reading up on it. It's a right confusing business, when you get down to it. Reminds me a bit of Brexit, that does - all the passionate opinions and the difficult choices. My history teacher says it’s massively complicated. Something about trying again after the last one failed to pass. He reckons the demographics have shifted. They have, lad. Younger voters, especially, seem to be more inclined towards independence. Makes sense, doesn’t it? They’ll be living with the consequences long after we’re gone. I remember the last one, 2014. My sister, bless her, spent weeks arguing about it with her husband. She was staunchly pro-union, wanted us to stay together. What did she say? Why was she against it? Oh, all the usual things, really. The economy, wasn't she? Worried about the pound, about trade, about what Scotland would do without England’s support. She’d been through a tricky patch financially, so having certainty was important to her. She was terrified of the unknown, I suppose. She told me, “Sheila, look at the price of petrol! Can you imagine what it’ll be if we start having a border?” Simple logic, you see. Right. So, what do  you  think? Are you pro or against? Now, that’s a tricky one, isn’t it? I can see both sides, I really can. Part of me, the Yorkshire part, thinks, “Mind your own business! Let them get on with it!” We've got enough dramas of our own to deal with, haven’t we? But then there’s a bigger picture, isn’t there? The UK, whatever its flaws, has been a force for good in the world. Splitting it up…it’s a big thing. My teacher was saying that if they do become independent, joining the EU again would be their top priority. Aye, that’s the talk, innit? Then you’ve got the border with England again, which is a nightmare. And what would happen to the nuclear submarines docked at Faslane?

Honestly, this lot are something else, aren’t they? Look at ‘er, proper kicking off about a DNA test. Like anyone doesn’t see it coming. Aye, they do, don't they? More drama than Corrie, that's for sure. Though, I reckon they  like  the drama. A bit of attention, innit? Aye, but the shouting! Can’t understand a word half the time. It's like everyone’s just… blurting. Listen to that woman’s elision! ‘Cause she’s… like… gone? She's 'gone'. Elision, that is? Is that what you’re calling it, Liv? I thought it was just… people talking fast. My nan does it all the time. 'Cause I'm… 'cause I’m… goin'. You’re tellin' me! My grandma's the worst for it. "Goin' to t'shops." "Seen 'im yesterday." It's a full code! But she says it so naturally. Makes you wonder if most folks do it and we just don't notice. I reckon we do. It's just more noticeable when people are properly riled up like on this show. It's that panicky energy, yeah? Makes the sound all… melted together. It's a proper clever trick, elision. All that sound disappearing. Like magic. I used to try and do it when I was little, but I just ended up sounding like I was mumbling. Right! Like you're hidin’ somethin'! You and your mumbling! But seriously, listen to the bloke now. He’s forgetting his T's already. “Just… put it… on… t’table.” That's a classic. It’s funny 'cause it's so… intrinsic, isn't it? Like we don’t even think about doing it. It just…  happens . Do you think they teach it in speech therapy? Doubt it. More likely they'd be tellin' folks  not  to do it. Proper posh, wouldn't they? "Please articulate clearly." Imagine trying to get Ricky Gervais to stop dropping his T’s! He’d argue for ages. “It’s part of my charm!” he'd say. Oh, he definitely would. He’d probably start a whole debate about regional dialects and the beauty of elision. All while deliberately dropping his T's, just to be ironic. Right, look at this! He’s saying... "I ain't gonna…" It's like a masterclass in Northern English conversation. It is, isn't it? Although, I still can't quite get my head around why anyone would voluntarily put themselves through this.

Oh, for goodness sake! He’s clearin’ it! Come on, lad, play it! Play it! Relax, Liv. It's only the second half. Plenty of time. You’d think this was the Champions League final with the way you're carryin' on. Aye, well, it  is  a pretty important game for us, innit? And don't you start with the "relax" business. You know how I get when I’m watchin’ the lads. It’s a serious business! Serious business involving a lot of shouting and frantic knitting. What  are  you making, by the way? Another scarf? Nah, it's for the little one. Blanket. Thought I’d get a head start. This is the design I’m thinkin' of. What d'ya reckon? A bit much, maybe? Blue and white? Very Sunderland. A little on the bold side, perhaps, but definitely... distinctive. Though, if it's a girl, might clash a bit. Have you got any other names in mind besides… Ethan, last time I checked? Ethan’s a good name! A classic. And we're still eh, discussin' things. Plenty o' time for names. We’ve got Willow, that’s a favourite of mine. Sounds nice, doesn’t it? Bit woodsy. Willow is lovely. My mum's always loved Willow. Remember the Olympics last summer? We were glued to the telly for hours. Australian swimmers were incredible. Aye, they were. Katie got all emotional when she was commentating on Adam Peaty's race. Proper blubberin' she was, poor lass. Reminded me o’ me Granny when England lost on penalties. You’re a chip off the old block then. So, any thoughts on something... less sporty for the baby’s name? Something a bit more… gentle? OH, GET IN! No! Reckless tackle! Seriously?! Right, gentle... Hmm. Hazel, maybe? Feels a bit… posh, don’t it? Not sure if it fits a wee bairn from Sunderland. Posh is good. It gives them options later in life. They don’t  have  to be posh, but… they'll have the choice. Your mam always said you were a bit too gritty for your own good. Me mam also said you talked like a robot sometimes. Shut yer gob, alright? Penalty saved! YES! Good save! Proper heroics there! See? You just needed a bit of excitement to calm you down. You know, knittin’ can be quite therapeutic, actually. I should try it sometime. You? Knittin'?

Right, so, Barry the Bee is still ranting about honey, is he? Honestly, that movie is so absurd, but the kids are utterly captivated. Barry is  really  clever! He's a lawyer! And he says humans steal all the honey! He fights for the bees! Like King Arthur! He has knights! Well, he does have a… rather unconventional court system. King Arthur, eh? You’ve been watching a lot of that too, have you? Is it the sparkly swords you like best? No! It's Excalibur! And the round table! Can we have a round table for dinner? Yes! And a crown! A really sparkly one, Mummy! Like the Queen! We're not having a round table, darling. And sparkly crowns are not strictly appropriate for Wednesday night pasta. Though, I admit, it would be rather fun. You know, sometimes I wonder… all this royalty stuff. Do you ever think about it? About being a princess? Yes! I would have jewels and a big palace! And I'd wave to everyone! I’d be a politician! I'd make everyone eat fruit! Especially royal fruit! Like… like plums and apples! Royal fruit? Where did you get  that  from? It’s important! Politicians should make sure everyone gets royal fruit! It’s healthy! Granny always said plums were good for you. Granny’s house had a plum tree! A  really  big one! She did. Granny’s garden was magical, wasn’t it? I always felt so… peaceful there. It's such a shame the house is just sitting empty now. Too much work to bring it back to life. It makes you think, doesn't it? Paying fortunes to go  into  palaces, funded by taxpayers… I wonder if it’s worth it sometimes. I mean, wouldn't it be better if we were a republic? But then who would wave at us? Good point. Someone else would wave, sweetie. Actually, you know what I'm looking forward to this weekend? The diving at the Olympic Stadium. It's going to be incredible. Will we be quiet? Like when you took us to the theatre? Precisely. Swimming requires intense focus. And silence from the audience is helpful. Speaking of focus, have you both taken your vitamins today? Vitamins are yucky! They don’t taste  that  bad. And they help you grow big and strong. Like Arthur's knights! Now, honestly, restaurants… I’m still dreading taking you two out to a nice restaurant.

Right, that’s the last of the garden gnomes. Honestly, I don't know how Mum accumulated so many! It’s like a gnome convention exploded in the back garden. They were a bit of a passion, weren't they? Each one had a name, you know. There was Bartholomew, and Penelope... and Reginald, the grumpy one. All sorts. Reginald the grumpy gnome! Only your mum, Evelyn. I’m still amazed we got that lot into the van. My back’s killing me. Honestly, clearing out an entire house… it's an archaeological dig, isn’t it? We’ve unearthed things I didn’t even  know  existed. Remember that box of feathered hats? Feathered hats? Like, really,  really  fancy ones? Were they like, ancient or something? Ancient enough to make you look like a flapper, Ethan. Mum had a thing for vintage theatre costumes, too. Bit of a magpie, your grandma was. I just liked a bit of colour, love. Life’s too dreary otherwise. Though, I did feel a bit silly wearing a boa to the shops. You always did, love. Speaking of dreary, that article I read today… about the state of the NHS. Honestly, it’s terrifying. My niece is waiting for an appointment for her shoulder. Six months! And she’s a nurse herself! It  is  awful, isn’t it? Keeps getting worse. The waiting lists, the staff shortages… I tried to book a check-up last month, and the first available appointment was November. November! My dad says it’s all because of the government, innit? He’s always going on about it. It's been going downhill for years, sadly. Not like when I was younger. You could get seen quickly… it was a lifeline then, the NHS. It  should  be a lifeline. Absolutely. I’m thinking about looking into those private healthcare options. It's a terrible thing to even consider, spending that kind of money, but… you just want to have some peace of mind. It's a slippery slope, isn't it? Creates a two-tier system. I was thinking about that auction down in Thirsk next month. They’ve got some lovely antique furniture. Might be worth a look. Could furnish the spare room. Thirsk! I haven’t been to Thirsk in… oh, decades! Remember that little tea room with the lavender cake? Delicious it was. Oh, I do! We went there after the horse racing one year.

Oy, that was a nightmare. Absolute nightmare trying to park down by the Walker. Seriously, is there a single space within a ten-mile radius? You're back! How was the exhibition? Was it worth the parking ordeal? The exhibition itself? Yeah, brilliant, honestly. That pre-Raphaelite collection at the Walker is always top-notch. But the parking… right, I ended up circling for almost forty minutes. Nearly had a right paddy, I did. Honestly, I was starting to think I'd have to hitchhike. Forty minutes? You're dramatic, Liam. I would have just taken a bus. Bus? Nah, wouldn't be me. Needed the car, I was lugging a massive bag from Primark. Got a right bargain on socks, you wouldn’t believe. Needed 'em. All me students got fungal infections just by breathing near 'em. Charming. Speaking of work… how's the assessment week going? Are you drowning in essays? Drowning is an understatement, love. It’s a tidal wave of grammar and vocab. Little Tommy keeps writing “their” when he means “there.” Drives me mental! Trying to explain it is like teaching a brick to tap dance. Sounds stressful. At least you enjoy teaching, though, right? I’m still battling the paperwork mountain here. That neuropsychology report is going to be the death of me. You’re doing amazing though, Rach. Proper clever stuff that you do. And speaking of clever… did you hear back about that Masters interview? The one at Manchester? Actually, yes! I got it! Interview’s next week. I'm terrified, but excited. Dead brilliant, Rach! Seriously, that’s fantastic news! Massive well done. You deserve it. So, Masters in Clinical Psychology… that’s a big step, eh? It is. It means loads of extra study, and probably more borrowing money… oh god, money. That’s another thing. Have you looked at those Christmas catalogues yet? Don't even! My mum’s already sent me a list of nephews and nieces with a list of demands longer than my arm. Looks like I'll be living on beans on toast again in January. Tell me about it! My family are the same. All wanting the latest gadgets. Maybe we should just agree on experiences this year? A nice meal out, or tickets to something? That’s not a bad shout. Less stuff to store, anyway. What about getting a pet? I saw this adorable little rescue dog online…

Honestly, Chloe, I'm  so  tired. Like, properly knackered. This week’s been mental. Three essays due and Professor Davies decided to schedule a surprise quiz on Chaucer. Chaucer! Who even  likes  Chaucer? Tell me about it! My coding assignment is trying to kill me. It’s like it actively resists being finished. And speaking of tired...did you see Harry Styles's new interview? He looks exhausted, poor love. No! Don’t spoil it! But yes, university is a vampire, sucking the life out of us. Harry Styles, though...so dreamy. Did you see the photos of him at that football match last weekend? His jacket was  everything . Oh, yeah! Man United, right? I saw them. Proper cute. Although, I’m more of a Chelsea girl myself. You know, like my dad. He’d kill me if he knew I was even mentioning Man United. He’s proper intense about footie. Your dad's always intense about something, innit? Remember when he nearly had a heart attack because we didn’t put enough cheese on the pizza last Christmas? Don’t remind me! He went on and on. Honestly, he’s got a funny side though, deep down. Anyway, back to Harry - I was just scrolling through Insta and saw that Millie Bobby Brown’s got a new tattoo. Little fairy wings. How cute is that? Oh, show me! Aww, it is. I’ve been thinking about getting something done myself. Maybe a little constellation on my wrist. Something subtle. What do you think? I reckon you'd rock it. You always were drawn to sparkly things. I’m thinking about a tiny hummingbird. Representing freedom, you know? I've been watching loads of wildlife documentaries. It's so relaxing. After dealing with code all day, a bit of Planet Earth is pure bliss. True! I've been needing relaxation. Actually, I was thinking, could we grab a coffee at that new cafe, "The Daily Grind," after lectures on Friday? They apparently do incredible salted caramel lattes. Ooh, yeah! That sounds brilliant. I've heard good things. Plus, I need to show you that TikTok I found. It's about cartoon dogs learning philosophy. It’s ridiculous, but seriously hilarious. Cartoon dogs doing philosophy? You're speaking my language! I’ve been binge-watching "The Owl House" again. It’s just…comfort food. Pure Disney magic. You know, the kind of stuff we used to watch at your grandmom's house when we were little?

Right then, Oisin, did you manage to catch any good Pokémon on your Skyper session with Liam tonight? He was telling me about this new evolution he’d found. Yeah, loads! He showed me a Galarian Yamask that evolved into a really creepy, but cool, Spiritomb. It took ages though, had to use like, five different berries to get it to hold still. "Poo-kay-mon!" He wants to play too, doesn’t he? Bless him. Liam’s a lucky boy, having you to teach him, isn’t he? He was saying he's struggling a bit with those Shadow Pokémon battles. It’s tricky. You gotta weaken them a lot first, then use a Purifying Crystal. He keeps using the wrong moves. I tried to explain it, but he gets distracted easily. He kept showing me pictures of his cat. Boys, eh? Always a distraction. Still, it’s lovely you’re helping him. Do you think you could pop over next weekend and play with him properly? We could have a little Pokémon tournament? Yeah, sure. As long as Mum's okay with it. We have that thing booked on the Saturday, don’t we? The guitar lesson. Oh, right, the guitar. You practicing much? Still struggling with that barre chord? A bit. It’s annoying. My fingers keep slipping. Mr. Davies said I need to build up calluses. Like I'm a construction worker! Well, you are building something, aren’t you? A musical career! Though maybe not quite requiring construction worker hands. Speaking of building… have you seen my slippers? I can't find them anywhere. They were by the sofa earlier. Right. You and your eyes everywhere. Liam's mum mentioned they're having some ramen next week. Would you and I like to join them? I think it’d be nice to get out. Ramen sounds good. As long as they've got that spicy miso one. I hate the plain one. "Ice cream!" Always thinking of ice cream, aren't you, love? Maybe we can have some after dinner. Although, you’ve already had a few spoonfuls tonight. Actually, I saw this ad online for some new skinny jeans. They’re, like, really dark wash. I was wondering if I could get a pair. Skinny jeans, are they? Really? I thought you were moving away from them. Don’t they clash with your… style, a bit?

Honestly, this cupboard is a black hole, isn't it? I keep meaning to tackle it, and then... well, life gets in the way. It's mostly just accumulated odds and ends. Though, look, I think I found something! Oh, goodness, what is it? Don't tell me it's another box of old Christmas decorations. I swear, we’ve got enough tinsel to decorate Buckingham Palace. No, no, better than that! I think... I think it’s the gardening set! Remember? The little plastic trowel and watering can? And the tiny terracotta pots. The gardening set! Oh, my word, yes! I'd almost forgotten about that. It was terribly bright orange, wasn't it? Ghastly orange plastic. But we loved it. We spent hours pretending to be enormous gardeners in Mum’s tiny patch of garden. Remember how we'd plant those little pebbles and declare them 'prize-winning roses'? I do! And we'd get so cross if Dad accidentally stepped on one of our ‘roses.’ He’d pretend to be devastated! He always played along so well. It was all terribly serious to us, of course. We were experts! He was a good sport, wasn't he? Always willing to indulge our little games. It feels like another lifetime, doesn't it? It was such a lovely summer, I remember. The roses  did  look rather nice, even if they were just stones. It always seems to be the summers that stick with you, doesn't it? So much sunshine, so much space to run around. And then… …and then you end up with boxes full of faded memories. What else is in here? Oh, good heavens, is this...? Let me guess... the Bako set? With the little wooden blocks? It is! The Bako! I can barely remember what it was even called. We called it... 'the building thing', didn’t we? It was all terribly abstract. Not like Lego. No, not like Lego. It was lovely, though. We’d build these enormous, wobbly structures, and then delight in knocking them down. We'd spend ages arranging them, trying to make some sort of sense out of it all. Remember the little wooden man that always went on top? He was missing his arm for years. Absolutely! We called him Captain Stubborn, because he never seemed to fall off, even without an arm. Finding this stuff is rather tiring, though.

Honestly, they’re relentless this year. I’ve already got three bites, and we’ve only been out for fifteen minutes. Three? You’re a trooper. I've only managed one, tucked away on my ankle. I’m using that ridiculous citronella spray now, though, so hopefully it'll deter the little blighters. Did you remember to put some on Elsie? Yes, loads. Smells like a walking citronella candle, poor thing. I feel like I’m giving her a scent allergy, but the thought of her getting bitten to bits is worse. It's just... unusual, isn’t it? We haven't had this many mosquitoes in Norwich for ages. Blame the mild winter, I reckon. Everything thrives. So, did you manage to get tickets for that Fontaines D.C. gig? The one at the Waterfront? No. Absolutely gutted. Sold out within five minutes. I stayed up until midnight trying to refresh the page, but it was hopeless. Everyone and their dog wanted to see them. You’d think they were the Beatles. Typical. I was hoping to go with you. I'm properly disappointed, actually. They're brilliant live, aren't they? The energy…it's infectious. We’ll have to keep an eye out for their tour next year, or maybe try and snag some resale tickets, though that's usually a gamble. I know. It's a last resort. I'm feeling a bit sorry for myself, to be honest. It’s hard enough getting out these days with Elsie – a gig seems like a distant memory. I know, love. It is. But we'll get there. We’ll find something. Maybe something smaller, more local? There's that new indie band playing at the Owl & Feather next month… Okay, that’s a slightly more manageable idea. Less jostling, less risk of losing the baby in a sea of people. Plus, the Owl & Feather does a decent pint. Exactly! See? There's always a silver lining. Although, speaking of jostling… the traffic getting here was horrendous. I swear, everyone decided to have a spontaneous road trip this afternoon. Tell me about it. I nearly swerved into a parked car trying to avoid that delivery van. It felt like rush hour at three o'clock. I’m trying to avoid the ring road home, think I’ll go the slightly longer route through Old Catton. Wise move. The A47 was a parking lot.

Blimey, that was a day. Honestly, Mrs. Higgins was having a right go at my putting today. Said it looked like I was trying to whack a dandelion head, not a golf ball! Oh, really? Mrs. Higgins? She always did have an opinion, didn’t she? At least you got some practice in. How was the rest of the course? Course was alright, bit soggy after all that rain last week. But the wind… the wind was playing havoc. Nearly blew my hat clean off the green at the seventh. Nearly cost me a birdie, that. You wouldn’t believe it. What about you? Still hammering away at those application forms? Ugh, tell me about it. Applied for another one just now. Marketing assistant. Sounds promising, but the requirements… they’re asking for experience I don’t realistically have. It’s so frustrating! I feel like I’m stuck in a loop. I know the feeling. Remember when I was trying to get sponsored? So many rejections, felt like giving up. But you’ve got this, love. You’re sharp, you’re clever… you just need to find the right fit. Maybe you should call your mum, see if she's heard anything about that recruitment agency she mentioned? Yeah, I probably should. I keep putting it off, though. She means well, but her advice tends to be… well, let’s just say it's enthusiastic. Reminds me of Mrs. Higgins, actually. Speaking of enthusiastic, did you hear about the Halloween party at the community centre? Halloween? Already? Feels like summer just ended. What’s the theme this year? Something ridiculous, I bet. Apparently, it’s a “Haunted Manchester” theme. They're going all out with the spooky decor. They’re even promising a ‘ghostly apparition’ or two. I’m tempted to go. It might be good to get out and about. Haunted Manchester, eh? Sounds a bit… much. I'm happy to stay in, put on a film. Speaking of which, did you catch that new series on Netflix? The one about the archaeologists? “Digging Deep”? Yeah! I binged it last night. It was surprisingly good, wasn't it? Really got me hooked. Though, all that dust and dirt… it made me realise how much I appreciate a clean toilet! I swear, I deep cleaned the bathroom this morning. You and your cleaning! You're obsessed, you are. I came in from the course, covered in mud, and you practically shrieked.

Honestly, Daniel, this cloud storage thing is giving me a headache. I’ve been wrestling with it all morning trying to upload these photos of Leo. He’s covered in mashed potato, you know, the usual. And it’s just… dragging. Ah, cloud storage, isn't it a grand thing until it decides not to cooperate? What platform are you using, love? Google Drive? Dropbox. Liam said it was the safest. Safer than Google, apparently. But right now, it feels less safe and more like a black hole sucking my afternoon away. Is that why you were shouting earlier? I was trying to game, you know? Lagging was awful. Sorry, darling. Didn’t mean to interrupt. Just a bit frustrated. Daniel, can you take a look? You’re the IT guru. Sure thing, Sarah. Let's have a look. Always happy to troubleshoot. Though, fair warning, sometimes it's just the internet being temperamental, and there’s not much I can do about that. Leo, stop that! He's singing again. He does that a lot, doesn't he? It's kind of cute, actually. It is. It’s exhausting, but it is. Anyway, back to the digital woes… I want to make sure all these photos are backed up before… well, before Leo does something even more potato-related. Right. Let me see. You’re uploading a LOT of images, Sarah. High resolution, are they? Of course! I want to print some. Liam says he wants a proper photo album. He's getting sentimental in his old age. Liam wants a photo album? That's surprising. He usually just puts stuff on Instagram. It’s throttling your upload speed if the resolution is that high. You could try reducing it – just a bit – and see if that helps. Or, you could schedule it to upload overnight. That usually works better. Schedule it overnight? That’s brilliant! Why didn’t I think of that? You're a lifesaver, Daniel. Just a bit of IT wizardry. Anything else I can do? Are we watching a film later? I was thinking maybe something action-packed. Possibly. Leo will probably be asleep by then. What did you have in mind? Something with explosions. And cars. Lots of cars. How about  Mad Max: Fury Road ? Daniel suggested it last time, but we didn't get around to it. Hmm, that does sound good. But maybe something a little less intense for Leo's sake if he's awake.

Honestly, David, you won’t believe what I overheard this morning. Apparently, Anon woke up, realised it was far too hot, and decided to wander downstairs in just his… well, his trousers. No top. You’re having a laugh, aren't you? Anon? In his pants? The boy’s usually a picture of meticulousness, especially about matching his socks. I swear! Little Maisie nearly choked on her cereal she was laughing so much. Apparently, he was heading for the fridge for a glass of water. Imagine the neighbours seeing that! Oh, God. I’m definitely going to tease him about this later. He’ll be mortified. Maisie's a little observant, isn’t she? He looked silly, Mummy! He did a little, didn't he, sweetheart? A silly little bear. Silly bear! Right, whose army of miniature fashion critics are we fostering here? Okay, okay, enough about Anon's sartorial choices. Let’s get back to something slightly more sensible. This extension - I've been having another think about the plans. Oh, really? More thinkering? Lay it on me. I was just thinking about how much more space the kids would have. Maisie keeps complaining there’s nowhere to build her Lego kingdom. I know, I know. I was looking at moving the kitchen out into the garden area, somewhere that gets the morning sun. It would open up the living room considerably, and we could have bi-fold doors straight out onto the patio. Think of it - barbecues, evening drinks… Oh, that  is  lovely. A proper outdoor kitchen area too? With a pizza oven? Well, let’s not get carried away just yet. But the potential is there. We'd need planning permission, obviously. And it’s a significant investment. It would be, but this house  is  our forever home, isn’t it? We need to start thinking about adding a little more practicality, especially now we have two little ones. The loft conversion is still a possibility, but I’m leaning towards your idea now. It feels…bigger. More space for everyone to breathe. Can I have a garden in the new room? Of course, darling. You could have the biggest garden ever! A fairy garden. Plants! Pretty plants! See? We’re already earning our keep! It would need to be secure, obviously. No escape routes for the little adventurers. And honestly, imagining a pizza oven… that’s tempting.

Honestly, David, this instant stuff is barely palatable this morning. Did anyone remember to order proper beans from that Italian roastery? I was hoping for something to kickstart the day. You and your artisan coffee, Alistair! It's a Monday, for goodness’ sake. A bit of Nescafe won’t kill you. Though, I agree, it’s not a patch on that stuff we got last month. Reminded me of that little place in Florence, you know? The one tucked away behind the Ponte Vecchio... Ah, yes! "Il Vecchio Chicco"! Wonderful place. I bought a whole bag of their blend, tried to recreate it at home, naturally. Utter disaster. My wife threatened to leave me over a burnt saucepan. Sounds familiar! My daughter tried to modernise our living room. 'Rustic farmhouse chic,' she called it. Involving a lot of distressed wood and… well, I won’t bore you with the details, but let's just say my wife has a very definite opinion on what constitutes stylish décor. Thankfully, she prevailed. Back to the builder we went. Distressed wood. A curse upon it! I’ve been attempting a bit of refurbishment myself, actually. Replacing the skirting boards in the study. Apparently, I'm not as adept at measuring and cutting as I thought. Oh, the joys of DIY! Remember that grant proposal deadline looming? It would be a lot easier without the ongoing battle with my rebellious skirting boards. Speaking of which, any news on that funding for the Hadron Collider comparative analysis? Sadly, no. The committee sent back a rather terse email. Apparently, ‘the link between particle physics and ancient Sumerian mythology is… tenuous.’ Tenuous! As if mythology isn't a perfectly valid lens through which to examine fundamental human questions about the universe. Bureaucracy at its finest. They'll probably fund a project on the optimal placement of decorative gnomes in suburban gardens instead. Absolute nonsense. It’s the same with everything. Even something as simple as finding a reliable water company. We've had leaks constantly. Feels like they're deliberately trying to drive us mad. You’re preaching to the choir! Thames Water’s customer service is an exercise in frustration. I've spent hours on the phone, being transferred from person to person, only to be told they'll 'look into it'. It's astonishing how inefficient these big corporations can be. You know, the scale of the Hadron Collider still blows my mind, though.

Right then, Operation Lego Sort is officially underway. Honestly, it looks like a rainbow exploded in here. Poppy, Leo, can you two please start by separating all the red bricks? Red! Red! I like red! Can I build a fire engine, Mummy? A really, really big one! Yellow's good too! Can I build a dinosaur? A super-big, stompy dinosaur! Absolutely! Fire engines and dinosaurs, marvelous. Just… keep the red and yellow separate for now, okay? We need a system. Otherwise, it will all just get muddled again. Remember what Granny says about organisation? Granny says tidy houses are happy houses! And Granny's house needs lots of tidying, doesn’t it? It does, doesn’t it? We’re going to be doing a bit of sorting and clearing out at Granny's next week, actually. You two will have to be extra helpful, okay? Maybe we can find some more Lego there too! Ooh, can we watch Harry Potter at Granny's? Please, Mummy, please? We might do, darling. If we're good helpers. But first, Lego. Now, Leo, you’re doing yellow, Poppy you’re doing red. What about blue? I’ll tackle blue. Then we’ll have to think about wheels, and special pieces… It's rather overwhelming, isn’t it? I’m half tempted to just build a giant Simpsons character. Like Bart? Bart’s funny! He says “Eat my shorts!” He does, doesn’t he? He's a classic. Though, perhaps we shouldn’t be encouraging that sort of language… What about Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles? Do you like them? Raphael is the best! He’s got the coolest sai! I liked Michelangelo! He’s funny! They are great. You know, we could go to the cinema next weekend! They’re showing that new animated adventure... Do you want to check what’s on and see if it’s suitable? Cinema?! Yay! Can we get popcorn? And chocolate?! Absolutely. Popcorn and chocolate. Although… speaking of chocolate… Perhaps we should leave the Easter chocolate for a  little  later. Too much sugar and you’ll be bouncing off the walls, and then sorting the Lego will be impossible! But it's yummy! It is yummy. But remember Granny’s saying about everything in moderation? Just like everything in this Lego pile! Now, let's focus. Red bricks, Poppy. Yellow bricks, Leo. Mummy will do the blues. We're a team, right?

Right, I'm back! Honestly, arriving home always feels… anticlimactic after a holiday, doesn’t it? Like, the real adventure is just unpacking. Liv! You're back! You look… sun-kissed! And postcards, how lovely. Let me get you a drink. Tea? Coffee? Something stronger? Stronger, definitely stronger. Gin and tonic, if you're feeling generous? My brain feels like scrambled eggs after navigating the Spanish train system. Seriously, that was an experience. Scrambled eggs sounds about right. How was Spain, properly? I’ve been picturing you lounging on a beach, utterly relaxed. Lounging was minimal! Barcelona was incredible, obviously – Gaudi is even more mind-blowing in person. But then I tried to get to Valencia and...chaos. Delayed trains, missed connections, a brief, terrifying encounter with a pickpocket. Oh my god, a pickpocket?! Were you alright? Yeah, thankfully didn’t lose anything major. Just my dignity, mostly. It was a bit of a stressful end to the trip, though. Still, the paella in Valencia was worth the trauma. Seriously, the best I’ve ever tasted. You  have  to try it sometime. I’m making a massive roast tonight, actually. Sunday tradition. Did you miss the football at all? Arsenal are playing Man U on Sunday, you know. Don't even. I actively avoided thinking about football while I was away. Needed a complete detox. Though, I did see a couple of guys wearing Arsenal shirts in Barcelona. Felt a bit homesick then. How’s work been? Anything dramatic? You know, same old, same old. A couple of new admissions, the usual staffing shortages… It’s busy, but good busy, you know? I’m finally getting some proper training on the DBT skills – Dialectical Behaviour Therapy. It’s fascinating actually, really giving me some tools to help people. That’s brilliant! Sounds really useful. I wish I was doing something that felt… impactful, like that. Coordinating spreadsheets doesn’t exactly change the world. Don't be silly! You're basically holding the whole project together. Without you, things would fall apart. And besides, you’re incredibly good at it. Speaking of changes, did you hear from Ben? I saw he posted something on Instagram. Ben. Don’t even go there. He’s apparently ‘moving on with someone else’. The caption was full of inspirational quotes about new beginnings. The cheek of it. Oh, Liv. Seriously? After everything? I’m so sorry.

Right then, let’s have a proper look at this, shall we? Gareth, put your feet up, love. Grandma and Grandpa are just settling in. Honestly, these gas bills are something else, aren't they? Proper daylight robbery, I say. Yeah, they’re mental. Is there anything on telly worth watching tonight? Think they got that new detective series on? Detective series? Bah! All that fancy forensic stuff. Give me a good old Poirot any day. Solving things with his brain, not a load of gadgets. Used to love Poirot, me and Arthur. Poirot was alright. Bit slow, though. Needed a bit more action, he did. Remember that time we tried to build a bird table, Elsie? Now  that  was action. Oh, Grandpa! You nearly hammered your thumb off, didn't you? Gareth, love, could you pop out to the shops and get some biscuits? Grandma loves a digestive with her tea. And some of those shortbread ones, if they've got 'em. Fine, fine. Anything else? I’m heading out, you know. Need to grab some new headphones too, mine are practically broken. Just a pint of milk, love. And check if they’ve got any bramble jam. Grandma's been asking for it. It reminds her of her mum’s preserves. Bramble jam! Now you're talking! My mum made the best bramble jam in Hull. Used to take first prize at the fair, she did! Used to use proper brambles, picked from the hedgerows herself. Not like this shop-bought stuff you get now. Aye, Elsie’s mum was a right clever woman. Could make something out of nothing, she could. Remember that winter we had no coal? She made soup out of practically anything. Turnips, carrots, the lot. Tasted… interesting. It did, Grandpa. But we were grateful for it! Gareth, are you off then? Tell them to put a few extra biscuits in the bag, will you? I reckon we'll have hungry folks later. Yeah, I’m off. Grandma, Grandpa, nice to see you both. Don't cause too much trouble for Mum, alright? Trouble? We’re model citizens! Just wishing we had a proper cup of tea like Elsie used to make. This stuff is a bit… weak. Aye, Elsie  did  make a good cup of tea. Strong as anything. And always a biscuit on the side. Honestly, you two! Always complaining! I’ll make you both a proper brew then, strong enough to stand a spoon in it.

Right then, you two. Are we still firmly in Neverland? Because you’ve basically transformed the kitchen into Skull Rock. We  are  Neverland! I’m Tinkerbell, and this is… this is Captain Hook’s crocodile! No, he’s Tick-Tock! And I'm Peter Pan! I’m going to fight Captain Hook!  Swish, swish!  Very impressive. So, you've been watching the Disney  Peter Pan  films again, have you? I saw you snuggling up with the animated one yesterday. Do you like the live-action one better too, with the fairies? The one with the really,  really  shiny fairies! They’re so pretty. And Tinkerbell's dress sparkles! I like the flying! When Peter Pan flies, he's fast! Faster than my bike! He is, isn't he? It’s a bit of magic, that is. You know, when I was your age, my mum used to tell me stories about Great Ormond Street Hospital. They do amazing things, don't they? They help children who are really poorly. Like…like Wendy's little brother? Yes, a bit like that. They help children get better, so they can have adventures, just like Peter and Wendy. They need lots of money to do that, which is why lots of people donate. Donate? Like, give money? Why? Yes, exactly. To buy medicine, and toys, and to pay the doctors and nurses who look after the children. Sometimes, people do things to raise money, like running marathons or selling cakes. Could we do something? To help the children at Great Ormond Street? We absolutely could. We could bake some cookies, or perhaps have a little treasure hunt and donate the 'treasure' we find! What do you think? A treasure hunt! Yes! And the treasure can be… gold chocolate coins! And we can draw pictures to give to the children! Happy pictures, so they feel better. Like Tinkerbell’s sunshine dust! That's a brilliant idea, both of you! Superb. It's lovely to hear you thinking about helping others. Now, back to Neverland! But perhaps after we’ve rescued Captain Hook from Tick-Tock, we can start planning our fundraising mission for Great Ormond Street? Yes! I’ll rescue him first!  Swish, swish!  And I'll sprinkle sunshine dust on everyone! Even Captain Hook! So he doesn’t feel sad. Quite right. Kindness is always the best magic. And you two are certainly proving it.

Honestly, this light is just breathtaking, isn’t it? Reminds me of those Turner paintings we saw in Tate Britain last year. Though, I’m desperately wishing I wasn’t heading to an airport to see it. I'm already missing my Year 8s. Don’t be daft, love. You’ll be back before you know it. And they’ll be thrilled to see you. Though, I still don’t understand why you chose Taunton as your first posting. Wildly different vibe to Exeter, wasn't it? Taunton’s got its charm, Maggie. Quiet. Less…fuss. Remember that little cottage we saw there once? The one with the rambling roses all over the front? Oh yes! We spent ages wandering around the shops afterwards, didn't we? Found that delightful little pottery place. You bought that ridiculous ceramic badger, Dad. Still got it, actually, sitting on the shelf in the kitchen. Reminds me of that one miserable rainy weekend when we were all crammed in that too-small rental near Minehead. Remember how the roof leaked? Leaked like a sieve! Good thing we had that paddling pool in the garden, kept the children entertained. Though, that journey back to Exeter was… eventful, to say the least. Exhausted everyone. God, these Devon roads can be testing. Especially at this time of morning. At least the traffic’s been manageable. I think I’ll have to set an alarm for 5 am from now on if I’m driving myself. It’s a shock to the system, waking up so early after teaching till nearly 4 pm. I’m running on fumes. You realize I’m practically a zombie before my first cup of coffee? You always were a late riser, darling. Just like your mother. Though, she could sleep anywhere, anytime. Remember when we lived in that house near Crediton? She fell asleep in the potting shed! She did! Absolutely remarkable woman. Speaking of houses, are you having any luck sorting out the housewarming party? It’s getting closer. It's chaos! I've sent out some invitations, but have to finalize the caterer. And figure out the music. It’s proving more complicated than teaching a class of fifteen year olds during exam season. I'm hoping to keep it relatively low-key, though. Just close friends and family. We'll be there, of course. Wouldn't miss it. Though, I'll probably stick to a corner and observe.

“Right then. Creeh-St-Michael. Seems a bit… quaint, doesn’t it? Much smaller than I expected. All this track work is a bother, though. Makes getting about a right kerfuffle. You waiting for a train too?” “Aye, that it is. Bit of a disruption, this. Needed to get to Barnstaple to see my daughter. She’s… she’s got a bit poorly. You heading far?” “Oh, that's dreadful to hear. I’m just going to Exeter, to see a friend, Millicent. She’s… well, she's in a hospice now. Sadly not long, I reckon. You know, it’s funny, isn’t it? I was just reading about a Swedish massage – apparently, it’s quite good for easing discomfort. Ridiculous idea, really, giving someone a massage when…” . “Swedish massage, eh? Never had one meself. Always thought it a bit… faffy. My wife, bless her, she was into all sorts of new-agey things towards the end. Aromatherapy, reiki... said it helped. Though, truth be told, I think it was the company that mattered most.” "Precisely! Conversation, a good cup of tea... that’s what matters. Though, thinking back on it, I should have insisted on a bit more nursery education for my daughter. Sent her to the village school, lovely as it was, but… there was a convent school nearby, rather stricter. Perhaps that would have given her a different edge.” “Nursery education, important stuff. My daughter, Alison, she went to a right good one. Good for the little ‘uns, developing those social skills, building confidence. Though, I confess, I didn't understand all the terminology they used then. 'Learning through play' – sounds a bit daft when you say it out loud, doesn't it? Still, seemed to work for her.” "Oh, the terminology! Don’t even get me started. When I was showing a piece at a gallery in London, the dealer kept using phrases like 'deconstructed narrative' and 'subversive aesthetic'. I just nodded and smiled. I’m an artist, not a philosopher! Sometimes, I feel like the whole world's got a bit… precious. This equality business, for example. It's wonderful in principle, of course, but sometimes it feels like people are trying far too hard to make a point." “Equality… blimey. It's changed a lot in my lifetime, hasn’t it? My wife, Margaret, she wasn’t one for marching with placards, but she was a strong woman.

Right, Mum, I’ve been having a proper look at this Crete thing. It's… a lot. A lot how, love? Too many ancient ruins? Not enough beaches? Don't tell me you're having second thoughts already! We've been planning this for months. No, not second thoughts exactly. It’s just… the flights are expensive, and then there's the transfers. And the hotel, while lovely looking on the website, is a bit further from Rethymno than I initially thought. I was picturing a ten-minute stroll, not a taxi ride. You always were a stickler for location, weren’t you? Remember when you were little and insisted we lived  exactly  opposite the park, or it just wasn’t fair? That was different. I wanted to swing on the swings immediately after school. This is a holiday! Relaxation is key. I just don’t want to spend half our time battling logistics. Well, we could look at Airbnbs closer to town. I did a little digging this morning, actually. Found a few apartments with balconies overlooking the harbour. Might be a bit more our speed, less “resort.” Oh, really? Don’t tell me you were having a sneaky look already! What are they like? Price-wise? And are they reliable? I’m not keen on ending up in someone’s student room. Have a look at this one. "Marina View Apartments." Three-star, apparently very well-reviewed. The owner Sarah is lovely, according to the comments. And the price… well, it's considerably less than the hotel for the same dates, about £80 a night. Hmm, it  does  look nice. And the harbour view is brilliant. What about parking? We’ll have the car, won't we? Sarah says there’s free street parking nearby, although it can be a bit tricky during peak season. But honestly, Rethymno is very walkable. We probably won't need the car much once we're settled. True. Though I was hoping to do some exploring, maybe drive up into the mountains. See some of the smaller villages. Then a car would be essential for that. Okay, so maybe the Airbnb is good for the main stay in Rethymno, but we could consider renting one just for a few days specifically for exploring. There are rental companies with depots in the town. That’s a brilliant idea, Mum! Smart! Splitting it like that would be much more sensible.

Blimey, that was a day. Lectures, the library… felt like my brain was gonna leak out my ears. Fancy a cuppa, yeah? Sure thing, love. Earl Grey alright? And how were the lectures? Anything interesting, or just the usual doom and gloom about the current economic climate? Earl Grey's perfect, cheers. It was a bit of both, to be honest. There was a decent discussion about emerging markets, though. Really got me thinking about… well, actually, it reminded me of something you were saying the other day about that new venture you're looking into. Oh? And what was that? I’m always wary of hearing myself compared to academic theory! No, no, it wasn't like that. You were talking about diversifying, right? Adapting to changing consumer trends. They were saying how crucial it is for businesses to be agile and responsive - especially in unpredictable times. It just... clicked. Thought of the rum market, you know? Always solid, but could you introduce a limited-edition, premium line playing on heritage and craftsmanship? You’ve been listening to me, haven't you? I appreciate your interest, truly. And you're right about the need for diversification. We can't just rely on the standard exports forever. This new project – ‘Island Gold’ – it’s all about exactly that. Smaller batch, using older fermentation techniques, a story behind every bottle. Luxury tourist market, primarily. Sounds dead good. Proper clever, that. Like, a bit of history woven in. Mom would love that, wouldn't she? She's been going on about preserving Barbadian traditions again. She would, wouldn’t she? Always has a good ear for authentic storytelling. Speaking of family, how’s your Auntie Carol doing? Did you remember to wish her happy birthday? Blimey, I completely forgot! Properly silly of me. I’ll give her a ring now, I promise. She'll be gutted. She was looking forward to hearing from me about the cricket, wasn’t she? Yes! She’s been glued to the matches. She keeps asking if you’re supporting the West Indies or just enjoying the chaos. A bit of both, to be honest. They're not exactly playing their best, are they? Still, good to see them out on the pitch. Makes you miss home, doesn't it? The vibe, the food… It does. Although, I must say, this Lincolnshire weather has been remarkably agreeable lately.

Right then, Bartholomew, you were saying about this Skype thing… still haven't quite got the hang of it, 'ave I? Keeps freezing up on me, like a trout in a puddle. Doesn’t seem right, chatting to folks through a screen. Feels a bit… disconnected, don’t it? It does take a bit of getting used to, dear. But think about it, Arthur! We can see each other, even though you’re all the way in Norfolk and I’m here. And Jeremy’s in Birmingham – we can all be together, in a way, without leaving our armchairs. That's the beauty of it, isn’t it? Though I’m still battling the lag. This Midlands broadband... not what it should be. You know, I was showing my niece, Chloe, some old travel brochures the other day – proper paper ones, remember those? – and she couldn’t believe you could see pictures of places before the internet! Pictures, aye. I ‘ad a globe once, years ago. A proper one, spinning and everything. Showed you all the countries. Want to see where Yorkshire was. Always dreamed of going there, I did. Read a lot about it. All those moors and heather… looks right proper. Yorkshire is lovely, Arthur. We went there for a week, ages ago, when the children were little. Stayed in a youth hostel, can you believe it? Dreadful bunks, but the walks were amazing. We visited York Minster, and the kids loved the Jorvik Viking Centre. Youth hostels! Taking me back. I led a few school trips to them when I was teaching. Always a bit chaotic, but full of character. Remember that trip to the Lake District? One of the boys got lost for a couple of hours... Lost? Goodness gracious! What 'appened then? He'd wandered off looking for a rare butterfly. Luckily, we found him eventually. Taught him a lesson about sticking with the group, though. Right, this is reet good, Annie. Proper lush. Thanks for havin' us round. No worries, Liv! Glad you like it. Give me a good Cumberland any day. So, about these flights… you’ve had a look at EasyJet then? I have. And Ryanair. And British Airways, just for comparison. Honestly, the price of a loaf of bread these days! It’s daylight robbery, isn’t it? Used to be able to get a decent loaf for under a pound. Now? Nearly two quid! Tell me about it, Dad. I noticed the same thing when I did the shop yesterday. Everything's creeping up. It’s getting difficult to budget properly, especially with everything else going on. Don’t even get me started. I spent an hour on the phone yesterday trying to understand what they were on about. Felt like I was talking to a computer. Oh, banks! They’re a nightmare. Remember when Mum tried to switch to that online-only bank? Took weeks of chasing! I think I’m sticking with HSBC for now, despite their... eccentricities. HSBC? And the woman behind the counter wouldn’t even look at me. Just kept reading from a script. It's the same everywhere, isn’t it? You used to be able to speak to a person, a decent person. I had a technical issue with my mobile phone provider last week – Three, as it happens. Spent ages on the phone trying to sort it out. Eventually, I had to escalate it to a supervisor, and even then… It’s like they actively make it difficult. Mobile phone companies... another breed altogether. Utter rip-offs. Speaking of which, has anyone heard about the new police funding? They're cutting it again, aren't they? Which is just ridiculous. I saw something about that, yes. Seems like they’re always cutting funds for essential services. Makes you wonder how they expect things to run smoothly. Happens even in the courts, doesn’t it, Brenda?

Right, so we’ve established Chloe’s obsessed with penguins. And honestly, I’m not arguing. They  are  adorable. But we need to move on to favourites. My turn! Okay, favourite holiday… has to be Greece. Last summer, we went to Crete, and honestly, the beaches were unreal. Crystal clear water, sun blazing… pure bliss. Aye, Greece sounds amazing! I've never been, but I’ve seen loads of pictures. Beaches are a big thing for me, though. I’d rather be anywhere warm and sandy, to be fair. My favourite holiday though… probably Zanzibar. It’s cheap, cheerful, and I love the arcades. It’s a right laugh, even if it is a bit tacky. What about you, Aoife? Best holiday you've had? Blackpool? Haha, you’re a woman of the people, Emma! My favourite… it was probably a trip to the Aran Islands, off the coast of Galway. Proper windswept and remote, but beautiful. Chloe, you already mentioned your penguins... They’re just… perfect, aren't they? Like little suited gentlemen. But other than penguins… I’m a big dog person. Specifically, golden retrievers. So much fluff! They’re just total softies. I’d love to get one when I’ve got my own place. What about you, Em? Favourite animal? Cats, definitely cats. I've got two, Bob and Maggie. Absolute divas, the pair of them. They’ll glare at you if you so much as look at them wrong. But they’re proper cuddly when they want to be. And they’re hilarious to watch chasing dust bunnies. Cats are lovely, I suppose. But dogs are just more… enthusiastic. I’m a horse girl, through and through. Always have been. Spent most of my childhood mucking out stables. Horses are majestic. I used to love going to the races with my grandad.

Honestly, this essay is killing me. "The impact of Impressionism on early 20th-century landscape painting." Where do you even  start  with that? It feels like I'm trying to squeeze the ocean into a teacup. Tell me about it! I’ve got a load on too. Mine’s on the symbolism in Victorian poetry - all doom and gloom and mortality. Makes you feel proper ancient, doesn’t it? Talkin’ about old age and decay. Proper ancient! I know, right? Makes you wonder if we should be learnin' about, I dunno, practical things, like how to navigate the tax system, rather than pondering Monet’s brushstrokes. Though, those brushstrokes  are  lovely, innit? I saw a Monet exhibition in London a few years back…it was breathtaking. Breathtaking is a good word for it. I reckon that's why we're doin' it, though, yeah? It's not just about the history, it's about the feelin'. My Gran used to love Van Gogh. She’d sit and stare at prints of sunflowers for ages. Said they reminded her of sunshine and brighter days. Aw, that's sweet. My nan was more of a David Hockney girl. Bright colours, wasn't she? Used to have a massive print of a swimming pool in her kitchen. Makes you think, doesn't it? What’ll  our  favourite artists be? Will future generations look at, like, final fantasy landscapes and say, “Oh, the raw emotionality of pixelated dragons!” Honestly! Imagine. "The existential angst portrayed through the flickering pixels of a mid-level boss battle." It'd be a whole new genre of art criticism. I was playin' Stardew Valley the other day, and I felt a genuine connection to my digital parsnips. Is that art? It’s got to be, hasn't it? It’s creating something, expressin' yourself. Even if it’s just a particularly well-placed scarecrow in your digital farm. Speaking of which, I'm completely behind on my actual farm – I mean, my essay. Where have you even  started  with the Victorian stuff? It feels like a black hole of depressing rhymes. Alright, listen. I broke it down. Basically, I'm lookin' at four poets – Tennyson, Browning, Arnold, and Rossetti. Focus on the common themes: loss, faith, and the decline of…well, everything. You know? Then, I’m pickin’ one or two poems to really dig into. Don't try to cover it all.

Honestly, I’m knackered. This Henderson project is  eating  my life. I swear, if I have to look at another Gantt chart, I might scream. Sounds rough. You’ve been putting in some serious hours. It sounds so heavy. You’re amazing for doing what you do, seriously. I feel guilty sometimes complaining about project deadlines when you're dealing with  that . Don’t be. Your job is important too.
