Seriously, though, what's really going on? Is it just the bins or is something else bubbling under the surface? It’s… I don’t know. I think he feels like I’m prioritising work over him. And he’s not entirely wrong. But he doesn’t understand how demanding this project is. It feels like we're living separate lives. Have you actually  told  him how demanding it is? Not just in a frustrated, ‘I’m working late’ kind of way, but actually explained the scope of it, the pressure you're under? I’ve tried. But he just sort of nods and then goes back to playing his video games. It’s like… he’s not really listening.

Right then, let’s have a proper look at this consent form, shall we? It's a bit… dense, innit? All these legal clauses. I’ve highlighted a few bits I'm not entirely certain about, particularly regarding data storage. Are we absolutely sure they’re following GDPR properly with recordings of the seminar? Yes, I’ve had a quick skim. It  does  look thorough, thankfully. I queried this last year about a different module – they assured me the university's IT department have everything in hand. It's standard practice now, apparently, to record sessions for accessibility and later review. I think we should just initial those specific points, acknowledging we've read the information. Worrying ourselves silly about it won't change the policy, will it? Aye, I agree with Eleanor on that. We’ve been through this dance before. Initial it, and move on. The real issue is the seminar itself, isn't it? We’re trying to cram a lot in. International business communication is a  massive  topic. So, are we still leaning towards the "cultural nuances" angle, or should we broaden it a bit? Well, I was thinking about the cultural nuances, definitely. It’s practically half the battle, isn't it? The bit about non-verbal communication – the difference between a head nod meaning "yes" in some cultures and something completely different in others. I’ve got some really good case studies on that, actually. From my work with Japanese clients, mostly. That’s excellent, Margaret. Truly. But perhaps we shouldn't  overwhelm  them with specific cultural examples straight off the bat. I was imagining starting with a broader overview - perhaps a section on the challenges of virtual communication and the importance of clear, concise language, regardless of culture. A bit of foundation setting, you see? I like that, Eleanor. A good grounding. Because then when we get into the specifics, like Margaret’s Japanese examples, it’ll land better. People will have a framework to hang it on. I’ve been looking at incorporating some interactive exercises - quick role-playing scenarios to demonstrate communication breakdowns. Perhaps one focusing on email etiquette across different countries? German emails are notoriously formal, aren't they? They are, aren’t they? And the Americans' tendency to end every email with "Best regards" even when you've just met them! It's peculiar, isn’t it? But the role-playing sounds good, Gillian.

Honestly, I thought it would be warmer by now. This Beijing chill is biting! Remind me again why we thought living here for five years was a good idea? Because we’re adventurous, love! And because the university offered us both incredible research opportunities. Remember all that excitement about the grant? Besides, you were the one practically leaping at the chance to study the evolution of Ming Dynasty pottery. I do. And the pottery  is  fascinating. It’s just... everything else feels a bit… overwhelming. I miss a proper Sunday roast. And a decent cup of tea. This jasmine tea is starting to taste like potpourri. Baby steps. We've only been here six months. And I've found a reasonably good bakery that does scones. Progress! Tell me, how was the lecture on Confucianism today? You seemed a bit flustered afterward. That’s because it was a disaster. Honestly, half the students seem to think Confucius invented the wheel. I tried to get them to engage with the complexities of his political philosophy, the critiques... and they just stared back blankly. It’s like they’re reading the textbook verbatim and nothing is sinking in. Teaching students unwilling to critically think is a universal problem, isn't it? Remember Professor Davies at UCL? He used to say, "Engaging a student’s apathy is the greatest academic challenge." He did have a point. Still frustrating though. And it made me think about the house again. The sheer  size  of it. It’s gorgeous, don’t get me wrong, but it's just… a lot. I feel like I’m living in a museum. It  is  spacious. We got an unbelievable deal, remember? Think of all the room for your pottery collection! And for when we eventually have… Don't worry, I'm not pushing. Just saying, it's a good problem to have. It's a good problem, yes. It's just… a lot of cleaning. I keep thinking about a smaller place, maybe something a little more modern, closer to the university. Less room for dust bunnies the size of small dogs. We can look, absolutely. But let's give it another six months. Get settled in properly. I quite like the feeling of space, to be honest. It encourages me to write. And besides, I’m finding the upkeep surprisingly… therapeutic. Therapeutic? You, battling with the ancient plumbing? Are you sure you’re not just enjoying feeling like a benevolent landlord?

Honestly, this is lovely, Liam, but I feel like we’re generating a  ridiculous  amount of leftovers. Are you sure you’ll eat all that carbonara? Mmm, yeah, definitely. Don't worry. I'm building up for a big project at work, need the fuel. Besides, leftovers are  good . Lunch sorted for the next few days. That's what Grandma used to say. "Waste not, want not," she'd drone on. I miss her really. Remember her pantry? It was like a museum of preserved everything. Jams, pickles, chutneys...all in those little jars. Yeah, and the wallpaper! That hideous floral print. Though, oddly, I do miss being at her place. Especially Christmas. The smell of the pine needles, her Christmas cake…it was just…reliable. Stable. Not like, you know,  everything  now. Exactly! It feels like everything’s just… accelerated. Speaking of accelerated, did you see that documentary about automated food production? Robots picking vegetables, designing new proteins… it's incredible, but also a bit unsettling. I did. It’s efficient, undeniably. Less food waste on the farm end, I suppose. Still, it kind of makes you think about industrialization on the grand scale, doesn't it? Like, Grandma's garden and her homemade jams - those were a response to previous industrialization, a way of holding onto something more personal. Totally. It makes you think about urban farming initiatives too, doesn't it? Those rooftop gardens in London… It's a tiny step, but a step towards reclaiming some of that food autonomy. I was reading an article about a school trying to grow their own vegetables for the canteen - brilliant concept. Good for them! We should push for something like that at my old school. They need to do more careers advice, honestly. They just kept steering everyone towards… well, the usual. Finance, law. Nobody ever suggested anything truly  different . I practically had to engineer my own path into engineering. Tell me about it! I felt similarly as a student. It's such a closed world, some of these industries. Like you said, finance and law are almost the default. I remember Mrs. Henderson trying to convince me to go into teaching – she was right, obviously – but the options presented felt pretty limited. No one ever talked about the actual  experience  of being a teacher, just the qualifications. It's not just the careers advice, is it? It’s the perception.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a walking, talking statistics package. Another grant proposal, another literature review… it’s all just numbers and correlations at this point. Sounds intense. You’re pushing yourself hard, aren't you? You mentioned feeling a bit burned out last week. Burned out is an understatement. I’m contemplating joining a monastery. Somewhere remote, quiet, with no academic papers to write. Just... peace. Though, I'd probably analyse the monks’ meditation habits. See if I can quantify enlightenment. You can’t quantify enlightenment, love. You'll drive yourself mad. What’s the grant for this time? Something about adolescent anxiety, I think you mentioned? Yeah, specifically the link between social media usage and anxiety levels in teenagers. It's huge, obviously, but proving causality is a nightmare. Everyone points to correlation, but pinning down definitive cause and effect... that’s the Holy Grail. And the funding bodies  want  the Holy Grail. It’s tricky, isn’t it? With everything influencing everything else. How are the participants doing? Are you seeing a lot of distress? Some. It's... confronting. You see how much pressure these kids are putting on themselves. The constant comparison, the need for validation… It's bleak. And then when you talk to their parents, they’re often completely oblivious or dismissive. "They're just being dramatic," you know? Ugh, the classic. It's the same with kids having learning difficulties, you know? Parents often downplaying it. It’s probably easier for them to avoid facing it. How's Sarah handling it, being around all that negativity? That’s what worries me most. She’s been a bit quieter lately, a bit more withdrawn. I think she’s internalising some of it, subconsciously. I suggested she spend some time with her grandma next weekend. A bit of fresh air and cake might do her the world of good. Good idea. Grandma's a genius at restoring emotional balance with a Victoria sponge. Listen, how about tonight, after dinner, we just… turn everything off? No work, no news, no scrolling. Just board games and Sarah's ridiculous drawings? That… sounds pretty amazing, actually. I’ve been meaning to clear out that box of old photos. Maybe we could do that too? Remember that ridiculous trip to Cornwall we took when we were younger? How could I forget? The rain, the seagulls attacking our sandwiches, the tiny caravan that smelled permanently of damp… It wasn’t the most glamorous holiday, but it was an adventure.

Cor, this tea’s gone cold. Didn’t rightly notice, did I? Everything feels a bit… grey today, doesn’t it? Like Norfolk on a November morning. It does, Arthur. It really does. You look a bit down, love. More than usual, I mean. Anything on your mind? You've been quiet as a mouse all afternoon. Arthur, you okay? You've barely touched your biscuit. And you never turn down a custard cream. Something’s up. Just… well, it’s the house, really. The council keep sending letters, you know? About the rates. And I ain't got that sort of money. Never have. Can’t see as I ever will. Makes a man feel… useless. Like a burden. Oh, Arthur, don’t say that. You’re not a burden. We're here, aren't we? We’ll sort something out. Have you looked at the Citizens Advice Bureau? They can advise you on benefits, things like that. Absolutely, Arthur. And have you shown them the letters? They’re legally obliged to help if you're struggling. And look, about the house… have you considered downsizing? Just a small flat, easier to manage, less to worry about. Downsizing? But this is where I’ve lived… well, nearly forty years now. Since Maggie and I… It's full of memories. All the good ones, mind you. Little Jenny’s drawings stuck to the fridge… Maggie's sewing basket… I know, Arthur. I know it’s hard. But holding onto a building you can’t afford... it won't bring her back, sweetheart. It’ll just keep dragging you down. And we worry about you. Seeing you like this… it’s difficult. Exactly. You've got to think about your own wellbeing, Arthur. You were so down after Maggie passed. Remember how much better you were when you started volunteering at the bird sanctuary? Watching those little blue tits nesting… that brought a smile to your face! Aye, the blue tits. Cheeky little things, they are. Always bumbling about, lookin’ for a crumb. Reminds me of Jenny when she was little. See? Even thinking about them brightens you a bit. Maybe you could get back to volunteering? Fresh air, meeting people… it’d do you good. I can drive you down there whenever you like, Arthur. And I'll even bring some extra sunflower seeds for the birds. What about this, we’ll book an appointment with the CAB next week?

Honestly, I’m still obsessed with this lash serum. It’s a game changer, isn't it? I know we were chatting about it last week. It really is! I finally bit the bullet and ordered it, the one you recommended, the 'LumiLash'? Takes ages to arrive, doesn't it? I keep meaning to get some cuticle oil. Do you use anything? I do! I got this little pot from Superdrug last month. It's got shea butter and almond oil in it. Smells divine! I’ll have a look next time I’m in.

Right, so, parking was a nightmare, weren't it? Absolutely mental. I swear, circling around for twenty minutes, just to find a space two streets over. Anyway, thinking about stuff like that, it makes you think, don't it? About your own future. It does. You and the Masters. How’s that interview going? You sounded a bit stressed about it last week. You get the kids engaged, you’re passionate about language, and you’ve clearly got a good head on your shoulders. You’ll smash it, mate.

Honestly, Sarah, I’m just drained. Absolutely drained. Another parent-teacher conference where I'm essentially explaining why little Timmy refuses to share his Lego. It's exhausting, isn't it? Trying to mediate miniature human dramas. Tell me about it. It’s not quite Lego-related, but dealing with Leo's tantrums over…absolutely anything…can feel like a full-time job. You're shaping young minds! And honestly, balance is a myth, isn't it? Some days I feel like I've earned a medal for just surviving, let alone contributing something meaningful. This whole caring thing...it's more consuming than I ever imagined. I know, I know. It's just… I see my colleagues, some of them have such polished lives. Weekend away here, promotion there. Don’t compare your behind-the-scenes to someone else’s highlight reel. Besides, you’re a brilliant teacher. I’ve seen the letters you send home, the extra effort you put in. Thanks, love. You always know what to say. It's just… Mark and I have been talking about me maybe taking on a slightly less demanding role, you know? Part-time. Just to… ease up a bit. Wow. That’s a big step. And don't you worry about finances. You'll figure something out. And honestly, your visits  are  the highlight of my week.

Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the rabbit hole I went down on Pinterest last night. Needed this whole evening, really. What about you? How's the research going? Anything exciting saving the world? It's alright. Lots of spreadsheets and data analysis. Exciting is not exactly the word I’d use. We’re looking at the impact of social media on consumer behaviour. Thrilling, isn't it? Remember Sarah’s birthday last month? She was  obsessed  with recreating that influencer’s lemon drizzle cake. It looked nothing like the picture, and she was so upset. Oh god, yes! That was a disaster! It was drier than the Sahara. I nearly choked. And she spent hours decorating it with those edible flowers... wasted! We ended up ordering pizza. Exactly! And all because she wanted to impress her followers. It's… sad, really. Speaking of birthdays, are we doing anything for Mum's this year? I’ve been meaning to ask. Aye, I’ve been thinking about it. I was looking at Pinterest, as you no doubt suspected, and there’s this amazing DIY bath bomb recipe. We could make a whole load for her. Remember how she used to love those fancy lavender ones? That’s a brilliant idea! Way better than another scented candle set. She'd appreciate the effort. Plus, we can customize them. Maybe some rose petals for her? Definitely rose petals. And glitter, of course! She can't resist a bit of sparkle. I also saw some really cool paper flower tutorials… maybe we could make a little bouquet to go with the bath bombs.

Right, so this one’s… interesting. It’s a brass chandelier, apparently 'vintage' but looks like it's been rescued from a pirate ship. What do you reckon, David? Pirate ship is a fair assessment, love. A bit much for the dining room, wouldn't you say? Remember what you said about wanting something… refined? Refined doesn't mean boring, does it? It just means not actively trying to scare the postman. This  is  brass though, which is what I’m looking for. And the price is decent, £45 delivered. Much better than that monstrosity from the antique shop last week. Agreed on the antique shop. I’m still trying to scrub the image of that taxidermied squirrel from my mind. So, brass is the key. What about those flush-mounted ceiling lights we looked at earlier? The ones with the frosted glass? They were quite elegant. They were, but they felt a little… impersonal, didn't they? Like something you'd find in a hotel lobby. I want something with a bit of personality. Okay, this one’s more promising. Chrome, with amber glass shades. Think that would work? Chrome and amber... Hmm. Send me the link. Let me have a proper look. Right, while you're doing that, I’ve been having another trawl through Rightmove. Oh? Anything exciting? Don’t tell me you’ve found a mansion with a moat. No moats. But I did find a semi-detached in Harpenden, four bedrooms, decent garden, and within our budget. Harpenden? That's a bit further out than we were initially thinking, isn’t it? Still, the train line is good, I know. What’s the catch? The kitchen's a bit dated, needs updating, and the photos aren't brilliant. But the location is fantastic – close to the schools and apparently a lovely little village feel. I’ve printed out the details. Harpenden… Right. Let’s have a look. Oh, that garden  is  lovely. And four bedrooms would be good, wouldn't it? No more squabbles about who gets which bedroom when the cousins visit. Exactly. And it’s got potential. We could do the kitchen ourselves, gradually. It wouldn't have to be perfect straight away. Okay, so this one’s a definite maybe. I’m adding it to my 'watch list'. What do you think about booking a viewing for this Harpenden place? Just to get a sense of it?

Honestly, it’s just relentless at the ward this week. Mrs. Higgins took a turn, poor love, and we were all running around like headless chickens. You wouldn't believe the paperwork they expect us to do now, too. It's a wonder we get any time to actually  care  for people, really. Tell me about it, Fiona. Things are hectic at Meadowbrook too. We've got two extra residents this week, and one of them, Mr. Davies, well, he’s really not making things easy. Keep wandering off, shouting for his daughter...it’s tiring, isn't it? Especially when the staffing levels are so low. It’s the same at Willow House, Auntie Sarah. We’ve had a couple of new people, and they're needing a lot of attention. I'm trying my best, but sometimes I feel like I'm spreading myself too thin. Did you hear about poor old Mr. Peterson? He fell yesterday. Luckily, he wasn't badly hurt, but it was still a scare. Oh dear! How awful for him. And for you, dealing with that. It’s just stressful, isn’t it? I’ve been thinking, actually, I might have to look at something slightly less intense. Honestly, the pressure…it's getting to me. I saw a posting for a nurse consultant at that private clinic near Sevenoaks. It wouldn't be quite the same as working with the community, but the pay is significantly better, and the hours are more regular. A nurse consultant! Fiona, that's brilliant! You'd be perfect for something like that. You've got years of experience, you're incredibly knowledgeable…they’d be lucky to have you. Don't undersell yourself, love. But, more regular hours? Sounds like heaven! I’m half tempted to look for something else myself, but finding something that lets me use my skills  and  pays the bills…it’s tough. Really, Auntie Fiona? A new job? That’s exciting! What’s it like at the clinic? Is it fancy? Fancy is probably a bit strong, Maisie. It's modern, clean, and they seem to actually value their staff, which is a rare thing these days. It’s mostly cosmetic and private patients, so less emergency work, thankfully. It would be a big change, though. I'd miss the familiar faces on the ward, the banter...and the charity cake sales, of course!

Right, this is exactly what I needed. That morning was a complete write-off. Three conference calls before 9 am – brutal. Tell me about it. Marking essays feels like a marathon sometimes. Though, I did stumble across something really interesting while researching sleep disorders for my year elevens. Oh? Let me guess, another study proving that everyone needs eight hours and will die if they don't? Not quite. This was about chronotypes. Apparently, we’re all wired differently. Some people are really ‘larks’ - natural early risers, full of energy in the morning. And others are ‘owls’ – they thrive later in the day, feel sluggish in the morning. Owls, huh? Definitely sounds like me. Remember that camping trip we did in the Lake District? I spent half the night shivering awake while you were dead to the world. You were complaining about the dew on your sleeping bag for a solid hour. Honestly, you woke up half the campsite! But it's fascinating, isn't it? The research suggests it’s largely genetic, and it impacts everything from productivity to mood. So, you’re saying I’m genetically predisposed to being grumpy before noon? Wonderful. Does it also explain why I always get hopelessly lost in unfamiliar cities? There’s probably a correlation! Cognitive function can be affected by sleep patterns, or lack thereof. It reminded me of that time we tried to navigate Edinburgh. You insisted on taking those tiny, winding alleyways, convinced you knew a shortcut. I  did  know a shortcut! It was just… less direct than Google Maps suggested. And a little more cobbled. And, okay, fine, considerably longer. But it was atmospheric! Atmospheric and utterly baffling. We ended up asking a bewildered old lady for directions. Honestly, sometimes I think you have a talent for finding the most convoluted route imaginable. I prefer to think of it as an adventure. Speaking of adventures… I’ve been looking at flights to Iceland. Fancy a few days Northern Lights hunting? Iceland! Wow. That's a bit sudden, isn’t it? It does sound amazing though. I'd need to have a proper look at the flight times and if I can get time off work. We can book a trip during the school holidays. I have been looking into some four-wheel-drive tours. That sounds great. Did you hear about Ben’s cousin, Geoff? He’s doing his pilot’s license now.

Right, okay, so I'm officially convinced. Hamsters are tiny, fluffy terrorists. Seriously, Winston almost escaped again last night. Had to lure him out with a sunflower seed. It's like negotiating with a miniature dictator. Aye, tell me about it! Barnaby's a right rascal. He chewed right through his water bottle last week. Mum were fuming, had to buy a brand new one. They’re just wee whirlwinds, aren't they? Can’t leave ‘em unattended for five minutes. Honestly! They’re adorable, of course, but the sheer amount of work… my cousin has three. Three! She says she’s basically running a tiny animal sanctuary from her bedroom. It's a whole thing. Are you lot finding they need a lot of enrichment? Nibbling toys and those little tunnels? Aye, enrichment is key, definitely. Little Maggie’s favourite is a cardboard tube. She drags it all over the cage and fills it with bedding. It’s hilarious to watch. But speaking of ginger… did you see that lad at the lecture this morning? The one in the orange jumper? Oh, you mean the one with the ridiculously bright hair? He tripped over the cable. Twice. Oh, good grief! No! I missed that. Were you filming it? You should’ve been! I saw a ginger cat in town yesterday. It was like, the reddest ginger I've ever seen. Like a little flame. The orange jumper lad was certainly memorable. There’s just something about gingers, isn’t there? They’re either incredibly charming or gloriously clumsy. No in-between. Any ginger lads in your families, anyone? My grandad was a right ginger, a proper character. Always telling jokes and wearing ridiculous hats. He used to say, "A ginger lad is just a lad with a bit of sunshine in 'is hair!" Made my mam cringe every time. My dad’s got a bit of a reddish tint to his hair. Nothing like a full-on ginger, but enough to get teased relentlessly when he were a kid. He still gets called "Rusty" by his brother. My Uncle Derek’s a ginger. Always wears a flat cap, you know, trying to hide it. It doesn't work. He looks like a particularly disgruntled hedgehog. But he's a lovely bloke, really. Just a bit…traditional. Do you think gingers  actually  have more personality or is it just a stereotype?

Right, okay. So, Genghis Khan just decimated Australia. Again. I swear, Dad, you're obsessed with conquering the Southern Hemisphere. Gotta diversify, son! Can’t put all your troops in Europe. Besides, Australia’s got a surprisingly strategic coastal advantage. You’re just not seeing the bigger picture. And it IS Genghis Khan! Respect the name. Honestly, the smell of your mum’s Christmas spices is absolutely overwhelming. Are you planning a Christmas feast in July, Margaret? It’s a bit much, isn't it? Don’t remind me. Every time we play this game, I feel like I'm slowly being suffocated by cinnamon and mulled wine. Though, chocolate is helping. . Chocolate’s a good morale booster. Especially when you're staring down the barrel of a Russian invasion. Speaking of which, you left Siberia wide open, Liam. Rookie mistake. I thought I was banking on reinforcements! It’s a calculated risk! And frankly, Siberia is a cursed land. No one wants it. Besides, you’ve been hogging all the dice. Are you worried your luck’s going to run out? Your father  is  a terrible dice roller. Honestly, it’s a wonder he ever got through sixth form with that level of randomness influencing his choices. Hey! I have clever strategies! It's just... sometimes the dice gods are against me. It's not my fault. Anyway, back to the game. Liam, are you going to defend North America or just let me waltz in and establish a Khanate of Canada? Look, I’m trying to strategize, but you keep distracting me with your empire-building ambitions. How many times have we played this? It feels like we’ve been at it since Christmas! We  have  been playing since Christmas, dear. Actually, since Boxing Day. And I’m still trying to figure out how you keep cards hidden. It’s practically cheating. It's a skill, Margaret! A buyer needs to be discreet. It's about anticipating the market. That’s completely different, Dad. This is a game of global dominance! You’re treating it like assessing supplier contracts. Speaking of contracts, remember when Aaron kept trying to convince me to invest in that… what was it? That Chinese Herbal remedy company? He swore it could cure everything. Don't remind me. He was so convinced. Remember how he mispronounced "Bai Yun Shan"? It was horrific. Sounded like… like a distressed badger.

Honestly, Maisie, I'm feeling properly useless. Everyone’s posting about internships and grad schemes, and I’m still just… browsing cat videos. Useless? Don't be daft, Chloe. You’ve got ages yet. And cat videos are essential for mental health, let's be clear. What's got you properly down then? Is it the whole career thing? It is. I mean, I enjoyed Sixth Form, but I still haven’t a clue what I want to  do . My mum keeps sending me links to solicitor training, bless her, but the thought of law makes me want to knit a very large, very itchy sweater. Solicitors are… not for everyone, yeah. My nan tried to steer me towards accountancy for years. Can you imagine? Me, crunching numbers? I’d rather wrestle a badger. But seriously, what  do  you like? Think back – what made you lose track of time, you know? Hmm… I did love photography. Remember when we went to Cornwall last summer and I spent ages snapping everything? The light was proper dreamy. But, like, is that a proper career? Can you actually  make  a living out of it? You can! Loads of people do. Wedding photography, portraits, fashion… Even just selling prints online. It’s tough, yeah, but it's doable. And honestly, you've got a good eye. I always think your photos are brilliant. Did you see that photo of Harry Styles on Instagram this morning? Seriously, who  is  he? Oh, don't even. What  is  he? He just pops up, looking effortlessly cool, and everyone loses their minds. It's wild. But back to proper grown-up stuff... I just feel so much pressure. You seem to have it all figured out, with your journalism degree and all. Don't be silly! I'm constantly questioning everything. Last week, I was convinced I was going to become a shepherdess in the Lake District. Then I remembered I'm terrified of sheep. It’s all a work in progress, Chloe. Everyone's faking it ‘til they make it, honestly. A shepherdess?! You’re brilliant. So, no baby lambs in your future, then? Because Auntie Carol's been hinting she's going to be a grandmother any minute now. She’s got a nesting instinct that involves crocheting tiny hats for everyone she knows. Oh, god, Auntie Carol. Don’t even start! My mum’s already been roped into photographing the whole birth.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is  killing  me with this project. "The impact of socio-economic factors on individual opportunity." Where do you even  start  with that? It’s just…massive. Yeah, it’s a beast, isn't it? I was thinking, maybe we could focus on, like, education? Seems pretty directly linked. My cousin, Raj, he goes to a decent school, but his family's struggling so much he basically has to work evenings to help out. He misses loads of homework time. Exactly! That's a good angle. It’s not just about access to good schools either, is it? It's about the resources at home – computers, quiet spaces to study, parents who can actually help. My little sister's trying to do her GCSEs in a two-bed flat with three other people. It's chaos. Mad, innit? You know, I was reading about that Universal Basic Income thing the other day - that could maybe make a difference. Giving everyone a base level of money to live on. UBI? Seriously? That’s…a bit idealistic, isn't it? My dad says it’s just giving people a free ride. He always goes on about personal responsibility. Like, if you don’t work hard, you don’t deserve anything. But isn’t it a bit simplistic to say that? Loads of people work  really  hard and still struggle. Raj's dad works two jobs and they're still barely scraping by. It's not about a free ride; it's about leveling the playing field a bit. Imagine if Raj had the time and headspace to actually focus on his studies, instead of panicking about bills. I get what you're saying. It’s just… politics, right? Everyone's got an opinion. Speaking of opinions, have you seen what's happening with that new AI research at Oxford? Apparently, they're getting it to generate original scientific hypotheses. No way! That's wild. Bit scary, though, isn't it? Like, what happens to all the scientists? Will robots be doing all our research? It's like something out of a comic book. I know! It's proper X-Men territory. Though, if it helps speed up scientific breakthroughs, like finding cures for diseases… that’d be amazing. It just feels like everything's being accelerated. Even consumerism. Have you seen the size of the adverts for Black Friday already? It's only October!

Honestly, this is lovely, Anon. It's so…you. Much nicer than that little flat you had in London. Though, I do miss having you closer. Thanks, Mum. It's… quieter here. That's good, mostly. It’s just… well, never mind. Did you have a good journey up? Perfectly fine, dear. Though the M25 was its usual chaotic self. Anyway, I wanted to tell you about the recording. It actually went rather well. I managed to capture a beautiful rendition of that Yeats poem, "The Lake Isle of Innisfree." Really? That’s amazing, Mum! You’ve always been brilliant at poetry. Can I hear it sometime? Absolutely! I’ll burn you a CD. It's been a real project, getting the acoustics right. You know how I am about sound quality. It's frustrating, really - you spend all that time perfecting the delivery, and then some rogue car horn can ruin the entire take. I can imagine. Everything needs to be  just  so, doesn't it? Like... like getting the right shade of paint for the hallway. Remember how long you agonized over that cream colour? Don’t remind me! It was a nightmare. Anyway, how are you doing, love? Still struggling to find something that… clicks? Yeah. Still. It's... disheartening, you know? I had that interview at the garden centre last week, but they didn’t call. Honestly, Mum, I feel like I’m just… existing. Now, don’t talk like that. You're a bright, capable young woman. We'll find something. Have you been keeping up with your physiotherapy? That’s important, especially with your knees. It’s… okay. The exercises are boring, and it hurts sometimes. I just feel so stiff. It’s getting worse, I think. Oh, darling. I understand. My joints are playing up something fierce these days. It's the age, I suppose. I've been trying this new turmeric supplement – supposed to be good for inflammation. It tastes dreadful, mind you, like muddy water. You'll try anything, won't you? Speaking of trying things... Have you been watching those weight loss programmes? The ones with the incredibly strict diets? Oh yes. The ones that promise you’ll lose a stone a week by eating nothing but kale and grapefruit? Don't even get me started! They’re all utterly ridiculous. It’s deprivation, plain and simple. I’d rather enjoy a slice of cake, thank you very much.

Right, nearly there then! Smells better than it looks, I reckon. This Yorkshire stew recipe is a right pain to get right, takes ages. You wouldn’t believe the amount of carrots my grandma used to chuck in. Mountains of 'em. It smells amazing, honestly. Much better than my attempt at pasta carbonara last week. That ended up looking like a gluey mess. My flatmate still refuses to let me cook Italian. Aye, well, some things are best left to the professionals, or at least, to people who grew up with a Yorkshire grandma! So, how was the conference? You were working crazy hours last week, weren’t you? Ugh, don't remind me. Absolute chaos. The keynote speaker, Professor Davies, cancelled at the last minute because of a family emergency. Like, literally an hour before he was supposed to go on. Thankfully, we had a backup, but scrambling to rearrange everything and brief him… it was manic. Cor, that’s a nightmare! Poor you. What happened then? Did it all go smoothly with the backup? Relatively. He was alright, a bit dry, but he kept to the schedule and everyone seemed engaged. The biggest issue was the AV. Halfway through, the projector decided it wasn’t playing ball. We had a guy frantically fiddling with cables for what felt like forever. Oh, standard, then. Tech always lets you down at the worst possible moment, doesn't it? Remember that time at the charity gala, when the lights went out and everyone thought it was a power cut but it was just a dodgy fuse? How could I forget? You looked brilliant in the dark, glowing with the emergency fairy lights! But seriously, dealing with technical glitches is half my job now. Production control isn’t all glamorous planning, you know. It's a lot of crisis management. I can imagine. My job's a bit like that too, just on a slightly smaller scale. I’m organising the annual accounts team away day next month. Trying to find a venue that’s accessible, has decent Wi-Fi , and won't cost a fortune... it's harder than it sounds. Tell me about it. Finding venues that tick all the boxes  and  have reasonable pricing is basically a superpower. Have you looked at the Willowbrook Country Club? I heard they do pretty good day rates. Willowbrook, eh? I'll have a look, ta.

Right, so, who's feeling a film night tonight? I’m proper knackered after that essay on Wordsworth - need some serious escapism. Ooh, yes please! I’ve been craving a good film. What were you thinking, Liv? Something cheesy? Anything but Wordsworth. Seriously. My brain feels like mush. Romantic poetry? Ugh. I’m well up for anything. Films, eh? Good shout. I was thinking something a bit… intense? Been watching a load of Nolan lately. Is anyone in the mood for a proper thinker? Nolan? Is that the one with the really confusing time thing? I don't think so, Uncle Finn, I want something with dancing! Like, a musical! Ooh, musicals! I'm totally on board with that, Maisie. Ever seen  Singin' in the Rain ? Classic. Dancing, eh? That’s a bit of a change of pace from the brooding superheroes we usually end up watching. I'm pretty easy to please, honestly. But a musical  does  sound fun. I haven't really watched one in ages. I’m happy to be swayed. I’m just generally against anything that requires too much brainpower right now. But if Maisie wants musicals… Please, please, please! Can we? I even brought some sparkly socks! Sparkly socks? You drive a hard bargain, Maisie. I'm still sticking by my Nolan suggestion, purely for the intellectual stimulation, mind you. But alright, a musical it is. I’ll admit,  Singin' in the Rain  is brilliant. See? Finn's got a good heart! I've got a few others in mind if  Singin' in the Rain  doesn’t take everyone’s fancy.  Grease  is always a reliable option, or even  The Sound of Music .  The Sound of Music ? Oh, that's a bit... wholesome, isn't it? Although, I do love the scenery.  Grease ! Definitely  Grease ! I love the costumes and the music. And Danny and Sandy! Classic romance.  Grease  sounds perfect. Let’s go with that. Can someone put it on? I need to zone out for a few hours. Right,  Grease  it is. Though, if anyone starts quoting lines, I’m leaving. Just saying. Yay! I'm so excited! Can I have popcorn?! Of course, Maisie. I'll make a huge bowl. Everyone needs popcorn for  Grease . It's practically a requirement. Right, let the nostalgia commence! And someone remind me to buy a leather jacket after this.

Oh my god, I need a cup of tea. Paris was… a lot. A lot good, I hope? You looked ever so tired when you dropped me off. Did you relax, love? Relax is a strong word, Mum. It was amazing, honestly. The art, the food... but my feet are absolutely killing me. I swear, I walked approximately a million miles. Million’s a slight exaggeration, isn't it, Liv? But welcome back! How was Paris? Pictures later, I hope? Definitely pictures. I’ll sort them out tomorrow. And yes, exaggeration aside, my feet feel like they’re going to fall off. I bought these gorgeous boots, vintage, you know, and they were  not  built for walking. Vintage boots, eh? Well, you can't go around wearing fancy shoes all day. Practicality, that’s what you need. Remember when I used to drag you around Norfolk broads in Wellies when you were little? You never complained then! Because I was five and you bribed me with ice cream! And those weren’t exactly stylish, Mum. Anyway, the best part was probably the little bistro we found near the Marais. The steak frites were to die for. Ooh, that sounds incredible. Did you manage to try any macarons? Those things are practically works of art. I did! Ladurée, of course. A little cliché, I know, but they were divine. Chloe - Sarah’s friend I met – she steered us clear of the tourist traps for the most part. She’s lived in Paris for a couple of years, proper expat she is. Sarah's friend? Sounds lovely. Is she alright? You know Sarah worries something fierce. She’s wonderful. Actually, speaking of friends, Sarah's been going on about this new pottery class she’s started. She thinks I should join. Pottery? That sounds relaxing! Good for stress. You've been looking a bit stressed lately with the project deadlines. That's what she says. But I'm not sure. I’m already juggling so much. The deadline for the Davies proposal is looming, and I think Mark is going to push it even further. He's being ridiculous. Mark? Still causing you bother, then? Honestly, some men… Doesn't he understand you've got a life outside of work? Apparently not. He just expects me to drop everything. I even twisted my ankle a little yesterday, trying to get away from him to look at a little antique shop.

"Hey, Chloe! Didn’t expect to see you lurking around here before your shift starts. Big lecture today?" "Tom! Hi! No, not today, thankfully. Just grabbing a quick coffee before heading over to the retail unit. My supervisor hat needs a scrub. How's your morning going? You look like you need another coffee too, honestly." "You’re not wrong. Prepping for my grammar lesson. It’s a nightmare this week – the passives. Absolutely nobody understands them. I ended up spending a good hour yesterday trying to explain the difference between ‘The letter was written by her’ and ‘She wrote the letter.’ It was a battle." "Oh, bless. Passives are the bane of everyone’s existence, aren't they? Even I struggled with them when I was doing my undergrad. Remember those referencing lectures? My brain nearly exploded." “Don't remind me! I still have flashbacks of MLA versus APA. Speaking of undergrad, you did your postgrad here, didn’t you? What was it in?" "Yeah, I did! Linguistics, actually. Bit of a change from retail supervision, I know! Focused on sociolinguistics. It’s fascinating, seeing how language changes depending on the context." "No way! Seriously? That’s amazing! I use bits and pieces of the British National Corpus all the time, just to pull up examples for my students. It’s incredible the data they’ve collected. Have you ever looked into the Malaysian dialect variations? My student from Kuala Lumpur was explaining some of them the other day – totally blew my mind." "I did a brief project on South London dialects – Croydon, obviously - for a module. The shifts in slang are surprisingly rapid. It'd be wild to compare that to something like Malaysian dialects. Did you see those firework displays down by the seafront last weekend? They were incredible." "I missed them! Was grading papers until midnight, the usual. Speaking of which, pay day can't come soon enough. This student loan situation is… stressing, to say the least. How are things with you on that front?" "Tell me about it! Retail doesn't exactly pay the bills. Being a supervisor does give me slightly more flexibility though, which is good. Gets me out of the long shifts sometimes. Oh, I saw a photo on Sarah's Instagram, she's back from Greece! Looks amazing." "Sarah from the library? No kidding! I need a holiday. I swear, if I hear one more student ask me about the difference between 'there,' 'their,' and 'they're'… I might spontaneously combust.

Right, so you’re  sure  you want to do this? Curry night’s a bit ambitious for a Tuesday, innit? And rice can be a nightmare if you mess it up. Nonsense, love. You've been moaning about wanting to learn to cook, and I'm happy to show you. Besides, Oscar’s fallen asleep, so we actually have a bit of time. Don’t worry, it’s easier than it looks. Now, did you get the basmati? Yeah, got a big bag. Got loads of vouchers from that meal deal we won at the school fair, remember? Thought we'd use 'em, but eating out every week gets a bit pricey. Home cooking’s gotta be cheaper, right? Absolutely. And healthier, potentially. Although, a proper vindaloo is  not  a health food, let's be honest. Okay, first thing with rice - rinse it. Really rinse it. Get all that starchy stuff off, otherwise it’ll be sticky and gluey. Like… like jellyfish. Jellyfish?! Why jellyfish? Just... imagine it. Gloopy and clingy. You don't want gloopy and clingy rice, do you? Wash it until the water runs clear, then put it in the pot. Now, for the water ratio. It's generally two parts water to one part rice. But see, this is where people go wrong. Two  exactly  equal parts? Nope. Needs slightly more water. Maybe two and a quarter. Two and a quarter? That sounds like a lot. What if it’s too watery? Then you simmer it, uncovered, until the water's gone and you've got these lovely little grains. Don’t stir it during cooking, though! That’s a myth. Stirring releases starch – back to jellyfish territory. And right, what curry powder did you get? The mild one, I hope. Oscar can’t handle anything spicy. Got the medium. Figured a bit of a kick would be good. Plus, I bought some jalapenos. Jalapenos?! Okay, hold your horses. Don't go overdoing it. You can always add more, but you can’t take it away. And remember, even a tiny sliver packs a punch. Are you using meat, or veggie? Chicken, yeah. Been marinating it in yogurt and lemon juice. Smells alright. Just hoping it doesn’t go off before we actually cook it. Mum said it looked a bit dodgy this morning. Oh dear. Best give it a good sniff and a squeeze. If it's slimy or smells weird, bin it.

Right then, everyone served. Bit of a feast for a Tuesday, eh? How's everyone's plates looking? Alright, I s'pose. Could do with more gravy. Everything's a bit… dry. It's lovely, Chloe! Thanks, honestly. I’m still surprised you managed to get everything sorted with your shift at the care home. Don't mention it. It's a Wednesday night thing now. Keeps me ticking over, doesn't it? Speaking of ticking over, Liam, how’s the job hunt going? Any luck? Nah. Nothin’. Sent off a few applications, but… you know how it is. Black hole. They don't even bother replying half the time. Liam, you need to be persistent. I volunteered at the animal shelter back in Kaiserslautern, sending out endless emails, making phone calls. It was tiring, but eventually, they called me in for an interview. Easier said than done, Elodie. You’re volunteering, you’re already doing somethin’ to fill your time. I’m… bein’ here, eatin’ your dinner. Feels a bit pathetic, doesn't it? Don't be daft, Liam! We’re happy to have you. And it’s not pathetic. It’s tough out there. Honestly, even finding part-time jobs is a nightmare right now. I’m having to pick up extra shifts at the café to make rent. That’s a shame, Josie. University must be costing a fortune on top of that. Are you thinking about those summer internships you were looking at? Yeah, I applied for a few. Fingers crossed. Fingers crossed something comes through. It would really put a dent in the student loan thing. What about online freelancing? I read an article about people making good money translating documents. You're quite good with languages, Josie. I looked into it a bit, but it seems really competitive. And you need a portfolio, right? I don't really  have  one. It's worth a shot though. Even just doing a few small projects. Keeps your skills sharp. Liam, seriously, have you looked at anything beyond warehouse jobs? There's loads of admin roles advertised now, with the new systems they're bringing in. I’ve had a look, aye. But they all want a degree. Or experience. I don’t exactly have loads of experience in… admin. Apart from managin’ to keep my laundry reasonably sorted, I’m scratchin’ for ideas. You’re quite organized, Liam.

This is reet good, this bread. Proper crusty. You reckon ANON’s managed to find a decent bakery round here, then? Everything down south just seems… fluffy. You're always on about bread, aren't you, Maisie? And yes, ANON did say they found a bakery just down the street. Apparently, the sourdough is to die for. Cambridge seems to have its things sorted, unlike… well, unlike where I’ve been living. Sorted? Aye, it’s alright. Seems a bit… quiet, mind. Not like Doncaster, that’s for sure. Loads ‘appenin’ all the time. So, you've been alright, then? Settling in okay with ANON? It's peaceful. That's... good. It’s been a change. It's very different from Crawley. It's good to have someone around. I’ve been doing a bit of walking, just around the area. Keeping active, you know? Doctor's orders, loosely. Walking, eh? Good on ya. I’ve been meaning to get back into it, proper. Work's been mental this past month. The Henderson account is drivin’ me up the wall. They want a themed gala, underwater, with actual projections of fish. Underwater! Where am I gonna find a massive tank?! Underwater? Sounds… ambitious. A bit much, doesn't it? I remember when I tried to get fit. I joined that gym in Crawley, but it was like a sauna in there, and I kept bumping into people. Gave up after a week. Aye, that sounds about right. Henderson's were all “immersive experience, interactive elements, unforgettable memories.” Right, but they're not offerin' to pay for somethin' that’s fundamentally impossible! I keep havving to say “within budgetary constraints, Mr Henderson, a full underwater experience is unlikely.” He just stares at me. Sounds stressful. You need to take some time out. Find some nice walks. Cambridge has some beautiful green spaces apparently. I’ll try, I will. But finding the time is the problem. It’s always somethin’. You know, I was thinkin’… remember Liam from university? The one who did archaeology? He’s doin’ some fieldwork in Greece now. Sent me a postcard. Said his digs have been amazing. Liam? Vaguely. From the student union bar, wasn't he? The one with the… beard? Aye, that's him! Proper beard. Anyway, he said they’re excavatin’ some ancient theatre. Sounds incredible. Makes me wonder what I’m doin’, caterin’ for Henderson’s underwater fantasies.

Right, Operation Clear-Up commences! Honestly, lads, you'd think a whirlwind had been through here. I cleared my plate, Mum. That's a start. It’s… substantial. I’ll tackle the living room, love. You get the kitchen? Bit mad about Hitler tonight, weren’t you, Liam? He was just really interesting! In a…historical sort of way. Interesting? Liam, you were practically giving him a pep talk during history! Don't get me wrong, it’s important to learn about him, but…romantising him isn't exactly the message we want to be sending, is it? He was just, like, a product of his time, Mum. It's just facts, not endorsement. Facts, yes. But  understanding  the context, and critically analysing it, is more than just reciting dates. Honestly, boys. Want to talk about something a bit more…pleasant? Like, did you see that Federer’s back practicing? Federer? Really, Helen? After all that debate about historical dictators? He's the answer? I did see, though. Seems a bit late for a comeback, doesn't it? Nah, he’ll be alright. Still got the touch, apparently. I saw some videos on Instagram. Instagram. Speaking of, did Sarah send you that pic from the tennis match, Finn? Yeah, she did. It’s… pretty good. Sarah? Your girlfriend, Finn? She sounds lovely. You’re being very quiet about her, aren’t you? What does she think of your fascination with history and dictators? She thinks it’s a bit…intense. But she's cool with it. She likes tennis though. That’s why she sent me the picture. So, she appreciates a good serve? Dad! You're embarrassing him! Typical. Leave him alone, Mark. Actually, Finn, it's good you have someone who's not afraid to gently point out when you might be getting carried away. It's healthy. And speaking of healthy, maybe a bit less time on Instagram, eh? Liam, are you even listening? Yeah, yeah. Clear up, tennis, Hitler’s opinions on facial hair. Got it. Facial hair? Liam, where did  that  come from? Well, he had a mustache. It’s relevant! Sort of highlights his…power persona. Right. Okay. That's enough historical analysis for one evening. Mark, can you grab the hoover? And boys, let's try to leave the house looking like we actually live here. Finn, tell me about Sarah - what does she like to do when she's  not  at tennis matches?

Oh, this is lovely, isn't it? Proper countryside now. Reminds me of when I were a girl, running about in fields like that. Not much left these days, is there? Aye, it is nice. Though I’m still trying to picture our new sofa fitting in the living room. It's huge, Mum! Honestly, the pictures online didn't do it justice. It'll be fine, Auntie Carol. Think of all the comfy evenings you'll have! And you can finally have a proper movie night without everyone squished on the floor. That’s true, love. But getting rid of the old one… that's the chore. I was thinking we could take it to the tip on Saturday. Fancy a trip, El? Saturday? Yeah, sure. Though, honestly, the tip is such a nightmare. That long queue… Remember last time we went, Auntie Carol? With that bloke arguing about his mattress? Don’t remind me! Such a kerfuffle. And didn’t ANON’s friend, Sarah, mention she’s struggling to find somewhere to store her stuff since they bought that new extension? They’ve got the whole family crammed in, apparently. Sarah and her lot. Poor love. It’s awful, isn’t it? Having all that family living on top of each other. Speaking of which, did you hear about what happened at the Beaver Scout Christmas party? Apparently, little Toby nearly knocked over the tree trying to grab for the sweets. Honestly, these youngsters! Keeps you on your toes, doesn't it? It’s a wonder they don't all learn to swear before they’re five. I used to have a right cheek from a lad at work, bless 'im. Said a word I wouldn't repeat in polite company! Oh, Auntie Carol! You shouldn't. But I understand – university’s full of it, you know? Absolute constant stream of expletives. Sometimes you just have to tune it out. Back in my day, you’d get a right telling off for swearing. My grandma... Oh, she was strict! Wouldn't tolerate it. Speaking of grandmas, remember your Grandma Betty? Always used to knit us those awful jumpers. Bright orange and green, garish as anything. Don’t! They were the bane of my life. Still got one tucked away somewhere, I think. A relic of a bygone era! We were so lucky to have her, though. She did her best.

Honestly, Mum, I'm feeling utterly drained. This whole redundancy thing at work is… a lot. Oh, love, I'm so sorry to hear you're still feeling down about it. It  is  a nasty shock, isn’t it? But chin up, pet. You’re a clever girl, a Project Co-ordinator! You’ll find something else brilliant, you will. Don’t you worry your pretty little head. Easy for you to say, you’ve got your lovely, steady job at the school. Managing exams – sounds terribly stressful, by the way. Stressful, yes, but it's  mine . And it's not all bad. The kids are alright, mostly. Say, did I tell you young Thomas from Year 11 got the grades he needed for uni? Proper chuffed he was. Anyway, don't dwell on my job, focus on  you . Have you started sending out applications properly? I've had a look, but it's just… overwhelming. All these job descriptions asking for experience I don't technically have. And the competition! It feels like everyone and their dog is looking for work. I need a proper lie-down and a vat of chocolate. Now, now, no vats of chocolate. You’ll undo all your hard work at the gym! Are you still going regularly? It did you the world of good last summer, didn’t it? All that stress relief, pumping those weights. I am, yeah. Three times a week. It's the only thing keeping me sane. Although, I nearly pulled a muscle the other day trying to do a new exercise. You know how Grandad always said I was too ambitious? He’d be having a good chuckle. Oh, your Grandad. Bless him. He was a character, wasn’t he? Always pushing you to be your best. He’d want you to get back on your feet and shining, love. Speaking of Grandad, I made his apple crumble recipe yesterday. I think I’ve finally perfected it! Really? Oh, please can I have some? I'm living on instant noodles and anxiety at the moment. Of course, love! I brought some over. We’ll have it with a cuppa when we get back. What about the weekend? Any plans? Sophie's birthday is next Saturday, remember? I completely forgot! Oh, crikey. Need to book something. So sorry! Don't you fret. I already rang around. Got a table at that Italian place you like, Bella Italia.

This is a bit… mushy, Mum. And I’m not really hungry anyway. Well, you ate half a shepherd’s pie yesterday, didn’t you? It’s good food, love. And you need your strength for the summer holidays. We need to figure out what we’re going to  do  with you for six whole weeks. I was thinking… could I maybe go to Liam’s? He’s got that new game, ‘Galactic Gladiators’ and he’s been begging me to come round and play. Liam, right. And his mum lets you play for hours? Last time you were there, you came home complaining about how noisy it was and that his little sister kept pinching your controllers. She’s older now, I think. And it's only for a few hours, Mum. Please? We’ll see. We’ve got a lot to fill in. Mick needs constant attention, you know. I can’t just leave him to run wild. And honestly, sometimes I’m completely lost with what he’s trying to say. He was going on about... “Doodly-boop Mick!” earlier. What does  that  even mean? Sounds like Mick-speak. He probably just wants to watch  Stick with Mick  again. He’s obsessed! Obsessed is an understatement! We've watched every episode at least five times. It's stuck in my head all day. I was trying to explain it to Mrs. O’Malley down the shops the other day, and she just gave me a confused look. “Doodly-boop,” she asked. "What's that all about?" You were trying to explain  Stick with Mick  to Mrs. O'Malley? Don’t laugh! It’s difficult! Anyway, we need plans. Liam’s games are fine, but it’s not constant entertainment. I thought maybe we could try out that Japanese class at the community centre? You’ve always said you wanted to learn. Japanese? Really? Where did that come from? I saw a flyer. It’s only a few mornings a week. And, well, it would give me a bit of a break to sort things out with Mick. Plus, I've been trying to remember a few phrases... "Konnichiwa." That's hello, right? I can never pronounce it properly.  Konnichiwa . Yeah, that’s it. Sounds cool. But afternoons are better, I reckon. More time to play. Alright, alright. What about guitar practice? You haven't touched it in ages. You could learn some proper songs instead of just messing around.

Right, so they've actually expanded the Citibike scheme down to Otterspool now. Can you believe it? I could cycle down there and get a pasty. A pasty? Seriously, Finn? That’s your big plan for a Saturday night? Trading a perfectly good film for a… pasty? Don't knock a good pasty, Liam! It’s practically a Merseyside institution. And it's not  just  a pasty. It's a cycle, a riverside stroll, maybe even a sneaky look at the docks. A whole experience, innit? An experience involving pastry and questionable fillings, you mean. This film’s brilliant, though. The writing's sharp, reminds me a bit of… Christ, what was that book I was reading last month? The one about the librarian with the falcon? Was it…  The Falcon's Ledger ? By that bloke, Ellis? I lent it to me mum, she loved it. Said it was proper clever, all them twists and turns. That’s it! You remember! Honestly, you absorb everything. Speaking of things I'm absorbing, I have a dentist appointment on Monday. Proper dreading it, to be honest. Oh, aye. The dentist. Absolute nightmare. I went last month, they said I needed a filling. Nearly choked on me own saliva, I did. You’re proper brave going though, especially with your… sensitivity, yeah? Sensitivity is putting it mildly. I practically require anaesthetic just to look at a toothbrush. You and me need a holiday, mate. Somewhere tropical, where the only dental concern is avoiding sunburn. Now you’re talking! I've been looking at flights to Greece. Think we could do a week on Santorini? All whitewashed buildings and blue domes. Paradise, innit? Paradise sounds lovely. As long as it doesn’t involve any drilling. Right, back to the film. What did you think of that bit just now? The bit with the ridiculous hat? The hat was brilliant! Proper daft. Reminds me of that gig we went to last year, with that band that wore matching inflatable costumes. It was mental. Remember the crowd going wild? How could I forget? I think I lost me voice that night. Shoulda known better than to try and shout over a room full of inflatable llamas. You were belting out the lyrics, though. Proper enthusiastic. You always go all-in, don’t you? That’s why I like you. Shut up. You're laying it on a bit thick there.

So, tell me properly, love. How was the first term really? You’ve been so busy you’ve barely had time to breathe, haven’t you? Honestly, Mum, it was… a lot. But good! Really good. The kids are brilliant, mostly. Little Leo kept trying to eat glue for the first week, which was a new experience. And Maisie’s a tiny whirlwind of glitter and enthusiasm. Sounds lively! Glue-eating, eh? Good job you’re there to stop him. I remember when Tom used to put worms in his shoes. The little rascal. Still, a whirlwind sounds much more manageable than worms in footwear. It is, mostly! The paperwork is what's killing me. Lesson plans, assessments, meetings…it never ends. Mrs. Davies – the head – is lovely, but she certainly keeps us on our toes. She wants everyone to be doing the ‘Mindful Monday’ activities. ‘Mindful Monday’? What's that then? Sounds a bit… trendy. It is! Basically, starting the week with guided meditation and breathing exercises for the class. It’s supposed to help them focus. I’ve been trying it myself, actually. Helps me too, after dealing with Leo and the glue. Fancy that. Meditation. Your grandfather would have had a fit! "Waste of time," he'd have said. Still, if it benefits the children… It's a different world now, isn't it? Thinking about holidays…Have you started looking into somewhere for Easter? That’s what I wanted to talk to you about actually. I was thinking… instead of another caravan in Skegness - remember those? - maybe we could do something a bit different this year. I found a lovely cottage in Cornwall. Just a week, but right on the coast. Cornwall? Oh, that sounds wonderful! Bit of sunshine, a proper beach… That's a lovely idea, love. How much are we looking at? I got some quotes. It’s a little pricier than Skegness, obviously. But I can cover a good chunk of it. Grandma has offered to chip in too. That's lovely of her. And wise! A bit of Cornish air would do us all good. We haven't had a decent proper holiday in ages. Though, Cornwall… Christening prep will be intense. I'm already dreading the baking. Oh yes, the cakes! Aunt Carol’s already promised to bring  her  lemon drizzle. Remember last time? It was basically solidified sugar. Don’t remind me.

Honestly, Anon has such good taste. Everything’s so calming. It's a world away from the chaos of my classroom! How’s everything with you, Maureen? It feels like ages since we properly chatted. It does, doesn't it, Chloe? Life, eh? It rushes by. I'm alright, thank you. A bit tired, to be honest. The end of term is always a killer, you know? Year 11s. Bless them, but… intense. How's the language teaching going? Still in Surrey? Still in Surrey, yep. The kids are lovely, genuinely. It’s the paperwork that’s the bane of my existence. Endless reports, schemes of work adjustments, meetings… you wouldn’t believe. Though I did introduce them to some really cool online games this term to help with vocabulary. They absolutely loved it! Oh, that's brilliant. Technology’s a lifesaver, isn’t it? I’ve been trying to incorporate more of it into my lessons too, though half the time, the projector decides it doesn’t want to work. You know what it's like! But tell me, are you seeing a lot of students struggling with grammar these days? It feels like they just...avoid it. Oh, absolutely! It's a recurring theme. They're so focused on fluency, which is important, of course, but neglecting the foundations. I'm trying to make grammar fun, using memes and silly scenarios, but it’s a constant battle. It's tempting to just let them get on with it and hope they pick things up. I had one student last week who genuinely thought 'their' was the same as 'there'! Oh, goodness. You hear the most things. My niece, Lucy, she's doing A-Levels now, and she’s the same. She's brilliant at essay writing, but she can’t tell you the difference between a verb and a noun! Speaking of family, how's your mum doing? Last I heard, she was trying to learn yoga. She's doing brilliantly! Yoga’s gone down a storm actually. She’s even convinced Dad to join her. He looks like a startled flamingo trying to do a downward dog, but he's giving it a go! Which is more than I can say for my attempts at anything sporty. Honestly, I'm happiest curled up with a book and a cup of tea. Have you seen that new cream blush from NARS?

Honestly, this spread is astonishing, ANON. You've really outdone yourself. It's… a feast! Feels more lavish than some Seders I've been to. Yeah, ANON's been prepping for weeks, haven't they? It's mad, innit? I’ve already had two helpings of charoset, and I'm not even sorry. Don't you start, Leo! You’ll scare everyone off. It  has  been a bit of work, yes. But it’s lovely to see everyone here, enjoying it. Dad, have you tried the matzah ball soup yet? I tried a new recipe this year, a little lighter… It's brilliant, actually! Really good. I was just saying to ANON that I’m craving babka something fierce. You make a mean one, ANON. Wish I had your patience for baking. Speaking of patience, I was just reading an article about the Ortolan. Apparently, it’s making a comeback in some circles in Italy – albeit illegally. The whole tradition of eating it with your eyes covered... it's ghastly, really. And so wasteful. Ghastly is putting it mildly, Penelope. Honestly, the lengths some people go to for culinary… experiences. My gran used to tell stories about her aunt, who emigrated from Poland to New York, and how she'd never eat anything remotely similar. Too much history, too much sadness attached. New York, huh? I’ve always wanted to go. Proper adventure, wouldn't it be? Maybe next year, after graduation? Definitely. We should plan it. I've got a few contacts over there, in the engineering world, could be good for networking too. Though, to be honest, I’m mostly going for the bagels. Seriously, are London bagels even remotely comparable? They are not, darling. They’re… a pale imitation. But let's be honest, this Seder highlights the strength of our traditions, doesn't it? Even when we’re scattered around the world, we maintain these rituals. My grandfather used to try and teach me Hebrew phrases - mostly nonsense, I’m afraid. Like, “Ha’Shanah tovah u’metukah!” which apparently is wishing you a sweet new year. My mum keeps trying to get me fluent. I can read a bit, enough to understand some of the prayers, but speaking? That’s a whole other level. I was thinking, after Passover, maybe we could all go to Paris? A little break, some culture... Paris! Sounds brilliant. Anyone fancy wandering around Montmartre?

Honestly, this discussion about eBooks versus physical books is getting  incredibly  heated, isn’t it? I thought book club was supposed to be relaxing! Oh, you know how they get. Margaret’s absolutely convinced the future is all digital, and Beatrice is practically throwing historical novels at her. Typical. Didn't expect it to get  quite  this intense though. It’s just a book, love. It’s more than just a book to some people, isn’t it? The smell, the feel of the paper… I get it. I've read a fair few eBooks myself, though – mostly for travel, you see. Less to lug around! Exactly! That’s the practical side I was trying to point out. I do love a beautiful hardback, don’t get me wrong. I've got a first edition of "Pride and Prejudice" that’s practically a family heirloom. But for a lighter read, something I'm not necessarily going to treasure forever, an eBook is brilliant. You're right, you are. But Margaret was going on about battery life and eye strain! Honestly, you’d think she’d designed the things herself. I told her, “Just get a decent lamp, dear, and charge your tablet!” Didn't go down well. She can be a bit… intense. Did anyone mention "Lessons in Chemistry"? I finally finished it last week. Absolutely wonderful. I was completely hooked. Oh, I've heard such good things! It's on my to-read list. So many books, so little time. Speaking of reading, how's that crochet project coming along, Lucy? Last time we spoke, you were embarking on a complicated blanket. It’s… progressing. Slowly. I’ve learned that intricate patterns require a  lot  of concentration. I'm about halfway through. It's going to be a massive, slightly wonky, but very homemade blanket for my niece. She’s just turned one. Wonky is charming! My niece, Maisie, is into knitting now. Can you believe it? She's six and she's got a pair of needles bigger than her fingers. Making scarves for everyone! Very cute, but a total yarn explosion in the house. Keeps her out of mischief, mind. That’s lovely. My nephew is obsessed with superheroes at the moment. All he wants to do is dress up and pretend to fly. We’re planning a superhero-themed film night next weekend – any good recommendations beyond the usual Marvel/DC stuff?

Right, this is ridiculous. Seriously, who designs this stuff? It’s like they  want  you to break your nails. Aye, lass, bit fiddly, innit? They’ve gotten a right laugh at us for these tiny tools. Here, lemme give it a go. See? Just needs a bit o’ pressure. You were wrestling with it like you were opening a safe. I was! I nearly dropped it in my pint. Imagine that - expensive new phone, swimming in lager. Not a good look, is it? Is yours all sorted then, Dr. Schmidt? Fancy getting your Nokia out so quickly. Well, I’ve had a bit of practice. Been a loyal Nokia man, you know. Always reliable. And “Dr. Schmidt” will do, but just Karl is fine, love. This one’s a beauty too. Classic, dependable. Reminds me of the ones I used to have back in Germany, before all these… complicated smartphones came along. What about yours? You’ve been quiet about your new iPhone. It’s…a lot. Honestly, after dealing with that SIM tray, I’m slightly terrified. It’s beautiful, dazzling even, but there's so much on it. I'm thinking about setting it up completely fresh, no connecting to my old accounts, just a blank slate. Less data for them to potentially…you know…hoover up. Sensible thinking, lass. Privacy's getting rarer by the day. But it’ll be a right faff, won't it? All the passwords, the settings… It’s not like these things just ‘work’ out of the box, is it? Remember that disaster with your grandma’s tablet? Don't remind me. Three hours I spent trying to explain how to turn the brightness up. It was like talking to a brick wall. Okay, okay, fresh start maybe  is  too drastic. I'm thinking I'll just transfer the essentials. Photos, contacts… but I'm no rushing to download every single app. Good plan. Let me have a look. What's your data plan like over here? Are you getting much signal? Nokia’s usually pretty good at picking up a signal, even in the wilderness. Remember that trip to the Lake District? Your phone was useless, but mine found a bar somewhere. I'll never let you forget that. This plan is supposed to be unlimited data, but I’m skeptical. I haven’t tried it properly yet. And the settings! So many options.

Ugh, this is a minefield! Right, so, about Finn's party… do we still think a Red Panda theme is good? He’s  obsessed  with them. A Red Panda theme is brilliant, love! Absolutely brilliant. Finn will adore it. Though, it might be tricky to get actual Red Pandas, wouldn’t it? Little Finn here seems more interested in knocking down my tower, though. Isn’t that right, love? Tee-hee! Boom! He’s a natural demolition expert. Anyway, decorations-wise, I was thinking a lot of red and orange. Maybe even some bamboo cutouts? And we could make little Red Panda masks. Oh, that’s lovely! Masks are a brilliant idea. Much better than another bouncy castle. Remember last year? He was bouncing for England! Honestly, I was knackered for a week afterwards. Do you think we should invite Emily and Liam? They’re always up for a game of something. Definitely Emily and Liam. Emily loves animals, she's got that fluffy Malamooche, remember? Buster? He's massive! But I think we should keep the guest list fairly small this year - just close friends. Sensible idea. It's much easier to manage. Little Finn is at his limit with too many people running around. He gets overwhelmed. Remember when we tried to take him to that pet shop in town? He wouldn’t let go of that little hamster! I remember! He was completely captivated. Speaking of pets, do you think I should get a cat? I’ve been thinking about it. Something small, fluffy… A cat? Oh, that’s sweet. Finn would love that! But are you sure you have the time? Remember how much cleaning up you had to do last time you were round playing board games?! Yeah, but I’m getting better at it. Besides, a cat would be good company when I’m doing homework. And they're quiet, right? Unlike some people I know. Cheeky! They’re not  always  quiet, darling. Some cats are little devils! Though, a little bit of feline mischief could be nice. What sort of cat were you thinking? I saw a picture of one online – it was like, a grey tabby with really big eyes. So cute. Have you ever seen a Japanese film? My teacher showed us one in class the other day, it was amazing. All moody and artistic. Japanese films? Oh, I don’t really watch them, love.

Right, so, Christmas in the Philippines… Liam, you’ve been going for ages now, haven't you? It must be something else. Like, really different from Barrow. Aye, it is, Maisie. Totally different. It's, like, the longest Christmas season in the world, practically! Starts way before December, with 'parol' decorations everywhere – those star lanterns. And it goes on until the Feast of the Epiphany, early January. My goodness! That’s quite something. Christmas should have a nice, tidy beginning and end, shouldn't it? We used to have carols sung on Christmas Eve, just outside the church. Lovely, crisp air. Bath always got a frost in December. Frost! Likely did. Bognor, on the other hand, was usually damp and drizzly. Though, Christmas was always proper festive. Mum would insist on a plum pudding, even though nobody really  wanted  it. Said it was tradition. So, Liam, what's the food like? Is it all… rice and… things? I’m trying to imagine it. Barrow Christmases are all about roast beef, Yorkshire puddings, and mountains of potatoes. And that plum pudding. Don’t get me started on the plum pudding. Well, there's rice, yeah, it's a staple. But Christmas is all about  Noche Buena  – the Christmas Eve feast. Lechon, that's roasted pig, is the star. And  Pancit , noodles. And  Bibingka  and  Puto Bumbong  - steamed rice cakes, sometimes with cheese or salted egg. Really sweet and savory. It's brilliant. Loads of family around, everyone laughing… it's loud, chaotic, but so much fun. Roasted pig! Heavens. That does sound… extravagant. Though my sister used to make a goose. Always smelled wonderful. Used to be a proper butcher’s shop in Bath then, you know. Not like these supermarkets now. Supermarkets! Don't even get me started. The quality’s gone down, you know. And the service… I remember when a butcher knew your name and your preferred cut. Same with the baker. Real community feel. That’s what’s missing, isn't it? Up in Barrow, we still have Mrs. Henderson’s bakery, on Park Street. She makes the  best  Eccles cakes you’ve ever tasted. Proper, old-fashioned. My grandma used to buy them every Christmas Eve. Eccles cakes! I've heard of them. Are they like, pastry and jam? Sounds delicious. My grandma, Lola, always made these tiny cookies called  Barquillos . They’re rolled-up, crispy things.

Honestly, this transcription is driving me mad. It’s a series of interviews with…well, let's just say very opinionated pigeon fanciers. Page after page of cooing and complaints about their rivals' breeding methods. Pigeon fanciers? Right, that's a niche. Sounds…thrilling. At least it’s not the council meeting minutes I had to wade through last week. Those were pure torture. Had Brenda from accounts go on a twenty-minute tangent about the font size on the meeting agenda. Font size? Brenda is a menace. I swear she actively seeks out the most frustrating elements of bureaucracy. But at least you’re getting paid to listen to pigeons, darling. I've been battling writer's block all week. Staring at a blank screen is remarkably depressing. Well, the money’s not great, but it keeps me busy. It's just the sheer  volume  of it. I'm thinking I need a serious Kindle investment. Less paper clutter. Oh, you should definitely get one. I’m glued to mine. Have you read anything good lately? I just finished that new Harlan Coben. "Run Away." Absolutely brilliant, kept me guessing until the very end. Proper detective stuff. Reminded me of the ‘Line of Duty’ finale, that twist! 'Line of Duty' was masterful. Though I must confess, I had to Google some of the police jargon. All those acronyms! Detective shows are my guilty pleasure, though. Nothing beats a good whodunit with a complicated plot. What are you reading now, David? I'm halfway through something a bit lighter, actually. A humorous account of a cruise ship disaster. Don't worry, it's not too grim. Just absurd and entertaining. Trying to cleanse the palate after all the Coben intensity. Cruises are terrifying. Far too many people in one place. I’d rather face a thousand pigeon fanciers than a buffet line. Though, speaking of food… these biscuits are lovely, Margaret. Did you make them? Yes, just a simple ginger biscuit recipe. Needed something to get me focused. The publisher’s breathing down my neck about the new book. They want it finished by the end of next month. It's daunting. End of next month? That’s not long at all! You’ll smash it, Margaret. You always do. What's it about, anyway? Still the historical fiction angle? Yes, this one's set during the Victorian era, with a fascinating, albeit slightly obscure, female botanist at its heart.

Blimey, this drizzle’s set in proper. Thought we’d have a bit of sunshine today, didn't we? Reminds me of that summer back in '68… now  that  was a summer. Remember '68, Elsie? Vaguely, Arthur. I was still at school. All those protests… it was all a bit of a whirlwind. More interested in boys and getting my A-Levels, truth be told. Did Colin ever call you back about that little job he mentioned? Colin? No, not a peep. Said he’d have a look at me CV, he did. Not that I 'ad much in the way of a CV, mind you. A few odd jobs over the years, nothin' serious. Always a bit hard, findin' work, wasn't it? Hard for everyone, Arthur. But you can't just sit around waiting for things to fall into your lap. I’ve been thinking… have you considered volunteering somewhere? The community centre is always looking for help with the gardening, and they need someone to sort the donations at the charity shop. Volunteering? Good heavens, Rupert. That sounds like... labour. Proper hard labour, probably. And I'm not exactly spring chicken anymore, am I? My back’s playing up something awful these days. Arthur, don’t be like that. It’s not all strenuous. And think of the company, dear. You'd be out and about, meeting people. It'd be good for you, honestly. You do get a bit… withdrawn sometimes. Withdrawin’? I’m perfectly content, thank you very much. Settled in me chair, got me telly, and a nice cuppa. What more could a man want? A bit of purpose, Arthur. A chance to contribute. Think about it. The community centre could really use an extra pair of hands. They're struggling to keep up with the demand. They even have a little allotment now, I hear. You always did have a knack for growing tomatoes. Remember those whoppers you used to produce back in Costessey? Aye, I did. Those were good tomatoes. Best in Norfolk, some would say.
