But that’s a long time ago, Rupert. Things change. And sometimes, Arthur, new things can be surprisingly nice. It wouldn't be like going back to work. It'd be… different. And it's something to do. You wouldn’t be stuck staring at the walls all day. I don’t know, Elsie… I don’t know.

Right, so the venue's confirmed, then? The Wrestlers’ Arms? I know it's a bit…rustic, but it's got charm, innit? And they do a decent pint.      Officially booked. I managed to haggle them down a bit on the room hire – you’re a star, Sarah! Seems a really good price considering how central it is. Sorted the DJ too, he specialises in 80s and 90s, as requested.      Excellent news, both of you. Just…are we sure about The Wrestlers’ Arms? It's got a bit of a reputation, doesn't it? I remember hearing tales…      Oh, come on, Maisie! Don't be daft. It's fine. A few lads having a celebratory pint after a footie match, nothing more. We'll keep an eye out, obviously, but don't you worry your pretty little head about it. Besides, it’s a Friday night; everywhere will be lively.      Lively is an understatement in Cambridge on a Friday! What’s all the buzz about? Sounds celebratory!      ELT Christmas do, Emily! We finalising details. Wrestlers’ Arms booked, DJ sorted. Sarah’s doing a cracking job.      Fantastic! Wonderful to hear. I'll need to add it to my calendar. Though, Wrestlers’ Arms…that rings a slight bell. Not exactly the most sophisticated establishment, is it?      Sophistication isn’t exactly what we were going for, is it? We wanted somewhere a bit more…relaxed. Somewhere everyone could feel comfortable.      I just…well, there was that incident with the pigeon last year. Apparently, someone let it in the bar, and it flew around in a panic.      Oh, that was Dave from Accounts! He thought he was being helpful. Honestly, some people! It was a right laugh, though, watching him chase it around with a napkin.      A pigeon chase! That does sound memorable. Though, hopefully, we won't have  any  wildlife on the premises this year. Speaking of which… I just rescued a bumblebee from my office window. Poor thing was trapped. I managed to coax it out with a bit of sugar water.      Oh, you’re an angel, Emily! Those little guys are so important.      Absolutely. We should probably put up some bee-friendly flowers around the Press, actually. Encourage pollinators. It'd be good for research, too - to monitor bee populations.      That’s a brilliant idea, Maisie! I'll flag it to the Estates team. Anything we can do to support biodiversity. Back to the party, though – do we need to organise any catering beyond the bar snacks?

Ugh, I'm absolutely  drained . Honestly, this week at school has been... a lot. Tell me about it. What's been so bad? Mr. Davies' history test? Because I swear, that was designed to fail people. Mr. Davies was bad, yeah, worse than usual. But it's not just that. It's... everything. Mrs. Peterson keeps giving us loads of practice questions in English, and they're all just  so  complicated. Like, she’s trying to trick us! And then there's the science project. Oh gosh, the volcanoes. Don’t even get me started. Mine keeps collapsing! I've used so much cardboard and glue, I'm starting to smell like a craft shop. Exactly! Mine is, like, actively  rejecting  the lava. It just dribbles down the side instead of erupting properly. My dad tried to help, bless him, but he mostly got glue on himself. It was a whole thing. Oh my god, your dad! He's terrible at DIY. Mine just offered moral support and snacks. Much safer. Have you even started your presentation for it? Started? I've got, like, three bullet points. I’m supposed to talk about plate tectonics and how the build-up of pressure… I just… I zone out. It's all just facts and figures. There's no  story ! I get that feeling. I'm trying to make mine a bit more engaging, you know? I thought I’d pretend I'm a volcanologist, reporting live from Pompeii. Dramatic, right? That’s actually brilliant! Way better than just listing facts. Maybe I could do something like that too… pretend I’m a geologist discovering a new volcano? See? Much more fun. What about Maths? Anything happening there? I'm still struggling with those simultaneous equations. Oh, Maths is… consistent. Consistently awful. Miss Harding keeps saying we need to “visualise” them, but I feel like I need a whole new brain to do that. I think she gets a kick out of watching us struggle. Seriously! It’s like she  wants  us to fail. I asked her for extra help after class the other day, and she just said, “Have you tried doing the homework?” Like, yeah, obviously! I wouldn't be asking for help if I  had  understood it. Exactly! It’s the classic teacher response. They just expect you to magically get it. You know, I was thinking… maybe we should actually  study  together?

Right then. That was lovely, wasn’t it? Best Indian I’ve had in ages. Though, honestly, I could still manage a bit of that mango kulfi… I'm stuffed, Mum! Absolutely stuffed. But yes, it was amazing. That garlic naan was exceptional. I think I ate half of it myself. You always were a fan of the garlic naan, Liv. Don't look at me like that. I ate well too! Just not quite as… enthusiastically. You are a growing lad, Thomas. Need your strength for that project, eh? How’s it going, anyway? Still wrestling with those spreadsheets? It's… a process. The client keeps changing their mind about what they want. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m herding cats. They wanted a blue theme last week, now it's suddenly got to be ‘earth tones and natural.’ It’s exhausting! That sounds incredibly frustrating. Reminds me of the grant applications I had to deal with back at uni. Endlessly refining, chasing up paperwork… it’s a special kind of soul-crushing. Tell me about it. Remember when I was trying to sell those garden gnomes at the market? One lady would say ‘Oh, the blue one is lovely!’ and the next would say ‘No, no, the red one suits my roses better!’ It never ends. You need a thick skin in sales, darlings. A really thick skin. I think I'm developing one now, Mum. It feels like I’m constantly firefighting. I had a meeting with the Head of Marketing today - she wasn't exactly thrilled with the progress, let’s put it that way. Oh no, really? What did she say specifically? Pretty standard stuff, I suppose. “Need to see more momentum,” “falling behind schedule," all the usual phrases. I tried to explain the client changes, but… you know how it is. They just want results. They always do. Don't let it get you down, love. You're a good lad, and you work hard. Just remember to breathe and take things one step at a time. And tell her you've got things under control! Project manage her! Exactly! Assert yourself, Tom. Be the boss. Easier said than done, when the ‘boss’ is the Head of Marketing! Still, you’re right, Mum. I need to stop stressing and just focus on getting the task at hand finished, one change request at a time.

Honestly, Sarah, it’s been a week. Absolute chaos. Tell me about it, love. Sounds like you need a strong cup of tea, then. So, what's gone mad then? Work, I’m guessing? Your face is tighter than usual. Work is… demanding. We’re pushing for this massive deal with OmniCorp, and the pressure is immense. It's all-nighters and constant meetings. But it’s not just that. It’s everything. Mia’s been getting into trouble at school. Oh, no! What’s she done now? Detention again? She’s always been a bit of a whirlwind, that one. Remember when she painted Mr. Henderson’s car bright pink? Don't remind me. This is slightly more serious. Apparently, there was an incident in the playground - a little pushing, a few names called… and now she's got a written warning and a meeting with the Head next week. Honestly, sixth form and already playing at being a rebel. Teenagers, eh? They think they know everything. It’s a phase. Just keep talking to her, you know? Trying to understand why she's acting out. Is it something to do with the others? That’s what I’m trying to figure out. She’s being so secretive. And then there's everything else. My mum's appointments are dragging on, you know? The oncologist still isn't giving definitive answers. It’s that limbo again. The scans showed… things. They’re just running more tests. Oh, love. That’s awful. I'm so sorry. You need to take care of yourself, you really do. You can’t keep burning the candle at both ends. Stress won’t help either of you. Are you sleeping? Sporadically, at best. I've been thinking about… maybe bringing in some help with the house? Just a few hours a week, to take some of the load off. You’re always so wonderfully efficient when you’re here, I was thinking... Don't be silly, love. You're working hard enough as it is. Besides, I’ve got Mrs. Peterson’s place now, and I'm not short on work. It’s a good thing for me, honestly. So, don’t worry about that. Tell me something a bit lighter, then! Did Liam finally sort out that leaky roof? Surprisingly, yes! He’s been with the building society, trying to get a loan for the repairs.

Right, I need a break. My brain’s 'ardened, proper hardened, it ‘as. Honestly, trying to understand this marketing theory… it’s like trying to herd cats. Dramatic much, Liv? You’re only on chapter three. And it  is  a bit dense, I’ll grant you that. What’s got you so riled up this time? It’s just…everything! I’m working shifts down at The Velvet Curtain, and Mrs. Higgins is on me like a ‘awk about everything. "Liv, are you polishing the brass properly? Liv, are you smiling enough? Liv, are you  genuinely  interested in Mr. Peterson's stamp collection?" I swear, that man could talk about perforated paper for three hours straight. And she expects me to act like I'm riveted! Oh, Mrs. Higgins. She’s a classic. My grandma’s a bit like that, always wanting everything done  just so . But you’ve dealt with tougher customers than Mr. Peterson, surely? You’re a Hull bartender, you’ve seen things. True, true. I’ve definitely mopped up more spilled drinks and defused more arguments than I care to remember. But it's the sheer relentless  observance . She’s constantly over my shoulder. It’s draining, especially when I’m trying to save up for, you know, everything. Rent, books... maybe a proper weekend off someday. I completely get that. University’s expensive enough without working to top it up as well. What are you saving for specifically, then? A holiday? Aye, a holiday would be reet. Somewhere warm, proper sandy. Somewhere I don't have to listen to Mr. Peterson wax lyrical about rare cancels. But mostly, just…a deposit for a flat. Somewhere that isn't my Auntie Brenda’s spare room. It's lovely of her, but…you know. Absolutely. Freedom! I’m just trying to avoid accruing a mountain of debt right now. I work a few hours a week at the campus coffee shop. It's not glamorous, mostly just making lattes for stressed-out students, but it pays the bills and gets me out of the house. A campus coffee shop…sounds almost relaxing compared to The Velvet Curtain. Though, I suppose you get your own share of demanding customers. Oh, you have no idea. You wouldn’t believe the arguments people have over oat milk. Seriously,  oat milk . And the complicated orders! "Extra hot, half-sweet, caramel macchiato with a sprinkle of cinnamon and a pump of vanilla – but not  too  much vanilla."

Right, so, anyone else completely burnt out after that freshers' week rush? I swear, I'm still seeing exclamation marks in my sleep. Tell me about it! Felt like I was constantly reshelving the same five books over and over. I'm dreaming of a beach, honestly. A quiet beach. No students. You're preaching to the choir, lad. Freshers’ week…it’s a trial, isn't it? Makes you long for…well, anything else. I’m desperate for a holiday. Thinking of heading back to Halifax, see me mum. A bit of peace and quiet up there does wonders. Halifax, is it? Lovely place, I’m sure. I was just thinking about a wee trip back to County Down, myself. Been far too long. The coast there…breathtaking, it is. County Down, that sounds fantastic! I've always wanted to see the Giant’s Causeway. I’m aiming for Cornwall this year, though. Bit closer to home, you know? My wife’s been nagging me about it for months. Something about cream teas and coastal walks. Can't argue with cream teas, can you? Absolutely not! Cornwall sounds lovely. I’m leaning towards somewhere a bit more…exotic, even if that just means somewhere with warmer weather. I was looking at Portugal, actually. Lisbon seems pretty lively. Portugal, aye? Good choice. I went to Algarve years ago. Stunning beaches, lovely food. Though, I nearly got swindled by a fella selling fake watches on the promenade! Learned my lesson there – stick to the supermarket for souvenirs. Ah, the perils of holiday shopping! I remember once, in Dublin, I bought a scarf that was advertised as 'pure Irish wool.' Turned out it was mostly acrylic! Still got it, though. Sentimental value, you know. Though, I'd rather spend my money on a good bit of seafood. See, that’s what I’m talking about! Good food is crucial to a holiday experience. My wife is already planning menus for Cornwall. Apparently, we  have  to try a pasty. Says they're a religious experience. A pasty? Right, well, I’ll add that to the list. Though, honestly, I’m happy with a simple sandwich and a view. Speaking of views, have you seen the sunsets from the library windows lately? Quite spectacular, really. They are, aren’t they? It’s a little perk of the job, that. Reminds you there’s a world beyond shelved books and overdue notices.

Oh, for goodness sake, look at that tackle! Honestly, he’s going to get booked, isn't he? He practically took out Henderson’s knees! Relax, Liv. It’s football. People get tackled. It's part of the game. And Henderson’s tough as nails, he'll be right. Besides, ref’s probably feeling generous tonight. Generous? You think Mike Dean’s feeling  generous ? He’s a legend for booking people for breathing sideways! And it was a blatant foul. See? Yellow card! I told you. You always predict the bookings, don’t you? It's a wonder you don't work for VAR. Though, knowing your luck, they'd probably find a way to blame you when something goes wrong. Cheeky git. I just have good football instincts, that's all. Seriously though, this match is gripping, innit? So much pressure on them to win tonight. Absolutely. It’s a crucial one. I’ve already spent way too much time crunching the numbers - win probability, expected goals… the usual PhD student nonsense. You've been number-crunching  football ? Seriously? Isn’t that a bit… dry? I’d rather just enjoy the drama. Did you factor in the emotional impact of the crowd? That's worth at least 0.5% in my book. I tried, believe me! But quantifying emotion is tricky business. Although, I did model for home advantage - it’s a consistent factor. Speaking of factors, feeling hungry? I was thinking about ordering some kebabs. Proper late-night grub. Kebabs? Now you're talking! Proper good ones, mind. Not those sad excuses you get from chain places. Remember that place we found in Durham, the one with the garlic sauce…  that  was a kebab. Vaguely. Durham was a while ago. I'm thinking somewhere decent here in Cambridge. There's that place on Mill Road, Istanbul Grill – they do a mean doner. Plus, you’re on a health kick, aren't you? This is your rebellion night. A rebellion night fuelled by doner meat? Sounds about right. Although, I am trying to be good. But a kebab...after a tense match...it  is  calling my name, isn't it? It’s practically shouting. Do you want lamb or chicken? And large pitta? Essential, obviously. Lamb, definitely. And yeah, large pitta, extra everything. And don’t you dare skimp on the chili sauce! Mind you, if we’re going all-out, we should get a portion of fries too.

Right then, that’s a bit strong, Grandma. You didn’t add enough milk, did you? Strong tea builds character, lad. You youngsters want everything diluted nowadays. Back in my day, you’d drink it black, and like it! Withington used to be proper for strong tea, you know. The water was different then. Mum, don’t scare him off! It's lovely, David. A little strong for me, but I’ll manage. How’s the flat looking, Mum? You've been tidying up a storm, I see. Had to! David's coming. Can't have him seeing the place looking like a midden. Though, honestly, what does a project manager know about a proper tidy? All those spreadsheets and plans... Easy, Mum. Project management is about keeping things organised, that applies to tea cups just as much as budgets, you know. Though, I must admit, battling a spreadsheet is usually less stressful than negotiating with building contractors. Speaking of stressful, how’s that big redevelopment you’re working on going, David? The one down in Manchester? It’s…a work in progress, let's put it that way. We hit a snag with the foundations. Apparently, there's a whole load of old brickworks underneath where they wanted to build. More diggin', more cost, more meetings. Brickworks! Used to know a fella who worked at a brickworks, Albert was his name. Strong lad, he was. Smelled of clay, that fella. And dust. Everywhere. Oh, do tell! What was Albert like? Did he have a family? Aye, had a wife, Elsie. Lovely woman, Elsie. They lived just off Moorside Road. He was a quiet one, Albert. But a good man. Always had a smile. He and Elsie used to come to the village fete every year. Always won the prize for the heaviest marrow. Amazing. It’s funny, isn’t it? You think about these massive projects, these modern buildings, and they’re built over the remnants of some bloke growing marrows. It is, actually. It just shows you, doesn’t it? How everything’s connected. You know, I was watching that old film, ‘Brief Encounter’ the other night. Makes you think about all the lives that have passed through a place. 'Brief Encounter'? Good choice. That's a classic. My mate, Liam, is trying to get into film editing. He's obsessed with that black and white aesthetic. Says it’s got a timeless quality.

Honestly, the school assembly this morning was a whirlwind. Mrs. Davies really went all out with the Shrove Tuesday performance. Did you see the costumes? Absolutely dreadful, but the kids loved it. Loved the hats, Mummy! The ones with the bells! 🔔 I wanted a bell hat! Why didn't I get a bell hat? Because you were being a little…distracted, darling. You were trying to build a pancake tower. Which, I must say, was impressively ambitious, but not quite conducive to hat-wearing. Now, are you two actually going to  eat  these pancakes or just admire them? I'm eating! See? . These are yummy! I don't want any more. They're too…flappy. Flappy? They’re pancakes, love. What’s too flappy about them? Reminds me of the Green Knowe stories, doesn't it? So many secrets hidden in old houses, just like the Old Keys and the Bogeyman. Tell me the Bogeyman story again! Later, sweetheart. After you've eaten a proper breakfast. Speaking of, there's a little boy in my class, Liam, he only had an apple for breakfast today. His mum’s struggling, you know. It just…it really gets to you. It makes you so grateful for what we have. Liam doesn't like pancakes? I don’t know, sweetheart. But some children don't always have the food we do. It's hard to think about while you're watching you two happily wolfing down pancakes. Can I have more syrup? Always a shift in priorities! Yes, of course. Anyway, I was thinking, maybe next weekend we could finally go to the Science Museum? You both were so disappointed last time we had to cancel. Science Museum! Yes! Dinosaurs and robots! And that volcano thing! The volcano thing. Precisely! And we could pop into Festival Hall afterwards. I saw they’re having that children’s concert with the orchestra. Might be a bit much, but…they love music. Can we go to the beach after, Mummy? Well, the beach in February might be a bit chilly, darling! We can hold that thought. First, let's focus on the current mission: getting these pancakes down your tummies. And then, brushes and hands washed before we tackle anything else! Essential for avoiding grumpy faces later. But I don’t want to brush my teeth  now ! Now, now. A sparkling smile is vital for volcanos and dinosaurs!

Honestly, this Kung Pao chicken is  chef's kiss . Best we’ve had in ages. Did you guys manage to snag all the spring rolls? Pretty sure I got the last four! Though, Liam, you ate like three as soon as it arrived, didn't you? Guilty! I was starving. Long day coordinating that supplier switch. It was a nightmare. Ms. Davies kept changing her mind about the delivery date. Seriously, the woman’s a whirlwind. Sounds stressful. At least you get paid. I’m wading through proposals for the Henderson account - it’s drier than the Sahara out here, honestly. Lots of impressive-sounding jargon, very little substance. You should send them a Bob the Builder GIF. "Can we fix it? Yes, we can!" Sometimes a little simplicity is what they need. Oh my god, brilliant, Ben! Seriously, that would be hilarious. Though, you'd probably end up explaining the structural integrity of building materials. Hey, I’m an agronomist, not a  complete  idiot. I can relate plant growth metaphors to business strategy. It’s a skill. Sure, Ben. Whatever you say. Did you see the news about the, uh, the Prince’s funeral? Pretty subdued atmosphere over there. It was on everywhere. It did feel a bit…empty, didn’t it? I mean, everyone respects him, obviously, but it's not like there's the same widespread grief as with the Queen. I think people are more…detached, somehow. Less personal connection with him, maybe? Although, my Nan was completely heartbroken - she said he reminded her of her late husband. Speaking of heartbreak, how's Chloe doing? Last I heard she was still reeling from…well, you know. She’s…better. Slowly. We took her to that new film, the sci-fi one, 'Stardust Echoes'. Actually quite good, even if it was a bit heavy for her at first. Distraction, you know? That’s good. We should all try and check in on her more. It must be awful. Gets lonely being the only one living miles away, house-sharing with everyone else. Yeah, definitely. I'll give her a ring later. Thinking about it, we should all go round for a games night next week. Something lighthearted. No proposal writing or supplier logistics allowed. Absolutely. Cricket’s on the telly then too. I could be persuaded to host. I've got that new barbeque I’ve been meaning to test out too.

You know, I was just thinking about Mrs. Higgins next door when we lived in Bristol. Remember her, Dad? The one who always had a prize-winning rose bush? Higgins, you say? Of course! Good heavens, that was a lifetime ago, wasn't it? Those roses were something else. Positively scandalous, the size of them! She’d get terribly cross if anyone even looked at them sideways. Fierce woman, your Mrs. Higgins. I do remember hearing stories about her competitive streak. Apparently, she and Mrs. Peterson had a full-blown feud over who grew the best marigolds one year! It ended up in the local paper, I think. That's right! It was ridiculous. Mum always said it was the highlight of the village fete. It felt so dramatic at the time, you know? Being a kid, everything felt like a huge event. They were a vibrant bunch, those neighbours. We didn’t have neighbours quite like that in Wolverhampton. More reserved, generally. Although, old Mr. Finch next door… he kept pigeons! Hundreds of them! Covered the whole garden. The noise... Pigeons! That's a brave choice for a garden companion. Did they cause trouble? Trouble? They were a menace! Droppings everywhere, cooing constantly. My wife, God rest her soul, was absolutely furious. She threatened to call the council, but I always managed to placate her. Pigeons were his passion. A harmless eccentricity, I suppose. Though I never did quite understand it. This is lovely, ANON! Thank you. You know, it’s funny thinking about neighbours. It feels like we connect with people so differently now. We’re all so plugged in, we lose a bit of that real, face-to-face connection. Absolutely. And the pace of life… It used to be you knew everyone on your street. Now, people move so frequently, it's hard to build those relationships. It makes you appreciate the memories, doesn't it? Like remembering Mrs. Higgins and her roses. You're right, you are. Technology... it's changed everything, hasn't it? Even driving. They’re talking about driverless cars now. Can you imagine? Letting a machine drive you around! It’s a bit terrifying, really. Although, thinking about it, it might be safer. No more road rage, hopefully. I do love driving, though. The freedom of it. But then, I don’t think I’d trust a computer with my little Fiat!

Right then, operation Chinese New Year feast is officially underway! Poppy, Leo, are you two helping with the decorations? I found some lovely red paper lanterns. Yes! I want to hang it by the window! Like a sparkly dragon's eye! Look! I drew a dragon! It’s got lots of planets! Oh, that’s brilliant, Leo! A dragon  and  planets! That’s very imaginative. Tell me, what planets does your dragon fly past? Umm… Jupiter! And… red one! And that one with the rings! Saturn! Excellent! You're a budding astronomer, you are. Poppy, how's your lantern hanging looking? Almost done! It's a bit tricky. Can I use some glitter? Lots and lots of glitter? It would make the dragon's eye  really  sparkle. Okay, okay, but just a little! We don't want to be finding glitter in the carpets for the next six months! You know, this reminds me of a story my grandma used to tell about Chinese New Year celebrations when she was a little girl in London. They used to write wishes on red paper and hang them on the lanterns… Wishes? Like… I wish for a new drum set? Exactly like that! What are you wishing for, Leo? I wish I could play really, really loud on the drums! Like a thunder dragon! I wish I was a mermaid! And I could fly on Barbie and the Great Adventure’s seahorse! Wonderful wishes! Poppy, are you still enjoying your aerial hoop classes? Mrs. Davies says you're getting so graceful. I love it! It’s like being a flying mermaid! But it’s hard sometimes. It  is  hard, darling, but you're working so well. And Leo, how are the drum lessons going? Are you keeping Mr. Henderson on his toes? I’m getting good at the beat! He says I have good rhythm. But it's noisy! Mum, can I practice now? Perhaps later, little thunder dragon. Let's finish the feast first. I'm thinking we’ll have sweet and sour chicken, egg fried rice, and maybe some spring rolls. Does that sound good? Yummy! Can we have fortune cookies too? I want to know my future! Of course! We always have fortune cookies. Are you hoping for a prince charming, Poppy? Nope! I want to be a famous aerial hoop performer! Just like the ones on TV! I want to be an astronaut… or a dragon trainer!

Right, so, this weather, eh? Wouldn't have picked this for Rome in May. Bit drizzly, innit? Yeah, proper rubbish. Thought it’d be all sunshine and gelato, you know? Luckily this bar's tucked away, nice and cosy. Found it by accident, actually. It’s lovely. Much better than that tourist trap near the Trevi Fountain. I swear, they charge you double just for the view. And it’s really bustling down there, felt like being in a rugby scrum. Tell me about it! I tried to grab a coffee there this morning. Ended up spending ten minutes just dodging selfie sticks. Anyway, Rome's charming regardless, even with the crowds. You guys liking it so far? Definitely. I'm loving the history, obviously. Been to the Colosseum, Roman Forum… a lot of walking though. My feet are killing me! My Air BnB is brilliant, by the way. Found a little place near Trastevere. Quiet backstreets, but still walkable to everything. It’s tiny though, barely enough room to swing a cat! But the owner, Maria, is an absolute gem. She even left a little basket of pastries for us. Sounds good. My place, near the Pantheon, is a bit… lived in. Let's just say previous tenants had strong opinions on interior design. But hey, it’s central! And the coffee’s decent, which is all I really need. You and your coffee, Liam! Honestly. Well, speaking of needs, we need to figure out dinner. I was thinking somewhere a bit more traditional tomorrow night? Not just pizza and pasta - although, let's be honest, I could eat pizza and pasta every day. I'm up for anything, really. Something with, like, proper Roman cuisine. I saw a place mentioned online that does Cacio e Pepe… apparently, they make it tableside. Ooh, sounds fancy! I’m in. I’m trying to attempt a bit of Italian, but I’m mostly butchering it. "Un bicchiere di vino bianco," that's about the extent of my repertoire. You’re doing alright! Don’t stress about it. It's a tough language. My Italian's horrific. I try to use Aussie slang, and they just stare at me blankly. "G'day, mate, can I get a cappuccino?" Doesn’t really land, does it? No, I can imagine! My cousin, Chloe, she practically lives in Italy now. Speaks fluent Italian and can even understand Neapolitan dialect.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed. This hen do planning is consuming my life! I’ve got three mood boards going - Vegas, Parisian, and ‘Roaring Twenties’ – and I can't decide which one is best. Vegas sounds… a bit much, doesn’t it? For Claire? I mean, she’s not exactly a showgirl. Parisian could be lovely, but a bit cliché? The Twenties theme is interesting though. Could you do a vintage bake-off as part of it? A vintage bake-off! That’s brilliant, Elodie! Claire would adore that. She's been obsessed with Great British Bake Off lately. Remember that disastrous attempt at a Victoria sponge she had last week? Oh,  don’t  remind me! It looked like a geological survey, not a cake. But seriously, Elodie, the Twenties theme is the strongest. Think flapper dresses, jazz music, maybe even a mocktail bar. We could get everyone to dress up. That’s what I was thinking! But then there’s the guest list. It’s massive. And trying to coordinate everyone’s availability is giving me a headache. Some of her uni friends are traveling from all over. Have you used a Doodle poll, or something similar? That’s usually foolproof for these things. And don’t stress too much about it. It's Claire’s hen do, not a military operation. Absolutely. Plus, you're doing an amazing job! Don't let the pressure get to you. Remember when we organised Sarah's 30th? That was a nightmare with the dodgy bouncy castle. Don't even mention the bouncy castle! That nearly ended in disaster. But you pulled it off, Olivia. And you’ll pull this one off too. So, vintage bake-off… are we thinking proper old-fashioned recipes? Yes! That's the idea. I’ve already started collecting some vintage cookbooks online. I was thinking a competition for the best Battenberg cake and a lemon drizzle. Simple, but classic. That sounds absolutely perfect. I'm a surprisingly decent lemon drizzle maker, you know. Might have to enter! Although, I’d need a few practice runs… Oh, you're entering, are you? Prepare to be beaten by a Mac Artworker! I've been watching a lot of baking tutorials lately. Trying to up my game, you know? You and your digital precision! It’ll be fascinating to see what you come up with. You could design the cake boxes, too!

Right, so, I’m thinking a bit more paprika in this. It needs a bit more…oomph, yeah? What do you reckon, Liam? You’ve got a better palate than I do, honestly. Paprika seems a bit…much for lentil soup, doesn’t it, Finn? It'll taste like goulash. Are you sure you’re not still feeling a bit rough? You were practically radiating heat yesterday. Nah, I’m alright now, honest. Just a dodgy bug, I think. Probably picked it up on the bus. Anyway, I’m feeling like experimenting. Besides, Mum always said, “A little spice never hurt nobody.” Or something like that. She always had some saying, didn't she? She did. And she usually wasn't wrong. But maybe a pinch of cumin instead? That’d complement the lentils better. So, about that trip to Barcelona... Have you booked anything yet? Barcelona. Don't even. The hotel situation is a nightmare. Everything decent is either booked solid or costs a fortune. I spent like, two hours last night scrolling through Booking.com. Found one place that looked alright, near the Gothic Quarter, but the reviews mentioned dodgy plumbing. Dodgy plumbing! Who wants dodgy plumbing on holiday? Sounds charming. Look, let me have a look. I’m pretty good at finding deals. Being an English teacher, I’ve had to bargain for things in some…interesting situations, eh? Plus, I know a few websites that aren't as heavily advertised. What’s your budget looking like? Honestly, not brilliant. Trying to keep it under £500 for the two of us, including flights if possible. It's tight, I know, but I’ve saved a bit. I was thinking we could eat out a fair bit, you know, tapas and stuff. £500 is doable. You’ll need to be smart about it, though. Maybe look at apartments on Airbnb instead of hotels? You get more space, often a kitchen, and it can be cheaper. Although, choosing a decent one can be risky. Yeah, I had a look at Airbnb. There were some absolute dives. One had a picture of a cat asleep on the bed. A  real  cat, not a decorative one. No thanks. I'd rather have dodgy plumbing than cat hair everywhere. Fair enough! Okay, let me do some proper searching tonight. I’ll have a browse and send you some links. Speaking of cooking...

Right then, Marjorie, let’s get this shopping list sorted. We need to be prepared for the week, don't we? Though, honestly, I'm still getting used to being back up North. Leeds is so… different from Margate. Different in a good way, I hope, Penelope? It’s lovely to have you here, you know. And yes, a list is a good idea. Don’t want to be running out of biscuits halfway through Wednesday, do we? Never! Biscuits are vital. And milk, of course. Oh, and that new fabric I saw at John Lewis? The floral one, for the cushions? Oh, yes! The chintz, wasn’t it? Very you. We can add that. What about for the cards? We need ages for everyone's birthdays. It’s like, where did the time go? My goodness, young Thomas is going to be fifteen! Fifteen! Honestly, it feels like only yesterday we were teaching him to tie his shoelaces. Time just races by. Reminds me, I saw these little calendar fobs at the market – quite charming, actually. With little pictures of cats. Would you like one? Cats, you say? Well, I do adore a good cat picture. Yes, please! But tell me, do you remember Miss Perkins and her art and craft days at primary school? She made us weave little rugs from scraps. Absolute chaos, but fun! Oh, Miss Perkins! Feathers flying everywhere! I remember trying to make a papier-mâché volcano that promptly exploded all over poor Timmy Henderson. He was not impressed! And the hockey boots! Those dreadful, heavy things. I tripped over mine at least twice a week. Divine! And remember building dens from blankets in the corner of the classroom? That was heaven. It was all so much simpler then, wasn’t it? Speaking of simpler times, I was thinking about university. You were so keen on sound recording, Penelope. I was! It was fascinating. I loved the technical side of it, the capturing and manipulating of sound. Though I did veer off into social history eventually. It seemed so important to document people's stories, you know? All those voices, fading away... Absolutely. That’s why I ended up teaching, really. Connecting with those voices, passing knowledge on. Though, looking back, the changes in computers... it's astounding. Do you remember those massive mainframe machines we used? Taking up entire rooms! Don't even start!

Honestly, it’s lovely here, Anon. Really. Much more… settled than that flat you had in London. And Holsworthy is so charming. I love that little bakery just down the road – the sourdough is  divine . It is… quiet. Very quiet. A bit too quiet, perhaps. I'm used to the bustle, you know? All the traffic, the people… it’s a stark contrast. Had a bit of a shock the first week, I must say. Oh, you’ll get used to it, David. That's Devon for you. Slow pace, friendly faces. The neighbours are lovely, aren't they, dear? Mrs. Higgins brought over a Victoria sponge the other day. Practically force-fed us the whole thing! She did! It was delicious, though. So generous. I've been trying to get to know them a bit, you know, pop over with a little something. It’s nice to feel like you're part of a community. How about you, Dad? Have you had a chance to chat with anyone? I… nodded at a gentleman the other day. He was trimming his hedge. Didn't get much beyond that. He seemed a decent sort. Rather particular about his roses, though. Oh, David! You need to be more proactive. Holsworthy folk are a friendly bunch, just require a little prompting. There's that walking group – the "Devon Dales Strollers." They meet every Tuesday. Might be a good way to meet people and get some fresh air. That's a brilliant idea, Dad! You could join them. I’m sure you’d enjoy it. Fresh air and a bit of scenery would do you good. Besides, they apparently have a lovely tradition of stopping at the pub afterwards for a pint. A pint, you say? Well, there  is  the Old George. I’ve walked past it a few times. Looks… respectable. Respectable  and  serving excellent local ales. Don’t let the roses intimidate you, David! They’re a gateway to friendship. And speaking of local things, what do you think of the news about the train line improvements? Finally, something positive. It's amazing, isn't it? Getting a direct line back to London would be fantastic for Anon, especially with their new job. It's a bonus, yes. The work is… demanding. Different from my management days, that’s for sure. It involves a lot of spreadsheets. And explaining things very slowly to people.

Aye, I’ve been lookin' at these telly screens, right? Proper big ones. 65 inch, some o' 'em. Reckon I could get one if I, you know… had a bit o' dosh. Don't start, Liam. You say that every week. And realistically, where are you getting this ‘dosh’ from? You've been glued to that phone all day, probably spending what little you have on… what even  is  that you’re looking at? It’s… well, it’s potential. Opportunities. A 65-inch OLED would be a game-changer. Picture quality, ya know? No more squintin' at that old set in the living room. Potential to spend more money you don't have, you mean. Honestly, Liam. Mum’s been saying she’s worried. Have you even looked at those job postings she printed out? Aye, glanced at 'em. All wantin' experience, don’t they? Like I’m supposed to magically conjure experience out of thin air. It’s a right laugh, it is. It's frustrating, I know. But you can't just dismiss everything. There was that warehouse job, Liam. They said they offered training. Warehouse? Stacking boxes all day? My back would be screamin’ by lunchtime. I need somethin’… creative. Somethin' where I can, like, use my brain. Right. And what creative outlet have you utilized this week, besides browsing Amazon for TVs? I’ve been watchin’ a documentary about drones. Think there's somethin' in that, ya know? Filmin' stuff, aerial photography… could be a right buzz. Drones? Liam, you struggle to load the dishwasher properly and you want to be a professional drone photographer? Be realistic. Have you even flown a drone before? Not yet… but I’ve watched loads of videos! It looks easy enough. I could even get one second-hand. See? Savvy. You're something else, you are. It's not just about flying it, it's about regulations, licences, getting good footage… it's a whole thing. Listen, I ordered a new phone case online today. Disaster. The colour was completely off. Said ‘forest green’ and it's like, highlighter yellow. No way! That’s ridiculous. Where'd you get it from? One of them dodgy websites? No, Amazon. Reliable, normally. I'm going to try and return it. It's a pain, though, all that packaging and filling in forms. This modern technology, eh? Supposed to make life easier, but it’s just added another layer of hassle.

Right, so, this is lovely, Anon. Really lovely. Much brighter than you described! Definitely feels…homely. Feels like a proper base for these coastal walks you were planning. It is, isn't it? Took a bit of doing, getting everything in, but worth it. Glad you approve, love. A far cry from that pokey flat in Southend, eh? It’s got potential, definitely. That radiator in the hallway looks like it’s been wrestling with a few pigeons over the years. You’ll need to sort that out before winter bites, Anon. Mum’s already assessing the structural integrity of everything! Don't worry, Anon, we can have a look at it together. Maybe even tackle it? I'm a bit handy with a screwdriver, you know. Though, honestly, a professional might be a better shout with the heating. Oh, radiators. They're all the same. Lasted longer than my last car, that's for certain. Remember that Ford Fiesta? Went on for years… until the exhaust fell off in the middle of the A12. Humiliating, that was. Oh, I remember! Honestly, Dad, you were pushing your luck. You kept it going with duct tape and prayer. Speaking of things that last, what’s lunch then, Anon? I’m starving. All this moving has worked up an appetite. I was rather hoping for something hearty after all that unpacking. Well, I was thinking of Sarah’s famous Cornish pasties! Got a few in the freezer. And some lovely apple crumble. Thought it would be a nice, comforting welcome. Ooh, perfect! You spoil us, Anon. And after lunch, we could actually plan that walk properly. I’ve been looking at some maps – there’s a lovely stretch just north of here, past Clovelly. Bit hilly, mind you. Clovelly! That's the one with the ridiculously steep cobbled streets, isn't it? Beautiful though. I’m in! We'll need to pack some water and those walking boots. Though, Dad, are you still rocking the sandals? Sandals are perfectly acceptable footwear for a stroll along the coast! Keeps your feet cool, you know. Comfortable too. Don't start on my footwear, young lady. Alright, alright, no need to get defensive. As long as you don't trip and roll down a cliff! It’s Christmas opening hours I am more concerned about. Are shops open on Boxing Day this year? I need to get another cushion for the sofa, the one Anon bought is falling apart already.

Right, that was genuinely fantastic. Your roasted vegetables are a masterpiece, honestly. I was craving something like that all week. Glad you enjoyed it! It’s a surprisingly simple recipe, actually. Just needed a good dose of rosemary and a generous splash of balsamic. So, how was your day battling the academic world today? Still wrestling with those cognitive biases in intervention programs? Wrestling is the operative word. I’m starting to think I’m creating more biases by  studying  them. It’s this whole feedback loop thing, you know? The more I delve, the more convinced I am that human behaviour is just fundamentally illogical. You're being a bit hard on yourself, aren't you? It's complex, sure, but there’s logic  within  the illogical. People act according to their perceived needs and experiences. It’s not random. I suppose. But trying to design an intervention that  systematically  corrects for, say, confirmation bias, when the very act of presenting information can trigger it… it's a nightmare! Professor Davies kept pressing me this afternoon about measurable outcomes. Measurable outcomes! As if you can put a number on someone’s ingrained thought patterns. Davies, eh? Still the bastion of pragmatism, I see. Look, I get it. It’s frustrating. But measurable outcomes are what gets funding, aren't they? You have to play the game, to some extent. Have you considered framing it as improved decision-making skills? That feels a bit more tangible. That's... actually a rather clever way to put it. "Improved decision-making abilities resulting from reduced susceptibility to cognitive biases." Sounds far less like I'm trying to rewire people’s brains. See? You’re brilliant. You just need to repackage it. Speaking of repackaging, I had a slightly insane day too. We're implementing a new assessment system in the school, and the sheer volume of consultations I’ve had with teachers, parents, and frankly, bewildered children, has been overwhelming. New assessment system? Oh dear. I remember how stressful the last one was. All those forms, all that data… It's worse. Much worse. This one's supposed to be ‘personalised’ and ‘holistic.’ Which translates to 'incredibly confusing for everyone involved' in my experience. I spent three hours explaining to Mrs. Higgins how to interpret a scatter plot showing a child's ‘learning trajectory.’ I think she genuinely thought I was trying to trick her.

"Right then, this is smashing, Brenda. You've really outdone yourself." "Oh, stop it, Dave! Just a bit of Sunday dinner. Glad you're enjoying it. So, Barry, you were saying earlier about the new interns at the college? How are they shaping up?" "Well, some are promising, some… less so. One of them, young Liam, he’s got a dreadful habit of using jargon. Absolutely drowning in it. Last week he told me we needed to ‘optimise synergistic outcomes’ when he meant ‘make sure we schedule the meetings better’!" "Oh, bless him! Sounds like he's trying too hard to impress. It's so common, isn't it? Especially fresh grads." "They do. Comes with the territory. Remember when I first started as a nurse, I was terrified of using the wrong acronyms. I’d write things down phonetically, just to be sure I was spelling them correctly!" "I know exactly what you mean, Wendy! All this new terminology they throw at you now… it’s overwhelming even for someone with a bit of experience. Still, you’d think they’d teach you that stuff properly. Speaking of overwhelming, I had a nightmare with Mrs. Higgins today. She insisted her cat, Mr. Fluffernutter, was a reincarnation of Elvis." "Mr. Fluffernutter? Good name for a cat! Elvis, eh? She must be having a laugh!" "You get all sorts, don’t you? At the college, we had a student convinced he could communicate with squirrels. Said they were offering him business advice." "That's wild! But you know, I read somewhere that animals are actually really good at picking up on human emotions. Maybe they  are  trying to tell us something!" "Maybe. Though I suspect Mr. Fluffernutter was simply after a saucer of milk and a scratch behind the ears. I’m left-handed, you know. Always have been. Do you find animals react differently to you, Chloe, being left-handed?" "That’s an interesting thought! I haven’t really considered it. My flatmate’s got a rescue dog, and he’s a bit of a handful, but I do find he seems to nuzzle into me more than he does her. Could be coincidence though." "Interesting. My grandson, little Thomas, is left-handed. He's a wee darling, obsessed with dinosaurs. He tried to teach my dog, Winston, the name of a Stegosaurus the other day. Winston wasn’t impressed!" "I'm right-handed, always have been.

Right then, Grandad, have a look at these! I baked 'em this mornin'. Proper clotted cream and strawberry jam – just how you like it. Scones, eh? Good lass. Always did fancy a good scone. Timperley used to have a bakery, you know, down on Dunham Road. Old Mrs. Higgins, she made them the best. A little denser than these, I reckon, but still… lovely. This jam's lookin’ alright, though. Is it proper strawberry? None of that artificial stuff? They look fantastic, Chloe. Really, you've outdone yourself. Scones are always a winner, especially with cream and jam. Reminds me of picnics in the Chilterns as a kid. We’d pack a basket full of things – sandwiches, fruit, and always,  always , scones. Thanks, Liam! Glad you like 'em. Aye, proper strawberry, Grandad. Got 'em fresh from the farmers market. It's important, isn't it? Real food. Bit of a shock these days, what they try and pass off as… well, everything. Tell me about it. Back in my day, you knew where your food came from. My mother used to grow most of it herself. Tomatoes, rhubarb, beans... the lot. Now, you can't trust a thing. And the portions! They’re enormous. It's the everything-bigger-and-faster mentality, isn't it? I was just speaking to a colleague the other day about sustainable sourcing for a project. It’s getting more and more crucial, but companies are often hesitant to change because of the perceived cost. Exactly! It's not just food, though, is it? It’s travel, too. Everyone rushing off to far-flung places. I've been lookin' at some trips, actually. Nothin' drastic, mind. Maybe Scotland next year. The Highlands have always beckoned. Scotland! Ah, I went to Scotland once. 1952, I think it was. With the army. Barracks up near Inverness. Cold, it was. Dreich. Though the scenery  was  something else. Mountains sticking right out of the water. We saw a stag, too! A big, handsome fellow. That sounds incredible, Grandad. I've always wanted to go to the Isle of Skye. The landscapes are just… breathtaking from the photos I've seen. I’m planning a business trip to Edinburgh next quarter, maybe I could sneak a weekend away. See, Liam? Fancy a trip to Skye after Edinburgh? We could even meet you! Grandad could come too, if he’s up for it.

Right, so, the feedback on Module 3 was... robust, wasn’t it? A lot of students struggling with the Hegelian dialectic. Honestly, I didn’t realise it would hit them  that  hard. Robust is one word for it. Chaotic feels more accurate. I saw a few panicked emails already. Don't worry too much though, it’s a tricky concept. They just need a little more scaffolding. Scaffolding! Exactly! I was thinking maybe a simpler, more practical example? Something less… abstract. I keep trying to illustrate it with the classic thesis-antithesis-synthesis, but they’re all just staring blankly. What about the whole Brexit debate? It’s infuriatingly real-world, and the core dynamics are very Hegelian. You could break it down, like, the initial thesis of remaining in the EU, the antithesis of leaving, and then the messy, ongoing synthesis we're all living through. That's brilliant, actually! Much more relatable than anything I've been trying to conjure up. It's already happening around them. It’ll make it feel less like an academic exercise and more... well, relevant. Did you manage to finish that reading list for the new seminar on postcolonial literature? I feel like I’m drowning in articles. Almost. I’ve got that Frantz Fanon piece locked and loaded, and I finally tracked down a really interesting essay by Gayatri Spivak on subaltern voices. I was rather obsessing about finding something that would balance the more theoretically dense stuff with a bit of practical application. Good, because I think they need a grounding in practical examples too. This course always feels a bit… detached to the students, doesn’t it? We're analyzing these incredible texts, but sometimes I wonder if they see the connection to their own lives, or to current events. Absolutely. And speaking of current events… did you see that new documentary on Channel 4 about the AI takeover? It was terrifyingly plausible. Don't remind me! I watched it last night. I couldn’t sleep afterwards. I’m genuinely worried about the implications for higher education. Will we even  be  lecturing in twenty years? Dramatic as always. But, yeah, it’s something to consider. Though, I think there'll always be a need for critical thinking and engaging in debate – skills AI can’t truly replicate. At least, not yet. Let's hope you're right. Although, on a slightly less apocalyptic note, I am starving.

Honestly, this coffee machine is a menace. It's been spitting out lukewarm, half-brewed coffee all week. I think it’s finally given up the ghost. Everything seems to be giving up the ghost these days, doesn't it? Though, I suppose that's the natural order of things. Retirement brings a certain… fragility to possessions, I've found. Fragility? More like deliberate sabotage. Manufacturers nowadays, they don’t want things to last. Planned obsolescence, that’s what it is. Designed to break so you have to buy another one. You’re going full conspiracy theorist again, aren’t you, Geoff? It’s just a coffee machine. Though, I will admit, I’m getting a bit tired of replacing things. Speaking of which…have you two had a chance to look into those removal quotes? I’ve called a couple. It's…alarming, the prices. The storage, too. So many boxes. So much…stuff. I’m beginning to wonder if moving everything here was the right thing to do. Right thing for who, Mary? For you, yes. Being closer to us is brilliant. But getting bogged down in the logistics...that’s a different matter. Did you get that one from that chap in Penrith? He seemed decent. I did. He was the cheapest, but the reviews were a bit mixed. A few people complained about them being late. Not ideal when you have a timeline. I’m thinking we might need to pad the budget a bit, just in case. We’re looking at close to £3,000 just to move and store everything, aren't we? It’s scandalous! Three thousand pounds! When I was a girl, you could buy a house for that. A  decent  house! Don't get me started on the cost of living. It's all gone mad. And this… this endless political arguing. Honestly, it’s exhausting. Tell me about it. Did you see what Starmer said about the new policies? It felt so... lukewarm. Like he's trying to appeal to everyone and ends up appealing to no one. He's lost the fire, hasn’t he? All that talk of triangulation... It’s not inspiring. Where’s the idealism? Where's the conviction? I used to be so passionate about the Labour party, back when… well, back when things felt different. Passionate? Mary, you used to argue with the headmaster about implementing socialist education reforms!

Right then, so we’re settled. This place is eerily quiet for a Saturday lunch, isn't it? Feels like we've hired out the entire restaurant. Yeah, proper spooky. Still, good for avoiding the queue, innit? So, about these pseudonyms… I'm still trying to wrap my head around why we needed them in the first place. It was a bit of a whim, really! Just felt like a bit of fun, especially on holiday. I’m going by ‘Esme’ for the week. Feels…pretentious, in the best way. You're 'Felix,' aren't you, Liam? Felix sounds fancier than me. I’m just easy, yeah? Less chance of getting recognised back in London. It's safer, you see. Oh, relax, darling. Who’s going to recognise you just by your name? I’m ‘Coraline’ – much more dramatic than Sarah, don't you think? And David, you’re ‘Rhys,’ right? Bit rugged, suits you. Rhys it is. Suits me alright. So, are we sticking to these all week or just for lunch? I'm getting confused already. Let's stick with them for the whole trip! It adds a little mystique. Anyway, speaking of things a bit…different, you know I’ve been researching Jewish dietary laws for a baking project, right? Kosher food is fascinating! Kosher? Like, no mixing meat and milk? I thought that was just something my Nan used to say. That’s a big part of it, yeah. And all sorts of other rules about how animals are slaughtered and how food is processed. It’s actually quite complex, but incredibly interesting from a culinary perspective. Imagine adapting classic recipes to fit those restrictions! Sounds like a nightmare for a baker. So, what are we eating then? This menu's surprisingly limited. I'm feeling Italian. Pizza, pasta… something with pesto? Pesto sounds good. But could we get some good chilli flakes to go with it? I need a bit of a kick. I swear, British food sometimes... lacks adventure. Adventure? You just need decent condiments! Proper Branston pickle, that’s adventure. Or a really good chutney. See, Australia's got nothing on a good English pickle. Now you’re just winding me up! We have bush tomatoes and lemon myrtle – that's a culinary journey right there! Although, I do miss a decent Scotch Bonnet pepper sometimes. Side note – have you seen the state of the canals around here?

Honestly, I’m starting to think Tinder is just a breeding ground for awkward silences and guys who only talk about their protein intake. Aye, tell me about it! I went on a date last week, right? Promised me he was into hiking. Turns out, “hiking” meant a five-minute stroll around the park followed by him talking about his crypto investments. Proper boring. Oh, bless. At least you got a date! I've been swiping for weeks, and the best I’ve got is a bloke who thinks 'Netflix and chill' is an actual suggestion for a first date. Like, read the room, mate! You’ve been unlucky, that's all. You just gotta filter better. I’ve had a few decent ones. Found a lad who plays guitar, actually. Not a  looker , mind, but he's got a laugh and seems alright. That's good going, Liv! You're brave, even considering a date! Remember what happened to me and the "musician" last month? Turns out his musical talent peaked at playing the recorder in primary school. He brought said recorder on the date. No! You’re kidding! A recorder?! Oh, Maisie, you are a magnet for disaster. Seriously though, what  are  people like? It's like a competition to see who can be the most utterly devoid of charm. It's the desperation, innit? Everyone’s lookin' for somethin'. And sometimes, they're just bein' honest about bein' a bit rubbish at the whole dating thing. It’s not always malicious. Maybe you're all being too harsh. There are good people out there! Just...hard to find weeding through the weeds. Anyway, speaking of dreadful people, has anyone heard from Liam lately? He keeps leaving his dishes in the sink. It's like living with a teenager! Liam's a menace. I swear he thinks the sink is some kind of magical disappearing bin. I've left passive-aggressive notes, I've glares...nothing works! We need to have a proper housemate meeting. Like, a formal agreement. "Liam, you wash your dishes or face the consequences!" Consequences like what, though? That's the tricky bit. Consequences like we hide all his socks? Or change the hot water temperature to freezing whenever he's showering? Now you're talkin'! Though I reckon we should maybe aim for something a bit less... drastic. Perhaps just report him to the landlords?

Cor, another day, another pile of bills, eh, Arthur? Feels like they keep arriving faster than I can manage, doesn't it? Though, mind you, that might just be me getting old and daft. Daft? You? Don’t be daft yourself, George. It’s the government, isn't it? Always finding new ways to squeeze us. Saw something on the telly last night, about cutting benefits again. Can you believe it? When we’ve already got bugger all. Oh, don't let's start on that, boys. It'll give me a migraine! Though Arthur’s right, the government’s a disgrace. Honestly, you'd think they hadn’t a clue how the rest of us live. Here, have a biscuit. Ginger snaps, your favourite, George. Lovely, Elsie, thanks. Ginger snaps are just the ticket. Still, it’s worrying, isn't it? I was reading about that Universal Credit system. Seems a right mess. They're changing the rules again, apparently. All this digital stuff too! I'm barely managing to use the internet to order my groceries, let alone navigate some complicated benefits portal. Universal Credit… that’s the thing that caused poor Mrs. Higgins all that trouble, wasn't it? She couldn’t even get onto the website. Ended up having to go down to the library! Ridiculous. Back in our day, you went to the post office, spoke to a proper person, sorted things out. Much more civilised. It is, Arthur. It is. I remember when things were simpler. And you knew who to talk to. Now it’s all automated voices and endless menus. Drives you round the bend! Though, I must say, I did manage to watch that new detective show last night, "Harrowfield Shadows." Quite gripping, actually. "Harrowfield Shadows"? Can't say I've heard of it. Is it any good? I've been mostly sticking to reruns of "Midsomer Murders." Reliable entertainment, that is. You know what to expect. Not like these newfangled shows that try to be too clever for their own good. "Midsomer Murders," aye. A bit predictable, but comfy, innit? Don't need thrills and spills at our age, George. Give me a good cup of tea and a murder in a picturesque village any day. Elsie, you watching that "Harrowfield Shadows"? Yes, darling. It's set in Yorkshire, gloomy moors and all that. Very atmospheric. The detective is a bit unconventional, but quite likeable.

Honestly, this Shepherd’s Pie is lovely, David, but I’m absolutely knackered. It is good, isn't it? You've outdone yourself, love. And knackered? What on earth did you get up to today? You seemed relatively calm when you left this morning. Relatively calm! That’s putting it mildly. The library was manic. The new systems training… well, let's just say it was less “training” and more organised chaos. I think Brenda ended up accidentally deleting three records. Three! And then Mr. Harrison kept asking me the same question every five minutes. Five minutes, David! Harrison. Bless him. He does get a bit… repetitive, doesn't he? You’ve got the patience of a saint, Sarah. Fundraising is stressful, but at least the complaints usually involve people wanting more raffle tickets, not accidentally erasing data. Exactly! It’s a different kind of stress, you know? This is… intellectual and logistical. Dealing with scattered data and slightly bewildered librarians. Yours feels more… people-focused. Wanting something, needing something. Is the annual appeal going well? It’s... progressing. We’ve had a good response from the usual suspects, the Johnson family have pledged a generous amount, as expected. But finding new donors, those precious early adopters, that’s proving a bit trickier this year. I spent most of the afternoon on the phone chasing up a grant application. Bureaucracy at its finest. They want a detailed breakdown of how we intend to spend every penny, down to the last teabag. The joys of paperwork. Remember when we used to travel all over the place for your fundraising events? That felt more exciting, more…alive. Now it’s all emails and interminable phone calls. I do miss that, to be honest. But times change. It’s cheaper this way, and lets face it, my knees aren’t what they used to be. Though, you know, Mrs. Peterson from the Women's Institute called today. Apparently, she's organised a bake sale to raise money for us. Oh, that’s lovely! Mrs. Peterson makes the best Victoria sponge in the world. We should go and support her. Absolutely. Speaking of supporting, how's Emily getting on with her essays? She sounded stressed last week. She's alright, I think. She says the history one is particularly difficult. Something about the impact of the Industrial Revolution on rural communities. Sounds riveting. She wants to watch something mindless tonight, though.

Honestly, this damp is just getting to me. Tarnow’s lovely, don’t get me wrong, but the humidity… it’s something else. Makes my joints ache something awful. Aye, it's a bit grim, innit? Though, to be fair, Bury’s got its share of damp too, just a different kind. Proper Lancashire drizzle. Been looking at pictures of home, actually. Mum posted some from the funeral. Looks… grey. Oh, really? Did you see many people you knew? It must have been terribly difficult, returning for that. Not loads, to be honest. A few old school friends, Mum’s side of the family… it was good to be there, though. You know, to pay respects. But it felt… hollow, somehow. Like a performance. And then coming back here... it's a big shift. I can imagine. It’s a strange feeling, isn’t it? This idea of ‘home.’ I’ve been wrestling with that a lot lately, living out here. Cambridge feels like a distant memory, and England… well, everywhere feels a bit… foreign. Yeah, I get that. It's weird, isn't it? Like, Bury will always be where I  come  from, but it's not necessarily where I  belong . Poland’s started to feel a bit like home for me, surprisingly. The people are lovely, and the prices are… well, manageable. You been looking at those apartments online, like we talked about? Briefly. They’re… small. And the heating. Oh dear, the heating. Honestly, at my age, a bit of central heating is the bare minimum. It’s not exactly conducive to a relaxed retirement, is it? I miss a good log fire. True, true. And you’ve always loved your roaring fires. It’s all a trade-off, I suppose. Lower cost of living versus… slightly less comfort. I've been thinking about maybe moving to Barcelona, actually. My mate, Sophie, moved there a couple of years ago and she’s loving it. Sunshine, tapas, and she says the language barrier isn't as bad as you'd think. Barcelona! That sounds lovely. Though, the thought of learning another language… it’s daunting. This teaching thing… it’s alright, I suppose. Keeps me busy, and the students are charming. Little Kaelin from Saudi Arabia just melts my heart. But it's not exactly a career for a graduate with a humanities degree, is it? No, but it’s  something , isn't it?

Honestly, this Earl Grey is a bit weak, innit? You’d think a London pub could manage a decent cuppa. You’re always complaining about the tea! It’s perfectly fine, Liv. Besides, we’re in a pub, not Fortnum & Mason. It’s about the atmosphere, isn't it? So much better than trying to find a spot in that rush-hour chaos. True, true. It  is  nice to just sit down for a minute. Work's been absolutely mental this week. They’ve given me the campaign for that new vegan burger chain – "Plant Power," they're calling it. Plant Power! It sounds like a superhero team for vegetables. Oh, that's brilliant! You’ll have a field day with that. So, plenty to write then, keeping you busy? Busy is an understatement. I'm basically living off caffeine and dry toast. I’m trying to make it sound… exciting. Like, "Unleash your inner chlorophyll!" or something equally ridiculous. The creative director seems to like it so far, which is terrifying. Sounds like you. You always have the most… inventive briefs. How's Sarah doing, by the way? Haven't seen her in ages. Sarah’s good! She’s training for that marathon. Insane, honestly, that girl. She’s been running like a lunatic every morning. She’s convinced she'll beat her personal best. I told her she needs to fuel properly, though. She lives on protein bars and that green sludge she calls a smoothie. Oh, the green sludge! I remember that. It looked like something you’d clean the bathroom with. Speaking of needing food, I’m starving. Fancy grabbing something later? There’s that little bakery just around the corner - they do amazing pasties. Ooh, a pasty! That does sound good. I’m practically craving carbs. I haven't had anything decent to eat all day. Those burger campaign photoshoots are… not conducive to healthy eating. All greasy chips and fake burgers. Right? It’s the irony, isn't it? I was helping out with a survey project analysing consumer buying habits the other day, and half the answers were "crisps" and "chocolate." We’re a nation of snackers. Absolutely. Though, thinking about it, I'm not sure I could face a pasty right now. Maybe something a little lighter? I don’t want to fall into a food coma. Good point. Okay, no pasties. How about we just grab some sandwiches then?

Right, that’s enough. Absolutely enough. Someone decided 6:30 AM was a perfectly reasonable time to start the day. Mummy? I was hungry. Hungry? At 6:30, Elara? You had a biscuit just before bed! Honestly, these early mornings... Finn! Are you awake too? Mmmph... mostly. Did I miss breakfast already? Not quite, sunshine. But you nearly woke everyone up completely. Elara here was the instigator this time. But I wanted porridge! With blueberries! Okay, okay. Porridge with blueberries it is. But no more catapulting yourself into the waking world before the sun's properly up, alright? We need our beauty sleep! And your dad needs his. Are we going to the park today? I want to build a really big den! We  might  go to the park, Finn. But first, we have a rather exciting plan. Remember how we talked about that Neon Moon event? The one with the lights and the music? The very one! I managed to get us tickets. It's tonight, just outside Cambridge. Apparently, they have a whole area dedicated to circus skills. Circus skills?! Can I be a juggler? Or a tightrope walker? Well, we’ll see how you do with a beanbag first. They’ll have some simpler things to try. It’ll be a bit like that time we saw that street performer in Brighton – remember when you tried to walk like him? And fell over! That was a  very  wobbly pavement! Exactly! Right, focus. Porridge. Then maybe some playtime, and then we'll get packed and ready to go this evening. Your dad will be up soon, and he needs a good breakfast to fuel him. Mummy, do people in Australia eat porridge? Hmm, good question. I don't actually know! I wonder. It's funny, I was reading about Australian slang the other day and kept stumbling across phrases like "fair dinkum." It's confusing! 'Fair dinkum'! What does that mean? Apparently, it means "genuine" or "true." Like, if you were being "fair dinkum" about wanting porridge, you  really  wanted porridge. I was being fair dinkum! I believe you. Now, eat up your porridge, my little "fair dinkums." And Finn, be careful you don't slosh it everywhere. Your dad wouldn't be best pleased if he had to clean up a porridge explosion before his coffee. I'll try! But it's very wiggly porridge! It is, isn't it?

Honestly, this whole Brexit thing still feels like a fever dream. Did we really vote for this? Well, you were barely old enough to vote then, weren't you, Rhys? It's easy to look back and think, "How could we have been so foolish?" But it wasn’t as simple as that, dear. People had genuine concerns. Genuine concerns that were skillfully exploited, I'd argue, Eleanor. Fear-mongering is a powerful tool, and it was wielded effectively. The arguments about taking back control...it resonated with a certain segment of the population, a segment feeling left behind. But control over what? Endless paperwork and trade barriers? It feels like we’ve traded one set of problems for a much more complicated one. And the impact on young people like me... it's just…limiting. My Erasmus exchange to Berlin just became infinitely more expensive and clunky. I agree, Rhys. The Erasmus point is particularly galling. It was such a brilliant program, fostering connections and understanding across Europe. To see it jeopardised is deeply regrettable. Though I remember a similar sentiment when we joined the Common Market back in the 70s. My father was absolutely convinced it was the ruin of Britain. Said we’d be beholden to foreigners forever. Your father was a staunch traditionalist, Eleanor. I recall him saying something similar when the Welsh language was gaining ground in public life. There's always a resistance to change, isn't there? Even when that change is clearly for the better. It’s a human characteristic, I suppose. But isn't that a bit of an excuse? Shouldn’t we, as a society, be able to look past ingrained prejudices and see what’s actually beneficial? Look at the farming subsidies, for example. Devastating for a lot of small farms because they can't compete with imports now. It's not an excuse, Rhys, it's an observation. And you're right, the impact on agriculture has been…significant. I was just reading a piece in  The Guardian  about the struggles in Devon. Farmers abandoning their land, you know. It's heartbreaking. The subsidies were always a flawed system, mind you. Historically, they favoured the larger landowners, disproportionately. Brexit has just exposed the cracks further. It's highlighted the inherent inequalities within the system. Driving down this road reminds me of… …my grandfather’s farm, just outside Nantyglo. Small holding, barely enough to scrape by, even  before  Brexit.

Right, so, we were talking about Helen Moss, weren't we? Remember how she used to weave those silly stories about the grumpy badger living under the oak tree in her garden? The one that stole Mrs. Higgins’ jam tarts? He had a little hat! And he tripped over a garden gnome wearing a blue pointy hat!  Giggles  Exactly! See, you two have got it. They were wonderfully ridiculous. Do you know, I was thinking about the Linton Book Festival, and how much I wish we could go this year. Can't we? Please, Mummy? There's always storytellers! Will they tell badger stories? Well, I don't know about badger stories specifically, darling, but there are always fantastic storytellers. This year, they've got someone who does theatrical adaptations of folk tales - really brilliant stuff. Reminds me a bit of what we used to do with Helen Moss, putting on little plays for the village fete. We could do a play! About the badger! I can be Mrs. Higgins and yell at him! You would, wouldn’t you? That would be brilliant! We could build him a little badger set from cardboard boxes. What about you, Leo? What role would you want? I want to be… the garden gnome! The one with the blue hat! He needs to be very brave. He  does  need to be brave, doesn’t he? Facing down a grumpy, jam-tart-stealing badger is a pretty daunting task. You’d need a sparkly sword! And he needs to trip over something else! Maybe a… a rubber ducky! A rubber ducky! The badger slips on the ducky! You two are a pair. Right, a badger, a gnome, and a rubber ducky... That's a story right there. You know, sometimes I think Helen Moss would be proud of you, coming up with these silly scenarios. Building a whole world from just a few simple ideas. Actually, it's a lovely way to think about storytelling. It's not about big, complicated plots, is it? It's about finding the fun in the everyday. Do you think Helen Moss  actually  had a badger in her garden? I like to think she did, darling. I truly do. And that she just made up all the funny things he got up to. It’s much more exciting that way, isn’t it? Maybe the badger had a friend who was a squirrel!

Honestly, I’m still getting used to this. Being totally vegetarian. It’s been, what, three months now? And I still occasionally dream of bacon. Three months and you’re mourning bacon? You were a dedicated carnivore, weren’t you? It’s a big shift. But look at you, wielding a curry spoon like a pro. It's pretty impressive. It  is  impressive. Especially considering you used to complain about anything vaguely green. And the curry smells incredible, by the way. Less questionable meat smells like that, I think. Okay, okay, lay off! It's a work in progress. But I'm really trying. It's just…sometimes the ethics of it all feel so heavy. Thinking about factory farms, the whole system… Totally. That’s why I've been diving deeper into stuff like cultured meat, you know? Shmeat. It’s wild to think you could grow a burger in a lab, without any animal suffering. Shmeat! I read an article about that. It’s still so experimental though, isn’t it? And the energy usage… Is it really more sustainable than, say, plant-based? That's the big question, isn’t it? Early prototypes needed a  lot  of energy, but they’re working on improving the process. The potential is huge, though. Imagine, completely cutting out the need for abattoirs. No more…the whole horrific process. It’s bizarre to think about, isn’t it? Like, hunting – even though it’s inherently violent – at least it’s…direct? There's a wild aspect. But mass farming and slaughter? It feels so removed, so obscured from people. They don’t see the suffering. It’s all about scale, I think. A single deer hunted and processed is… grim, but still. Hundreds of thousands of animals living in horrific conditions before being efficiently slaughtered? That’s a different level. I’ve done some shifts at care homes where the sheer mechanical efficiency of things can be…distressing. Exactly. And I read some stuff about how the stress of factory farming affects the meat itself, nutritionally. Less omega-3, more inflammatory acids… Basically, you’re getting less benefit and more potential harm. Which is just brilliant. Which is why I've been taking these vitamin B12 tablets. My doctor recommended them. Apparently, you can't really get enough from plants alone. Smart. I'm looking into getting some vitamin D supplements too. Living in London, you barely see the sun.

Right, nearly ready. Smells alright, doesn’t it? Bit ambitious, making a paella on a Tuesday, but I fancied something different. Sounds lovely, love. Much better than that shepherd's pie you did last week. No offence, mind. It needed… seasoning. A  lot  of seasoning. Paella? Ooh, fancy! Are there prawns? I’m addicted to prawns at the moment. Honestly, I could live on them. Of course, there are prawns! Wouldn’t be paella without 'em. And chicken, and chorizo… it’s a right proper mix. Just hoping the rice doesn't end up like glue again. You know how dodgy supermarket rice can be. Speaking of dodgy things, the washing machine’s making that awful grinding noise again. You heard it this morning, didn't you, love? Yes, I heard it. I told you, David, we need to get it looked at. It’s been making that noise for months. It’ll die completely if we don’t. Seriously? It sounds like a badger’s trapped in it. Last time it did that, it spat out the entire contents covered in grey fluff. Remember? Don’t remind me! It looked like a sheep had exploded in the laundry room. Honestly, that was a nightmare cleaning that up. I think I still find the occasional fleck of fluff. Well, you were the one who put that angora sweater in with the towels! Honestly, David... It was an accident! I thought it was just a regular jumper. Besides, your sister’s wedding is coming up. We  need  that machine for all the fancy dresses. Speaking of weddings, did you see Sarah’s photos from hers? They were gorgeous! That venue was absolutely stunning. All those fairy lights… Oh yes, she did have a lovely wedding. Although, her mother kept going on about how the canapés weren’t  quite  as good as the ones at Lady Penelope’s garden party. Honestly, some people… You're telling me! Margaret always has to find something to complain about. Remember that time she critiqued the floral arrangements at his brother's funeral? No way! Seriously? Wow. That’s… intense. It is, isn't it? Some people just can't help themselves. Anyway, back to the wedding. I was thinking maybe we could get the internet sorted out before then. It’s been patchy beyond belief lately, and trying to show people pictures of the grandkids is a nightmare.

Honestly, you two. Butterfly forks. Really? I spent a fortune on proper silverware, and all you want are the novelty ones. They’re cool, Mum. And O’s obsessed with them. You saw him, practically drooling over them at the party. Yeah, and I like them too! It’s more fun than the regular ones. Plus, they’re good for stabbing peas. Stabbing peas is not a reason to use novelty forks, Ivor! It’s just... a bit much, isn't it? Especially when we're having a relatively sophisticated supper. O, what do you think? Are butterfly forks appropriate for a salmon en croute? O thinks they absolutely are. He said they add ‘pizzazz.’ His words, not mine. Pizzazz. Oh, dear. Well, I suppose one evening of pizzazz won’t hurt. Speaking of things a little out of the ordinary... did you both see the news about the Remembrance Day pause? Two minutes of silence practically shut down the whole of London. Yeah, it was pretty crazy. My teacher said it was really important to remember. It was a bit weird seeing everyone just… stop. Even the cars. It was silent. Really silent. It is important. A lot to remember, isn't there? It always makes me think about my grandfather, actually. He fought in the war.
