He never really talked about it, but… you could feel it. This quiet weight about him. Did he ever tell you any stories? A few, very few. Mostly just about rationing and the blackout. It was a different world. Thinking about all that happened today, it’s also made me think about birthdays. Yours is coming up soon, Ivor. Have you given any thought to what you want? Not really. Maybe a new game? Or some LEGO. I’m hoping for a new graphics card. My computer’s so slow, it’s embarrassing. Always the technology. You young people! O, you're still going on about wanting to go to Russia, aren't you? Absolutely. I’ve been reading about St. Petersburg. The architecture is amazing. And the history! It’s like stepping back in time. You could try learning some Russian. You think I have time for that? Between school and gaming… Well, it wouldn't hurt. It  is  a fascinating country, though. A complicated one. I remember reading a history book about it when I was your age, O. So much upheaval.

Right, so, Cornwall it is then? It's just…the logistics of getting everyone there are a bit of a headache. Especially with Leo’s allergies. Cornwall! Cornwall! Will there be mermaids, Mummy? Pirate ships! Are there pirate ships in Cornwall? Possibly, darling. Maybe we’ll find a sunken treasure! And maybe, just maybe, we’ll spot a mermaid. But let’s be sensible, shall we? More importantly, we need to find somewhere that takes allergies seriously. Remember what happened at that pub in Brighton? Yucky! My tummy hurt! Exactly! So, no more risking it. I've been looking at a few cottages online. They advertise being allergy-friendly, but you know how that goes. I’ll need to vet them  thoroughly . Can we build sandcastles? Really, really big ones? Absolutely! We’ll build the biggest sandcastles Cornwall has ever seen. Although, Leo, remember no eating the sand, alright? It’s not chocolate, even if it looks a little brown. Silly Leo! Thinking about it, it won't just be Cornwall. There's Adventure Island to consider later this summer. Remember how much you both loved the log flume last time? The splashy one! Yes! And the carousel! With the horses! Right. So, Cornwall in August, Adventure Island in July. It's quite a lot, isn’t it? I’ve also been meaning to get us all to that V&A exhibition on textiles. It looked fascinating online and I thought it might inspire some creative projects. Though, honestly, after marking those GCSE history papers… History is boring! You’re probably right. It  was  exceptionally boring this year. So much badly written essays about the Tudors. Honestly, some of them… Anyway! Practicalities. I’m thinking we need to book those cottage places  now . It's popular, Cornwall, especially during the summer. Have you both got anything you really  want  to do while we're there? I want to see a badger! A badger? Right, noted. Badger spotting will definitely be on the itinerary. I want to collect seashells! Lots and lots of sparkly ones! Sparkly seashells it is. Anything else? Perhaps something a bit more…grown-up? Can we have ice cream every day? Ice cream! Yes! That, my dears, is a very reasonable request. Ice cream every day it is. Now, let's have a look at these cottages... and maybe book that dentist appointment for Leo while I'm at it.

Ugh, Mr. Davies really set us up for failure with that history essay. 'Analyze the impact of the Industrial Revolution on Victorian social structures'? Seriously, who even  likes  that much detail? Tell me about it. I spent like, three hours last night just trying to understand what ‘social stratification’ even  meant . My mum had to explain it, and she just looked bewildered. Exactly! And he expects us to use primary sources. Primary sources! Where am I supposed to find a Victorian factory worker's diary just lying around? I ended up quoting Wikipedia, which I know is terrible, but I was running out of time. Don’t worry too much about it. Mrs. Sharma said she'll be lenient if we just show we've  tried . Did you hear about Liam getting detention? Liam? For what? Typical. Probably messing around in maths again. Nah, apparently he argued with Mr. Peterson about the seating plan. Said it wasn't fair. Mr. Peterson’s face was red as a tomato. Prefects are cracking down, you know? Trying to be all proper and stuff. Good luck with that. Slough High’s never going to be Eton. Remember last year when they tried to enforce the uniform code completely? It lasted, like, a week before everyone started wearing their hoodies anyway. True. Still, it’s a bit awkward. Especially with the party coming up. I heard some whispers about Mrs. Davies patrolling the area around the community centre. No way! That’s insane! Are they seriously going to police a  school party ? What are they expecting, a riot? I don't know, man. Just seems a bit intense. At least it’s a chance to see Chloe. I’ve been meaning to talk to her about that film, ‘Across the Spider-Verse’. Did you see it? Yeah! Absolutely blew my mind. The animation was insane. I keep replaying the pizza scene. It's my new favourite. You know my sister's allergic to strawberries, right? Vaguely… Why? Well, apparently Chloe's bringing a homemade cake for the party. And it's strawberry. We need to warn her before she accidentally poisons my little sister. Honestly, Sarah's drama when she gets an allergic reaction...it's not pretty. Oh, right. Definitely need to do that. Speaking of allergies, remember when David ate that peanut bar at the cricket match? Don't remind me! He went bright red and started wheezing.

Honestly, this road is a nightmare. I swear, they designed it specifically to test your patience. And all for five minutes’ worth of saving on petrol. Dramatic as ever, Liv. It’s a bit bumpy, yeah, but it's certainly not the M25 on a Friday afternoon. And it  is  faster, objectively. Just embrace the wobble. Embrace the wobble? Aye, easy for you to say, Mr. Smooth-Ride. You're sat in yer fancy car, probably got heated seats and lumbar support. I’m practically bouncing out of me seat! You wouldn’t last five minutes on a bike on this road. Okay, point taken about the lumbar support. But you know I've been getting back into cycling, right? Remember that new trail I was telling you about down near St Albans? Vaguely. Something about a converted railway line? Sounds fancy. Not proper cycling, like scraping your knees on gravel and battling a headwind. That's cycling. It has some gravel sections! And the headwind is… challenging. Seriously though, it’s a really nice route. Long, but mostly flat. Perfect for building back up stamina. I was thinking of heading out Saturday. Fancy joining me? Saturday? Don’t be daft. I’ve got that data validation for the new corpus deadlines looming. It’s likely gonna take up me whole weekend. Besides, a Saturday ride means getting up at the crack of dawn, doesn’t it? I’d rather face a grumpy database than a grumpy alarm clock. Come on. You need to de-stress. All that database wrangling can’t be good for you. Think of it as… corporate wellness. Fresh air, exercise... building resilience. Resilience against what? Potholes? I’m already resilient against potholes, thanks to this road trip. Besides, I'm watching the England cricket. It's the second test! Oh, please don't start with the cricket. You know how I feel about it. All standing around waiting for something to happen. Don’t be like that! It’s tactical! It’s strategic! It’s...well, it involves a lot of standing and waiting, but it’s  important  standing and waiting. And England's looking good! Root's batting like a dream. Root  always  looks like he’s batting like a dream. He’s stubbornly consistent. I’d rather be out on my bike, actually  doing  something. Feel the wind in my face, you know? You and your wind!

Right, okay, so Golden Dragon or Happy Wok? It's the age-old question. Ooh, Happy Wok, definitely. Golden Dragon's noodles are always so…gloopy. Remember last time? I swear I could’ve used them to patch a hole in the wall. Gloopy is the perfect word! And their sweet and sour sauce is just intensely yellow and vaguely artificial. Happy Wok’s actually respectable. They don't skimp on the vegetables, either. See? I knew you’d agree. Golden Dragon is just… disappointing. Okay, Happy Wok it is. What are we thinking? Usual suspects? I’m feeling adventurous tonight. Less usual, more...experimental. I saw a dish online, "Spicy Sichuan Mapo Tofu," sounded interesting. Mapo Tofu? Seriously? You know I can't handle any spice, right? My mouth starts sweating, I turn red, and I start hiccuping uncontrollably. It's not a pretty sight. Yeah, we remember the incident with the jalapeno popper at that barbeque last summer. Okay, scratch the Mapo Tofu for you, Liv. What about you, Emma? What are you craving? I'll have the Mapo Tofu, then. And maybe some spring rolls. And definitely the plum sauce. Loads of plum sauce. Okay, fine. I'll stick with my reliable Kung Pao Chicken. Extra peanuts, please! And rice, obviously. Loads of rice. I need to counteract the zero spice. Right, and I’m going for the Lemon Chicken. Always a winner. How about starters? Anything else besides the spring rolls? Their seaweed salad is pretty good. Light, refreshing... balances out the fiery tofu. I'm good on starters, thanks. Just the chicken and rice for me. Less to deal with afterwards. Okay, so one Mapo Tofu, spring rolls, plum sauce, Kung Pao Chicken, extra peanuts, rice, and Lemon Chicken. Anything else? Drinks? I'll have a Diet Coke. You? Orange juice for me, please. Right. And I think I’ll have a Coke too. Okay, total comes to… £48.75. That’s ridiculous! £48.75?! For Chinese food? Seriously? Are they sending us gold bullion with each dish? Maybe they’re factoring in the cost of living crisis. Everything’s gone up. I know, but still! Last time it was… significantly less. Okay, let me check the app again, see if there’s a promotional code or anything. “Chinese Food Discount?” "Takeaway Tuesday?" Nope, nothing. Maybe they’ve upped the portion sizes? Unlikely. They’ve always been stingy with the meat in the Kung Pao.

Honestly, Moira, it's just… demoralising, isn't it? The state of the NHS. I was reading a report earlier, about waiting lists… it’s absolutely appalling. Makes you wonder where it's all heading. Tell me about it, Paul. You read the reports, I  live  it. It's worse than the reports even suggest. We’re stretched so thin, it's not even funny. And the politics… don’t even get me started on the politics behind it all. Honestly, I spend half my shift fighting fires and the other half filling out paperwork. It’s draining. I can only imagine. I’ve got a niece, bless her, she had to wait nearly six months for a scan. Six months! For something that needed addressing sooner rather than later. It's deeply concerning. You know, my dad always talked about the NHS with such reverence. It was just… the bedrock of British society, wasn’t it? It  should  be. Still is, in many ways, but... it’s struggling. Used to be you could walk into A&E and get seen quickly. Now? Forget about it. Even for minor things. It’s a lottery. I've seen people in genuine distress just sitting there for hours. And the staff! You must be seeing the impact on your colleagues. All over worked. Oh, it’s breaking them. Burnout is rampant. People are leaving in droves. It's a vicious cycle, really. Fewer staff, more pressure, more people leaving. I’ve got a neighbour, Sarah, she was a physiotherapist. Brilliant woman. Walked out last year. Said she couldn’t take it anymore. Ended up opening a little yoga studio. Says it’s the best decision she ever made. A yoga studio, eh? Sounds rather idyllic compared to the battlefield you’re all facing. I remember lecturing a student last year, doing a dissertation on the social impact of austerity on the NHS. Painful stuff. It’s not just about money, though, is it? It’s about the fundamental  belief  in a public service. Exactly. It’s about valuing people. And right now, I don’t think we do. Thinking about neighbours, speaking of which... you know Mrs. Davies next door? The one with the prize-winning roses? Vaguely. The one who always glares at me if I accidentally park slightly over the line? That's the one. She fell down the stairs last week.

'Alright, Arthur? Bit of a frost this morning, eh? Nearly took me by surprise on my way to the shops. Reckon they’ll be putting the heating on full blast inside, mind you, with everything going on.’ ‘Klaus! Aye, a proper nip in the air. Reminds me of winters when I were a lad. Wouldn’t get a word of complaint outta folk back then, though. 'Appy days, they were. Though cold, like I said.’ ‘Happy days, eh? Can’t quite say I recall a lot of ‘appy days myself, growing up over in Germany. Different sort of cold, mind. Bone-chilling and…quiet. Less shouting, you know? Though, I’ve got to say, Liverpool’s got a certain… vibrancy.’ ‘Vibrancy? That’s one word for it, lad. I’d call it a right carry-on half the time. Still, beats the silence. You read about this business with them police down the road, then? Raidin’ places, makin’ arrests...’ ‘I did. Awful business, isn't it? I hope they’re focusing on those genuinely causing trouble, though. It’s easy for these things to spill over and affect everyone, isn't it? My neighbour, Mrs. Patel, she was absolutely terrified. Said it felt like the 80s again, you know, all the tension. She’s been here twenty years, never caused any bother, and now…’ ‘Twenty years, eh? Just like my sister, Sheila. Over in Bournemouth. Moved down there for a bit of sun, she did. Says she misses Liverpool, though. Says there's nothin’ like a proper chippy and a bit of banter. You ever had a proper scouse chippy, Klaus? The ones with the mushy peas that are actually… mushy? Not those frozen things.’ ‘I’ve made a point of it, Arthur. Can't say I'm a chip connoisseur, but I have definitely sampled a few. The mushy peas  are  something else, though, aren’t they? Speaking of moving, I'm still trying to sort out my daughter's visa. Little troubles with the paperwork, keeps getting delayed. Seems immigration’s a right palaver these days.’ ‘Immigration… Aye. They don't make it easy, do they? My grandson, Liam, he’s gone off with a Polish girl. Lovely lass, she is. But getting the paperwork sorted for her… nightmare. Bureaucracy, eh? Eats you alive. Used to be, you knew everyone round here, kept an eye out for each other.

Honestly, the initial proposal for this new corpus was… ambitious.  Very  ambitious. I mean, tracking conversational drift across social media platforms in real-time? It's a brave new world of data, isn't it? Aye, tell me about it. I’ve been spendin’ me days wrestlin’ with it. The sheer volume is somethin’ else. Tryin' to filter out the bots and the… well, the  nonsense  is a full-time job in itself. It’s a right can o’ worms, darlin’. You're not wrong! I've been looking at user-generated content for a new series of graded readers, and you wouldn't believe some of the phrases people use. It’s like a whole new language sometimes. Makes you question everything you thought you knew about grammar. Well, that’s precisely what we're hoping to capture, isn’t it? Authentic language use, not just what's in textbooks. It’s crucial for materials development – giving learners something realistic to aim for. I was just reviewing the initial annotation guidelines... quite extensive. Absolutely. The granularity is key. But it also raises some fascinating ethical questions, doesn’t it? Especially when dealing with public social media – consent, anonymity… it’s a minefield. I spent a chunk of last week hashing out concerns with the legal team. Exactly! I’m so glad you brought that up, Amelia. It’s been a major headache for me. Getting the ethical clearance was a nightmare, and we’re still working on protocols for handling sensitive data. My US background makes this especially tricky, too – data privacy laws are  very  different. Sounds stressful. I just worry about the impact on real people. Like, will someone’s tweet end up in a textbook and they don't even know? Feels a bit… unsettling. I get that. We're striving for a balance, though. It’s not about exposing individuals; it’s about identifying patterns and trends in language. It's about understanding how language evolves organically. The potential for research is incredible. Think about tracking the adoption of new slang terms, tracing shifts in grammatical structures over time… It could revolutionise our understanding of how language changes. Precisely. Think of the data we can glean about regional variations in online communication. We could map dialectal shifts in real-time. My postgraduate dissertation focused on exactly that, you know – how social media is blurring regional boundaries. That’s fascinating, Amelia!

...and honestly, the sheer volume of streaming services these days is bewildering. You’re spending more time  choosing  something to watch than actually, you know, watching it. It’s like a second job, isn't it? Proper palm-sweating decision-making. Tell me about it! My wife’s fallen down a deep, dark hole of Korean dramas. It’s fascinating, to be fair, but she spends ages scrolling. Ends up watching ten minutes of something and deciding it's not for her. Hours gone. I've tried suggesting things, obviously, but then I'm accused of not appreciating the nuance of the storytelling. Hull's a different world when it comes to appreciating a good drama, let me tell you. Nuance! That’s the word they always throw around. I was trying to explain the concept of 'bath chair chic' to my niece the other day. Trying to describe the aesthetic – slightly faded grandeur, a hint of eccentricity, the overall feeling of comfortable disinterest… She just looked at me blankly. Said it sounded like a washing machine advertisement. Oh, bless her! That’s brilliant. You tried to inflict proper Somerset on her. See, that’s the thing about trying to explain culture, isn’t it? It's inherently… unexplainable. Like trying to describe the feeling of a proper Yorkshire pudding. It’s  got  to be experienced. Exactly! It's the backstory, the context. It's why I'm sticking with my PhD rather than trying to disseminate academic papers to the general public. The complexity is lost. My students… well, bless their hearts, they often want me to summarise entire centuries of intellectual thought in bullet points. Don’t get me started on teaching! When I was doing guest lectures at the university, I had a student ask me, genuinely, "So, is Latin still useful?" Like, I didn't know whether to laugh or weep. I ended up saying, "Well, you'll be able to read ancient Roman graffiti, I suppose." Oh, that’s wonderful! You've no choice but to develop a wicked sense of humour, do you? I’ve been trying to teach myself some Italian, you know. Mostly so I can actually order food without embarrassing myself when I go to Rome next year. Italian! That's ambitious. I've always wanted to learn Spanish. It just seems… so much easier than anything else. Plus, the cultural richness!

Right then, let’s have a proper look at this, shall we? Grandad’s been using a fair bit of electric, hasn’t he? And Gran, your tea bags are getting a bit pricey too, love. Yeah, Grandad was watching those nature documentaries all week. Apparently, there’s this amazing otter family near Selby. He was glued to it. Otters are marvellous creatures! Reminds me of when we used to go crabbing down at Bridlington. Used to get a right load of ‘em, we did. Not like now, all fenced in and posh. Aye, Bridlington was somethin’ back then. Proper seaside town, it was. Not all these… theme park things now. Alright, alright, reminiscing is lovely, but the electricity bill needs tackling. Young Liam, you could maybe remind your Grandad to switch the telly off at the wall when he’s finished watching his otters? Bit of a saver, that would be. I will, Auntie Carol. But he already forgets to turn off the lights. It's a constant battle, honestly. He’s getting on, you know. Memory ain't what it used to be. Used to remember every single bus route in Hull, backwards and forwards. Now… not so much. I know, Gran. It's just… we don't want the bill to be bigger than my mortgage payment! And it’ll be lovely if he can help out a little, even if it's just a small thing. So, Liam, maybe a gentle reminder before bedtime too? Anything you can do? Okay, yeah, I’ll say something. Although, he’ll probably just tell me I’m wasting my breath. He’s got that stubborn streak, you know. Aye, he's always been a stubborn one. Remember when he argued with Mrs. Higgins about the placement of her roses? Went on for weeks, that did. Oh, I do! She ended up moving them just to shut him up! A right cheek, she was. See? He's still his old self. Right, moving on. The washing machine's playing up again. I think it needs a new belt. Can't you just Google how to fix it, Auntie Carol? There are tons of videos on YouTube. And you think  you  should be fixing the washing machine, Mr. Sixth Form? You’ve got your own studies to worry about, love. Besides, I’ll have a look, but if it’s serious, it’ll need a proper engineer.

Honestly, look at this light, Liam. It’s just… perfect for photos. I wish I'd taken more when we were wandering through that tea plantation earlier. You were too busy trying not to trip over the uneven ground. Remember nearly taking out that poor farmer with your flailing arms? That was a moment! He seemed remarkably unperturbed, actually. Very zen. I should have asked him to pose with me. Think of the caption: “Lost in translation, near disaster, but the tea was lovely.” You and your captions. You'll drive social media crazy. Speaking of photos, did you manage to download those from Sarah's wedding? I've been looking forward to seeing them. Almost! They’re pinging over now. The Wi-Fi is, as always, delightfully temperamental. But I think I got most of the good ones. Sarah looked absolutely radiant. Remember how stressed she was beforehand? Vaguely. It was a whirlwind of floral arrangements and seating chart dramas. I mostly remember consuming an alarming amount of canapés. Did David give a speech? He did! A surprisingly emotional one, too. He teared up a couple of times. Apparently, he’d been practicing it for weeks, but he still forgot half of it. Typical David. He always was a bit of a sentimental mess. I'm glad they're happy. Speaking of friends, have you heard from Emily lately? I was thinking about her yesterday. It must be nearly a year since she moved to Australia, isn't it? Last I heard, she was loving the surfing lessons, though she complained about the size of the spiders. Apparently, they're massive. Australian spiders! No thanks. I'm perfectly content with the pigeons and the occasional rogue squirrel we get back home. How's the teaching going? Still enjoying Medieval Literature? It’s… good. The students are engaged this semester, thankfully. We're tackling Chaucer at the moment. I’m trying to make it a bit more accessible, less dry dusty stuff. You know, showing them that it's funny and relevant! Good for you. Trying to connect the past to the present is always key. I'm battling with a particularly resistant group of undergraduates on the Romantic poets. They seem to think Byron was just a pretty face. Well, he was rather handsome, wasn’t he? But you're right, they need to dig deeper. Perhaps a lecture on scandalous behaviour and aristocratic excesses would do the trick?

Ugh, mornings. Seriously, why do they even exist? My head feels like it's been through a tumble dryer. Tell me about it! Saturday night was… intense, wasn’t it? Remember when Liam tried to do that ridiculous dance move in The Phoenix? I’m still cringing. Oh my god, the worm! The absolute worm! He looked like he was wrestling an invisible octopus. And then he tripped over Sarah’s foot! Proper chaos. Honestly. I was trying so hard not to laugh, but it was just… a lot. My nan would've been mortified. She doesn't approve of much dancing, let alone questionable worm attempts. My mum would’ve been mortified by the sheer volume of VKs I consumed. She's always going on about my liver, innit. “Think of your poor liver, Chloe!” as if I haven’t heard it a million times. Same. My mum's obsessed with my health. Reminds me constantly I need to be eating more greens and less… well, everything else we were consuming last night. Speaking of which, did you see that new vegan place that opened up near campus? Proper good looking online. No, haven't! Is it pricey though? Because my student budget is screaming at me already. I spent way too much on that sparkly top last week. Thinking I should start posting some of my outfits online, maybe. Could be a little side hustle, you know? Yeah, that’s a good shout! You’ve got a good eye. I’ve been trying to get into exercising properly, but it’s so hard to motivate myself. I downloaded one of those fitness apps, but I just end up scrolling through TikTok instead. I know, right? It’s a vicious cycle. I tried running last week. Managed about five minutes before I gave up and got a donut. My dog, Winston, was giving me serious side-eye. He’s judging my life choices, I swear. Winston sounds adorable! My cousin just got a puppy, a little Frenchie. Apparently, they're complete divas. My auntie’s constantly posting pictures of it. It's cute, but a bit much. Honestly, social media. Don’t even get me started. Everyone's lives look so perfect. Little do they know, most of us are fuelled by pasta and regret. Totally! Remember that bloke, Ben, from our history class? Always posting these perfectly curated pictures of himself at the gym.

Right, so Nan’s coming next Saturday, officially. She booked the train tickets this morning. Which means… Operation Hunsonby Grandmother Hospitality needs to be in full swing. Dad's offered to pick her up from Penrith, right? Aye, he did. Though, you know, he'll probably spend half an hour complaining about the state of the train station. Honestly, the man. Standard Dad. You can set your watch by it. Still, it’s good he’s offering. Less for us to worry about. Are you getting enough peas, love? You’re looking a bit pale. I’m fine, thanks, Dad. Just thinking about the logistics. I was thinking we could clear out the spare room properly, give it a good dusting. And maybe Nana would appreciate a vase of flowers? She loves daffodils, doesn't she? Daffodils would be lovely, yes. Though, honestly, she’ll mostly just want to sit and complain about the price of tea. It's a ritual, isn’t it? It is, isn’t it? Still, a little complaining is part of the charm. Right, flowers – check. Dusting – check. We need to think about evening entertainment. Nan isn't really up for walking around the lake anymore, is she? No, her knees aren’t what they used to be. We could put on a bit of FIFA, she does enjoy watching. Although, last time, she was shouting at the referee for a rather lengthy period. Oh, she was! Absolutely ballistic about that penalty decision. Said it was "a disgrace to the beautiful game!" To think, she used to knit for me, not critique professional footballers. Times change, I suppose. Exactly. But seriously, FIFA is a good option. Or maybe we could get one of those old black and white films she likes. Those musicals with Fred Astaire? Fred Astaire it is then. Less chance of her verbally attacking the television. Although, knowing her, she'll probably critique his dancing. She'll find something to pick at, I guarantee it. Though, remember that episode last Christmas when she accused young Liam, our neighbour’s son, of deliberately cheating at Monopoly? Oh, God, yes! Saying he was using "dark forces" to stop her buying Park Place! He was only seven years old, love! You can’t blame a child for a bit of strategic property acquisition. It’s just business. Strategic manipulation, more like! Honestly, it was all a bit much.

Honestly, you wouldn't believe the day I’ve had. Mrs. Peterson’s cat decided to climb the curtains again. Took me a good half an hour to coax it down. And then, just as I was getting her settled, the bin men didn’t turn up! Strikes again, you know? Makes everything so much harder. Bin strikes! They’re relentless, aren’t they? It’s a nightmare for everyone. At least you’re used to the chaos, being a care assistant. Chaos is an understatement, Liam. It’s more like organised mayhem sometimes. Anyway, talking about things causing mayhem... remember when Dad tripped and nearly took the laptop with him last week? Nearly did! Saved it at the last minute, I did. Bit of a fright, though. Wouldn’t want to break that thing. Costs a fortune these days. Still, wouldn’t mind a new one myself, you know. This ancient one barely works. Can’t even get a decent signal. So, Dad, are you alright? You seemed a bit… preoccupied earlier. Did you remember to charge your phone? Phone’s fine. Just… remembering things. It’s funny, isn't it? How your memory plays tricks on you. Used to know every road in London like the back of my hand. Now… Don’t dwell on it, Dad. You're still brilliant at remembering obscure facts about the Victorian era. Remember that time you told us about penny dreadfuls? Oh, yes! And the one about the pigeon post? Absolutely fascinating, albeit a bit random. These afternoon teas are always lovely. It’s nice to have everyone together. You’ve put on a lovely spread, Liam. Though, honestly, I still think we should stick to tap water. All this bottled stuff is such a con. That's a debate for the ages, isn’t it? I read an article the other day claiming some bottled water is just filtered tap water! It's all marketing. Speaking of debates, anyone brave enough to try that didgeridoo I found in a charity shop? A didgeridoo? Good heavens! Sounds like a swarm of bees trapped in a tube. No thank you. I’ll stick to my tea. I’d love to see you try, Dad! It's probably a good way to keep your lungs strong, though. Do you ever think about how different colours make you feel? Like, what colour is happiness? Ooh, good question!

Honestly, this coffee is  amazing . Best I've had since leaving Bury, that's for sure. Better than a lot back home, if I'm being honest. Did you catch the United game last night? Such a nail-biter! Oh, dear, no, I missed it. I was trying to track down a lesser spotted woodpecker in the park. No luck, sadly. The results? Please tell me we didn't lose. We drew. 2-2. Late equaliser. Typical, really. Gave everyone a fright. But hey, a point’s a point, eh? It’s just…sometimes I feel so far away from it all. Even just the football. It’s silly, I know, but it hits you. You know? Homesickness sets in. I understand completely. It's that feeling of detached observation, isn't it? Like you’re watching someone else’s life. I get that, especially this time of year. It’s the SAD kicking in, I think. Poland isn’t exactly bathed in sunshine at the moment. Tell me about it! I’m trying to compensate with Vitamin D supplements, but it’s not the same as a proper walk in the countryside. Speaking of, I had a student today, young Jakub, completely panicking about his IELTS exam next week. He's worried he won't pass. Oh, poor love. It's such a pressure cooker, those exams. Do you think he'll be alright? I do, I do. I’ve been drilling him on the speaking section. He’s a bright lad, just needs to calm down. It's just... you feel a bit responsible, doesn’t it? Like their future rests on your ability to teach them the subjunctive mood. Absolutely. It’s a huge responsibility. I remember when I was teaching…a lifetime ago. Did you know there’s a farm just outside Tarnow recruiting seasonal workers? Picking strawberries, apparently. Though I can't imagine it’s terribly glamorous. Really? That’s interesting. I might tell my friend, Liam. He's been moaning about his job at the warehouse. He's a proper outdoorsy type, loves his dogs. He’s got two Labradors, you know. Absolute hooligans, but he adores them. Dogs are the best, aren't they? Give you unconditional love. I occasionally dog-sit for my niece. It's a welcome distraction. Did you see that article in  The Guardian  about the proliferation of doom-scrolling?

Honestly, the most ridiculous thing happened at work today. We're prepping for this massive product launch, right? Millions riding on it. And apparently, someone shipped the wrong shade of blue dye. Millions of units potentially ruined! Aye, reet bad luck, that! Sounds like proper chaos. You’d think with all the computers they’ve got, they’d get things like that right. What were you doing when you found out? Blue? Seriously? You know, I spend my days lifting concrete blocks. It’s not glamorous, but at least I'm pretty sure the grey is always the same shade of grey. No room for error there, eh? I was doing a final quality check, blessedly. Imagine finding out  later ! My boss nearly exploded. He sent a frantic email, all caps, demanding to know how this could happen. I just wanted to hide under my desk. Oh, I know the feeling. My boss at the conference centre is like that when something goes slightly off-kilter. Did you manage to sort it? Eventually. There’s a small batch already printed with the right colour, and they're rushing a correction order. Fingers crossed. It was a stressful few hours, though. Speaking of stressful… how’s the dating scene treating you, Chloe? Still swiping endlessly? Don't even  start , Liv. It's a right mess, it is. I've been on, like, five dates in the past month, and they've all been… underwhelming. One bloke spent the entire evening talking about his stamp collection. Stamps, Liv! Stamps? Seriously? Maybe he's a secret millionaire stamp collector! You never know. That’s what I said to my mum. She said I was being silly. But honestly, who wants to hear about perforated paper for two hours? Okay, that  is  awful. You deserve better. What are you looking for, generally? Someone who can hold a conversation, for a start! Someone who’s not afraid of a bit of banter. And ideally, someone who doesn't collect stamps. Is that too much to ask? Don't knock his stamps! They might be worth a fortune. Listen, there's a lads' night next Saturday. You’re coming, right? Might meet someone. Lads’ night? With the rugby-loving lot? I think I’d rather spend the evening with my stamp collection. Don’t be like that! It’s just a bit of fun. And you never know who might be tagging along.

…and honestly, the supervision’s been a bit of a nightmare this term. Professor Davies seems to think my chapter on phonological adaptation is revolutionary. Revolutionary! It’s… it’s competent, really. Just competent. He keeps suggesting I bring in Chomsky, which, you know, feels a bit…forced. Davies, eh? Classic. Sounds like academic posturing to me. Happens all the time. Reminds me of that conference in Chengdu. One guy insisted his research on panda vocalizations was unveiling the secrets of the universe. Pandas! Speaking of which, did you see that bit about the new cubs at Whipsnade? Bit of a marmalade explosion, apparently. No, didn't! Wonderful news though. Pandas are brilliant. Think about the landscape they inhabit in China – completely different from anything we have here. Dense bamboo forests, misty mountains... makes Devon look a bit… tame. Tame is putting it kindly. Remember that drive we did through Dartmoor once? Nearly lost the car. Didn’t see another soul for hours. So many narrow lanes, hedges right up against you…felt like driving through a green tunnel. Absolutely. And the salt on the chips in those little seaside towns! So much more generous than down south. Always felt like the Yorkshire chip shops were secretly holding back, though. Precisely! It’s a crime, it is. It wouldn't go amiss in Bodmin, either. Anyway, Chengdu reminded me of teaching TEFL over there. The kids were brilliant, so hungry to learn. I had this one student, Xiao Wei, whose English was astonishingly good, but he couldn't stop correcting  my  pronunciation. Ah, the trials of a TEFL teacher. Always loved hearing those tiny corrections. Do you still keep in touch with any of your Chinese friends? Not as much as I should. WeChat’s become a bit of a black hole, hasn't it? So many messages, so little time. Xiao Wei's actually working in Paris now, apparently. Says it’s the only place to go for decent coconut cake. Paris, posh! Imagine, Parisian coconut cake. You'd have to try it. Speaking of Paris... remember that terrible tourist trap we got caught in near the Louvre? All those little trinkets shoved in your face? Don't remind me. Thankfully, we managed to escape with only a miniature Eiffel Tower. It ended up as a paperweight for my aunt. So, you were saying about Chengdu... Did you ever get a chance to see anything beyond the conference?

Honestly, this is mental. Absolutely mental. Four hours on a motorway…four hours! And for what? To listen to Aunt Maureen drone on about her prize-winning marrows for the next three? You're exaggerating, love. They’re good marrows. And she’s been looking forward to this all year. Think of Uncle George, he’ll be chuffed to see everyone. Chuffed? He’ll probably fall asleep in the gravy boat again. Remember last Christmas? I was trying not to laugh, but it was hard! And Aunt Maureen will be trying to get me to knit him a new one. As if I’ve got time to be knitting gravy boat cozies! I'm drowning in data as it is. Well, the project at work  is  pretty demanding. But seriously, a few hours with family isn't the worst thing in the world. Besides, you haven't seen them since… well, since Christmas, hasn't it? Aye, too true. Just… all these traditions. The forced small talk, the endless cups of lukewarm tea... it's exhausting. Do you think they’ll ask about the flat again? “Still renting, love? When are you going to buy?” They’ll probably mention it, yeah. But don’t let it get to you. You know they just worry. They want you settled. And you will be, eventually. Trust me, the property market'll calm down. "Eventually" feels like a million miles away. I was looking at that little cottage near Durham, remember? The one with the garden? It’s completely out of reach now. Every time I check, the price has gone up another five grand. It's just… bleak, isn’t it? It’s frustrating, definitely. But look, we're making progress. Remember how much  those  places were costing last year? It’s a market, it fluctuates. And you're doing brilliantly with your job. That’s a massive step in the right direction. Speaking of which, did you remember to email me those summaries from the corpus? I need them for the presentation on Friday. Oh, blast! I completely forgot. I meant to do that before we left. Sorry! They're on my laptop, alright? I'll get them over to you tonight, swear. Massive apologies. I’m such a scatterbrain sometimes. No worries, honestly. I’m used to it. You’re busy. Just prioritize it, yeah? It’s really important. Friday’s presentation could make a difference for the new design phase.

Honestly, I'm still reeling from last week. That whole debacle with Mark... it was just… exhausting. Aye, poor lass. I can't believe he actually said that to you at the gallery opening. Right in front of everyone, weren't it? Right cheek, that man. I’d have slapped him. Not literally, mind, but... you know. Slapping anyone isn’t the answer, Millie. Bit extreme. Though, yeah, what he said was pretty rough, wasn’t it, Chloe? Extreme or not, Liam, it felt pretty awful in the moment. It felt like everything I’d compromised on, all the effort I put into trying to make things work… just dismissed. He basically implied my job was irrelevant, that it just got in the way of him enjoying his ‘real’ life. Right, that’s rotten. Absolute rotten. You're a Production Controller! That’s a proper important job, innit? Me mum’s always saying, “It’s not all about fancy galleries, love. Someone needs to  make  things happen.” Thanks, Millie. That’s... actually really nice to hear. Especially coming from someone who understands what it’s like feeling undervalued. Your dad’s business always seemed to be your whole life, didn't it? Aye, proper hard work, that business was. But it was ours, weren’t it? And having a bit of your own thing is important. Listen, are you alright though? You look a bit peaky, to be honest. Not that Cambridge air, is it? I’ve actually been feeling a bit under the weather all week. I think I’m getting a cold. It’s probably stress related, if I’m honest. The whole Mark thing did a number on me. You should get it checked out. Mum's always going on about how quickly colds can turn into something worse. Especially with her asthma. I know, I know. But I've been so busy… and then dealing with Mark... everything just felt monumental. I didn't have time to care about a sniffly nose. Champion, you are, lookin' after yerself. But don't you go pushing yourself too hard, love. Honestly, sometimes you gotta admit when yer knackered. It's alright to rest. Me Nan always used to say, "A bit of fettle won’t kill ya, but it’ll make ye better." Your Nan sounds like a wise woman, Millie. Seriously, Chloe. Don’t neglect it. And Liam’s mum’s right, it  can  turn into something nasty.

Honestly, Liam is driving me  mad . Liam? From the community outreach project? What’s he done now? He seemed alright when we met him for that initial briefing. Alright? He’s actively sabotaging my attempts to get the presentation finished! He’s insistent on using Comic Sans for the headings. Comic Sans! Do you  believe  it? I tried to explain that it’s unprofessional, it screams amateur, it actively detracts from the serious nature of the project... and he just winked and said, “Adds a bit of personality, doesn’t it?” Oh, Liam. Some people just cling to their fonts like lifelines. You know, I had a patient last week who insisted on being addressed as ‘Your Majesty.’ It's the little things, isn't it? It's horrifying! It’s a multi-million pound programme, and he wants it to look like a five-year-old designed it. And then he backtracks when the senior manager looks at him funny. It’s so frustrating watching him try and cover his tracks. I’m practically pulling my hair out. Sounds stressful. You're working way too hard. Are you getting any sleep? You look a bit washed out. Not really, no. I'm constantly checking emails, re-doing his sections, trying to anticipate where he's going to mess up next. It's exhausting. I could really do with a day off, honestly. And maybe a new Liam. Well, the day off is more achievable, I think. Listen, about the Liam situation... have you tried just laying out  why  Comic Sans isn't suitable in a proper, formal email? No winking, no joking, just a bullet-pointed list of reasons. Sometimes a bit of cold, hard logic is all it takes. I considered it. But he'd just claim I’m being “restrictive” and “squashing his creative spirit.” He's  amazing  at playing the victim. Right, a specialist. Okay. So, other than Liam’s font-related crimes, how are things at work? Anything positive? Actually, yeah. Sarah from HR is being really supportive, which is good. She kept saying she’s seen this sort of thing before with Liam, and to just document everything meticulously. Apparently, he has a history of... creative disagreements. Good! Documentation is your friend. You’re doing the right thing, keeping a record. So, on a less stressful note, how are things with Mark? Still…quiet? Yeah.

Right, so, I was thinking about this story Mrs. Davies was telling in class today – about the Green Knight. It’s quite fascinating, isn’t it? The whole concept of a knight who isn’t what he seems… a test of bravery, a punishment, a reward… Was he naughty, Mummy? Was the Green Knight naughty? That’s a really good question, sweetheart. In a way, yes. He broke a promise, didn’t he? But he also brought a challenge, a chance for the knights of the Round Table to prove themselves. It's complicated, isn't it? Sometimes, things that seem bad at first can lead to something good. Like… like when you accidentally spill your juice, and we have to clean it up, but then we get a lovely, tidy table. Is that soup, Mummy? Does it have carrots? Yes, darling, it’s carrot and coriander soup. And it's very good for you – gives you lots of energy for fighting dragons! Speaking of which… Do you both know about Robin Hood? Yes! He steals from the rich and gives to the poor! He's good! But stealing is bad, isn’t it? It  is  bad, generally. But Robin Hood was stealing from people who had  far  too much and weren’t using it fairly. He was trying to make things more equal. That’s what makes him a hero in the stories – he was doing something that seemed wrong to help people who were struggling. It’s about intention, isn’t it? He had good intentions, even if his actions weren't always… entirely legal. So, like when I share my toys with Leo, even though I really want to play with them all by myself? Exactly! Sharing is a good thing, even though it can be a bit hard sometimes. It makes someone else happy, and that makes  you  feel happy too. Now, have you two ever heard of Jack the Giant Slayer? Yes! He fought a giant! Did he win? He did! But it wasn’t just about strength, was it? Jack had to be clever. He tricked the giant. Sometimes, being kind and clever is better than being big and strong. The giant was… well, he wasn't very nice to people, was he? He was greedy and scary. That's the opposite of good, isn’t it? What about witches? Are witches good or bad?

Right, so, the school trip. It's actually happening then, isn't it? Little Anon's off making a film. Bit nerve-wracking, sending them off for the whole day. It is, a little, but they’re so excited! Miss Davies seems really organised, and it’s a fantastic opportunity for them. They’ve been planning it for ages. Though, I still worry about them. Film! Film! Click! Click! Action! See? Total movie stars already. How’s her leg today, by the way? Still sore from that fall at the park? It is a bit tender, yes. I've given her some Calpol, but she’s still hopping around like a little rabbit sometimes. She says it’s her ‘movie star hopping’. Look! Big camera! Brilliant! That's fantastic, love. Really captured the essence of filmmaking. Listen, about the gym... I’m trying to actually  use  the membership. Thinking of hitting the treadmills tomorrow morning, before work. Need to shift this… It wouldn't do you any harm! I’ve been going a couple of times a week. It's a good way to blow off some steam after a long day of marking. They've got that new virtual reality running thing, have you tried it? No, what's that then? Sounds a bit daft. It’s actually pretty good! You wear these goggles, and it feels like you’re running through different landscapes – a rainforest, a Parisian street… even a moonscape! It distracts you from the fact you’re just pounding away on a treadmill. A moonscape, eh? Tempting. Though, I’d probably just end up tripping over my own feet while pretending to be an astronaut. Speaking of temptations... did you manage to resist the doughnut shop yesterday? Don’t even  ask . I walked past, and the smell alone nearly did me in. I got a single one though, a raspberry ripple. Just one. One? That’s discipline, right there. I nearly bought a dozen. It's the weather, I swear. This mildness is messing with my willpower. It’s not properly cold, so I don't  feel  like I need to earn my treats. It’s odd, isn’t it? Usually, this time of year, it’s freezing, and you're craving soup and a hearty roast. But it’s been strangely… pleasant. Though, I am a little worried it’ll get chilly at night. We need to make sure Anon has an extra blanket for the film trip.

Honestly, Bernard, this rain. It’s been relentless this week. Makes you feel a bit…damp in the soul, doesn’t it? Tell me about it, Arthur. Drove down from Hove, and it was like navigating a car wash the whole way. Brighton’s always a bit wetter than Sussex, though, isn't it? Good thing we chose a spot with a view of the pier, at least. Trying to pretend the grey isn't seeping into my bones. Speaking of bones… I had a check-up last week. The doctor poked and prodded and generally made me feel like a rusty hinge. Cholesterol’s a bit up, apparently. He suggested more exercise. More exercise? You, Arthur? You’re practically cemented to a chair grading essays. What's he suggesting, a marathon? Something like that. He suggested a brisk walk every day. Said it would do me good. I’m half tempted to join that Green Party walking group they’ve started up. Gets you out, meets people… and saves the planet, apparently. The Green Party, eh? You and your idealism! I'm worried about them, myself. Heard on the radio that their latest proposal about business rates is going to cripple small businesses. Absolutely crippling! I mean, I’m just trying to keep my little workshop afloat. Can’t afford another tax hike. It is a tricky balance, isn't it? I understand their concerns about the environment, but you can't just choke off the lifeblood of the economy. What about young people trying to find jobs? It's hard enough as it is. My niece, Emily - remember? The one who studied graphic design? - she’s still bouncing between freelance gigs. Emily? Good girl, Emily. Yes, I remember. Finding a decent job these days… it’s a lottery. I've got a lad working for me, Jake. Bright lad, wants to learn, but finding someone willing to pay a decent wage, especially for someone starting out… it’s a struggle. I'm trying to give him a good start, you know? More than I had when I was his age. Absolutely. It's a different world now. Speaking of different worlds, have you been to any of those boot sales down by Devil's Dyke recently? They've got some truly bizarre things. I picked up a rather fetching ceramic owl last week. My daughter found a vintage record player.

Honestly, this cider's nae as good as back home. They do a proper bramble cider in Sunderland, you know? None of this… watered-down stuff. You always say that, love. Every pub outside of the North East, apparently, serves inferior cider. It’s a running joke now. But, hey, at least the atmosphere’s decent. Much better than that stuffy academic bar. Aye well, it's a pub! You’re supposed to be able to relax, not feel like you need a PhD to order a drink. So, you were saying about your research? Still stuck on those blasted orchids? Pretty much. It’s fascinating, don’t get me wrong, but proving the link between their root microbiome and drought resilience is proving… difficult. It's a lot of tiny, invisible things, and they don't exactly shout their secrets. It's just, the funding is predicated on specific, demonstrable results, and I'm feeling the pressure. Sounds stressful. Mind you, my job’s having its own dramas. We’re doing this deep dive into consumer behaviour regarding… sustainable fashion. It’s a minefield already. Turns out most folks are happy to  say  they care, but actually changing their habits? Forget about it. Right? Like, the performative activism. "I recycled this cardboard box!" while simultaneously ordering everything with prime delivery from Amazon. Exactly! And the greenwashing is ridiculous. It's like, "This t-shirt is 80% organic cotton… and 20% made from plastic bottles fished out of the ocean by underpaid labourers in Bangladesh.” It's just… a lot. I was reading about Patagonia recently, and they're actually trying to  discourage  consumption. Now  that's  a brave move. Financially, anyway. You could almost see Elon Musk doing something like that… if he wasn’t so obsessed with going to Mars. Don’t even get me started on that man. Honestly, he's like a toddler with a gigantic bank account and a serious attention deficit. It's just… exhausting watching him. Reminds me a bit of Trump, come to think of it. Just crapping on about whatever’s popped into his head. There's definitely a shared strain of bluster, that's true. Though, Trump's antics had more tangible, and frankly worrying, political consequences. It’s weird, isn’t it? How someone can build a whole following on just… saying things. Aye, it is. It's like the whole system's lost the plot.

Honestly, the light here is just  divine , isn’t it? It makes you want to paint - though I’m hopeless, of course. You’d have more luck, wouldn't you, with your art history background? I make a better audience than an artist, love. Though I did once attempt a watercolour landscape of the Lake District. Let’s just say it resembled a very confused pile of green and brown. Did you manage to finish marking those essays on Victorian literature? They looked brutal when you were knee-deep in them last night. Nearly. Just one left. And honestly, the level of analysis was… varying. One student actually argued that  Bleak House  was a subtle commentary on the importance of interior design. I almost choked on my tea. Goodness. Well, that's certainly... ambitious. Better than that student I had last week who claimed Hamlet was just about wanting a really good sandwich. A sandwich? Really? Apparently, his reasoning was that Hamlet's constant procrastination stemmed from a deep-seated craving he couldn't satisfy. Pure genius in its own, warped way. It’s days like those that make you question the entire education system, isn’t it? And remind you why we need to encourage critical thinking, even if it's dressed up as sandwich-based philosophy. Exactly! And it’s not just the analysis, it's their engagement with the material. I showed them that documentary about the orcas off the coast of Scotland, remember? The one about their social structures and how they learn their hunting techniques from their mothers? Vaguely. The one you were so excited about? You were practically vibrating with enthusiasm. I know! And barely a ripple of interest. Honestly, killer whales! They’re utterly fascinating. The complexity of their communication, the matriarchal societies… it's a world away from the tragic love and loss of Dickens. But equally compelling. People are desensitized, I think. They’re bombarded with… well, with the frankly ridiculous levels of violence on television these days. I watched that new crime drama last night – the amount of actual  shooting … I felt slightly numb by the end. Precisely! It’s just constant. It normalizes it. And then they’re surprised when they don’t have an emotional response to something truly remarkable like, say, a pod of orcas hunting together. Speaking of surprising… did you see that article about the council trying to evict that group of squatters from the old textile mill?

So, you’ve actually been  running  a hostel, Liam? That’s quite a change of pace from, well, anything I knew about you! I mean, Costessey isn't exactly teeming with backpackers, is it? No, no it ain't. It were a bit of a… impulse, really. My brother, Arthur, he’d been runnin’ it down in Norwich, but his arthritis got the better of 'im. Said he couldn’t be lugging suitcases anymore. Asked if I’d give it a go. Needed somethin’ to do, didn't I? Ten years of nothin’ but daytime telly gets a bit wearyin'. And how’s it going, Liam? Are you enjoying it? You always were a people person, even if you did hide it behind that Norfolk reserve. It's got its moments. Right enough. The youngsters, mind, they’re mostly alright. Bit loud some evenings, but mostly respectful. Some of 'em are proper clever, too. One lad, from Japan, built a little robot out of scrap he found! Proper little engineer, he were. A robot? Really? Now that’s impressive! What kind of robot was it? Oh, just a wee thing. Wheels, arms that moved. He said he was working on artificial intelligence. Fancy that, innit? All this science… You wouldn’t think someone who used to spend their days watchin' the telly would suddenly be surrounded by budding scientists! Still, it must be fascinating. I used to have all sorts of children through my childminding business. Some were just delightful, little sponges soaking up everything. You were a childminder, Margaret? I didn't know that! Any little geniuses amongst them? Oh, I wouldn’t say geniuses, but there was certainly a couple who showed real spark. One was fascinated by engines, bless him. Always taking apart his toy cars and trying to put them back together. It rarely worked, mind you, but the enthusiasm! Reminds me a bit of your robot lad, Liam. That reminds me of my father. He worked in an abattoir, you know. Terrible job, really. The smell… but he were always tinkering. Fixin’ things. He’d take apart an old engine, just to see how it worked. Said he learned more about engineering fixin' things than he ever did in school. Hardworking man, my dad. My mum and dad had shops, back-to-back. My dad had a butcher's shop, actually, not far from the abattoir, in fact.

Honestly, Mark, I'm feeling a bit defeated this evening. This lecturer's course… the sheer volume of papers with, well,  questionable  academic literacy is just astounding. It's not that they lack intelligence, you can see that glimmers through, but expressing complex ideas with clarity and precision? It's a real struggle. Yeah, I can imagine. You've always had a knack for spotting those little weaknesses in argumentation – a really sharp eye for logic. I’ve noticed it in your feedback, too. What’s giving you the most trouble? The structure, the referencing, or something else? It’s a combination, really. The referencing is consistently patchy – occasionally brilliant, then suddenly citing a blog post as primary source material. The structure… it’s like they have a point to make, a genuine insight even, but it’s buried under layers of waffle. And the vocabulary… they overuse these fancy, vaguely impressive words, but they don't really  mean  them. It’s… performative, rather than substantive. So, a case of trying to sound clever rather than being clear? We see that a lot, don't we? Especially with students who are new to higher education. It's easy to fall into that trap when you’re bombarded with all that academic jargon. It's a confidence thing, I reckon. Possibly. But these are postgraduate students, Mark! You’d think they’d have a better handle on it by now. It reminded me, oddly, of my time working recruitment. Recruitment? Seriously? You never mentioned that! I didn't, did I? Before I went into teaching, I was a recruiter for about five years. Mostly in the financial sector. You wouldn't think it has much to do with academic literacy, but it does, actually. How so? Recruiters are all about selling, aren’t they? Exactly! And selling, at its core, is about persuasion. You’re trying to convince someone – a potential employer, or a candidate – that you're the right fit. You're crafting arguments, presenting a narrative, and using language strategically. You learn to mask weaknesses, highlight strengths, and use buzzwords to create a desired impression. It’s a very similar skillset – though with completely different ethical parameters, of course. I had one candidate once, utterly unqualified, but he spun this elaborate tale about ‘synergistic partnerships’ and ‘leveraging core competencies’ that almost convinced the hiring manager. Sounds like something a postgraduate student would write!

Honestly, I still can’t believe Professor Davies set that assignment. "Analyse the socio-economic impact of the industrial revolution on Northern mill towns." Like, seriously? It's drier than Bolton in August. Tell me about it! I nearly choked on my tea when I read it. Bradford’s massively impacted, obviously, being a former wool centre, but trying to find something  new  to say about it... torture. It does seem a bit… daunting. I'm Maya, by the way. I’m finding it hard to focus in here. It’s so busy today. Liam. Nice to meet you, Maya. Yeah, it's rammed. Tuesdays always are. Progress in Northern Mill Towns... riveting stuff. I work down at the Argos near the Quays, so I get my fair share of industrial revolution chat from people complaining about the price of toasters. A sales assistant, Liam? See, that's much more exciting than analysing production figures! You probably see all sorts. Liam: You have no idea. I swear, half the population of Salford thinks an Argos knows everything. Had a lady ask me yesterday if we sold… a hamster wheel big enough for a small dog. No! You’re kidding! Liam: Swear on my mum’s gravy boat. It was a genuine request. That's brilliant! I'm studying History too, actually. But I'm specialising in South Asian migration patterns. Less toasters, more journeys. Interesting! I'm doing English Literature, focusing on post-war narratives. My dissertation's on how working-class Bradford influenced the writing of some local poets. It’s weirdly fascinating, once you get into it. I’m Chloe, by the way. I'm Emily. And I'm… floundering slightly with this industrial revolution thing. Architecture’s my passion, actually. I want to restore old textile mills, you know, give them a new lease of life. Make them into art spaces or apartments. That's a wonderful idea, Emily! Preserving history while making it useful. It's so important. It sounds like it would have a positive benefit. Chloe: It does, yeah. You’d be doing amazing work. I'm always banging on about revitalising forgotten spaces. Bradford's full of them, sadly. Bombed out in the war, then just… left to fade. Liam: My nan lived through a lot of that bombing. She used to tell stories – proper terrifying ones. Said the air raid sirens sounded like a banshee.

Honestly, this hummus is banging. Thanks, ANON. Proper feast this is. Though I'm still a bit full from that scone I had earlier. Yorkshire scones are a whole different level, ya know? Glad you like it! It was ANON's grandmother’s recipe, apparently. And yes, I completely agree about Yorkshire scones. They're a national treasure. So, you were saying something earlier about your cousin joining the military? Aye, I were. He's signed up. Proper shocked me, to be honest. Liam, ya know? Always had his head in a computer game, building ridiculous mods. Not exactly the military type, if you get my drift. Wow, that  is  unexpected. What made him decide to do it? Did he talk to you about it at all? I can barely handle the thought of joining a book club, let alone something like that. Nah, not really. Said he needed a 'change,' wanted to 'do something worthwhile.' Vague, innit? His mum's proper distraught, bless her. Says he didn't tell her properly what he was up to. Seems a bit dramatic, but you know mums. It does seem a little sudden. I can imagine it’s worrying for your family. Have you seen that new film,  Dune ? It’s got a pretty intense military vibe, ironically enough. Though obviously, it’s sci-fi, so a bit different.  Dune ? I keep hearing about it. Is it any good? I'm terrible for having a right catch-up with films, that’s the honest truth. Always something going on. Work’s been a right frenzy prepping for the pharmaceuticals convention next month. You wouldn't believe the amount of dietary requirements to cater for! Gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free... It’s bonkers. It's brilliant, honestly. Visually stunning, and the story’s got real depth. It’s got Timothée Chalamet, you know? And Zendaya. Worth a watch if you get a chance. Speaking of depth, I’m reading this magazine about AI development. It’s fascinating and terrifying in equal measure. AI, eh? Now you're talking my language! That’s where Liam’s interests probably lie. He's a whiz with computers. Used to fix my mam's ancient laptop when she couldn't get the internet working. Said it was 'therapeutic.' Therapeutic laptop fixing? That's a new one! It's amazing how much is happening in the tech world.

Honestly, did you  see  Liam’s face when I said I was designing a community centre, not another luxury apartment block? Like I'd betrayed him or something! Typical Liam. He’s got that whole ‘romantic artist’ thing going on, doesn't he? Everything has to be steeped in angst and brooding stares. A community centre just doesn't fit the narrative. Mate, you’re preaching to the choir. He probably thinks it’s some kind of capitalist sell-out. Remember when he nearly had a breakdown because I filmed that documentary about the council estate revamp? "Exploitation of the working class!" he declared. Exactly! And I was trying to explain the social benefit, the increased opportunities... he just mumbled something about ‘gentrification’ and went off to stare at a pigeon. Pigeons are  deep , Chloe. Don't underestimate Liam's appreciation for avian melancholy. Right. Melancholy pigeons. So, speaking of London types, my cousin Beatrice and her  absolutely insufferable  fiancé are coming up next weekend. They wanted to visit the Peak District, naturally, but I suggested we all meet here. Figured it'd be easier to steer them away from climbing sheep. Honestly, Londoners, eh? Like they’ve discovered a completely new world just because it doesn’t have a Pret a Manger on every corner. Don’t even start, Tom. Beatrice is… intense. She’ll spend the whole weekend subtly judging our ‘rustic’ lifestyles. Exactly. And her fiancé, Alistair, is even worse. All inherited wealth and vague pronouncements about "disrupting" industries. He'd probably try to 'disrupt' a pub quiz. The horror! So, what's the plan for keeping them entertained without them realising they're being subtly patronised? We could take them to that new art gallery in Sheffield. It’s actually really good, contemporary stuff. Might at least distract them. Good shout, Maisie. Although I foresee Alistair complaining that it’s “not quite avant-garde enough.” Or maybe we just barrage them with stories about the local football team. Anything to prove that life exists beyond the M25. Actually, that's brilliant. Just relentlessly train the conversation on the football. Beatrice will be horrified, and Alistair will look utterly bewildered. Perfect. Speaking of things that are a bit perplexing, did you see that article about the new housing developments near Winchester? They’re practically building mansions next to the council estates. It’s just… jarring. It’s disgusting, isn’t it?

"It's… bright, isn’t it? Very… minimalist. Not like how I remember your place in Brighton, love. Much less clutter.” “Mum! We decluttered! Remember all that insistence on keeping every ticket stub and dried flower? We've moved onto a more… functional aesthetic." “It’s a bit smaller than the Brighton flat, yeah. But we like it. Sussex’s lovely, honestly. Much quieter.” “Quieter’s good. Less of that racket the young people make, eh? Though, I don’t mind a bit of music now and then. As long as it’s not that… thump-thump-thump stuff.” "Your father and his musical tastes! Remember when he tried to convince me ABBA was ‘avant-garde’?” "They  were ! Ahead of their time! All that layered vocal stuff..." "Dad, you still play ABBA on repeat sometimes." "So, Mum, you mentioned you'd brought some spices? I'm desperately trying to spice up my cooking. It’s all a bit… bland, to be honest. Teaching English all day, my brain barely has room for anything else, let alone flavour combinations." "I brought my garam masala. It’s a good one, I mixed it myself. And some fenugreek seeds. Don't be scared, they have a slightly bizarre smell, but they add a lovely nutty flavour to curries.” "Ooh, sounds promising! We could try making that Korma you showed me, Mum. Remember? The one with the cashews?" "Cashews! You know, I saw a man at the bookies the other day... playing roulette. He bet everything he had on one number. Cashews. Said it was a premonition. Lost it all, of course.” "Dad, please. Don't bring gambling into a polite conversation. Especially when we're trying to discuss the joys of spices." "So, the kitchen – you like the kitchen, right? We just got that new induction hob. Makes things so much easier. Although, I’m still trying to master the art of scones. I keep burning them." “Oh, scones! The pronunciation is key, isn't it? Scone, like 'gone,' not like 'cone'! It’s been the downfall of many a cream tea.” "Exactly! It’s a regional thing, of course. Down in Kent, everyone says 'cone' though. It’s terrible, really.” "Kent… reminds me of the time I tried to win a prize at a seaside arcade. Spent twenty quid on those claw machines. Claw machines! Never did win a stuffed penguin. Had diverticulitis after all that stress, too.”

Honestly, this housing market is mental, isn’t it? Saw a two-bed flat near the station advertised for nearly £700 a month. In Cambridge! I’d need to be winning the lottery to afford that. Proper daylight robbery, it is. Tell me about it. I've been looking at places around here too, even just to consider expanding my search radius. It's… discouraging, to say the least. My parents are saying I should just move back down to Kent, but I really want to stay up here and see where this civil engineering thing takes me. Kent’s lovely, mind, but Cambridge does have a certain charm. I’m just visiting me Auntie Carol, you know? She's got that little antique shop on Mill Road. Always a good laugh in there, she is. Found a proper bargain teapot last time - you should pop in sometime. I might just do that. I need a palate cleanser after all this structural analysis. Speaking of which, the project I’m working on at the moment is driving me absolutely mad. They're pushing for this new bridge design which… well, let's just say the wind load calculations are giving me nightmares. It’s theoretically sound, apparently, but I'm having a real hard time visualising it holding up in a gale. Sounds stressful. You alright, love? You’re lookin’ a bit peaky. It’s the weather, innit? Proper grey and drizzly all day. Makes you want to curl up with a cuppa and a good book. It’s not just the weather, I think. It’s just the pressure, you know? My supervisor, Professor Davies, is brilliant, but he’s got  very  high standards. He keeps saying, “Think bigger, think bolder!” which is great, but sometimes I just feel a bit… small. Aye, I know that feel. My job, it’s not exactly saving the world, is it? But it’s important, in its own way. Wrangling data for linguistics research. I’m currently making sure a massive corpus of Northern English dialects is properly tagged and accessible to academics. It’s less structural bridges and more… structural language, I suppose. Though sometimes the errors are just as frustrating! Found a mislabeled entry the other day calling someone “reecal” instead of “reckon.” Took me ages to track down. Reckon! I've heard that one. My grandmother on my German side used to say it all the time.

Honestly, I'm buzzing after that client meeting. They actually  liked  the whole campaign proposal! It's a huge relief, you know? Been weeks of rewrites. That's brilliant, love! So chuffed for you. Copywriting must be a right brain-teaser. You've always been good with words. Remember when you wrote that poem for Mrs. Henderson's retirement? Absolutely lovely. Oh yes, I do! Little Maisie got a bit weepy reciting it, didn’t she? Goodness, time flies. Maisie’s got her own little girl now, you know. Tiny thing, like a little rag doll. She does! And she’s just adorable. I saw her at the school gates last week. Leo, her daughter, is into dinosaurs at the moment. Keeps roaring at everyone. Classic toddler. My nephew’s the same. Obsessed with T-Rexes. Anyway, speaking of work, how are things at the ward, Sarah? Still manic, I imagine? Don't you know it! Absolutely flat out. We’ve got this new agency nurse, Bethany, who’s... well, let’s just say she’s a learning curve. Bless her heart, she tries, but she keeps getting things muddled. The medication rounds are a nightmare at times. Had to gently correct her three times yesterday. Oh dear. That's tricky, isn't it? You’ve got to be so careful with medication, obviously. Mrs. Davies nearly had the wrong dose last month – thankfully I spotted it before it went to her. My heart nearly stopped. It's terrifying, isn't it? Especially with Mr. Henderson - he gets so confused sometimes. You really have to be on your toes. He asked me yesterday if I was his granddaughter. Oh, poor Mr. Henderson. It's heartbreaking seeing people lose their memory. Do you ever feel… drained by it all, Sarah? Some days, love, you feel like you’re running on empty. It’s rewarding, of course, knowing you're making a difference, but the emotional toll... it’s heavy. We try to look out for each other, though. We have a good team. We do. We all support each other. It's hard going, but you can't do it on your own. I went home last Tuesday and just collapsed on the sofa. Couldn't even face dinner. Needed a good hour just to decompress. I know the feeling. It's nice to come home and just switch off. I’ve been trying to get into yoga.
